title: FW_ State Bill Information - FS .msg
subject: FW: State Bill Information - FS
body:
FYI, please see below on recent proposed State legislation related to the Department of Water Resources’ California Water Plan. Looks like this bill is currently in committee but you can take a look at how it is currently amended. Recommend reviewing this and keeping an eye out on it. May be worth looking into how the “California Water Plan” is related to the Water Supply strategy we were directed by the Board to align with for the RWER.

Here are some highlights from my first glance and cursory review:

Existing law requires the Department of Water Resources to update every 5 years the plan for the orderly and coordinated control, protection, conservation, development, and use of the water resources of the state, which is known as the California Water Plan. This bill would require a number of new items as part of this plan:

  *   establish a stakeholder advisory committee, to expand the membership of the committee to include tribes and environmental justice interests
  *   develop a comprehensive plan for addressing the state’s water needs and meeting specified water supply targets
  *   provide recommendations and strategies to ensure enough water supply for all beneficial uses
  *   require the plan to include specified components, including an economic analysis and a long-term financing plan
  *   require the Department of Water Resources to develop the long-term financing plan, as provided, to meet the water supply targets and include the final financing plan as part of each update
  *   require the department to conduct public workshops to give interested parties an opportunity to comment on the plan and to post the preliminary draft of the plan on the department’s internet website
  *   include findings and declarations relating to water supply and climate change

DPW’s Watershed Protection Program recommended sharing the following bill with OSEJ.

SB 366<https://ctweb.capitoltrack.com/public/publishbillinfo.aspx?bi=ad%2fpvKpWGOPmkzHJiyft%2f2T0Vrau4eG1UPqF%2fTTfVASNJxhMEJLiTpfCNJ5JqKV3>
(Caballero<https://sd14.senate.ca.gov/> D)   The California Water Plan: long-term supply targets.

Current Text: Amended: 3/22/2023   html <https://ct3k1.capitoltrack.com/Bills/23Bills/sen/sb_0351-0400/sb_366_98_A_bill.htm>   pdf<https://ct3k1.capitoltrack.com/Bills/23Bills/sen/sb_0351-0400/sb_366_98_A_bill.pdf>

Introduced: 2/8/2023

Last Amend: 3/22/2023

Status: 3/22/2023-From committee with author's amendments. Read second time and amended. Re-referred to Com. on RLS.

Location: 2/8/2023-S. RLS.

Summary: Existing law requires the Department of Water Resources to update every 5 years the plan for the orderly and coordinated control, protection, conservation, development, and use of the water resources of the state, which is known as the California Water Plan. Existing law requires the department to include a discussion of various strategies in the plan update, including, but not limited to, strategies relating to the development of new water storage facilities, water conservation, water recycling, desalination, conjunctive use, water transfers, and alternative pricing policies that may be pursued in order to meet the future needs of the state. Existing law requires the department to establish an advisory committee to assist the department in updating the plan. This bill would require the department to instead establish a stakeholder advisory committee, to expand the membership of the committee to include tribes and environmental justice interests, to prohibit a member of the committee from serving longer than the development of 2 updates, and to require the committee to meet a minimum of 4 times annually. The bill would require the department, in coordination with the California Water Commission, the State Water Resources Control Board, other state and federal agencies as appropriate, and the stakeholder advisory committee to develop a comprehensive plan for addressing the state’s water needs and meeting specified water supply targets established by the bill for purposes of “The California Water Plan.” The bill would require the plan to provide recommendations and strategies to ensure enough water supply for all beneficial uses. The bill would require the plan to include specified components, including an economic analysis and a long-term financing plan. The bill would require the department to develop the long-term financing plan, as provided, to meet the water supply targets and include the final financing plan as part of each update. The bill would require the Director of Water Resources to provide an oral and written report to the Legislature, each year by May 1, regarding the progress made toward meeting the water supply targets, as specified. The bill would also require the department to conduct public workshops to give interested parties an opportunity to comment on the plan and to post the preliminary draft of the plan on the department’s internet website. The bill would include findings and declarations relating to water supply and climate change.

Notes:  3/23/2023 A-3/22/2023 to: Info PDS, DPW

title: Indian Health Council- Water Equity Introduction.msg
subject: Indian Health Council- Water Equity Introduction
body:
Good afternoon, Angelina,

First, I want to thank you for Tuesday’s conversation about nutrition and well-being with our Public Health team. I enjoyed being reminded of our relationship with food and was a little extra grateful for life after. ?? I hope you and Barbara can work together on the pilot grant to bring nutritional foods to your communities and that we can submit a letter of support. Please reach me if you need any follow up on these initiatives.

Secondly, I want to share information about our current Regional Water Equity Project (RWE) and see if it would be appropriate for you or other team members at I.H.C to participate. This a region wide assessment that involves engagement from communities to tell us what is or is not happening with water sustainability in their communities. I have attached a quick fact sheet for your review and copied my colleague Elise who is leading the project. Essentially, this assessment will provide a report to our County Board of Supervisors this fall to inform them of water equity concerns, which we anticipate will serve as a reference document for future policies and grant funding. It would be meaningful to have more Native participation.

I was thinking that I.H.C could provide valuable participation in the upcoming 1-hour virtual workshops through the summer, especially if I.H.C still provides wastewater services or water testing to tribal homes.

It would be great to connect you with Elise and any members of your team that you think would benefit from joining in. If you have availability next week or the following week, please let us know. In the meantime, please let us know if you have any questions.

I appreciate your time,

Subject: Heads up on review of Draft RDF Implementation Playbook in November

Dear County team,
Our LUEG Executive Office is working with our consultant, USD Energy Policy Initiatives Center (EPIC) on developing an “Implementation Playbook” for the Regional Decarbonization Framework (RDF). This playbook is intended to be an accessible resource by governments, community, business and individuals to get to zero carbon emissions in our region. It is not a plan and will not have specific targets or measures. The final version of this playbook will be presented to the Board of Supervisors for adoption in Spring 2023.

We would like you (or your department) to review the Draft Implementation Playbook. You would be receiving the Draft RDF Implementation Playbook on the morning of November 10. We would like your comments back by the end of November 15. Given that it is a long weekend in between, and a Board meeting week following it, we recognize that there is a limited amount of time for this review. We would appreciate it if you can pencil in your schedule the time to please review this document (which is expected to be of substantial length) so that we can turn them in to EPIC to make the necessary edits.

Here is the timeline:
11/09 Wednesday: EPIC to send Draft RDF Implementation Pathways document to LUEG by cob
11/10 Thursday: LUEG to distribute document for review
11/11 Friday: Veterans Day
11/15 Tuesday: LUEG comments due to EPIC by cob

If you would like a briefing to go over the RDF project, we would be glad to schedule it. Please let me know.

Thank you for your assistance on this,
Murtaza

title: FYI_ UCCE Contract Renewal and Negotiations.msg
subject: FYI: UCCE Contract Renewal and Negotiations
body:
Hi team -

FYI, our Agriculture, Weights, and Measures department has a 5-year contract with the University of California Cooperative Extension to support education and outreach. Below, they have indicated that a number of new technical advisors have either come on board or are coming on board. In the next couple of months AWM will be developing new objectives for this contract which could be aligned with County efforts - such as what we are doing in OSEJ.

I am sending this as an FYI so you can take a look at the current contract objectives. Once the next contract's objectives are developed, I will share with each of you for you input and perspectives before they are finalized.

(Side note for Elise/Jacob - for our meeting tomorrow with AWM on RWER, we could ask to be connected with the Fire Advisor for additional technical information on the financial risks component).

Please reach out if you have any questions. Thank you!

Rebeca

From: Cooper, Garrett <Garrett.Cooper@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Sent: Monday, May 22, 2023 5:05 PM
To: Buonomo, Heather <Heather.Buonomo@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Hemmens, Jason <Jason.Hemmens@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Whipple, Richard <Richard.Whipple@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Tolchin, Christine <Christine.Tolchin@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Wonsidler, Michael <Michael.Wonsidler@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Kelly, Meghan <Meghan.Kelly@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Moss, Claire <Claire.Moss@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Hamburger, Ariel <Ariel.Hamburger@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Nicoletti, Vince <Vince.Nicoletti@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Appel, Rebeca <Rebeca.Appel@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: UCCE Contract Renewal and Negotiations

Good afternoon,

AWM and LUEG will be entering to negotiations with UCCE to renew and establish a new 5-year contract. We will be working to establish new objectives that align with the goals of the County and then also align with some of the new advisors that they will bringing on. I have attached a copy of the current scope of work for reference and then the new advisors they will bringing on and expected start time are:

Fire Advisor: new position that has already started

Organic Waste Management Advisor: new position that has already started

4-H Advisor: Starts on August 1st

Plant Pathology Advisor: Within next three months

Urban Agriculture Advisor: Early 2024

Food Systems and Environmental Issues Advisor: Early 2024

Indigenous Farming Advisor: Early 2024

I wanted to reach out to each of you because I will be reaching out soon to the departments to determine if there are any objectives or projects that you would like considered for this 5-year contract. UCCE's work is typically concerned with providing education and outreach and their focus is on the agricultural community and providing nutrition education.  County priorities that I see UCCE having an affect on are CAP, stormwater and water quality in the region, organic recycling, food and nutrition insecurity, decarbonization efforts.

I wanted to check in and see if when I reach out if you would be the correct individuals to reach out to or if you had more specific SMEs that you would like me to work with.

Let me know and then I can begin to reach out to those individuals.

Thank you,

Subject: [External] County Grant Opportunity - Timelines for the EPA $1M Climate grant (guaranteed to SD Region)

Hey Emily,

Due to strict and short timelines, I wanted to make you aware of yesterday’s EPA announcement for Climate Pollution Reductions Grants (CPRG) as part of the Federal Inflation Reduction Act.

The CPRG provides grants to states, local governments, tribes & territories to develop & implement plans for reducing GHGs.  These grants will be provided in two phases;  $250M for non-competitive planning grants to develop strong climate pollution reduction strategies, followed by $4.6B for competitive implementation of these plans.  Of the planning grant allocations, up to $1M will be allocated to each of 67 most populous metropolitan areas nationwide.  The San Diego region falls within this category.

According to an EPA CPRG webinar this morning, municipalities, local air pollution control agencies & local governments within a metropolitan statistical area (MSA) must coordinate to identify an eligible lead organization to administer the cooperative agreement.  This lead organization must then submit a Notice of Intent to Participate (NOIP) to the EPA by April 28, 2023.  Letters of support by other entities in the area are also recommended.

The timeline for metropolitan areas is as follows:
March 1, 2023   - EPA issues CPRG guidelines
****April 28, 2023    - Metro area must submit NOIP (no extensions)****
May 31, 2023     - Metro area must submit application (no extensions)
Summer 2023    - Funding to all grantees awarded.

More information can be found on the EPA CPRG website<https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__www.epa.gov_inflation-2Dreduction-2Dact_climate-2Dpollution-2Dreduction-2Dgrants&d=DwMFAg&c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&r=cmnxsfnGVoEhSUB2PWZNOJEWm5lW6-ufe_sm9kiRmQQ&m=oSB1VwwSoN2d5qr1akkdq9Ay5CRvCJLf80Yd05yJzOc&s=4pWfIzPOH2nVC92ZBm8OxJmNwCiaf61RRZPOWvd-JI4&e=> and a recording of today’s webinar will be uploaded in a few days.

Let me know if we can be supportive somehow.

Thanks,

From: Mikey Knab <mikey@climateactioncampaign.org<mailto:mikey@climateactioncampaign.org>>
Sent: Monday, January 9, 2023 5:01 PM
To: Baxamusa, Murtaza <Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov>>; bpollard@ucproject.org<mailto:bpollard@ucproject.org>; Nicole Capretz <nicole@climateactioncampaign.org<mailto:nicole@climateactioncampaign.org>>; Brenda Garcia Millan <brenda@climateactioncampaign.org<mailto:brenda@climateactioncampaign.org>>; Galena Robertson <galena@climateactioncampaign.org<mailto:galena@climateactioncampaign.org>>; Corinna Contreras <corinna@climateactioncampaign.org<mailto:corinna@climateactioncampaign.org>>; c.paz@ucproject.org<mailto:c.paz@ucproject.org>
Subject: [External] County RDF Outreach Concerns

Murtaza,

Climate Action Campaign and Urban Collaborative Project have been working together to share best practices and methods for this outreach campaign. We're writing jointly to share some concerns about the County's systems pertaining to the RDF outreach process. Our hope is that these can be addressed quickly, minimizing any potential negative impact they may have on the overall success of the project.

In order to increase the likelihood of a successful outreach campaign, we have the following concerns/requests:
1.       The language used in the County's official materials is not consistent with how our communities communicate. We would like to be able to "say it plain," using vernacular and language that our communities will find engaging.
2.       The imagery on the County materials is not particularly interesting, relevant, or focused on the types of communities to which we're attempting to connect. We would like the ability to use imagery that is relatable to those with whom we're hoping to engage.
3.       We would like to have adequate time to review and offer edits to materials before sending them out to our communities. Currently, we still do not have flyers for some of the districts, and the convenings are scheduled this month.
4.       Bureaucratic approval seems to take a very long time. Our ability to motivate community members to engage is hindered by a lack of available information and approved materials. We request that all details of convenings, including logistics, communications collateral, and run-of-show details be shared with us at least one month prior to the convenings themselves. This will allow us to share pertinent details with community members to garner support and participation.
5.       We cannot expect our communities to feel motivated to participate in this process if we do not know exactly what will be happening at these convenings. We request that a detailed run-of-show be shared with us as soon as possible. This should include our speaking role, welcoming participants and explaining the impact that the RFP Implementation Playbook can have on their communities. Proper outreach also requires logistical details like parking information, translation services available, virtual meeting links, tabling information for community partners, etc.
6.       Food at convenings should be provided and the type of food should be shared with invitees early to help encourage attendance. CAC agreed to provide food for convenings in districts 1, 2, 3, and 5, however, Urban Collaborative Project is still awaiting response to their request that food be provided at the district 4 convening, which is scheduled in eight days.
7.       We are concerned that we are lacking some level of transparency in terms of County approval for actions related to this outreach. If we knew who the ultimate decision makers were, we may be able to minimize delays on approvals for materials, logistics, etc. Is it possible to share this with our teams?
8.       We have heard that Supervisor Vargas may be in Sacramento on 1/18/23, which is the date scheduled for the District 1 convening. We've been telling community members that they can expect to see her there. Can you confirm that the Supervisor for each district will actually be attending their respective convening in person?
Thank you for your time and attention to these concerns. We know that the County is committed to achieving great results for San Diego residents, particularly in communities of concern, and we are hopeful that addressing these issues as soon as possible will help make that a reality.

Please let me know if you are able to connect to discuss further this week.

Thanks,
--

Mikey Knab (he/him)

Director of Policy

Climate Action Campaign

Subject: Re: [External] Fwd: District 5 RDF Questions

Hi Sarah,
David (D1) called me and said he just spoke with Sonja Robinson. He asked three questions, below were my responses:

  1.   Why did we close comment period on RDF? We did not close comment period on RDF, we will continue to receive comments and address them until the Board meeting. Sonja is referring to the initial draft of the Implementation Playbook that we put out for public comment. We took it down today so that we can address the over 200 comments we received and prepare it for the Board. We are preparing an online tool that is a resource using a regional database of climate action activities that will continuously be updated with community input in the future, so there is no deadline on comments for updates of this tool. [David said it is good that we are creating an online tool.]
  2.  She says the numbers about cost are wrong in the RDF? I have referred her comments to UCSD and they are preparing a response. [David said that is good, we will wait for their response.]
  3.  She says rooftop solar is not prioritized in RDF? There are many scenarios that are focus on rooftop and infill solar (Scenario 7 & 9) that we directed by the Board. As to implementation cost, this is a regional study and not intended to cost projects, that is work we can do in the future if Board directs for example, technical assistance on community solar. [David said that is what the Chair wants.]

Murtaza

Cc: Blackmun, Michael <Michael.Blackmun@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: Final Details: Voluntary Conservation & Land Management Assistance Workshop

Good morning all,

Thank you again for your participation in next week’s Voluntary Conservation and Land Management Assistance Workshop! You are receiving this email because you have confirmed you plan to attend the workshop in person. I have attached a table layout schematic so you know where to go when you arrive, I’ve also included a map of the COC so you know where to park and which building we will be in if you’ve never been here. I’ve included the day-of logistics I circulated previously for your reference. And as always, please continue to share the workshop flyer with your stakeholders! We are looking forward to another successful event this year and want to ensure we reach as many people as possible.

  1.  Please arrive at 3:30 PM to set up your table for the event. Tables will be provided, please bring a tablecloth and any materials you plan to distribute during the event.
     *   Wi-Fi is available on our campus, so if you have a virtual component you will have the capability to do so.
  2.  Refreshments will be provided during the break from 5:30-6 PM. This will not be a meal but snacks and refreshments only.
  3.  This will be a zero waste event. DPW will be providing some recycling, trash and organic waste containers for the event, along with signage. The organic waste is composted onsite or placed in EDCO’s green organic waste dumpster.
     *   Please refrain from bringing any single-use plastic products. Paper products and wooden/bamboo utensils (or even reusable ones) are fine.
     *   The event ends at 7 PM. Please bring all of your materials with you when you leave (pack in-pack out!).

Please let me know if you have any questions!

Thank you,

We would love to invite you both to participate in this Agricultural Workforce Initiative in San Diego County. Led by Foodshed Small Farm Distro and funded by a CDFA Workforce Development Grant, this new initiative aims to support farmer-led training and workforce development in the region.

Subject: Re: [External] Re: Connecting re: Water Decarbonization

Murtaza ~ Yay, you know Cary!

I know: I loved Cary's book Becoming American (very relevant to me, as I'm a naturalized US citizen; my father was an Austrian engineer ~ hence my “techie bent").  Cary has helped me understand history ~ and how to create a better future, too.

Climate action is my biggest passion.  The 2012-ongoing SW USA droughts-drying due to climate change, has driven me to focus on freshwater tech innovations, in addition to conservation, for climate resilience.

I met Cary in 2014 when he chaired the City Council’s advisory Water Policy Implementation Task Force (2012-2014) that put mandatory watering restrictions in place, putting San Diego water savings "ahead of the curve" when then-Gov. Brown mandated 25% watering cuts during the drought).  As you know, drought regulations created considerable energy (& GHG) savings via conservation alone.
*Significant additional reductions in water demand can be created by water-&energy-efficiency innovations in the water and industrial sectors; so
water tech innovation should be a bigger priority to effect such water -> energy -> GHG savings.

Cary’s Task Force was “techie”, so besides conservation policy, they also advocated freshwater cleantech innovations (like reuse), all supported by a City Council financing vote in advance of the 2015 desalination and reuse plant plans.

Cary personally advocated that San Diego become  a fresh“Water (not just maritime) Tech Innovation Zone” (so Qualcomm hosted our Water Tech Alliance and touted their Intelligent Solutions for recycled water, energy and cost savings [at Petco Park, for example] after Cary set up WTA).  Cary and I co-wrote a SDUT op-ed urging our region to grow our fame based on innovations along with infrastructure.

Policy can really help spur and support innovation.  The County’s push for incentives (e.g., the IRWM "Conservation Homes” funding) of onsite stormwater capture could be connected to the MS-4 Alternative Compliance off-site credits aka Mitigation Banking that lets landowners and developers receive credit for meeting permit requirements by supporting stormwater projects at off-site locations.  City and County mitigation banking can be great for bottom-line financial and water decarbonization considerations.

Looking forward to our meeting!
Cheers,
Gaby

Gabriele Schubert

On Mon, Mar 6, 2023 at 3:34?PM Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>> wrote:

Good afternoon Dr. Lerner,

My name is Elise Ruiz, and I am a Group Program Manager with the County of San Diego’s Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice (OSEJ). I am reaching out to you today to inform you about the Regional Water Equity project that OSEJ is currently leading. We are working with JB with UCSD and she may have informed you about this effort:

In September 2022<https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/bosagenda.sandiegocounty.gov/cob/cosd/cob/doc?id=0901127e80f0faf8__;!!Mih3wA!GvtYTK-e8lpPHszG7mlnkW71Kcqm_x9TcdKpr4T7Pc8gGjpB3m8S7leKpGzUfoDdLvFxExHJzq_A4fwlNSk__jmIyGI$>, the County of San Diego Board of Supervisors directed staff to take a proactive, regional approach to address the drought crisis through drought management and water sustainability practices, and to align with how California legislatively recognizes the human right to water, as stated in Assembly Bill (AB) 685. Due to continuous climate change impacts, the strain on water resources will increase and affect all communities, especially those who are disproportionately impacted by water scarcity across the San Diego region.

County staff is partnering with water solution experts Geosyntec, and a supporting team including the University of California, San Diego and Re:Focus, to study these issues and provide recommendations for future Board direction. The regional drought management and water sustainability practices will be driven by three guiding principles:

•         Regional Collaboration - Consider the whole region, including local municipalities, Imperial County, and binational cities.

•         Adapt to a Hotter, Drier Future - Align with California's Water Supply Strategy<https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/resources.ca.gov/-/media/CNRA-Website/Files/Initiatives/Water-Resilience/CA-Water-Supply-Strategy.pdf__;!!Mih3wA!GvtYTK-e8lpPHszG7mlnkW71Kcqm_x9TcdKpr4T7Pc8gGjpB3m8S7leKpGzUfoDdLvFxExHJzq_A4fwlNSk_2S9irm8$>, focusing on potable and non-potable water reuse in the short-, mid-, and long-term.

•         Community, Environmental, and Industry Engagement – Learn from and partner with communities, tribes, and industries throughout various sectors impacted by issues related to water equity, and barriers to water sustainability.

We are currently in the phase of project development and beginning to collect data through one-on-one interviews, which will be used to support the Regional Water Equity Report to disseminate results at the end of this year before the Board hearing. We would greatly appreciate if you would consider being an interviewee for this process to better understand how we can identify opportunities for water sustainability practices. Good afternoon Mary,

I hope this email finds you well and that you are enjoying the beautiful spring weather! I wanted to thank you for such a wonderful opportunity to tour the Pauma Reservation and local farms last month. Our team was so grateful, and our families were thrilled to have fresh local produce!

During our visit, I may have mentioned that I am working on a Board directed effort called the Regional Water Equity project. I would like to reach out to you to see if you are interested in collaborating on this effort, as this regional assessment includes a focus on agricultural collaboration for water sustainability and equity opportunities. I’ve added some additional project details for your reference:

In September 2022<https://bosagenda.sandiegocounty.gov/cob/cosd/cob/doc?id=0901127e80f0faf8>, the County of San Diego Board of Supervisors directed staff to take a proactive, regional approach to address the drought crisis through drought management and water sustainability practices, and to align with how California legislatively recognizes the human right to water, as stated in Assembly Bill (AB) 685. Due to continuous climate change impacts, the strain on water resources will increase and affect all communities, especially those who are disproportionately impacted by water scarcity across the San Diego region.

County staff is partnering with water solution experts Geosyntec, and a supporting team including the University of California, San Diego and Re:Focus, to study these issues and provide recommendations for future Board direction. The regional drought management and water sustainability practices will be driven by three guiding principles:

•        Regional Collaboration - Consider the whole region, including local municipalities, Imperial County, and binational cities.

•        Adapt to a Hotter, Drier Future - Align with California's Water Supply Strategy<https://resources.ca.gov/-/media/CNRA-Website/Files/Initiatives/Water-Resilience/CA-Water-Supply-Strategy.pdf>, focusing on potable and non-potable water reuse in the short-, mid-, and long-term.

•        Community, Environmental, and Industry Engagement – Learn from and partner with communities, tribes, and industries throughout various sectors impacted by issues related to water equity, and barriers to water sustainability.

We are currently in the phase of project development and beginning to collect data through one-on-one interviews, which will be used to support the Regional Water Equity Report to disseminate results at the end of this year before the Board hearing. We would greatly appreciate if you would consider being an interviewee for this process to better understand how we can identify opportunities for water sustainability practices and better understand what challenges and opportunities local famers may have. If you are interested, please reply to me directly with some of your availability and I can coordinate scheduling a Teams Meeting with our technical consultant, Geosyntec and Re:focus.

Additionally, I’ve included a Fact Sheet for further information about the project and Board direction, and a Save the Date for our public kick-off event on April 26th. Subject: [External] Re: Regional convenings on climate & health - MEETING REQUEST

Dear Murtaza, Dr. Wooten, and ALL,

Thanks for organizing the convenings, Murtaza -- it was nice meeting you in person yesterday.

Dr. Wooten, it was a pleasure to interact with you on stage and on the street!

ALL, last night, I managed to make the classic old mistake of trying to present too much material in a very short presentation. I haven't done that in a long time, but it made me think about ways to make the important points in very short and accessible ways. So, i thought it might be useful to share those points about how climate change impacts our impactful weather in case you'd like to convey them to the audiences in future convenings:

Heat waves are getting more frequent, longer-lasting and more intense, as in most other places around the world. In California, heat waves are also becoming more humid, which prevents them from cooling down at night. This is already happening. We can clearly see these trends in the observed temperature data.

Precipitation regime is extremely variable (volatile) in California -- especially SoCal -- and it will get more volatile as storms become less frequent but more intense. The current situation of floods during drought exemplifies the kind of volatility that we expect to see more of as the world continues to warm.

Wildfire season will lengthen and strengthen from its October peak in SoCal into November and December. The first winter rain storms will progressively be more and more likely to come later and dry vegetation will more and more likely persist into the winter -- into the peak of the Santa Ana wind season (December). The Thomas Fire<https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Fire__;!!Mih3wA!AK0TZTR5FXMtBqA3Q4v4LyaUE5PPWo89hNQnTYwP_VBUgNnn8ig8PSescNznsdlIPVh6f74faHQjYKDh-N7XFExcSMDmDMTB$> (record largest wildfire in SoCal) burned through December 2017 into January 2018. Thomas is an example of a late-season wildfire spread by consecutive Santa Ana wind events common in December -- an example of large late-season wildfires we expect to see more of in the future.

I hope this is useful.

Best wishes to ALL

Sasha

title: Re_ _External_ Re_ Water Equity Survey Questions.msg
subject: Re: [External] Re: Water Equity Survey Questions
body:
Hi Elise,

Amazing! These are great - I'll work with our Comms team to integrate into our next newsletter.

Yay! I have you on the agenda for the SD Green New Deal Alliance meeting. We can alot 15-20 minutes for any additional questions that people may have.

Thank you and looking forward to it!

In Gratitude,
ali

On Mon, Jul 31, 2023 at 4:21 PM Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov> > wrote:

	Good afternoon Ali,

	Thanks so much for reaching out about the August 28th presentation, we are looking forward to this opportunity! The presentation usually takes about 10 minutes, and can be shortened if needed. We are still in the process of determining who would present from our team, and I will make sure to get you their info and bio once confirmed.

	A few other follow up items:

	*	I’ve attached the blurb we would like to include for the newsletter, please feel free to let me know if the wording should be adjusted or if you have recommendations of how previous RDF newsletters may have been drafted.
	*	I’ve also included the social media collateral that has been sized for posts. Please let me know if that dimension/quality works.

	As for the survey questions below, sorry if I overlooked this in previous emails, but yes absolutely please feel free to add modifications to the water equity question as we discussed during our meeting.

	Thanks so much!

	Elise

	From: Ali Mariko Dressel <ali@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:ali@climateactioncampaign.org> >
	Sent: Monday, July 31, 2023 1:03 PM
	To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
	Cc: Facendini, Bethany (She/Her/Ella) <Bethany.Facendini@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Bethany.Facendini@sdcounty.ca.gov> >; Boerboom, Jacob <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
	Subject: [External] Re: Water Equity Survey Questions

	Hi Elise!

	How long would you like for a presentation on water equity to the San Diego Green New Deal Alliance? I'm in the process of making the agenda now, so let me know who you would like to deliver the presentation, and I can send them the invite <https://us02web.zoom.us/j/88490319799> . The alliance meeting will be virtual on August 28, 5:30-6:30pm. It would also be great to send a bio and headshot whenever they get the chance as well!

	Thank you!

	In Gratitude,

	ali

	On Wed, Jul 19, 2023 at 5:14 PM Ali Mariko Dressel <ali@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:ali@climateactioncampaign.org> > wrote:

		Hi Elise!

		SO great connecting with you all as well!

		Thanks so much for these questions! After speaking with our team, would it be alright with you if we reworded the water equity question slightly? To something like "What does water equity (accessibility, supply, quality, etc.) mean to you?

		You can see our survey here <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScVn3Pm1N5dDb0EThfghb7stMNWC1xIDWSgEkl58Od5Dps_aw/viewform?usp=sf_link> . I already added the questions, but we may modify that first question with your permission. We ask for zip codes, County District (with reference to a map), and email addresses.

		We also have been sharing the deep dive events coming up and will share in upcoming list-servs and newsletters.

		In the meantime, I'm working on compiling our upcoming events and additional questions from the team, so I'll send those to you soon! All of our monthly reports also have the attached survey results (which I'll compile and send soon as well).

		In Gratitude,

		ali

		On Wed, Jul 19, 2023 at 12:09 PM Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov> > wrote:

			Hi Ali,

			It was so good to talk with you earlier this week! Thank you for all the effort your team is putting into this!

			Here are the survey questions to add to the RDF survey, and we greatly appreciate your suggestion to break out the topic by water to gather more focused responses:

			*	What does water equity mean to you?
			*	What are the biggest challenges you and your community face with water or drought impacts?
			*	What are some ways you currently conserve water or plan to conserve water?
			*	[Provide space for additional responses]

			Additionally, is CAC collecting any additional information on this survey such as zip codes or contact info if participants are interested in receiving more information? Looking forward to hearing how communities respond to these questions!

			Thanks so much,

			Elise Ruiz, Group Program Manager

			(she, her, ella)

			Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice

			County of San Diego Land Use and Environment Group

			C: (619) 455-6865

EPA is hosting a webinar to provide information about the upcoming $2 billion Environmental and Climate Justice (ECJ) Program Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) including who is eligible for the grants, eligible projects, and more. In addition, EPA is looking to gain input from border communities on the development of the ECJ Program NOFO by facilitating a discussion to hear ideas on allocating funding and providing resources to meet the needs of border communities.

This listening session is for community-based organizations, environmental justice organizations, environmental justice advocates and leaders, federally recognized tribal governments, tribal community representatives, civic and faith-based organizations, and local governments who represent border community interests. Other potential eligible entities are welcome to attend, including academic institutions.

Simultaneous English and Spanish interpretation will be provided.

For questions about this webinar or to request reasonable accommodation for a disability, interpretation, and/or translation services in a language other than English and Spanish, please email ECJRFI@epa.gov <mailto:ECJRFI@epa.gov> .

La EPA organiza un seminario web para brindar información sobre los próximos USD 2000 millones del Programa de Justicia Ambiental y Climática (ECJ), la Aviso de Oportunidad de Financiación (NOFO), incluyendo quién es elegible para las subvenciones, los proyectos elegibles, y más. Además, la EPA quiere obtener la opinión de las comunidades fronterizas sobre el desarrollo del Programa NOFO de ECJ facilitando un debate para escuchar ideas sobre la asignación de fondos y la provisión de recursos para satisfacer las necesidades de las comunidades fronterizas.

Esta sesión de escucha está dirigida a organizaciones comunitarias, organizaciones de justicia medioambiental, defensores y líderes de la justicia ambiental, gobiernos tribales reconocidos a nivel federal, representantes de comunidades tribales y gobiernos locales que representen los intereses de comunidades fronterizas. Se invita a participar a otras posibles entidades elegibles, incluidas las instituciones académicas.

Habrá interpretación simultánea en inglés y español.

Si tiene preguntas sobre este seminario web o desea solicitar adaptaciones razonables por discapacidad, interpretación o servicios de traducción en un idioma distinto del inglés y español, envíe un correo electrónico a ECJRFI@epa.gov <mailto:ECJRFI@epa.gov> .

title: RE_ _External_ Re_ Water Equity Survey Questions (1).msg
subject: RE: [External] Re: Water Equity Survey Questions
body:
Good afternoon Ali,

Thanks so much for reaching out about the August 28th presentation, we are looking forward to this opportunity! The presentation usually takes about 10 minutes, and can be shortened if needed. We are still in the process of determining who would present from our team, and I will make sure to get you their info and bio once confirmed.

A few other follow up items:

*	I’ve attached the blurb we would like to include for the newsletter, please feel free to let me know if the wording should be adjusted or if you have recommendations of how previous RDF newsletters may have been drafted.
*	I’ve also included the social media collateral that has been sized for posts. Please let me know if that dimension/quality works.

As for the survey questions below, sorry if I overlooked this in previous emails, but yes absolutely please feel free to add modifications to the water equity question as we discussed during our meeting.

Thanks so much!

Elise

From: Ali Mariko Dressel <ali@climateactioncampaign.org>
Sent: Monday, July 31, 2023 1:03 PM
To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Cc: Facendini, Bethany (She/Her/Ella) <Bethany.Facendini@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Boerboom, Jacob <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: [External] Re: Water Equity Survey Questions

Hi Elise!

How long would you like for a presentation on water equity to the San Diego Green New Deal Alliance? I'm in the process of making the agenda now, so let me know who you would like to deliver the presentation, and I can send them the invite <https://us02web.zoom.us/j/88490319799> . The alliance meeting will be virtual on August 28, 5:30-6:30pm. It would also be great to send a bio and headshot whenever they get the chance as well!

Thank you!

In Gratitude,

ali

On Wed, Jul 19, 2023 at 5:14 PM Ali Mariko Dressel <ali@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:ali@climateactioncampaign.org> > wrote:

	Hi Elise!

	SO great connecting with you all as well!

	Thanks so much for these questions! After speaking with our team, would it be alright with you if we reworded the water equity question slightly? To something like "What does water equity (accessibility, supply, quality, etc.) mean to you?

	You can see our survey here <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScVn3Pm1N5dDb0EThfghb7stMNWC1xIDWSgEkl58Od5Dps_aw/viewform?usp=sf_link> . I already added the questions, but we may modify that first question with your permission. We ask for zip codes, County District (with reference to a map), and email addresses.

	We also have been sharing the deep dive events coming up and will share in upcoming list-servs and newsletters.

	In the meantime, I'm working on compiling our upcoming events and additional questions from the team, so I'll send those to you soon! All of our monthly reports also have the attached survey results (which I'll compile and send soon as well).

	In Gratitude,

	ali

	On Wed, Jul 19, 2023 at 12:09 PM Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov> > wrote:

		Hi Ali,

		It was so good to talk with you earlier this week! Thank you for all the effort your team is putting into this!

		Here are the survey questions to add to the RDF survey, and we greatly appreciate your suggestion to break out the topic by water to gather more focused responses:

		*	What does water equity mean to you?
		*	What are the biggest challenges you and your community face with water or drought impacts?
		*	What are some ways you currently conserve water or plan to conserve water?
		*	[Provide space for additional responses]

		Additionally, is CAC collecting any additional information on this survey such as zip codes or contact info if participants are interested in receiving more information? Looking forward to hearing how communities respond to these questions!

		Thanks so much,

		Elise Ruiz, Group Program Manager

		(she, her, ella)

		Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice

		County of San Diego Land Use and Environment Group

		C: (619) 455-6865

EPA is hosting a webinar to provide information about the upcoming $2 billion Environmental and Climate Justice (ECJ) Program Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) including who is eligible for the grants, eligible projects, and more. In addition, EPA is looking to gain input from border communities on the development of the ECJ Program NOFO by facilitating a discussion to hear ideas on allocating funding and providing resources to meet the needs of border communities.

This listening session is for community-based organizations, environmental justice organizations, environmental justice advocates and leaders, federally recognized tribal governments, tribal community representatives, civic and faith-based organizations, and local governments who represent border community interests. Other potential eligible entities are welcome to attend, including academic institutions.

Simultaneous English and Spanish interpretation will be provided.

Through the ECJ Program, EPA will distribute $2 billion to community-based organizations and other eligible entities through grants and technical assistance. These funds will be used for ECJ Program grants and technical assistance for environmental and climate justice efforts that benefit vulnerable communities.

La EPA organiza un seminario web para brindar información sobre los próximos USD 2000 millones del Programa de Justicia Ambiental y Climática (ECJ), la Aviso de Oportunidad de Financiación (NOFO), incluyendo quién es elegible para las subvenciones, los proyectos elegibles, y más. Además, la EPA quiere obtener la opinión de las comunidades fronterizas sobre el desarrollo del Programa NOFO de ECJ facilitando un debate para escuchar ideas sobre la asignación de fondos y la provisión de recursos para satisfacer las necesidades de las comunidades fronterizas.

Esta sesión de escucha está dirigida a organizaciones comunitarias, organizaciones de justicia medioambiental, defensores y líderes de la justicia ambiental, gobiernos tribales reconocidos a nivel federal, representantes de comunidades tribales y gobiernos locales que representen los intereses de comunidades fronterizas. Se invita a participar a otras posibles entidades elegibles, incluidas las instituciones académicas.

Habrá interpretación simultánea en inglés y español.

Si tiene preguntas sobre este seminario web o desea solicitar adaptaciones razonables por discapacidad, interpretación o servicios de traducción en un idioma distinto del inglés y español, envíe un correo electrónico a ECJRFI@epa.gov <mailto:ECJRFI@epa.gov> .

Subject: [External] Request a Community Presentation on the RDF Playbook

RDF Team,

I belong to a group with the United Methodist Church in Escondido.  We are putting on a Climate Change Forum for our community.  Can we get a representative from your team to come speak about the RDF Implementation Playbook?

  I attended the District 5 Public Workshop on the RDF and have since read through the Implementation Playbook.   I find it to be an amazing tool for those of us who are seeking guidance on how to support actions for reducing GHG emissions in our sphere of influence.  We would like the presentation to be an overview of the playbook and how it is organized.  It would help our audience to make sense of the overwhelming issue of Climate Change because the playbook breaks it up by including a person’s sphere of influence, the five pathways for each, and the types of tasks involved in climate action.

We plan on having the forum on April 15, probably from 2:00-3:30. We are reaching out to three other speakers, so your talk would be one of those.  I hope you can be part of our event.

Thank you,
Gina Ruiz
760-616-4376

Please see below for a copy of the link to the short submittal form. You can submit the form linked below now, and just note to hold off on posting until January if you would like. Or just submit the form in January. Also, I noticed the website address posted on the notice may be incorrect. Should it be sandiegocounty.gov/RDF?

About Engagement Center:

The Engagement Center<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/engagement/home.html> website serves as a central information hub for the public to access information about County community engagement opportunities. It features an “Upcoming” section to highlight near-term public input activities such as workshops, virtual meetings, and online engagement tools (surveys and others) aimed at collecting public feedback on projects, programs, or policies. The site is linked to the County’s main website and featured on County News Center and County TV and presents an additional option for departments to promote their public input activities.

How to feature your public input activity on Engagement Center:

Please submit the form below. Information about your public input activity will be reviewed by CCO to make sure it fits the size of the fields for the online posting and posted on Engagement Center. If there are any questions about your submittal, we will contact you. If you would like assistance in populating the submittal form, I am happy to do it based on information that is provided to me on an existing project webpage, other notice, or email, etc. Just let me know.

Public Input Activity Submittal Form<https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:l:/s/FG3-CCO-CommunityEngagement/FMgLgd6Qq_ZBhuTczOuEnesBzgidG_qHF6NhAMHpceUFWA>

Please take the time to explore all the features on the Engagement Center website. Additional sections include:

  1.  Get Involved: Featuring information about the Board of Supervisors, Planning Commission, Commissions and Committees, and Volunteer Program
  2.  Learn About the County: Providing information about how the County functions through the Strategic Plan and award-winning “What Does the County Do?” video.
  3.  Stay Connected: Linking visitors to our County News Center and social media platforms
If you have any feedback or questions about the website or the Public Input Activity Submittal Form and process, please share them with me. We look forward to receiving your submittal forms and thank you in advance for your support of the site.

In service,

Natalia Hentschel

Great!

Please see below for a copy of the link to the short submittal form. You can submit the form linked below now, and just note to hold off on posting until January if you would like. Or just submit the form in January. Also, I noticed the website address posted on the notice may be incorrect. Should it be sandiegocounty.gov/RDF?

About Engagement Center:

The Engagement Center<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/engagement/home.html> website serves as a central information hub for the public to access information about County community engagement opportunities. It features an “Upcoming” section to highlight near-term public input activities such as workshops, virtual meetings, and online engagement tools (surveys and others) aimed at collecting public feedback on projects, programs, or policies. The site is linked to the County’s main website and featured on County News Center and County TV and presents an additional option for departments to promote their public input activities.

How to feature your public input activity on Engagement Center:

Please submit the form below. Information about your public input activity will be reviewed by CCO to make sure it fits the size of the fields for the online posting and posted on Engagement Center. If there are any questions about your submittal, we will contact you. If you would like assistance in populating the submittal form, I am happy to do it based on information that is provided to me on an existing project webpage, other notice, or email, etc. Just let me know.

Public Input Activity Submittal Form<https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:l:/s/FG3-CCO-CommunityEngagement/FMgLgd6Qq_ZBhuTczOuEnesBzgidG_qHF6NhAMHpceUFWA>

Please take the time to explore all the features on the Engagement Center website. Additional sections include:

  1.  Get Involved: Featuring information about the Board of Supervisors, Planning Commission, Commissions and Committees, and Volunteer Program
  2.  Learn About the County: Providing information about how the County functions through the Strategic Plan and award-winning “What Does the County Do?” video.
  3.  Stay Connected: Linking visitors to our County News Center and social media platforms
If you have any feedback or questions about the website or the Public Input Activity Submittal Form and process, please share them with me. We look forward to receiving your submittal forms and thank you in advance for your support of the site.

In service,

Natalia Hentschel

Subject: RE: [External] Upcoming RDF Gatherings

Hi Bethany,

Thank you for following up on this! I am working on addressing Ali’s questions below and updating the CBO tracking sheet with her helpful outreach dates.

*As a side note/update – I’ve been in touch with Brenda with CAC who has notified me about the Imperial Beach Democratic Council meeting on 8/3 (which we will discuss with Sarah in tomorrow’s DCAO check-in) and the Cafecito chat on 8/9 (this is a Spanish event and I am working on translating the RWE presentation to Spanish so we can be prepared for future Spanish events).

Let’s connect during our next meeting on how we should strategize attendance for these events in the coming months as we begin to work on the report review phase.

Hope you both have a wonderful evening!

E

Subject: [External] Upcoming RDF Gatherings

Hello Water Equity Team!

Apologies for my delay in getting these to you - I was PTO for the later half of last week.

Below is a list of our upcoming gatherings as well as a few follow up questions from our team.

Upcoming RDF Gatherings:

*	7/24 - Mira Mesa Community Planning Group (D3)
*	7/25 - RDF Gathering with Spanish Speaking Community at Borrego Springs Library (D5)
*	7/27/27 - Vista Climate Action Plan Meeting (tentative) (D5)
*	8/2 - Podcast on KickitLabs (D5)
*	8/3- RDF Presentation to Imperial Beach Democratic Club - 6-8 pm @Seaside Candy 150 Palm Ave.  (D1)
*	8/8 - RDF Presentation/Listening Session with Valle de Oro Community Planning Group in Rancho Santa Fe (D2)
*	8/9 Virtual RDF Presentation (Spanish) to Casa's Cafecito (zoom) - 5-6 pm (D1)
*	8/16 - Virtual Community Climate Chat with East County (D2)
*	8/23 - In Person Community Climate Chat with Coastal San Diego County (Location TBD but likely a coffee shop in Encinitas) (D3)
*	8/24 - Gathering with Unsheltered Community at Shoreline Services in PB (D3)
*	8/? (Date TBD) - RDF community session with Solana Beach Eco Rotary Club
*	9/2 - RDF tabling at Orgullo Gay Escondido (D5)
*	09/23 - RDF tabling at Oceanside Zine Fair (D5)
*	9/? (date TBD) - RDF presentation/listening session with Solana Center for Environmental Innovation
*	Early Fall (Date TBD) - tabling at the Southwestern Community College
*	10/12 Read aloud; discussion, lesson; hands on activity on RDF at VAPA (elementary school with Mrs. Spinks) (D5)
*	10/22 (tentative) - Youth Climate Event - RDF presentation, hands-on activities, speakers, breakout sessions at MiraMar College (D3 & D2)

Questions from the CAC Team:

*	At your earliest convenience, can you send us that specific language and talking points to use at our gatherings and newsletter communications?
*	If you have a 2-3 sentence blurb describing the project, that would be great as well!
*	Do you mind if we change the wording of the water equity question from "What does water equity mean to you?" to "How are you connected and/or impacted by water accessibility, supply, quality, etc.?"  or something along those lines?

You can see our survey here <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScVn3Pm1N5dDb0EThfghb7stMNWC1xIDWSgEkl58Od5Dps_aw/viewform?usp=sf_link> . I already added the questions, but we may modify that first question with your permission. We ask for zip codes, County District (with reference to a map), and email addresses. Please let me know if you would like me to send over all of the monthly reports that we have already done as well.

We have already integrated the questions into our surveys and gatherings (including a recent tabling event in Imperial Beach and at the Lakeside Library), and we will continue to do so going forward!

Excited to work in collaboration on this project going forward.

In Gratitude,

Ali

--

Ali Mariko Dressel (she/her)
Climate Justice Policy Coordinator
Climate Action Campaign
(505) 377-1139

title: RE_ _External_ Upcoming RDF Gatherings (3).msg
subject: RE: [External] Upcoming RDF Gatherings
body:
Hi Bethany,

Thank you for following up on this! I am working on addressing Ali’s questions below and updating the CBO tracking sheet with her helpful outreach dates.

*As a side note/update – I’ve been in touch with Brenda with CAC who has notified me about the Imperial Beach Democratic Council meeting on 8/3 (which we will discuss with Sarah in tomorrow’s DCAO check-in) and the Cafecito chat on 8/9 (this is a Spanish event and I am working on translating the RWE presentation to Spanish so we can be prepared for future Spanish events).

Let’s connect during our next meeting on how we should strategize attendance for these events in the coming months as we begin to work on the report review phase.

Hope you both have a wonderful evening!

E

Thank you,

Bethany

Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice <https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/osej/>

Land Use and Environment Group

From: Ali Mariko Dressel <ali@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:ali@climateactioncampaign.org> >
Sent: Monday, July 24, 2023 12:29 PM
To: Facendini, Bethany (She/Her/Ella) <Bethany.Facendini@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Bethany.Facendini@sdcounty.ca.gov> >; Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov> >; Boerboom, Jacob <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
Cc: corinna <corinna@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:corinna@climateactioncampaign.org> >; Brenda Garcia Millan <brenda@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:brenda@climateactioncampaign.org> >
Subject: [External] Upcoming RDF Gatherings

Hello Water Equity Team!

Apologies for my delay in getting these to you - I was PTO for the later half of last week.

Below is a list of our upcoming gatherings as well as a few follow up questions from our team.

Upcoming RDF Gatherings:

*	7/24 - Mira Mesa Community Planning Group (D3)
*	7/25 - RDF Gathering with Spanish Speaking Community at Borrego Springs Library (D5)
*	7/27/27 - Vista Climate Action Plan Meeting (tentative) (D5)
*	8/2 - Podcast on KickitLabs (D5)
*	8/3- RDF Presentation to Imperial Beach Democratic Club - 6-8 pm @Seaside Candy 150 Palm Ave.  (D1)
*	8/8 - RDF Presentation/Listening Session with Valle de Oro Community Planning Group in Rancho Santa Fe (D2)
*	8/9 Virtual RDF Presentation (Spanish) to Casa's Cafecito (zoom) - 5-6 pm (D1)
*	8/16 - Virtual Community Climate Chat with East County (D2)
*	8/23 - In Person Community Climate Chat with Coastal San Diego County (Location TBD but likely a coffee shop in Encinitas) (D3)
*	8/24 - Gathering with Unsheltered Community at Shoreline Services in PB (D3)
*	8/? (Date TBD) - RDF community session with Solana Beach Eco Rotary Club
*	9/2 - RDF tabling at Orgullo Gay Escondido (D5)
*	09/23 - RDF tabling at Oceanside Zine Fair (D5)
*	9/? (date TBD) - RDF presentation/listening session with Solana Center for Environmental Innovation
*	Early Fall (Date TBD) - tabling at the Southwestern Community College
*	10/12 Read aloud; discussion, lesson; hands on activity on RDF at VAPA (elementary school with Mrs. Spinks) (D5)
*	10/22 (tentative) - Youth Climate Event - RDF presentation, hands-on activities, speakers, breakout sessions at MiraMar College (D3 & D2)

Questions from the CAC Team:

*	At your earliest convenience, can you send us that specific language and talking points to use at our gatherings and newsletter communications?
*	If you have a 2-3 sentence blurb describing the project, that would be great as well!
*	Do you mind if we change the wording of the water equity question from "What does water equity mean to you?" to "How are you connected and/or impacted by water accessibility, supply, quality, etc.?"  or something along those lines?

You can see our survey here <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScVn3Pm1N5dDb0EThfghb7stMNWC1xIDWSgEkl58Od5Dps_aw/viewform?usp=sf_link> . I already added the questions, but we may modify that first question with your permission. We ask for zip codes, County District (with reference to a map), and email addresses. Please let me know if you would like me to send over all of the monthly reports that we have already done as well.

We have already integrated the questions into our surveys and gatherings (including a recent tabling event in Imperial Beach and at the Lakeside Library), and we will continue to do so going forward!

Excited to work in collaboration on this project going forward.

In Gratitude,

Ali

[?xlsx icon] 2023 Bi-weekly DCAO-OSEJ Check-ins.xlsx<https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/LUEG-OSEJ/EbeIysR-1fVOhUW1ffwfMrYBxvYwP3J5T-yaHC0giZlsog?e=bttY2z>

Subject: Announcement: Welcome Bethany Facendini, OSEJ GPM Community Engagement

Greetings All,

I am thrilled to introduce Bethany Facendini, our new Community Engagement and Outreach Manager for the Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice (OSEJ). Bethany is an experienced community organizer and sustainability advocate, and she will lead our efforts to engage and empower diverse communities throughout our region for climate action.

Bethany will develop and implement strategies to foster community connections and participation in environmental justice and sustainability initiatives. She will work closely with community benefit organizations, leaders, practitioners, and residents to create opportunities for collaboration and partnership.

Bethany brings a wealth of experience and expertise to OSEJ, including numerous community engagement roles in the San Francisco Bay Area and beyond, most recently with Sonoma County Regional Parks as the Community Engagement Division Manager. There, she directed marketing, communications, and cross-sector partnerships, as well as created sustainability and equity-based programs for diverse audiences, community needs assessments, and evaluation systems. In addition, Bethany helped increase the number of culturally relevant programs for under-represented populations (BIPOC, youth impacted by systems, people with disabilities, and families with low incomes). She also served as Sonoma County Human Services’ Community Engagement Manager where she led community programs to increase awareness of services and community outreach events; cultivated relationships between private, governmental, and non-profit organizations to improve partnerships; and built community networks to connect marginalized groups to programs and services. From 2013 – 2015 as the Community Engagement Coordinator for the Sonoma County Department of Health Services, Bethany worked on community engagement and outreach to advance health equity systems change initiatives. She has a Master of Arts in Environmental and Social Justice and a Bachelor of Arts degree in English and LGBTQ Studies. She also has an Urban Environmental Education Certification from Cornell University.

Bethany has world travel and living abroad experience in 46 countries, mostly economically developing nations, and recently returned from a year-long sabbatical traveling solo around the world.

We are excited to have Bethany on board and look forward to her leadership in advancing our environmental justice and sustainability goals. Please join me in welcoming Bethany to our team.

Enjoy the day,

eden

Eden Brukman, Chief Sustainability Officer

Land Use and Environment Group

subject: RE: CBO Regional Water Equity - Water Questions
body:
Fantastic! In general, the questions look fine. A couple observations (take or leave as y'all see fit to gather the information you need):

*	Q2. Is there value to asking this as a question at the personal level or offer it as "you and your community" to encourage them to speak about what they know?
*	Q2 and Q3 are both framed as concerns/challenges; is there a question that can be asked that is situational or neutral in its implications to help balance the inquiry? How do you use water? What strategies have you observed or used to support water conservation? Or something along those lines for context...
*	It might be useful to have a general field for other comments they may want to share about water that doesn't fit into the formal responses.
*	(I imagine that CAC is requesting zip code or similar geolocator.)

Thrilled that this outreach is moving forward. Thanks, team!

eden

Subject: [External] Meeting Opportunity: Climate Action Delegation from Saudi Arabia

Good afternoon Dahvia,

I hope you are having a great week.

I am reaching out from the San Diego Diplomacy Council to see if you or another County representative is interested and available to meet with an incoming International Visitors Leadership Program <https://eca.state.gov/ivlp>  (IVLP) delegation we are hosting.

Through IVLP, the U.S. State Department's flagship professional exchange program, we will be hosting a delegation exploring "Approaches to Climate Change Challenges" later this month. Featuring 11 subject matter experts from Saudi Arabia, this delegation will be exploring:

*	Current policy frameworks of environmental laws, protections and conservation efforts
*	Strategies for reducing carbon emissions
*	Integrated approaches to develop climate resilient solutions which support vulnerable populations and maintain biodiversity

Please see bios attached for the visitors.

Would you be interested and available to meet with this delegation from 1:30 - 3:00pm on Wednesday, June 21?

During this meeting, we hope to discuss incentives provided by San Diego County to encourage sustainable building practices throughout the region, with a particular focus on remodels and renovations, and developer relations.

Let me know if you or one of your colleagues is available to meet with this delegation

Thank you very much - I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Warm regards,

Subject: [External] Meeting Opportunity: Climate Action Delegation from Saudi Arabia

Good afternoon Dahvia,

I hope you are having a great week.

I am reaching out from the San Diego Diplomacy Council to see if you or another County representative is interested and available to meet with an incoming International Visitors Leadership Program <https://eca.state.gov/ivlp>  (IVLP) delegation we are hosting.

Through IVLP, the U.S. State Department's flagship professional exchange program, we will be hosting a delegation exploring "Approaches to Climate Change Challenges" later this month. Featuring 11 subject matter experts from Saudi Arabia, this delegation will be exploring:

*	Current policy frameworks of environmental laws, protections and conservation efforts
*	Strategies for reducing carbon emissions
*	Integrated approaches to develop climate resilient solutions which support vulnerable populations and maintain biodiversity

Please see bios attached for the visitors.

Would you be interested and available to meet with this delegation from 1:30 - 3:00pm on Wednesday, June 21?

During this meeting, we hope to discuss incentives provided by San Diego County to encourage sustainable building practices throughout the region, with a particular focus on remodels and renovations, and developer relations.

Let me know if you or one of your colleagues is available to meet with this delegation

Thank you very much - I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Warm regards,

Here are some high-level points for alignment, I’m happy to also meet separately to discuss if needed.

  *   Planning and Development Services is evaluating actions that the County can take to support climate smart agriculture in the unincorporated parts of the county to support the Climate Action Plan Update and reduce greenhouse gases in our community.

Good afternoon Dustin,

I am Rebeca Appel and I work in the County’s new Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice. Nicole Boghossian Ambrose from LUEG Exec Office provided us your contact info.

We are working on a Regional Water Equity report which was directed by the Board <https://bosagenda.sandiegocounty.gov/cobservice/cosd/cob/content?id=0901127e80f0818a>  last September. By partnering with DPW for the unincorporated area aspects, this report will identify strategies to address drought impacts regionally, and opportunities to capture and reuse stormwater in the unincorporated area. In addition, there are some components of the Board direction related to financial risks caused by extreme weather conditions caused by droughts, like floods and fires, as well as potential financial investments. Therefore, we are hoping to connect with you (or someone from your team) as we are beginning this process to get an understanding of what has been done at the County and how we may be able to bring it into this report.

Please let me know and I can find some time on our calendars. Thank you in advance!

subject: RE: checking in on outstanding items for Wed 4/26 RWER assembly
body:
Hi Danielle,

Thanks for the follow up. We’re having a nice time and working with a view of the snow up here!

  *   Our IT manager Jon, has reached out for additional IT support, who should be in office tomorrow and let us know if he can support/has recommendations.
  *   I have secured a total of 3 table cloths, Rebeca and Jacob will bring them. So we are covered!
  *   Please see the PPT attached. I spoke to John Flores today who will provide me slides tomorrow, however there is a placeholder for his segment.

I will be available tomorrow as well throughout the day, until our flight later in the evening. Thanks for all the help!

Elise

From: Danielle Sevilla <danielle@murakawacommunications.com>
Sent: Monday, April 24, 2023 12:24 PM
To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Cc: Boerboom, Jacob <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: [External] checking in on outstanding items for Wed 4/26 RWER assembly

Hi Elise,

Hope your presentation went great yesterday and that you are enjoying your conference!

I wanted to check in on the following:

  *   IT support - have you heard back from them to confirm that we will have tech support for Wednesday? If not, we will not be able to utilize the overhead projector and screen
  *   Tablecloths - were you able to secure tablecloths? Please let me know at your earliest convenience so that if not, I can bring paper ones
  *   PowerPoint - do you know when you'll be able to send me the final slide deck? Even though per our meeting you said that you would be bringing County laptops with the PP loaded and that we would run everything from there, I'd like to have the PP so that we can review to be prepared, as well as load it on our computers just in case.
Please let me know if there are any other outstanding items for us to check in about.

Thanks Elise!
--Danielle

If so, it would be handy to have this additional context.

Nicole

Hello team,

We currently have 45 people registered on Zoom to attend the above-noted meeting.  I've attached the full registration list for your reference.

Please see below for the questions we've received along with the Zoom registrations:

Rebecca Falk
rebfalk7@gmail.com<mailto:rebfalk7@gmail.com>
92004
BSCSG
Options provided by the RDF need to use correct costs and
 issues when evaluating utility scale solar/wind/other projects
 versus rooftop/distributed solar.  Sacrificing our backcountry
 communities with utility scale projects should be off the table
and especially when it is not needed.  We have to address climate
change and we also have to makes sure future generations have a
livable earth with people,  animals and plants who all need an
environment that hasn't been destroyed.

An Nguyen
annguyen1225@gmail.com<mailto:annguyen1225@gmail.com>
92129
How is equity and environmental justice being considered in this plan?

Janis Waller-Cramer
tefillintheblank@yahoo.com<mailto:tefillintheblank@yahoo.com>
92115

Lea Santos
catopalecsantos@gmail.com<mailto:catopalecsantos@gmail.com>
92127

Frank Buncom IV
fbuncom4@gmail.com<mailto:fbuncom4@gmail.com>
Firstly,  I am working to start an ocean farming company in San Diego to help restore our oceans,  provide nutritious food and fertilizer,  and create green jobs. My partners and I have begun crafting our plan to launch Salt & Earth Farm and would love to see how ocean farming fits into the county's decarbonization framework and how we can have this team as an ally through the permitting and leasing process.

Secondly,  the county is working to plant more trees to increase the tree canopy,  particularly in underserved neighborhoods. Through my work with New Leaf Climate,  I want to better understand how the county plans to buy trees for urban and forested settings and delve into the intricacies of why trees are being planted in each setting.

Thanks
--Danielle

body:

subject: RE: Deep Dive Thoughts
body:
Oops, was just informed that we did use a zoom slide (thanks, Jacob) – I totally missed it. My apologies!

From: Appel, Rebeca
Sent: Thursday, July 13, 2023 10:49 AM
To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Cc: Boerboom, Jacob <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: Deep Dive Thoughts

Good morning Elise,

Great job yesterday! There was a lot of on-the-fly decisions and pivoting on the event, so huge kudos to you for navigating it all so smoothly. I think the team also did a great job and there were some really insightful comments made by our participants (going back our conversation about pulling quotes for the report – these deep dives could be a great way to grab some quotes from!) ??

I did have a few thoughts that I wanted to share for your consideration (my apologies, I had some of these thoughts after the first deep dive, but had to leave our debrief early):

*	Consider allowing ~3-4 minutes to let folks join the meeting so they do not miss the intro also ensure to read the cover slide and welcome folks to “Deep Dive: XXX (bring in the title)” – help set the stage to the specific topic
*	Consider using these zoom slides ( TEMPLATE RDF_Implementation Playbook Slides for Working Groups.pptx <https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:p:/s/LUEG-OSEJ/ESa-zjxsJxFEtT1NUIYgRasB03yTCE3-N87n_OW6KvFOIg?e=Ex8hTm> ) for introducing using zoom, chat, and there is in interpreter - folks need to click the globe (at the bottom of the zoom platform)

	*	I know most are familiar with zoom but its helpful and this would also help allow some time for folks to join and not miss the great content of the RWER and the presenter

*	I also think it would be good to say that “this meeting is being recorded and will be posted on our website for future viewing” (or something along those lines). I know zoom notifies participants, but it is still good to say it and verbally let folks know why.

Please let me know if you have any questions at all or would like to discuss. It has been great to be on these as a team and engage directly with folks. Hope you have a great Friday-eve!

Rebeca Appel, Group Program Manager

(she, her, ella)

County of San Diego Land Use and Environment Group

Subject: Delegation from Saudi Arabia - OSEJ and PDS

Hi Nicole,

As we briefly discussed, the County has been invited to meet with a delegation from Saudi Arabia on this coming Wednesday, June 21 from 1-3:30pm. This is through the International Visitors Leadership Program <https://eca.state.gov/ivlp>  (IVLP) which is the U.S. State Department flagship professional exchange program. This invitation was offered by the San Diego Diplomacy Council yesterday (originally received by Dahvia, who sent to myself and Caroline Smith).

Tyler and I just met with the coordinator at the San Diego Diplomacy Council and it appears to be similar to when we welcomed the Japanese delegation, just on very short notice. Here are some details:

*	The topic of delegation trip is "Approaches to Climate Change Challenges"
*	The 11 individuals span government, private, and entrepreneurship and are traveling with 3 interpreters
*	The delegation is most interested in exploring and hearing stories from us around:

	*	Current policy frameworks of environmental laws, protections and conservation efforts
	*	Strategies for reducing carbon emissions
	*	Integrated approaches to develop climate resilient solutions which support vulnerable populations and maintain biodiversity

*	The delegation is currently in D.C. Once in San Diego, they will meet with Scott and Nilmini from USD-EPIC, and then they head to Imperial Valley for solar panels and lithium.

Some logistic and proposed approach:

*	They have asked us to host, and therefore, we could reserve a room at the CAC
*	They have asked for presentations and discussions to fill the 90 minute slot. Therefore, we propose:

	*	OSEJ Overview (Rebeca) & RDF presentation (Rimga) (same as the Japanese delegation)
	*	Discussion
	*	CAP Presentation (Tyler) (and potentially: Other Sustainability Programs)
	*	Discussion

Questions for you:

*	How should we brief this up to Sarah? Based on our experience with the Japanese delegation, would Sarah want to participate?
*	Could I have some assistance with logistics? With our recent experience with the Japanese delegation, it would be great if Yasamin would be able to help.

	*	Such as room reservations, reaching out to Board offices (if we want), coordinating refreshments and gifts (if needed/desired)

Thank you!

Rebeca Appel, Group Program Manager

(she, her, ella)

Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice

County of San Diego Land Use and Environment Group
