Subject: FW: Earth Day

Good afternoon Elise and Anali,

First, I want to introduce you both to one another. Elise is in OSEJ with me and works as the project manager on the Regional Water Equity Report. Anali is a nutritionist in Public Health who works with tribal families on nutritional programming. Both of you have mentioned interest in attending the June 24th tribal Earth Day event at La Jolla so I wanted to coordinate a few items and maybe schedule a touch base meeting on June 21st at 10.a.m.? Would that work for you?

Attached is the event flier but here are some additional details to note and planning ideas ??

Event Details:

*	Arrive 9:30 a.m. to set up 1 shared table.
*	Event time: 11:00 a.m. -3:00 p.m.
*	Intertribal Earth Day with 8 surrounding tribes
*	Anticipate 600 tribal community guests
*	Anticipate 50 vendors from local agencies and tribes
*	Zero Waste event-
*	Pack lunch, sunscreen, and water (just in case!)
*	No cell service in the area
*	Pack own chairs

Supplies for Table:

*	Use LUEG tablecloth- Roberta
*	Roberta brings table and canopy
*	QR code for OSEJ website-Roberta
*	Water Equity information – Elise?
*	Fruits and freebies- Anali
*	Public Health QR Code to website/info- Anali
*	Maybe we can come up with an interactive activity for the table…?

Travel Arrangements:

*	I will likely travel from home as I live in Riverside County. I am not sure if they two of you would be interested in carpooling but maybe its an option. An OERJ team member may also tag along but I will find out early next week.
*	Cell service is bad once you pass the round about by Rincon off HWY 76. The event is on the same turn off as the La Jolla Trading Post (gas station/casino). There are campground signs to take you below the gas station, but they are faded. ??

Thank you both for your support. It should be great weather!

Roberta Leash, Group Program Manager, County Tribal Liaison

title: RE_ Financial Risks Chapter .msg
subject: RE: Financial Risks Chapter
body:
Hi Jacob,

Thanks so much for walking us through the great work you put together. Here are my notes and links.

Suggest starting with how we are defining financial risks and financial investments (as part of the board direction)

1e. Identify financial risks caused by extreme weather conditions caused by droughts, like floods and fires.

1f. Identify financial investments needed for resilience approaches that reduce risks and impacts that are exacerbated by extreme weather conditions caused by droughts like floods and fires.

Notes

  *   Start big with CA - then zoom into our region-- what about our different geographies?
     *   Like does extreme weather look different in mountain regions to our coastal areas? Would be good to highlight if possible
  *   County vulnerability assessment 2021: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/gpupdate/VulnerabilityAssess-AdaptRpt.pdf
     *   The County Vulnerability Assessment and Adaptation Report, prepared by Ascent Environmental and adopted by the Board on July 14, 2021 (1) as part of the General Plan’s Safety Element, predicts severe climate change impacts on the unincorporated areas of the region, including higher frequency and intensity of extreme heat events, droughts, and wildfires. To illustrate this, the impacts of climate change on the County’s unincorporated areas will vary based on medium-to-high greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions scenarios from the historical average (1961-1990) to the mid-21st century as follows:
        *   Maximum temperatures will increase from 75.3°F to between 80.5-81.4°F average annually.
        *   Extreme heat days will increase from four days to between 34-45 days on average annually.
        *   Heatwaves (which are four or more consecutive extreme heat days) will increase from a frequency of one every five years to between six to eight heat waves per year.
  *   California Climate Assessment: https://www.energy.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2019-11/20180827_Summary_Brochure_ADA.pdf
     *   California’s Fourth Climate Change Assessment stated that “California is one of the most ‘climate-challenged’ regions of North America; its historical climate is extremely variable, and climate change is making extreme conditions more frequent and severe... [and we need to] rapidly reduce climate pollution to avoid the worst effects of climate change”[1]. This assessment identifies the following impacts of climate change on the San Diego region:
        *   Temperature is projected to increase substantially, by 5°F to 10 °F by the end of the 21st century. Along with mean temperature, heat wave frequency will increase, with more intensity and longer duration.
        *   Precipitation will remain highly variable but will change in character, with wetter winters, drier springs, and more frequent and severe droughts punctuated by more intense individual precipitation events.
        *   Broadly, wildfire risk will likely increase in the future as climate warms.
        *   Sea level along the San Diego County coast is expected to rise approximately 1 ft by mid-21st century, and 3 ft or potentially much higher by 2100.
        *   Recent work in the San Diego region showed that heat-related health impacts are observed at lower temperatures in the coastal region than in the inland and desert regions. This is in part due to coastal residents being less acclimated to heat and less likely to have air conditioning.
        *   Climate changes felt by San Diego County will also occur in northern Baja, Mexico. Binational coordination of climate adaptation measures present potential for significant benefit to communities on both sides of the border.
  *   Yes to using the lit review prepared for the San Diego context
  *   Resources and links to Office of Emergency Services: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/oes/emergency_management/oes_jl_mitplan.html
     *   The Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan is a countywide plan that identifies risks and ways to minimize damage by natural and human-caused disasters. The plan is a comprehensive resource document that serves many purposes such as enhancing public awareness, creating a decision tool for management, promoting compliance with State and Federal program requirements, enhancing local policies for hazard mitigation capability, and providing inter-jurisdictional coordination.
        *   The Board of Supervisors of the County of San Diego adopted the revised 2023 Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Base Plan on February 7, 2023.
           *   Suggest reading the Board Letter and Minute order as well as seeing if there was a presentation that day.
           *   https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/oes/emergency_management/HazMit/2023/MJHMP%20SD%20County%20Base%20Plan%202023.pdf
     *   San Diego County Resilience Review Working Group: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/oes/emergency_management/plans/Resilience-Review-Reports/SDC_RESILIENCE%20REVIEW%20REPORT_WILDLAND%20FIRES_FINAL_20190909.pdf
     *   Resiliency Review Program: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/oes/emergency_management/plans/Resilience-Review-Reports/SDC_CRP%20CAPSTONE%20DOCUMENT_FINAL_02_13_2020.pdf
  *   Identify financial investments needed for resilience approaches - what do we mean by this?
     *   How are we interpreting this? What investments exist for resilience
  *   Maps developed for the RDF regional convenings – urban heat island effect and fire hazard: [?Folder icon]  Maps<https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/LUEG-OSEJ/Eu0o4u8zIAlLuypCqsNCGIkBFO6T1OWn3RY08RtwdisIcw?e=aeGKqN>

Next steps discussed:

  *   Jacob to develop outline of this section of the report
  *   Rebeca to connect team with OES to discuss (checking with Nicole/Stephanie)
  *   Elise developing roles/responsibilities for overall RWER
  *   Once ready and have outline and timeline, brief Eden, then when appropriate, brief Sarah
  *   Also can connect with Ross Martin about the report and data we have, what we need, etc.
     *   risk factors mashed up with HPI/CalEnviroScreen

Hi all,

Thank you for the feedback. It would be most helpful to gather contact recommendations sooner than later as I am preparing a follow-up to Farm Bureau, as it has been a week since we met. I would like to be proactive as they gave a lot of feedback and expressed frustrations about topics outside of the topic of water and want to provide them with resources to address their concerns outside of the Water Equity scope. I am still learning the many of moving parts to the County departments and functions – I appreciate any feedback/guidance while we build this relationship with this important stakeholder.

Additionally, I am planning on joining the PDS meeting with Farm Bureau next month to provide an update on Water Equity, and will continue to meet with Farm Bureau as the comprehensive report results become available to share.

Thank you,
Elise

Hello Elise.
In reviewing your report, I agree with Mel. The context surrounding the connections you would like to make would be helpful. PDS does meet with the Farm B monthly and in that meeting they discuss any development permits needed, Code enforcement issues, and stormwater permit and enforcement issues which we enforce due the Regional Water Quality Control Board. I do see there were questions about pesticide which may include AWM and PDS depending the issue so we may want to connect to discuss. I can circle back with the POD in AWM to discuss their regulatory interaction with Farm B and see if there is any follow u up there.

Regarding Future reports, one of the main reason for the biweekly outreach meetings is to discuss and review outreach efforts, and from the Farm B and other stakeholders engaging in your OSEJ project and to discuss which ones need to be addressed further and elevated.

I am available if you want to chat or we can follow up at the next OSEJ outreach biweekly which I think is set for next Tuesday.

Thanks

Cc: Lee Friedman <LFriedman@sdcommunitypower.org<mailto:LFriedman@sdcommunitypower.org>>; dtipping@sdge.com<mailto:dtipping@sdge.com>; ahomer@kelleydrye.com<mailto:ahomer@kelleydrye.com>; Huber, Michael J CIV USN COMNAVREG SW SAN CA (USA) <michael.j.huber20.civ@us.navy.mil<mailto:michael.j.huber20.civ@us.navy.mil>>
Subject: [External] IEA "Decarbonization" Panel: kick-off meeting request

Hi Chris, Byron, and Elise,

Thanks for agreeing to participate on a panel discussion called "Decarbonization: A Path to Zero" during this year’s Industrial Environmental Association (IEA) conference. The panel will take place during the IEA conference on June 1. See the attached Word document (also pasted below in this email) for more panel context.

We're calling the format of this panel a "curated conversation" led by a scripted Q&A. During the panel, we will have one combined PowerPoint that addresses the questions posed by the Moderator (me). I will advance the slides while you, the Panelist, answer a particular question.

Since this panel format is more involved than others, I would like to meet with you a few times in advance of the June 1 panel. During our first meeting we can meet each other, discuss the scope of the conversation, and determine the cadence of our future meeting schedule and deliverables.

If scheduling gets complicated, I can set up Doodle polls, but I’ll take a chance with the first meeting date.

Are you available the afternoon (1 – 5 p.m.) of either Thursday, March 16 or Friday, March 17 to meet?

Thanks,
Chad

***

Decarbonization: A Path to Zero

In 2022, California lawmakers passed a series of climate-related bills. Assembly Bill 1279 reiterated the state’s plan to reach carbon neutrality by 2045, and building off Senate Bill 100, California Senate Bill 1020 has a target of 100% renewable and carbon-free electricity economy wide by 2045.

But as the San Diego region faced the possibility of blackouts during the summer of 2022 due to grid-related strain from heatwaves, storms, and wildfires, it leaves some to wonder how the state will achieve its stated goals.

During this session, representatives from San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E), San Diego Community Power (SDCP), and the County of San Diego will discuss efforts underway to harness regional ingenuity and help meet state goals.

FORMAT
Curated Conversation with one main PowerPoint managed by moderator (no individual PowerPoint presentations)

SESSION DATE/TIME
Thursday, June 1, 2023 @ 3 p.m.
https://ieaca.org/conference/

MODERATOR

  *   Chad Reese, Environmental Affairs Manager, San Diego County Regional Airport Authority
PANELISTS

  *   Christopher Summers, Director – Origination, Energy Supply & Dispatch, SDG&E (confirmed) https://www.linkedin.com/in/christopher-summers-439b6233/
  *   Byron Vosburg, Managing Director, San Diego Community Power (confirmed) https://www.linkedin.com/in/bvosburg/
  *   Elise Ruiz, Decarbonization Program Manager, County of San Diego (confirmed) https://www.linkedin.com/in/elise-ruiz-emsl-environmental-biologist/

Chad Reese
Environmental Affairs Manager, Planning & Environmental Affairs
Office 619.400.2780  |  Mobile 619.866.5817
creese@san.org<mailto:creese@san.org>

San Diego, California 92101

body:
Good morning Eira,

Thank you very much for the comprehensive and insightful overview! And thank you for the attachments. We will review and send you any feedback we may have.

On the request related to the RDF analysis, I took a cut at summarizing Chapter 5 (Natural Climate Solutions) of the results and analysis of carbon storage and sequestration potential for the purpose of the tax-defaulted parcels assessment. I’ve attached Chapter 5 for your reference as well. Please let me know if you’d like to discuss or if sending shapefiles will be useful. I do not have them currently, but I can reach out to the authors.

Summary of criteria and results from Chapter 5 RDF:

  *   The authors used SanGIS’s “ECO_VEGETATION_CN” (date of data: August 2021; downloaded August 2021) and added an associated carbon value which was later calculated to visualize carbon storage and sequestration potential by vegetation type. See Figure 5.3 on page 14 and Figure 5.4 on 15 of the attached PDF.
  *   The values assigned to each vegetation types came from literature and varied depending on the type of vegetation. Each value is shown on page 46 of the PDF (Appendix 5.A Methods, data, and sources for carbon stock and flow data and sources).
     *   This appendix provides the methodology used to calculate the sequestration and carbon storage of vegetation types and has all the literature sources. The maps that were eventually developed aggregated by broad land use type based largely on IPCC land use types.
  *   Page 13 has table 5.2 (pasted below) shows the results of Chapter 5 analysis – that “the biodiverse and ecologically rich natural landscapes in the San Diego region have significant potential for both carbon storage and for annual carbon sequestration”

Subject: Annual list of tax default properties

Hello land acquisition roundtable colleagues,

In our last meeting we discussed revisions to the County’s process for liquidation of tax default properties. Specifically D3 would like to empower DPR (and other departments if appropriate) the authority to claim tax defaulted properties in support of a wider spectrum of County initiatives, i.e., not just habitat conservation but also flood control, fire protection, climate action and decarb, agriculture, watershed protection, etc. A D3 board letter will likely be docketed for Jan 25.

Coincidentally, the Treasurer & Tax Collector is preparing to initiate the annual auction process for tax defaulted properties. The board letter will move forward next Tuesday Jan 10. This year it includes over 500 properties. After the BOS action there is a short window of time where public agencies and eligible non-profits can exercise a right of first refusal on any of the properties before they are auctioned in early March.

Reviewing such a large number of properties in a short time is a heavy lift for our team. The DPR acquisition team will do an initial screening review and identify a short list of properties that might align with one or more of our roundtable criteria. Those properties will undergo a deeper dive analysis.

Here’s my ask…if you are able to assist in the initial screening review please connect with DPR acquisitions manager Eira Whitty. Thanks!

Brian

INTRODUCTION: (scientific, analyses, integrated actions)

OVERVIEW: (government, business, community)

Transportation (driving, EVs, fuel use, carpool, biking, walking, transit)
Workforce (trades, office)

Natural lands/ working lands i.e. Ag (agriculture land, Trees, wetlands, carbon removal, storage, reducing ag methane)

Water use/supply (indoor water uses, outdoor uses, reuse)

Subject: RE: OSEJ/RDF Steering Committee Agenda

Hi Murtaza and all -  great meeting on Friday and we received a lot of DCAO input and direction. I added the main action items below, based on Sarah’s feedback.

  1.  Regional Decarbonization Framework
     *   DCAO: we need to foster the business community as well as workforce. Wherever we talk about green jobs we need to talk about green industry. They go hand in hand.
                                                               i.      Murtaza need to follow up with David Flores - the items on green industry that Sarah shared was not included in Chairwoman's talking points
                                                             ii.      We need to highlight both -- it is not one or the other -- Sarah needs help reinforcing this piece with D1 (or else we will face obstacles in the business community.

     *   DCAO feedback on Symposium: Donna needs to be engaged on this -- she needs to take the lead on this. Sarah requests a meeting (30 min) to talk about the symposium
                                                               i.      We need to come back with Sarah on our plan to move forward, then have another call with David and other partners

     *   DCAO feedback on D3 convening: need to put a timeframe of when the convening needs to take place. If she can't make it then we need to move forward on it. Hold them to a timeline (because we need it for the BL, Board hearing, etc.). Can't have their district missing in this.
     *   DCAO question for us to consider: Because we are bringing this home through public health -- for purposes of when we go to the Board - should we tee up some joint Public Health approach/PPT for March hearing?
     *   DCAO: how many Playbook copies are we printing? Maybe print one for each Board office and our office -- like 30 or 40
     *   DCAO: Sarah wants information as the comments come in on the Playbook -- we may not include things proactively -- but have them discuss in the public setting
  1.  Regional Equity Group
     *   For when Murakawa meets with Sarah: how do we ensure all of our communities are represented? Not just cities, but unincorporated as well. Who will they engage? Who are the players for the
                                                               i.      What info do we need to provide them so they are educated about San Diego region dynamics -- this will be important
                                                             ii.      Connect Murakawa with PDS EJ team

  1.  Regional Water Equity Project
     *   DCAO: always Board office that moves a Board letter forward - they should be in the know. But also the whole Board took action. Start with key Board office, and then say that we are going to share with all office because we need to meet the needs. Different Board offices will have different perspectives of this -- like all the ag and Borrego Springs (worst groundwater impacted in the State) -- they have critical needs.
                                                               i.      For the one pager -- who needs to weigh in, in additional to the Board offices -- Donna, Michael. Need people far removed to review and provide insight

     *   DCAO: would like a timeline on all aspects of outreach, when will we start to make the pitch - before it starts
  1.  Misc.
     *   DCAO briefing request: would like a briefing on Spring Valley communities in terms of what we are doing for TCC grant.
                                                               i.      How are PDS and DPW involved in these conversations
                                                             ii.      As we are moving forward on SLTF -- what is the alignment, what is the overlap
                                                           iii.      Anything related to road planning, housing planning
                                                           iv.      How are we pulling this all together globally
                                                             v.      How is the work we are doing as part of TCC -- into the parcel by parcel analysis and SLUF

Hi Jordan,

Thank you so much for your response and interest to participate in this effort.

Yes, this would be an equity focused interview covering water quality, accessibility, and drought impacts as it relates to agricultural operations. We will have the interview questions sent to you ahead of time so you can prepare. The financial piece is more related to risk assessment of extreme weather, which is being covered through a separate consulting effort. This data will be available in the final deliverable, the Regional Water Equity Report, in case you are interested in the results.

I will check Geosyntec’s availability for next week. I will also follow up with an email introducing you to the Geosyntec team. I look forward to connecting with you!

Subject: Pala EPA and County Water Equity Project

Good afternoon, Shasta,

I am the new and first official County-Wide Tribal Liaison in the County of San Diego. I met with Pala Tribal Council this past Wednesday and they provided me with your contact information to coordinate potential partnerships with your EPA Department. My colleague Elise and I would really like to connect with you to share what we have going on in the County and to learn more about what Pala is working on.

One of our current projects is a region-wide Water Equity Assessment that we just kicked off at the end of April and will continue through the summer through a series of 6 virtual workshops. We would love to have Pala and other tribes’ participation. Essentially, the outcome of this assessment is a report that identifies areas of concern for Water Equity in the region and that report will be in front of our Board of Supervisors and will likely be used as a reference tool for future policy and funding. I’ve attached a quick fact sheet for your review because it’s important to note that the project surrounds topics of drought conditions and water sustainability through greywater, wastewater, and stormwater capturing.

If you have time in the next week or two, can we set up a time to share more information? Our workshops start near the end of June.

Thank you and have a joyful weekend,

Subject: Notes from today's meeting with Supervisor Vargas

DISTRICT 1 ATTENDANCE

Chair Nora Vargas & David Flores

COUNTY STAFF ATTENDANCE

Murtaza Baxamusa, Elise Ruiz & Yasamin Rasoulzadeh (LUEG)

Dr. Wilma Wooten & Jo Ann Julien (PHS)

BRIEF OUTLINE

The goal is to get community engagement in these issues at the intersection of climate and justice:

·                     Recognizing district community needs?

o        Wildfire, heat waves, air pollution, flooding?

·                     These climate events are increasingly becoming more frequent and their impacts on our communities are becoming more harmful, especially for our vulnerable residents?

o        For example, seniors and those with asthma or other underlying health conditions can have severe impacts from the air pollution caused by fires?

o        Working with Dr. Wooten, Public Health Services

·                     The good news is there are opportunities for investments and good green jobs. For example, the California Air Resources Board is investing billions of dollars in clean technology for transportation?

o        The state is also focused on incentivizing in well-paying careers in these new technologies?

o        Working with Regional Equity Group to develop social equity indicators for CAPs

MEETING NOTES

OVERVIEW - Murtaza began the meeting with outline (see above) the overall purpose and schedule of the Regional Convenings, as well as explaining guest speakers’ topics.

Murtaza: At the August 31 hearing we had completed the Framework’s Technical Report and heard about the need to work on implementation. Now drafting the IP, which are collaborative pathways to work together. The intentional outcome after the Convenings is that the received feedback for the Regional Decarbonization Framework Implementation Playbook (RDF IP) will be used for updates and direction on regional actions from the Board of Supervisors during the Board Hearing tentatively on March 15. The key goal of these Regional Convenings scheduled over the next two weeks will be district by district, and we will hold one specifically for tribes as well at a later time. We are also focusing on how our residences are being impacted and what the County is doing. These topics are focused on the intersection of climate and justice and keeping that consistent throughout these discussions.

Chair Vargas: Is that information going to be shared with the public? When we talk about climate change with the equity lens, usually equity/EJ is assumed, but that is not always expressed or elaborated on. How do we share that effectively? That is my goal.

Murtaza: We have a couple of slides in the presentation to expand on this, and express that equity is not a standalone topic – it flows through all sectors and integrated in every component of this effort. For example, from the fire hazard data in the D1 (Murtaza shared district map), the district is at risk of poor air quality from wildfires and impacts to habitat. The most important thing is to engage communities who have not been involved in these abstract climate topics.

Chair Vargas: I love that, I agree.

Murtaza: Because these impacts are becoming more frequent, this effects vulnerable residents even more. This has driven the work with Dr. Wooton’s team and the Public Health Services (PHS) research, who is putting together a team of experts in health science to research how we can address these concerns.  David wanted me to touch on the long-term plan and what goes beyond March. The long-term plan with this is to focus on green jobs, where we can build on equity while bringing in investment to our communities and addressing climate change at the same time. I know you mentioned the funding from CARB concerning sustainable transportation transitions, and how do we get our communities to benefit from those funding opportunities. One of our thoughts is that focusing on the RDF, our office can work with the Social Equity Group that your office is proposing to develop social equity indicators for climate action.  You also mentioned how is equity being operationalized – This involves working with the community through this regional Equity Group. We can develop a guidance document that is common and with input from all regional agencies.

Murtaza: Clarified Vargas schedule –

Chair Vargas: This is very important to me. I want to attend.

Vargas will be going to CARB Senate Confirmation on the 18th of January – arrives in SD at 6:20, and suggested to wants to close convening event. Wants to go straight to events location when arrives and will listen to event virtually as much as possible. A D1 Team Member – (TBD) to make announcement that this is a priority and state that Vargas is listening and will be on the way to the event. Vargas team to also make a video to help as a contingency plan.

Jo Ann Julien: Explained general overview of PHS presentation – Will have climate science/atmospheric rivers and climate change, expertise on how climate change effects the residence. This will Go over equity and equal access with maps and visuals for data. Wooton will be more general of intersection of CAPH and identified vulnerability. Wooton will go over indications: transportation/air conditioning. This will satisfy Vargas interest in addressing equity - Then focus on what the County is doing and ground these impacts based on Zip codes and CBOs interests.

[Dr. Wooten joined at this time, and requested PHS staff to present a couple of slides]

Dr. Wooten: Explained the BRACE process which is a State adaptation of CDC brace program. Includes 5 components:

·         Vulnerability assessment,

·         Projecting the Disease Burden,

·         Assessing Public Health Interventions…

·

Chair Vargas: Wants to showcase Wooten’s BRACE visuals and data in the State of the County address. Believes the intersection is very important. Health has been her focus even before she became Supervisor.

Dr. Wooten: (details of presentation will be shared with D1) Explains that this is normally a 1-hour presentation and will be condensed to 15 minutes for this event.

Chair Vargas: Additionally, to be in line with some of these topics (i.e. tree canopy coverage and heat island effect) the goal is to plant 10,000 trees and want to connect it to this concept.

Murtaza: To summarize. We will be reaching out to your office for a video message as backup for Wednesday. David also asked me to remind you that your regional equity Board Letter with D3 for January 25 provides for a workshop/symposium that brings together business, labor, investors…. We can also have federal/state agencies to talk about economic opportunities that create green jobs.

Chair Vargas: Let’s do this. David, make sure it is in the Board Letter.

Subject: RE: Voluntary Conservation & Land Management Assistance Workshop Pre-Meeting

Good morning all,

Thank you to those of you who were able to attend the meeting yesterday. I wanted to provide the information that was discussed to the rest of the group.

  1.  Confirmation & Workbook Pages
     *   If you have not done so, please confirm whether you will be participating in this year’s workshop. If you would like to participate but cannot attend in person, we can still include your program in the workbook. Attached is the workbook from last year, please review and provide any updates as needed ASAP.
  2.  Overview Presentation
     *   Linked here<https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1pk6u_ye-Zy_1nI2YRp9O1kjy7TYDsgPx/edit?usp=share_link&ouid=111114943435889553036&rtpof=true&sd=true> is the presentation that was used last year to provide an overview of the programs participating in the workshop. Please review your slide and voiceover recording. If you would like to update your slide and/or voiceover, please submit this no later than EOD February 17th.
  3.  Advertising
     *   Please share the attached workshop flyer with your stakeholders! We are looking forward to another successful event this year and want to ensure we reach as many people as possible. Please share the flyer via email or post around your public offices to raise awareness about the event.
  4.  Day-of Logistics
     *   Please arrive at 3:30 PM to set up your table for the event. Tables will be provided, please bring a tablecloth and any materials you plan to distribute during the event.

                                                               i.      Once I get the final confirmation of those attending in person, I will provide a layout of the room with table numbers so you know where to go.

                                                             ii.      Wi-Fi is available on our campus, so if you have a virtual component you will have the capability to do so.

     *   Refreshments will be provided during the break from 5:30-6 PM. This will not be a meal but snacks and refreshments only.
     *   This will be a zero waste event. DPW will be providing some recycling, trash and organic waste containers for the event, along with signage. The organic waste is composted onsite or placed in EDCO’s green organic waste dumpster.

                                                               i.      Please refrain from bringing any single-use plastic products. Paper products and wooden/bamboo utensils (or even reusable ones) are fine.

     *   The event ends at 7 PM. Please bring all of your materials with you when you leave (pack in-pack out!).

Thank you all for your participation! Please let me know if you have any questions.

Cc: Amos, Siana <Siana.Amos2@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Trisha Murakawa <trisha@murakawacommunications.com>
Subject: [External] prep for Regional Convenings

Good afternoon,

Hope this email finds you all well and getting ready to celebrate the New Year!

As we prepare for our kick-off meeting and the regional convenings, we have a few questions for you:

  *   Contact information for each location: It would be helpful to have contact info so that we can inquire about tech availability as well as set up/break down, logistics; this will help inform what equipment we need to bring and what the video/A/V people need to be prepared for, and what our team needs to be prepared for when doing set-up/breakdown, unless you or someone on your team can answer these types of questions for us
  *   Satellite sites noted on the list of venues: What exactly does this mean?  Is this a location where folks can watch the livestream and participate in Q & A from, will our team need to include the satellite location in our staffing? Please provide additional information.
  *   A/V, video, livestream, interpretation: Confirmation that our team will be providing the A/V support, videographer, livestreaming, and interpretation for each meeting
  *   Copy of slide presentation deck, even if it is still being developed: - Can we get this at your earliest convenience so that we can begin familiarizing ourselves with it?
  *   Copy of LUEG presentation: Can we get this at your earliest convenience so that we can begin familiarizing ourselves with it?
  *   Team members and VIPS: List of team members to be introduced at the meeting, as well as any VIPS who may attend who should be acknowledged (in addition to each supervisor), so that we can be prepared for introductions and acknowledgements when we open each meeting
  *   Health/science experts speaking at the events: The tentative program you provided lists Dr. Eyal Oren D2/D5; Dr. Tarik Benmarhnia D4 - what about D1, D3?
  *   Collateral materials, translation (public notice/invitation/event flyer, handouts, slide deck, signage, poster boards, etc.): Per our call with Murtaza, you will be taking care of these items for this first series of meetings, please confirm; please let us know how we can be helpful in producing these pieces, what support we can offer. Please advise if we will be providing the written translation for them and if so please provide us with copies of each as soon as possible so that we can get them translated as well as for our own review and reference, as well as a deadline for turning them around
  *   Fact sheet: as with the above noted, in our call with Murtaza he said you would be taking care of the initial one - how can we support this effort, and will it need translation?
  *   Refreshments: Please advise if we will be providing refreshments for each meeting (light refreshments i.e. water, coffee/tea, pastries, etc.)
  *   Community-based partnerships: What is the status of the community-based partnerships; please let us know how we can support this component. We are happy to help set up the infrastructure if you are still working on it, as well as provide recommendations, if this would be helpful
  *   Outreach for meetings: How are the meetings being publicized to the community?
  *   Social media: Our scope includes a calendar and content for social media postings; will this also be deferred until the next series of meetings, or should we prepare for this for the January 2023 meetings? How does this fit into your vision for this first series of meetings given the accelerated timeline?
  *   Sign-in sheets, comment cards, mic: We will bring sign-in sheets for the registration, should we also bring comment cards for folks who prefer not to get up and speak/ask questions? FYI we recommend a standing mic for people to line up at for the Q & A sections but can discuss this further and see what your preference is

While many of these questions may be addressed in our kick-off meeting, whatever information we can get sooner would be helpful for our preparation. We want to be sure that we can hit the ground running since the meetings are just a couple of weeks away!

Thank you,

--Danielle

Subject: [External] prep for Regional Convenings

Good afternoon,

Hope this email finds you all well and getting ready to celebrate the New Year!

As we prepare for our kick-off meeting and the regional convenings, we have a few questions for you:

  *   Contact information for each location: It would be helpful to have contact info so that we can inquire about tech availability as well as set up/break down, logistics; this will help inform what equipment we need to bring and what the video/A/V people need to be prepared for, and what our team needs to be prepared for when doing set-up/breakdown, unless you or someone on your team can answer these types of questions for us
  *   Satellite sites noted on the list of venues: What exactly does this mean?  Is this a location where folks can watch the livestream and participate in Q & A from, will our team need to include the satellite location in our staffing? Please provide additional information.
  *   A/V, video, livestream, interpretation: Confirmation that our team will be providing the A/V support, videographer, livestreaming, and interpretation for each meeting
  *   Copy of slide presentation deck, even if it is still being developed: - Can we get this at your earliest convenience so that we can begin familiarizing ourselves with it?
  *   Copy of LUEG presentation: Can we get this at your earliest convenience so that we can begin familiarizing ourselves with it?
  *   Team members and VIPS: List of team members to be introduced at the meeting, as well as any VIPS who may attend who should be acknowledged (in addition to each supervisor), so that we can be prepared for introductions and acknowledgements when we open each meeting
  *   Health/science experts speaking at the events: The tentative program you provided lists Dr. Eyal Oren D2/D5; Dr. Tarik Benmarhnia D4 - what about D1, D3?
  *   Collateral materials, translation (public notice/invitation/event flyer, handouts, slide deck, signage, poster boards, etc.): Per our call with Murtaza, you will be taking care of these items for this first series of meetings, please confirm; please let us know how we can be helpful in producing these pieces, what support we can offer. Please advise if we will be providing the written translation for them and if so please provide us with copies of each as soon as possible so that we can get them translated as well as for our own review and reference, as well as a deadline for turning them around
  *   Fact sheet: as with the above noted, in our call with Murtaza he said you would be taking care of the initial one - how can we support this effort, and will it need translation?
  *   Refreshments: Please advise if we will be providing refreshments for each meeting (light refreshments i.e. water, coffee/tea, pastries, etc.)
  *   Community-based partnerships: What is the status of the community-based partnerships; please let us know how we can support this component. We are happy to help set up the infrastructure if you are still working on it, as well as provide recommendations, if this would be helpful
  *   Outreach for meetings: How are the meetings being publicized to the community?
  *   Social media: Our scope includes a calendar and content for social media postings; will this also be deferred until the next series of meetings, or should we prepare for this for the January 2023 meetings? How does this fit into your vision for this first series of meetings given the accelerated timeline?
  *   Sign-in sheets, comment cards, mic: We will bring sign-in sheets for the registration, should we also bring comment cards for folks who prefer not to get up and speak/ask questions? FYI we recommend a standing mic for people to line up at for the Q & A sections but can discuss this further and see what your preference is

While many of these questions may be addressed in our kick-off meeting, whatever information we can get sooner would be helpful for our preparation. We want to be sure that we can hit the ground running since the meetings are just a couple of weeks away!

Thank you,

--Danielle

From: Ali Mariko Dressel <ali@climateactioncampaign.org <mailto:ali@climateactioncampaign.org> >
Sent: Friday, July 28, 2023 12:37 PM
To: Viskanta, Rimga <Rimga.Viskanta@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Rimga.Viskanta@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
Subject: [External] RDF Clarity and New Direction

Hi Rimga!

Thanks again for being the moderator for Nexus! It's going to be great to have you there!

Regarding the RDF, after our last meeting, we've done some internal discussions and clarified our scope a bit. With the new direction around focusing on identifying specific climate action projects, I wanted to quickly confirm that we are on the right track.

*	Instead of focusing on engaging as many individuals as possible from Communities of Concerns, we will focus now on reaching organizations who are actively working on climate action projects that would benefit from the County's support or would help inform the Regional CAP and other future climate policies. These organizations will continue to be within and uplift Communities of Concern.
*	We will also highlight and focus on reaching local council offices and policy makers who are actively working on or identifying capital improvement projects that may benefit from the RDF as a reference or that may become part of future CAPs.
*	We are communicating that the RDF is a guide for implementing climate action throughout the region and can be used to inform climate policies on local and regional levels. While the County cannot lead the projects themselves, the County may be able to help provide resources in the form of grants, the RDF guidebook, etc.
*	After speaking with the Water Equity Team, we are incorporating water questions into our community gatherings and surveys.

Going forward, we do have a few followup questions as well!

*	When will the Convenings be? After speaking with the Water Equity team, it sounds like they will be in November afterall. Can we schedule a meeting ASAP to discuss programming, roles, and next steps? We are running out of time to book places and we should start promoting those soon for effective turnout.
*	If we are to focus on gathering feedback from organizations about specific projects, do you still need demographic data? If so, do you want that data coupled in a full survey like it currently is, or should we create a smaller demographic data only survey that accompanies the feedback that we receive in other ways (discussion, posters, notes, testimonies, etc.)
*	What do your project portfolios look like? How can we best compile project information to match and add to your existing portfolios?

Thank you!! I super appreciate your time and collaboration on this!

In Gratitude,

ali

Subject: FW: RDF Supplemental Research - Sustainable Ag Guide

FYI - An example of how to send out an email for reviewers ??

From: Appel, Rebeca
Sent: Wednesday, November 9, 2022 8:31 AM
To: Cooper, Garrett <Garrett.Cooper@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Garrett.Cooper@sdcounty.ca.gov> >; Farmer, Tyler <Tyler.Farmer@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Tyler.Farmer@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
Cc: Baxamusa, Murtaza <Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov> >; Hanson, Elise A <EliseA.Hanson@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:EliseA.Hanson@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
Subject: RDF Supplemental Research - Sustainable Ag Guide

Good morning Garrett and Tyler,

Thanks for joining our RDF workshop on Monday! I hope you found it productive and useful.

As I have shared with both of you in past meetings and discussions, we are working with UCSD Urban Studies and Planning (specifically Dr. Amy Lerner who was one of the facilitators on Monday) on looking at how to elevate sustainable agriculture and food systems in the RDF. Part of this work was Board directed back in February of this year.

We are finalizing a draft that will go to Sarah to review mid-December/early January, and then be posted for public comment before we anticipate taking it to the Board in Spring 2023 when we’re planning for the Board to consider adoption of the RDF. I wanted to send a note to both of you as we would really appreciate a review by AWM and PDS (highlighted timeframe). I’ve added a high-level timeline below.

November 28 – December 6: County to provide comments on draft

December 12: Revised draft to DCAO for review

January 16: Public posted draft

End of January: Ag specific workshop to discuss draft and facilitate feedback

Early February: Public comment ends

Mid-February: Final version & final review by County before docketing

I’ve attached the one-page concept paper that is guiding the work as an FYI. Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to set up a time to talk through this more. We really appreciate you’re review of this, as we know there are many parallel and aligning efforts already occurring in our region. Thank you!

Rebeca Appel

She/her/hers <https://www.mypronouns.org/>

Group Program Manager

Land Use and Environment Group | County of San Diego

San Diego, CA 92101

As a reminder, the roles are to be a Mural operator/note taker to type responses into the digital sticky notes, or a co-moderator to ask questions, lead the conversation, manage the chat, and feed audible/written responses to the note taker. Each room will assign 2 OSEJ team members to carry out this task. *Please note - staff will need to create a Mural account, and we will follow up with the team with guidance on that.

Please respond directly to this email to let me know if you have a preference in roles, otherwise you will be assigned to a role for each event. Additionally, please also include a confirmation of which dates you are available for each event.

*       Your preferred role

o   Mural operator/notetaker,

o   co-moderator, or

o   both/rotate roles

*       Dates you are available for each event in the series

As always, please feel free to reach out if you have any questions before the first workshop on June 28 at 12pm. I will follow up with an email before this event with an agenda, assigned roles, and preparation details.

Have an excellent weekend!

Elise

body:
Hello,

I am so sorry, I thought I had already responded. This is outside of our realm. We only know about sustainable agriculture practices and strategies ancillary to our regulatory work as a means to help direct our farmers. I think the following speakers from the recent Climate Smart Agriculture Event hosted by UCCE would be a perfect suite for your needs.

*	Tapan Pathak, PhD, UC ANR Specialist - Climate Adaptation in Agriculture, UC Merced and UC Division of Agriculture and Natural Resources, tpathak@ucmerced.edu <mailto:tpathak@ucmerced.edu> . Tapan's presentation included discussion of climate change impacts to agriculture. He included focus on how temperature and water stress will/are impacting crop growing seasons and vulnerability to diseases, pests, and other issues. He included discussion on various pathways to incorporate specific ("climate smart") agricultural practices to improve agricultural outcomes in spite of climate change as well as avenues for agriculture to participate in carbon sequestration as a means to mitigate future climate change. There was discussion on the valuation of agriculture related to regional accounting for GHGs, and discussion on how soil and plant health relates to increased carbon sequestration, etc. There is also reference to a new book that will be released soon, namely the "Agriculture Resource Book."

*	Tom Corringham, PhD, Staff Research Economist, Scripps Institute of Oceanography, UC San Diego, tcorringham@ucsd.edu <mailto:tcorringham@ucsd.edu> . Tom's presentation included discussion of water and changing climate within California as compared to other regions, as well as how water is used competitively amongst different sectors (namely the ag-urban-environmental sectors). He included review of temperature trends and future outlooks/impacts.

*	Elias Marvinney, PhD, Assistant Project Scientist, Plants Sciences, UC Davis, (858)246-1000, emarvinney@ucdavis.edu <mailto:emarvinney@ucdavis.edu> . Elias' presentation included discussion of the linear versus circular agriculture production processes, and how to incorporate climate smart steps into the system to reduce energy use, reduce generation of GHGs, and increase carbon sequestration throughout the agriculture process. There was specific discussion on ways farmers can increase carbon in soil and vegetation through stewardship, treating plant diseases, and managing green waste onsite (e.g., incorporating back into the soil).

The presentations from these speakers should be posted to the following website and may be worth checking out. CAAS 2023 Documents - Climate and Agriculture in San Diego County (ucanr.edu) <https://ucanr.edu/sites/Climate_Resilient_Agriculture/Symposium/CAAS_2023_Documents/>

Another idea is for someone from the DPW water rebate programs to provide some information on ways the County is incentivizing water conservation and supporting water efficiencies - Scott Norris (Scott.Norris@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Scott.Norris@sdcounty.ca.gov> ) is the primary contact for the water rebate programs . And/or Joel Kramer (joel.kramer@rcdsandiego.orgfrom <mailto:joel.kramer@rcdsandiego.orgfrom> ) the Greater San Diego Resource Conservation District could speak on their programs that support carbon sequestration, underrepresented farmers with drought financial support, and other resources.

I hope this helps and again, I am sorry for the delay. If I  don't get back to you within a few days, please feel free to remind me moving forward.

Thank you,

Jordan Key

Deputy Agricultural Commissioner & Sealer

County of San Diego, Department of Agriculture/Weights & Measures

Rosa/David,

From: Baxamusa, Murtaza
Sent: Friday, January 6, 2023 2:41 PM
To: Flores, David <David.Flores@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:David.Flores@sdcounty.ca.gov>>; Olascoaga, Rosa <Rosa.Olascoaga@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Rosa.Olascoaga@sdcounty.ca.gov>>
Cc: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>>
Subject: RE: Regional Water Equity project - update and request

Thanks for taking my call, Rosa. As we are meeting with Geosyntec today, your guidance was very helpful.

To summarize, here are some key points in our call:

  *   The Regional Water Equity report should include innovative strategies to increase community awareness, particularly in the binational region, such as promotoras. New strategies should include education/outreach and follow-up, so that the recommendations that come out benefits communities to meet the goals. Identify where can the County step in? (e.g. in recent flooding)
  *   The Affordable Housing study should include water reuse, graywater, stormwater and address how we attract federal, state and regional funds to build more affordable housing. Look at LIHTC, REAP 2.0, SANDAG, HCD, state housing bonds at different levels of AMI. How do we include low-income renters in this conversation?
  *   The insurance issues can be included in the main report that focuses on outreach to low-income owners/renters. We may not need a quantitative assessment of flood insurance (like fire) for the region for this purpose.

Elise (copied) is going to be coordinating the research and outreach on this project. I will request approval for the solicitation of experts for a specialized affordable housing study.

Murtaza

Hi David and Rosa,
Thank you for your direction on the scope on the contract and input on our outreach plan. Geosyntec has been given the notice to proceed on the work and they will begin the research on a regional water assessment right away.

We wanted to briefly connect with you about a couple of clarifications regarding affordable housing and insurance risk. This should take about 15 minutes, knowing your busy schedules. We would appreciate if you can meet soon before we proceed on these items. Please let us know your availability.
Thanks,
Murtaza

Cc: Anaya, Marisol <anaya.marisol@epa.gov>; Helgesen, Jessica <helgesen.jessica@epa.gov>; Espinoza, Alicia <Alicia.Espinoza@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: [External] FW: Register Now! Tribal Listening Session for the Inflation Reduction Act’s Funding to Address Air Pollution at Schools

FYI…

Hello Roberta, I hope all is well!  I wanted to share this announcement with you. We are sharing with our Tribal contacts, but if can help us spread the word and encourage folks to attend and submit their input, that would be greatly appreciated!  This would be the time for Tribes and those who work with Tribes to give input on what this funding should cover--for example, should it cover facilities that accommodate after school programs, pre-schools, childcare centers (which many times also serve as preschools), head start programs, etc. Many of our local tribes have these types of facilities and not necessarily official schools and it would be great if they could also use these funds to improve those indoor environments. Rehabbing those buildings would be key in improving environmental health and eliminating some of the sources of indoor air pollution <https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2022-05/IAQ-One-Page-Flyer-Final-508c.pdf>  that lead to health disparities in tribal communities.

E-introducing all of you in case you haven’t met (and looping you all in as FYI):

Subject: [External] FW: Register Now! Tribal Listening Session for the Inflation Reduction Act’s Funding to Address Air Pollution at Schools

FYI…

Hello Roberta, I hope all is well!  I wanted to share this announcement with you. We are sharing with our Tribal contacts, but if can help us spread the word and encourage folks to attend and submit their input, that would be greatly appreciated!  This would be the time for Tribes and those who work with Tribes to give input on what this funding should cover--for example, should it cover facilities that accommodate after school programs, pre-schools, childcare centers (which many times also serve as preschools), head start programs, etc. Many of our local tribes have these types of facilities and not necessarily official schools and it would be great if they could also use these funds to improve those indoor environments. Rehabbing those buildings would be key in improving environmental health and eliminating some of the sources of indoor air pollution <https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2022-05/IAQ-One-Page-Flyer-Final-508c.pdf>  that lead to health disparities in tribal communities.

cc: "Ruiz; Elise" <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Megan Otto	<MMOtto@Geosyntec.com>; "Boerboom; Jacob" <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov>;	Lauren Case-McFate <Lauren.Case@Geosyntec.com>
body:
Hi Stephanie,

Thank you again for the meeting today.

Really fast, I wanted to answer the number of tribes question. Pechanga is listed (and should remain listed-thank you) because they purchased land in SD region and are considered stakeholders, but their government is in Riverside County. Capitan Band does not have a government or enrolled members but is historic land held in common by Barona and Viejas.

This brings us to 18 federally recognized sovereign tribal governments in the San Diego region, 1 non-federally recognized tribal government in the region.
Federal recognition provides sovereignty (emphasizing difference between the two just in case).

The imperial county tribes looks correct to me.

I’ll work with Elise on the other pieces.

Thank you and enjoy the weekend,

Roberta Leash

title: RE_ RWER - Farm Bureau Interview & Water Committee.msg
subject: RE: RWER - Farm Bureau Interview & Water Committee
body:
Hi Elise,

Thanks for letting us know! To clarify, would you like us to attend? I am available and glad to attend as support. I think it is always best to have a team whenever we go and present somewhere, but its up to you and Eden (and how it has been discussed). I also highly recommend this be brought up for awareness on Tuesday with EO.

I anticipate many questions from attendees being asked about the report itself which we wont be able to answer as it is not finished and we should not speak to what is only in internal draft form. But we can take all their ideas, perspectives, and input for consideration. Do you have potential Q/A prepped?

I also think its best to keep to OSEJ. Departments have specific protocols and avenues in connecting with the farm bureau and as its only a few working days away, it doesn’t allow for a lot of time for coordination.

From: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Sent: Friday, June 30, 2023 1:05 PM
To: Appel, Rebeca <Rebeca.Appel@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Boerboom, Jacob <Jacob.Boerboom@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: RWER - Farm Bureau Interview & Water Committee

Hi both,

I met with Katie Byrne from Farm Bureau yesterday, she and I discussed the stakeholder interview questions that Farm Bureau members have given feedback on and wanted more clarity before providing responses. I am working with Geosyntec/Re:focus to address some of their comments, however, I wanted to let you both know that Katie asked that I join the Farm Bureau Water Committee meeting in person on July 11th at 3pm at the Escondido headquarters to present the Water Equity project and address these questions further. I am in the process of confirming what the goal and structure of this meeting will look like, but it sounds like we will have an opportunity to have Q&A and potentially do on the spot interviews. Please check out the meeting details on the Farm Bureau website<https://www.sdfarmbureau.org/calendar/monthly-water-committee-meeting-3/>.

As you know, our contractors are now processing data from all scoped stakeholder interviews, and there are a few high-priority groups that I’ve been trying to track down to include outside of our contractor’s scope (farmers, binational partners, & tribal organizations). This may be a great opportunity to engage with the farming community in a group setting for our outreach efforts.

I wanted to get this on your radar to not only share for your interest/participation, but also to provide a pathway for any other departments who may be interested in joining for agricultural collaboration and address water concerns on a larger level. Please let me know your thoughts and if you would be interested in joining. They do offer a virtual option, but Katie highly recommended this be in person.

For your reference – here are the questions I’ve sent for clarity to Geosyntec/Re:focus and cc’d you both:

·               Question D states “Where and how would more sustainable agriculture be a value add?” Are we talking about for the farmer or the consumer? Can you clarify what you mean by “portfolio of work” and “growth and scale”?
§  I spoke with farm Bureau and provided context that the County is interested primarily in value add for the farmer.

·               Question E states “What do you see as the biggest gaps and hurdles to scaling sustainable agriculture?” What do you mean by scaling sustainable agriculture?

·               Question G states “what kinds of regional projects have been gaining momentum locally?” What kind of projects are we talking about?

Thanks!

subject: RE: RWER Task 2 - Review Strategy
body:
Hi Elise,

I reviewed the executive summary and the last chunk of pages. I left a few comments and made a few suggested edits. Overall, it was insightful and well written. Here are some of my notes:

*	Glossary of terms up front was so helpful
*	Suggest removing all reference to Regional Water Equity Project, and just use "effort" (lowercase) and Regional Water Equity Report - because that is ultimately what the result of the effort will be
*	Changed some references when it comes to the Board direction in exec summary and on page 1 (as a reminder, Board cannot direct staff - they can only direct CAO, but if we add that it then its unnecessary info so refined to say directed the effort)
*	Page 36 image is so impactful (didn't read the whole section but was just scrolling through) and that image tells a huge story about a coordinated strategy for cross border water supply. It is not just a San Diego -Tijuana thing but the whole southern border

	*	If it isn't already - should be emphasized in the final takeaways

*	What is on page 44 to describe the considerations and constraints for the solutions/strategies would be just what is needed for the Ag memo - it helps set the reader up for how the solutions are considered
*	Conclusions table - the last one says work with academic community to look at 7 solutions and emerging technology - why 7? Thinking this is a great conclusions table that could stand on its on, and begs the question why 7 and what the reasoning is

title: RE_ RWER Task 2 Review Update.msg
subject: RE: RWER Task 2 Review Update
attachments: RWER Draft Task 2 Memo_OSEJ & DPW Comments.docx
body:
Hi Megan and Stephanie,

Thanks for all the hard work and effort that has gone into this deliverable! Our team was very impressed and we all agreed that it sets a great tone for the overall report. The glossary upfront was very helpful, and the data indicators in the tables made the information easy to follow.

After our review, we agreed to not cut/trim down any of the tables at this time of the review process, but may have different feedback once we incorporate further departmental/executive review. As you go through comments, here are a few key takeaway points:

  *   We recommend changing “Regional Water Equity Project” to “Regional Water Equity” effort, as this will most likely be the approved project name moving forward. We could use Regional Water Equity Report (RWER) to indicate the comprehensive report itself
  *   Spelling/Term Recommendations: Please use “graywater” and “stormwater collection”
  *   The points focusing on the strategy and connectivity of water supply throughout the southern boarder (Section 3.1.1/Table 6) is very insightful and that table/concept is a tool we’d like to use for high level presentations/outreach, and want to make sure that is expressed in key takeaways. Let’s talk more on this.

Thanks and we look forward to discussing this more with you!

Elise

Hi Elise,

Just checking in on our inquiry below regarding Northern Baja regions to focus on?

Also, please see attached for a revised Stakeholder Interview List that has three phases described below.  I’d like to provide a short summary of our thinking behind this.  The graywater focus interviews are more technical in nature, so we feel like we can get those going sooner than later.  For the Task 2A longer list of stakeholders (15 to be interviewed), we didn’t want to start with too many as there are some decisions that still need to be made regarding the 15 to be interviewed.  Therefore, we only proposed 4 stakeholders on this list where we feel they would provide good input and would take less strategy to establish the interviews.  Most agricultural stakeholders are split between Phase 2 and Phase 3, we think the Phase 2 list could likely be reviewed by your team fairly quickly and would take less messaging strategy (e.g. for the national agriculture stakeholders that were proposed by re-focus).  We anticipate that the local agricultural stakeholders will take more strategy and are therefore listed under Phase 3.

  1.  Phase 1 – these stakeholders would require less strategy on messaging during the interview where Geosyntec/subs could be ready for interview scheduling now.
  2.  Phase 2 – these stakeholders require some strategy, and a meeting between Geosyntec/County is necessary to finalize messaging.
  3.  Phase 3 – these stakeholders require a lot of coordination between Geosyntec/County and require strategic messaging during the interviews.

Let’s plan to discuss this at our standing meeting on Wednesday and any questions you may have.  If possible, I think a good goal would be to get some of these Phase 1 stakeholder interviews going in a week from now to stay on schedule.  I’ll also plan to update the Sharepoint site with this revised matrix.

Thank you,

Stephanie

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for getting these questions to our team so quickly. Below is some feedback on the agriculture piece:

3. Task 5 – Agriculture Focus
C. What are your top priorities when it comes to sustainable agriculture in San Diego County?

  *   I think this should be re-worded. Many farmers are interested in sustainable agriculture - however, there are decision points to make between carbon benefits, water costs, and production… so suggest instead, "What are your top priorities when it comes to agriculture in San Diego county? And how would you/do you rank between carbon benefits (sequestration) and water?" (or something along those lines)

I’ll follow up if there are any other recommendations from staff.

Thank you,
Elise

Hi Elise,

Just checking in on our inquiry below regarding Northern Baja regions to focus on?

Also, please see attached for a revised Stakeholder Interview List that has three phases described below.  I’d like to provide a short summary of our thinking behind this.  The graywater focus interviews are more technical in nature, so we feel like we can get those going sooner than later.  For the Task 2A longer list of stakeholders (15 to be interviewed), we didn’t want to start with too many as there are some decisions that still need to be made regarding the 15 to be interviewed.  Therefore, we only proposed 4 stakeholders on this list where we feel they would provide good input and would take less strategy to establish the interviews.  Most agricultural stakeholders are split between Phase 2 and Phase 3, we think the Phase 2 list could likely be reviewed by your team fairly quickly and would take less messaging strategy (e.g. for the national agriculture stakeholders that were proposed by re-focus).  We anticipate that the local agricultural stakeholders will take more strategy and are therefore listed under Phase 3.

  1.  Phase 1 – these stakeholders would require less strategy on messaging during the interview where Geosyntec/subs could be ready for interview scheduling now.
  2.  Phase 2 – these stakeholders require some strategy, and a meeting between Geosyntec/County is necessary to finalize messaging.
  3.  Phase 3 – these stakeholders require a lot of coordination between Geosyntec/County and require strategic messaging during the interviews.

Let’s plan to discuss this at our standing meeting on Wednesday and any questions you may have.  If possible, I think a good goal would be to get some of these Phase 1 stakeholder interviews going in a week from now to stay on schedule.  I’ll also plan to update the Sharepoint site with this revised matrix.

Thank you,

Stephanie

Hi Stephanie,

Great interview with DEHQ today!

This method you’ve created for the stakeholder interviews list is great, and I appreciate the breakdown. I’ll work internally to plan for Phase 1 next steps, and I’ll also have some updates for you regarding the outreach timeline by the time we meet for our check-in on Wednesday.

Regarding the northern territories of Baja: Tijuana, Tecate, and Mexicali are confirmed to be included, however, I am in the process of confirming if Playas de Rosarito should also be included in this research. Due to the service area that Tijuana’s State Commission for Public Services, CESPT manages, Rosario may also be a part of those water systems. I’ll follow up with more.

Elise

From: Stephanie Zinn <Stephanie.Zinn@Geosyntec.com>
Sent: Monday, February 6, 2023 1:13 PM
To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Cc: Megan Otto <MMOtto@Geosyntec.com>
Subject: [External] RE: Standing Meeting Acton Items

Hi Elise,

Just checking in on our inquiry below regarding Northern Baja regions to focus on?

Also, please see attached for a revised Stakeholder Interview List that has three phases described below.  I’d like to provide a short summary of our thinking behind this.  The graywater focus interviews are more technical in nature, so we feel like we can get those going sooner than later.  For the Task 2A longer list of stakeholders (15 to be interviewed), we didn’t want to start with too many as there are some decisions that still need to be made regarding the 15 to be interviewed.  Therefore, we only proposed 4 stakeholders on this list where we feel they would provide good input and would take less strategy to establish the interviews.  Most agricultural stakeholders are split between Phase 2 and Phase 3, we think the Phase 2 list could likely be reviewed by your team fairly quickly and would take less messaging strategy (e.g. for the national agriculture stakeholders that were proposed by re-focus).  We anticipate that the local agricultural stakeholders will take more strategy and are therefore listed under Phase 3.

  1.  Phase 1 – these stakeholders would require less strategy on messaging during the interview where Geosyntec/subs could be ready for interview scheduling now.
  2.  Phase 2 – these stakeholders require some strategy, and a meeting between Geosyntec/County is necessary to finalize messaging.
  3.  Phase 3 – these stakeholders require a lot of coordination between Geosyntec/County and require strategic messaging during the interviews.

Let’s plan to discuss this at our standing meeting on Wednesday and any questions you may have.  If possible, I think a good goal would be to get some of these Phase 1 stakeholder interviews going in a week from now to stay on schedule.  I’ll also plan to update the Sharepoint site with this revised matrix.

Thank you,
Stephanie

  3.  Phase 3 – these stakeholders require a lot of coordination between Geosyntec/County and require strategic messaging during the interviews.

body:
Hi Megan and Stephanie,

Thanks for the great updates today!

I wanted to give you an update that I checked with our outreach/communications staff regarding onboarding for Moses Mortada as a binational support for this project and there are no concerns or processes needed from the County’s side of things. This would only change if there is direct contact with elected officials/staff, but since outreach will be led with our communication protocol we won’t run into that situation. I think this sub will be a great addition!

Thank you,
Elise

From: Stephanie Zinn <Stephanie.Zinn@Geosyntec.com>
Sent: Monday, February 6, 2023 1:13 PM
To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Cc: Megan Otto <MMOtto@Geosyntec.com>
Subject: [External] RE: Standing Meeting Acton Items

Hi Elise,

Just checking in on our inquiry below regarding Northern Baja regions to focus on?

Also, please see attached for a revised Stakeholder Interview List that has three phases described below.  I’d like to provide a short summary of our thinking behind this.  The graywater focus interviews are more technical in nature, so we feel like we can get those going sooner than later.  For the Task 2A longer list of stakeholders (15 to be interviewed), we didn’t want to start with too many as there are some decisions that still need to be made regarding the 15 to be interviewed.  Therefore, we only proposed 4 stakeholders on this list where we feel they would provide good input and would take less strategy to establish the interviews.  Most agricultural stakeholders are split between Phase 2 and Phase 3, we think the Phase 2 list could likely be reviewed by your team fairly quickly and would take less messaging strategy (e.g. for the national agriculture stakeholders that were proposed by re-focus).  We anticipate that the local agricultural stakeholders will take more strategy and are therefore listed under Phase 3.

  1.  Phase 1 – these stakeholders would require less strategy on messaging during the interview where Geosyntec/subs could be ready for interview scheduling now.
  2.  Phase 2 – these stakeholders require some strategy, and a meeting between Geosyntec/County is necessary to finalize messaging.
  3.  Phase 3 – these stakeholders require a lot of coordination between Geosyntec/County and require strategic messaging during the interviews.

Let’s plan to discuss this at our standing meeting on Wednesday and any questions you may have.  If possible, I think a good goal would be to get some of these Phase 1 stakeholder interviews going in a week from now to stay on schedule.  I’ll also plan to update the Sharepoint site with this revised matrix.

Thank you,
Stephanie

Stephanie Castle Zinn

Hi Elise & Murtaza,

As I mentioned to you both last week, I have been on standby for jury duty and I have now been called in for Monday. So, I wont be able to make our morning meetings. It would be great if you could still discuss the Mgmt Fellow candidates and let me know if there are any stand outs for you. I would be happy to discuss Tuesday AM my impressions of them as well.

Elise – I won’t be able to make our quarterly chat, but maybe we can connect on Tuesday about it. I have added some items to the water slide, but please feel free to add/edit. We typically include fiscal, outreach/engagement, and key project items/timeline. We also need to add speaking notes, as this will most likely be Jennifer presenting to the CAO.

Murtaza - I also added something to the agenda that I was hoping to discuss. We should reach out this week to each Board office (separately) and offer an RDF briefing of what is to come in March so we can schedule them for the week of 2/20. Thinking we can brief them similarly to how you’ve briefed Sarah in past RDF meetings – walking through each recommendation (I’ll put a few slides together). Before we do this though, please check with Sarah/make her aware.  Once we have her okay, if you want to email Board offices (cc me) and then I can work on scheduling.

FYI-I also set up time for us to do a full rehearsal in the chambers.

Thanks!
Rebeca

Subject: FYI: UCCE Contract Renewal and Negotiations

Hi team -

FYI, our Agriculture, Weights, and Measures department has a 5-year contract with the University of California Cooperative Extension to support education and outreach. Below, they have indicated that a number of new technical advisors have either come on board or are coming on board. In the next couple of months AWM will be developing new objectives for this contract which could be aligned with County efforts - such as what we are doing in OSEJ.

I am sending this as an FYI so you can take a look at the current contract objectives. Once the next contract's objectives are developed, I will share with each of you for you input and perspectives before they are finalized.

(Side note for Elise/Jacob - for our meeting tomorrow with AWM on RWER, we could ask to be connected with the Fire Advisor for additional technical information on the financial risks component).

Please reach out if you have any questions. Thank you!

Rebeca

Subject: UCCE Contract Renewal and Negotiations

Good afternoon,

AWM and LUEG will be entering to negotiations with UCCE to renew and establish a new 5-year contract. We will be working to establish new objectives that align with the goals of the County and then also align with some of the new advisors that they will bringing on. I have attached a copy of the current scope of work for reference and then the new advisors they will bringing on and expected start time are:

Fire Advisor: new position that has already started

Organic Waste Management Advisor: new position that has already started

4-H Advisor: Starts on August 1st

Plant Pathology Advisor: Within next three months

Urban Agriculture Advisor: Early 2024

Food Systems and Environmental Issues Advisor: Early 2024

Indigenous Farming Advisor: Early 2024

I wanted to reach out to each of you because I will be reaching out soon to the departments to determine if there are any objectives or projects that you would like considered for this 5-year contract. UCCE's work is typically concerned with providing education and outreach and their focus is on the agricultural community and providing nutrition education.  County priorities that I see UCCE having an affect on are CAP, stormwater and water quality in the region, organic recycling, food and nutrition insecurity, decarbonization efforts.

I wanted to check in and see if when I reach out if you would be the correct individuals to reach out to or if you had more specific SMEs that you would like me to work with.

Let me know and then I can begin to reach out to those individuals.

Thank you,

Garrett Cooper (He, Him, His)

Deputy Director
