Cc: Aghassi, Sarah <Sarah.Aghassi@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Demorest, Erin <Erin.Demorest@sdcounty.ca.gov>; De La Rosa, Michael <Michael.DeLaRosa@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Durckel, Donna <Donna.Durckel@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Appel, Rebeca <Rebeca.Appel@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Hanson, Elise A <EliseA.Hanson@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: Updates on Regional Decarbonization Framework (RDF)

Dear Board Staff,

Since the Board update on August 31, our RDF team has completed 10 workshops that cover all 5 topics in Special Topics Working Groups. These working groups are intended to provide community and stakeholder input into the drafting of the Implementation Playbook that will be presented to the Board in Spring 2023. The working groups used an innovative Engage platform<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/> that allows users to directly comment on documents and see or respond to others’ comments. We also tried out a new format with curated stakeholder presentations on specific decarbonization topics that we intend to provide as an “Ideas Bank”. The video recordings of these workshops and presentations are now available on the RDF website: Regional Decarbonization Framework (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/sustainability/regional-decarbonization.html>

In addition, our team wanted to highlight the following activities:

  *   There are two virtual public meetings scheduled for December evenings, that we would appreciate if you can help us get the word out:
     *   December 6<https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZwrdO-vqzksHNDuW7GN9aiIXGa4L9WTeTmB> (Spanish-language community meeting)
     *   December 13<https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZAkc-6gqT8tHNAOUAiw5iW8C3675rYRCQxM> (Public workshop on Draft Implementation Playbook)

We will be sending out notices in the coming weeks.

  *   RDF is being presented as an information item at SANDAG’s Sustainable Communities Working Group next Thursday, November 17 (Item 5). Location, agenda and Zoom information here: SWCG | 11.17.22 (sandag.org)<https://www.sandag.org/uploads/meetingid/meetingid_6175_33093.pdf>
  *   Some notable past events from our RDF team since our last update to the Board:
     *   Moderated a panel on Natural Climate Solutions at the Lesly K. McAllister Symposium on Climate and Energy Law<https://www.sandiego.edu/epic/symposium/> at the University of San Diego School of Law on November 4.
     *   Presented at the Global Conference on Sustainability in Higher Education<https://www.aashe.org/conference/> on November 3.
     *   Participated in the Marquee Panel at NEXUS Climate Conference<https://www.climateactioncampaign.org/post/nexus-recap> on October 21.
     *   Organized panel at the California Climate and Energy Forum<https://eecoordinator.info/forum-program-2/> on September 21.
     *   City Council informational presentations at National City<https://www.nationalcityca.gov/Home/Components/Calendar/Event/13184/786?curm=9&cury=2022> (Item 6.1 September 20), Carlsbad<https://www.carlsbadca.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/11504/638006528101870000> (Item #12, October 11)
  *   For your awareness, the Air Pollution Control District released a “Draft 2022 Regional Air Quality Strategy<https://www.sdapcd.org/content/dam/sdapcd/documents/grants/planning/2022RAQS_Final_10242022.pdf>” (RAQS). The draft RAQS discusses collaboration with the County RDF on programs, policies and strategies to reduce emissions, and APCD highlighted the alignment on the RAQS with RDF in their public workshop yesterday.
  *   As we had informed you in summer, the County’s Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice, in partnership with the San Diego Foundation, was selected for the Partners for Places grant award<https://www.fundersnetwork.org/partners-for-places-eight-u-s-communities-receive-nearly-1-3-million-in-grants-for-community-led-sustainability-projects/> from The Funders Network. This award is for outreach to refugees, asylees and immigrant communities as part of our community engagement efforts on decarbonization. With the assistance of The Global Action Research Center, the San Diego Foundation and us have selected Youth Will, Majdal Community Center and Partnership for Advancement of New Americans as our community partners for the Partners for Places grant award.

And finally, we are working on RDF Regional Convenings for each Supervisorial District in the latter half of January. We appreciate each of you for confirming the dates on the Supervisors’ calendars for each District! We are now working on finalizing the facilities, program, community/CBO partners and facilitation/marketing contracts to support these events. We are also excited to partner with the Public Health Services for our speakers. We will keep you posted and looking forward to coordinating with your respective offices for these convenings.

Thank you!

Murtaza

________________________________________

Murtaza H. Baxamusa, PhD, AICP

Program Manager for Regional Sustainability

Land Use and Environment Group

Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice

County of San Diego

Hi team,

In my first round of data mining from the CAC monthly reports (UCP did not have as many reports available) highlighting the RDF convenings and community chats, I was able to gather some insight which I think will be helpful for our conversation with UCP tomorrow. Although these responses did not come directly from UCP surveys/D4, I think the interest from these surveys is very aligned with RWE.

What topics would you like to see more of at our next event?
Unique Responses:

*	Water pollution and shortage
*	Water problem; Colorado River is drying and where will water come from in the future?
*	Distribution of climate appropriate landscaping, fruit trees, vegetables to reduce water demand but enhance decarbonization via plants and local agricultural supply; shade to offset heat islands

Nonunique Responses

*	Nature-Based Solutions, Such as Protecting Wetlands, Clean Air and Clean Water

	*	Estimated 65% of total responses included water as a future topic of interest

I have more digging to do, but wanted to share preliminary findings ahead of tomorrow’s meeting.

Have a great evening!

Elise

Hi friends,

I am excited to work on this project with you and to meet with UCP on Thursday!

I sent the agenda and supplemental materials, excluding the milestones doc since it differs from the timeline we need to get input by, to Carmina so she has them to digest before we gather. I did alter the meeting agenda slightly for flow and clarity, including an opportunity for Jacob to speak about the Deep Dives. I will try to facilitate us through it all on time. Would somebody be willing to take notes and review the next steps captured (with completion of task dates) at the end of the meeting? I can plan to send them out to them in a follow up invite for an in-person meeting. I can take notes, and let’s plan to store them here if that sounds like a good approach:  CBO Meeting Agendas <https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/LUEG-OSEJ/EmnI-cbzkbBArnSMTubHH7QBpG0klVJw4_QKXXreRCfu-Q?e=mIHCcq>

Yes, please send them my way – We can get an idea of what specific water topics may be of concern before Thursday, but I think we may need until next week to organize and clean up data to get it ready to share with others/EO team (if necessary). This can be a helpful tool to guide water outreach by topic of concern.
*	I am curious if either of you will have time to “data mine” these reports for water related feedback to include with the report? I mentioned that this opportunity was discussed at the CAC meeting to Eden and she was happy that the reports would be utilized in this way. I am able to cover this and have time tomorrow afternoon to provide results to the group by EOD for a brief overview to prep for the UCP meeting on Thursday. Then can continue to finalize through the rest of this week.
*	Can you identify a presenter for the San Diego Green New Deal Alliance meeting on August 28, 5:30-7:30pm? Elise will you be able coordinate the details with Ali before you leave? Yes, I will secure and confirm a speaker for this meeting. Will follow up with the group once that is finalized.
*	Elise, maybe we can get the parameters of the CAC enewsletter submission from Ali on Monday and then would you or Jacob be able to put this together by next week? This sounds like a good approach – We have plenty of existing material that we could use for this newsletter that we could pull from starting this week. I suggest we pull from the General Dot Point Sheet:  OSEJ_RWER_General Dot Points_05.16.23.docx <https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/LUEG-OSEJ/ERVMkBuo2c1IgJ-prRLWC58BTXO3Ik6mbCWEskDvUw9Ypg?e=Yv4KS7>  to get some ideas going. Jacob could you take a look at this if you have time this week and I can help finalize by next week?

Is there anything else that we are missing with the follow-up items from the meeting?

I also wanted to mention that I do not want to overstep. Eden directed me to manage the CBO relationships and outreach efforts, so I am trying my best to coordinate. I am open to your feedback if my approach is not working for you two as the project leads. I am enjoying the opportunity to work more closely together to meet our desired outcome of optimal community outreach for this awesome effort.

Thanks all!

Bethany

title: Water Equity Project.msg
subject: Water Equity Project
body:
Good afternoon, Sam,

I want to introduce you to Elise Ruiz, our Group Program Manager in OSEJ. Elise is working on a big Water Equity Project directed by the Board of Supervisors, and I thought it would be great for the two of you to connect and discuss potential outreach opportunities and collaboration.

The project is focused on an assessment of water equity and sustainability through stormwater capturing in our diverse communities. I am assisting with tribal outreach, but I thought you might have connections with CBOs that could benefit from joining this initiative. To me, racial inequity leads us to conversations about water, housing, infrastructure, health, and environmental injustice. Elise is highly focused on engagement from all communities in the region.

Attached is brief fact sheet about the project but Elise could provide you more information about her goals for outreach and outcomes. Elise, if you would like me to participate in this conversation, please feel free to include me on the invite. ??

Thank you and have a lovely week,

Roberta Leash (She/Her/Hers)

body:
Hi Megan,

Thank you for this update. I will work with our team internally to review these suggestions and confirm which we will use and follow through with the communication protocol.

This is a great list, and we appreciate the thought going into “Plan B” interviewees.

Thanks,

From: Megan Otto <MMOtto@Geosyntec.com>
Sent: Friday, March 17, 2023 2:35 PM
To: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Cc: Stephanie Zinn <Stephanie.Zinn@Geosyntec.com>
Subject: [External] Water Assembly Techncial Speaker Suggestions

Hi Elise,

This morning we connected with JB again on the Water Assembly Planning. For the Technical Presentation component, JB suggested adding at least one technical expert in addition to UCSD’s literature review summary. The lit review could take about 10 minutes, identifying region-specific challenges, leaving 20 minutes for the other speaker(s). JB provided a few suggestions for technical experts, for your consideration:

  1.  Jeffrey Mount<https://www.ppic.org/person/jeffrey-mount/>, Public Policy Institute of California (first choice)

He could speak to the drought in terms of long-term trends, provide context for this year, and discuss what is on the horizon, first from a State perspective, but also identifying challenges specific to the RWER region.

  1.  Dr. F. Martin Ralph<https://mralph.scrippsprofiles.ucsd.edu/>, Director, Center for Western Weather Extremes<https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/>, Scripps Institute of Oceanography
Local technical expert on the physical process related to extremes in precipitation, climate projections, etc.

  1.  Luca Delle Monache<https://ldellemonache.scrippsprofiles.ucsd.edu/>, Deputy Director, Center for Western Weather Extremes, Scripps Institute of Oceanography
  2.  Tom Corringham, Research Economist, Center for Western Weather Extremes<https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/>, Scripps Institute of Oceanography

We are assuming that you would initiate contact if any of the suggested speakers sound good, but let me know if you would prefer another approach or support there.

We were also curious if you could provide more information on the affordable housing analysis, which was part of the original scope of work but was later removed. It would be helpful to know if there is overlap between that effort and UCSD’s charge to assess “implications for housing conditions, availability, and costs as measures are needed to adapt to drought, fire hazards, and shortage.”

Thanks,
Megan

title: Regional Water Equity - April 26th Planning.msg
subject: Regional Water Equity - April 26th Planning
body:
Hi Lara,

I’m sorry I didn’t have a chance to respond to your Teams message on Thursday – It was a packed day and I’ve been trying to manage the water project with a lot of changes lately.

First, thank you for working on the IRWM contact list, I will be presetting to the RAC this Wednesday, and it will be helpful to continue working with that group as things are moving fast.

The project has been a bit overwhelming, and we are working on a tight timeline to make the April 26th Water Assembly kick-off event come together. One thing that I brought up to Crystal and Stephanie is that we will need a speaker during this program to cover a technical piece concerning the drought status (UCSD was originally scoped for this work but has too much to cover with the literature review). I would like to check in with you to see if you may have any contacts who could fill this role and present a 10-15 minute presentation on April 26th? We would need all material/PPTs ready by April 14th, so I know this is a big ask.

Additionally, if you do not have any contacts, UCSD recommended these potential presenters:

  1.  Jeffrey Mount<https://www.ppic.org/person/jeffrey-mount/>, Public Policy Institute of California (first choice)

He could speak to the drought in terms of long-term trends, provide context for this year, and discuss what is on the horizon, first from a State perspective, but also identifying challenges specific to the RWER region.

  1.  Dr. F. Martin Ralph<https://mralph.scrippsprofiles.ucsd.edu/>, Director, Center for Western Weather Extremes<https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/>, Scripps Institute of Oceanography
Local technical expert on the physical process related to extremes in precipitation, climate projections, etc.

  1.  Luca Delle Monache<https://ldellemonache.scrippsprofiles.ucsd.edu/>, Deputy Director, Center for Western Weather Extremes, Scripps Institute of Oceanography
  2.  Tom Corringham, Research Economist, Center for Western Weather Extremes<https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/>, Scripps Institute of Oceanography

If you have time to secure a person either from this list or from your own recommendation, it would be really helpful to have your support with this task. I have mentioned this to Crystal and Stephanie, so if anyone can secure a presenter let’s keep each other posted.

Please feel free to give me a call this week if that’s easier, and thanks for all your effort on this project!

Elise Ruiz
She/her/ella<https://www.mypronouns.org/>
Group Program Manager
Land Use and Environment Group | County of San Diego
1600 Pacific Highway, Room 212, MS: A-6
San Diego, CA 92101
(619) 455-6865

body:
Hi all,

I had a productive meeting with the planning committee for the Water Assembly on April 26th. During today’s meeting, we met with Stephanie Gaines with DPW, Murakawa, Geosyntec, and JB with UCSD. During this time, the team discussed various components that are still in the works, given this tight timeline. One major piece to this equity focused project, is bringing in folks who can represent the wide geographical regions of this project binationally/Imperial County/Tribal communities.

@Baxamusa, Murtaza<mailto:Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov> I am in the process of building and confirming participants for the Equity Panel you recommended (2-3 speakers who will address water equity in regards to their communities/sector based on binational/Imperial County/Tribal communities). These individuals will record a 2-3 minute voice over which will accompany a slide, contributing to a 8-10 minute segment at the beginning of the program.

I am reaching out to all of you for the following requests and guidance:

  *   I am interested in bringing in Roberta Leash as our internal Tribal Liaison to either:
     *   Speak on behalf of her community regarding water equity as an Equity Panelist for the Tribal Communities of Imperial County
     *   Read the Land Acknowledgement at the beginning of the program
     *   Provide contacts to support a Tribal Community Member for the Equity Panel
     *   (I can meet with Roberta to see what her interest/availability is for this effort, but want to reach to all of you first for guidance)
  *   I am looking for support and recommendations on additional binational individuals who may be able to speak to the Water Equity role

In order to stay within this timeline, we are hoping to secure these individuals as soon as possible and to record a voice over and translate all necessary material by 4/14. Please let me know what guidance you all may have or contacts you may have in mind for these suggestions. I am in touch with and reaching out to multiple folks for this Equity Panel effort based on stakeholders lists, interview lists, and my own research. I will keep you all posted if I can secure individuals asap, but I am trying to cover all of our bases.

Additionally, I think it would be most suitable to hold the “OSEJ Weekly w/exec Office” meeting on Tuesday 4/4 at 9am for solely Water Equity, and team members who are a part of this effort.

Thanks for all your continued effort on this project!

title: Some ideas___.msg
subject: Some ideas...
body:
Hi Elise,

As we discussed, I wanted to send some ideas on how to brief MDLR next on RWER (feel free to not use, this is just my perspective):

  *   Share screen of the 6 topics and dates and times
  *   Share that the intent of these 6 workshops
  *   Go through each, one by one and explain:
     *   What is the topic?
     *   Why was this chosen?
     *   Who is the desired attendee?
     *   Who is presenting and how was that decided?
     *   How is engagement going with the presenters?
  *   Share the flow of the overall workshop, for example:
     *   Welcome and housekeeping (5 mins)
        *   Set the expectation with Murakawa that no matter what need Spanish interpreter and recording
     *   Brief project presentation
     *   (and what ever the next items are)
  *   Then let him ask questions

For example, it could be something like:

  *   From end of June to early September, we will be hosting “Deep Dives” – virtual workshops to take a deeper dive into 5 topic areas being explored for the Regional Water Equity project.
  *   These virtual workshops look to educate the public and build the public’s engagement and knowledge of the effort to continue engaging at the 2nd water assembly and to comment on the draft report that would be released in September.
  *   Financial Risks & Investments will be the first deep dive workshop. This directly ties to the Board’s direction to identify financial risks caused by extreme weather conditions caused by droughts, like floods and fires as well as identify financial investments needed for resilience approaches that reduce risks and impacts of extreme weather.
  *   This topic has come up in many of the interviews, especially with our agricultural stakeholders as there has been crop loss in the region due to flooding.
  *   The presenter we have for this will be XXX and they have XYZ expertise, etc.

I would suggest something very short like this for each topic, and share the overall flow of each meeting (such as… These topics are the main focus of the deep dives, but we will also be providing a brief project presentation to set the stage on the overall effort.”

You could also share with him that these are modeled after the RDF Ideas Banks but are reformatting them to fit the needs of this effort.

Hope this is helpful!

title: San Diego County Regional Water Equity Report (RWER).msg
subject: San Diego County Regional Water Equity Report (RWER)
body:
Good afternoon Mr. Roy,

Thank you for your time this morning. I am following up with information about the Regional Water Equity Assessment/Report. As I mentioned to you over the phone, we are at the tail end of stakeholder interviews and would love to get your interview included in our report by the 31st of May. I have attached a fact sheet on the project and the interview questions that we would like to ask you with our GeoSyntec consultants if you are able to participate. I have cc’d Elise Ruiz who is the lead of this project in the Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice.

Essentially, this process of assessing what communities are/are not able to do to reach water equity in terms of sustainability through stormwater capturing, wastewater systems, and greywater strategies will provide a report to the County Board of Supervisors this September. We see this report being a reference to future policy and potential funding.

I saw that you accepted the calendar invite for Thursday the 25th at 2:00 p.m. to meet with Elise and me. If you find that you might be available to do the interview then, we could a lot more time and check with GeoSyntecs availability.

Thank you again!

Hi friends,

Status Update - Revised RDF Playbook Reflects Community Comments

Thank you for your interest and involvement in the County’s Regional Decarbonization Framework (RDF) and the Let’s Get There Playbook. We appreciate your thoughtful contributions to this initiative. Since a preliminary draft of the Playbook was released in January this year, we received over 500 comments through our Engagement Portal <https://lnks.gd/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJidWxsZXRpbl9saW5rX2lkIjoxMDAsInVyaSI6ImJwMjpjbGljayIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZW5nYWdlLnNhbmRpZWdvY291bnR5Lmdvdi9yZGYiLCJidWxsZXRpbl9pZCI6IjIwMjMwOTI2LjgzMTg3NzAxIn0.aUJE7w62PYmRWMQ-A3uFVTIjFKUb0ECYHV1k0UROyPs/s/2571186562/br/226868852521-l> , by email, and in-person and virtual comments at regional convenings hosted in each of the five Supervisorial districts.

 

Good news! The updated Playbook draft is now on our Engagement Portal <https://lnks.gd/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJidWxsZXRpbl9saW5rX2lkIjoxMDEsInVyaSI6ImJwMjpjbGljayIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZW5nYWdlLnNhbmRpZWdvY291bnR5Lmdvdi9yZGYiLCJidWxsZXRpbl9pZCI6IjIwMjMwOTI2LjgzMTg3NzAxIn0.EXN4LeoCyN1v7H-kNjJREnmZl4kLxymBZCfK5bj24Qs/s/2571186562/br/226868852521-l>  where you can see how comments received to-date have been incorporated while we develop the interactive Playbook website.   

 

This latest draft of the Playbook includes the following key changes from the January version:  

 

*       80 edits to the Playbook’s suggested actions to clarify terminology or provide more context surrounding the action.  For example, we clarified that tree planting projects should not conflict with rooftop or parking lot solar projects and explained that school recycling programs should focus on organic waste reduction.

*       118 new decarbonization actions and 9 case studies based on feedback that reflects varied solutions for our diverse communities.  For example, one new action suggests exploring policies that could allocate the cost-savings benefits of photovoltaics to tenants in multi-family buildings.  Another new action suggests a community-scale analysis of green transportation options, such as bike lane usage and walkability, since neighborhood characteristics can differ widely depending on whether one lives in a rural, suburban, or urban area.

*       Modified text throughout to clarify that the Playbook is an evolving resource that will be informed by the learned experience of individuals and communities.

*       Explained that the term “disadvantaged communities” is used in the context of aligning with federal and state funds and that representation terminology would be developed in consultation with communities in the future.

*       Clarified that expediting permits and fee waivers for renewable energy projects only refers to rooftop and parking lot solar on or adjacent to buildings, and do not apply to utility-scale projects.

*       Explained that some of the comments pertaining to the energy section of the Technical Report will be addressed through the Energy Supply Study approved by the Board on May 24, 2023. The Study will deepen infill renewable energy analysis and add data and guidance based on localized community conditions and needs.

The RDF Team will continue our outreach as the Playbook evolves. We are committed to help identify strategies and actions most suited to your unique needs, as there is no one-size-fits-all approach. The RDF Technical Analysis, Workforce Analysis, and Playbook are meant as guides that offer individuals, organizations, communities, and the region flexibility as we harmonize our responses to global climate changes.

body:
Good afternoon, Board Staff~

OSEJ is pleased to announce a series of events from June 28 through September 6 that will engage the community on various aspects of the County’s Regional Water Equity <https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/osej/waterequity/>  effort, and we hope you can help us spread the word.

ABOUT THE EVENTS

There will be six virtual 1-hour workshops on a variety of water sustainability topics. Each workshop will include a brief presentation followed by structured interactive discussion to better understand our communities’ experiences with these topics.

OUTREACH REQUEST

We would appreciate your assistance sharing information about these events with your constituents. For your use in social media and other outreach channels, the events flyer is attached and sample social media post is below. The topics, dates, and times of all events are also noted on the flyer.

Social Media Post Examples:

*         Main Title – “How has the drought impacted your life, community, and home? Join us at an upcoming Deep Dive workshop to share your water story!”

*         Subtitle Examples

o    “Join the County’s Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice Deep Dives to explore a variety of water topics including: water sustainability practices, stormwater reuse in affordable housing, and financial risk and investments due to extreme weather.”

o    “Join the County’s Office of Sustainability and Environmental Justice this summer to explore the financial impacts of drought and explore other water topics. We are hosting virtual workshops and want to hear from you.”

*         (Attach social media graphic with workshop details)

We plan to update you on our progress to date for the Regional Water Equity Report, including outreach and the planned memo to the Board of Supervisors during the Board staff briefings on June 22.

Thanks in advance for your help. Please feel free to contact the team with questions or if you’d like more information: osej@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:osej@sdcounty.ca.gov>  or elise.ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:elise.ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov>

subject: UCSD workshops
to: Amy Lerner <amlerner@ucsd.edu>; Juli Beth Hinds <jhinds@ucsd.edu>; "Gordon McCord" <gmccord@ucsd.edu>
body:
Dear UCSD team,

The approach on the following workshops has been approved. The next steps for the UCSD team are:

Workshop #1: Please place a hold on November 7 on all your calendars and reserve the PEB space. It would be helpful to begin drafting an agenda/program that we would be discuss with Sarah on September 2.
Workshop #2: We will be coordinating with the Planning and Development Services Department and get back to you.
Workshop #3: It would be helpful if we can develop a timeline. We will be coordinating with our Vice Chair Nora Vargas.

Thank you!
Murtaza
____________________________

  1.  Enterprise-wide Alignment of RDF
Date: November 7, 2022 (back-up would be November 4, 2022)
Participants:  County of San Diego internal department leadership, internal stakeholders
Duration: Full-day 2-part workshop
Location: 7th floor terrace at the Public Engagement Building

This workshop would provide an initial convening of County of San Diego leadership and departments engaged in the implementation of decarbonization across municipal functions:  (1) Departmental Sustainability Planning, led by LUEG; (2) the Land Acquisition Roundtable, led by Parks & Recreation; and (3) the renewable energy siting framework in the RDF.  This workshop would focus on the County departments’ short/mid/long term goals towards sustainability; geospatial and policy relationships, conflicts, and potential synergies among and between land acquisition for park, conservation, and recreation purposes; and the extent of land area for new solar and wind energy required by alternative strategies in the RDF.  This approach would help build a common understanding of the policy levers and constraints for the departments in relationship to GHG reduction, and the distribution and extent of each set of land use needs, supporting the goal of identifying potential synergies including opportunities for multi-benefit uses of land for agriculture, water and watershed sustainability, recreation, and regional habitat linkage.

***This workshop would be in tandem with the preparation of document defining the scope of work regarding the team’s advisory role for LUEG and the RDF. [Ref: Tasks 2.1 & 2.2]

  2.  Sustainable Land Use Framework (SLUF)
Timeline: Early 2023
Participants: County’s Planning & Development Services Department, external stakeholders
Location: First floor lab on the ground floor of the Public Engagement Building

This workshop will focus on the themes adopted by the Board in September 2022 in the context of the General Plan for the unincorporated area of the County. It would not be framed as RDF implementation but would examine the potential alignments of SLUF with decarbonization pathways. These themes could include: (1) decarbonization of buildings, communities, and transportation through policies and land use; (2) increase opportunities for sustainable and resilient development and housing for all; (3) support green economies, innovative infrastructure, agriculture, and sustainable best practices; (4) conserve and protect existing natural habitats and resources, and increase access to open and green spaces; and (5) prioritize social equity and environmental justice in sustainable land use policies, programs, and plans.

  3.  Binational Regional Climate Action Plan
Timeframe:  Last quarter 2023/first quarter 2024
Participants:  Jurisdictions in San Diego County with CAPs (municipalities; SANDAG; Unified Port of San Diego; US Department of Defense); California Office of Policy & Research
Invited Guests:  Governments of Baja California Norte; City of Tijuana; UABC

The third workshop would engage stakeholders across the county and San Diego-Tijuana region in evaluating the consistency and commonality of purpose and strategies among and between the individual Climate Action Plans (CAPs) adopted pursuant to State directives and local initiative.  UCSD students would prepare assessments of each plan in a unified framework illustrating the baselines, policies, action steps, and reporting metrics across the region.  The workshop will focus on building common awareness and purpose; exchanging strategies and ideas; identifying areas of potential re-alignment; and building a binational baseline for emissions and measures. This workshop would explore the possibility of a Binational Regional Climate Action Plan.

**UCSD also could extend some of the mapping into Baja California to illustrate trans-border issues, notably for transportation, housing, watersheds, and habitat.

_____________________________________
Murtaza H. Baxamusa, PhD, AICP
Program Manager for Regional Sustainability
Land Use and Environment Group
County of San Diego

Dear UCSD team,

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

Nicole from our office is leading this effort, and I wanted you all to be acquainted with it (see her email below) since it may come up in our meetings on RDF implementation and USP workshops. If you would like we can set up a meeting with Nicole.

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

Nicole from our office is leading this effort, and I wanted you all to be acquainted with it (see her email below) since it may come up in our meetings on RDF implementation and USP workshops. If you would like we can set up a meeting with Nicole.

Murtaza

On Wed, Jul 27, 2022 at 2:32 PM Baxamusa, Murtaza <Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov>> wrote:

Dear UCSD team,

The approach on the following workshops has been approved. The next steps for the UCSD team are:

Workshop #1: Please place a hold on November 7 on all your calendars and reserve the PEB space. It would be helpful to begin drafting an agenda/program that we would be discuss with Sarah on September 2.

Workshop #2: We will be coordinating with the Planning and Development Services Department and get back to you.

Workshop #3: It would be helpful if we can develop a timeline. We will be coordinating with our Vice Chair Nora Vargas.

Thank you!

Murtaza

____________________________

  1.  Enterprise-wide Alignment of RDF

Date: November 7, 2022 (back-up would be November 4, 2022)
Participants:  County of San Diego internal department leadership, internal stakeholders
Duration: Full-day 2-part workshop

Location: 7th floor terrace at the Public Engagement Building

This workshop would provide an initial convening of County of San Diego leadership and departments engaged in the implementation of decarbonization across municipal functions:  (1) Departmental Sustainability Planning, led by LUEG; (2) the Land Acquisition Roundtable, led by Parks & Recreation; and (3) the renewable energy siting framework in the RDF.  This workshop would focus on the County departments’ short/mid/long term goals towards sustainability; geospatial and policy relationships, conflicts, and potential synergies among and between land acquisition for park, conservation, and recreation purposes; and the extent of land area for new solar and wind energy required by alternative strategies in the RDF.  This approach would help build a common understanding of the policy levers and constraints for the departments in relationship to GHG reduction, and the distribution and extent of each set of land use needs, supporting the goal of identifying potential synergies including opportunities for multi-benefit uses of land for agriculture, water and watershed sustainability, recreation, and regional habitat linkage.

***This workshop would be in tandem with the preparation of document defining the scope of work regarding the team’s advisory role for LUEG and the RDF. [Ref: Tasks 2.1 & 2.2]

  2.  Sustainable Land Use Framework (SLUF)

Timeline: Early 2023

Participants: County’s Planning & Development Services Department, external stakeholders

Location: First floor lab on the ground floor of the Public Engagement Building

This workshop will focus on the themes adopted by the Board in September 2022 in the context of the General Plan for the unincorporated area of the County. It would not be framed as RDF implementation but would examine the potential alignments of SLUF with decarbonization pathways. These themes could include: (1) decarbonization of buildings, communities, and transportation through policies and land use; (2) increase opportunities for sustainable and resilient development and housing for all; (3) support green economies, innovative infrastructure, agriculture, and sustainable best practices; (4) conserve and protect existing natural habitats and resources, and increase access to open and green spaces; and (5) prioritize social equity and environmental justice in sustainable land use policies, programs, and plans.

  3.  Binational Regional Climate Action Plan

Timeframe:  Last quarter 2023/first quarter 2024

Participants:  Jurisdictions in San Diego County with CAPs (municipalities; SANDAG; Unified Port of San Diego; US Department of Defense); California Office of Policy & Research

Invited Guests:  Governments of Baja California Norte; City of Tijuana; UABC

The third workshop would engage stakeholders across the county and San Diego-Tijuana region in evaluating the consistency and commonality of purpose and strategies among and between the individual Climate Action Plans (CAPs) adopted pursuant to State directives and local initiative.  UCSD students would prepare assessments of each plan in a unified framework illustrating the baselines, policies, action steps, and reporting metrics across the region.  The workshop will focus on building common awareness and purpose; exchanging strategies and ideas; identifying areas of potential re-alignment; and building a binational baseline for emissions and measures. This workshop would explore the possibility of a Binational Regional Climate Action Plan.

**UCSD also could extend some of the mapping into Baja California to illustrate trans-border issues, notably for transportation, housing, watersheds, and habitat.

_____________________________________

Murtaza H. Baxamusa, PhD, AICP

Program Manager for Regional Sustainability

Land Use and Environment Group

County of San Diego

to: "Cooper; Garrett" <Garrett.Cooper@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Dang; Ha"	<Ha.Dang@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Alfaro; Suedy" <Suedy.Alfaro@sdcounty.ca.gov>;	"Lintvedt; Inga" <Inga.Lintvedt@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Sjoblom; Randall"	<Randall.Sjoblom@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Beaumont; Anne"	<Anne.Beaumont@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Abbott; Jamie"	<Jamie.Abbott@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Buonomo; Heather"	<Heather.Buonomo@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Glueck; John-Ross"	<John-Ross.Glueck@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Harbert; Amy"	<Amy.Harbert@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Appel; Rebeca"	<Rebeca.Appel@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "De La Rosa; Michael"	<Michael.DeLaRosa@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Demorest; Erin"	<Erin.Demorest@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Hanson; Elise A"	<EliseA.Hanson@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Acosta; Migell"	<Migell.Acosta@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Albright; Brian"	<Brian.Albright@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Oakes; Chelsea"	<Chelsea.Oakes@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Salomon; Johanna"	<Johanna.Salomon@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Trojanowska; Kasia"	<Kasia.Trojanowska@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Bray; Kelly"	<Kelly.Bray@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Farmer; Tyler" <Tyler.Farmer@sdcounty.ca.gov>;	"Slovick; Mark" <Mark.Slovick@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Talleh; Rami"	<Rami.Talleh@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Benham; Crystal"	<Crystal.Benham@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "James; Kamilah"	<kamilah.James@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Gade; Derek" <Derek.Gade@sdcounty.ca.gov>;	"Morgan; William" <William.Morgan@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Pasumarthi; Murali"	<Murali.Pasumarthi@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Pirouzian; Ali"	<Ali.Pirouzian@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Whipple; Richard"	<Richard.Whipple@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Agahi; Sara"	<Sara.Agahi@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Tubongbanua; Peejay"	<Peejay.Tubongbanua@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Rasoulzadeh; Yasamin"	<Yasamin.Rasoulzadeh@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Boghossian Ambrose; Nicole"	<Nicole.Ambrose@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Isicson; Robin"	<Robin.Isicson@sdcounty.ca.gov>; "Marchesano; Charles"	<Charles.Marchesano@sdcounty.ca.gov>
body:
We began the journey on the Regional Decarbonization Framework (RDF) last year in January when our Board of Supervisors directed us to work with UCSD on bringing the best available science to address a challenge that none of us can address in silos on our own – that of decarbonizing every major emitting sector in the region no matter where the emissions originate, for emissions know no boundaries.

As we are now transitioning from study to implementation, we are asking what can we do collectively in partnership with universities, business, labor and community, that will give us greater efficiencies in scale and speed to address climate change in the most effective and humane way possible. All of us from the County have sustainability embedded within the strategic direction of each of our departments. The goals of this workshop are to think about what more can we do? How do we implement sustainability within our core functions? How do we add value to our existing programs so that they also meet the goals of decarbonization? What new programs can achieve a better outcome?

We are meeting offsite at the Public Engagement Building at UCSD to visualize that greener future.

This workshop begins a new chapter in our relationship with UCSD as an academic partner to help us figure out how to implement this framework. This will be the first in a series of three workshops over our 3-year partnership. The UCSD team will focus on the implementation of the RDF for this workshop.  While of course there are many intersecting issues, the exercises will focus on land-based implications of RDF as well as simply getting everyone more proficient in the vocabulary and implications of the RDF itself. We will also walk through specific scenarios so that we leave the day with a practical understanding of how this framework can inform the work we do on a day-to-day basis in all our departments.

Thank you and looking forward to seeing you on Monday,

Murtaza and Sarah

Cc: Marchesano, Charles
Subject: All Day Offsite Workshop at UCSD
When: Monday, November 7, 2022 9:00 AM-4:00 PM (UTC-08:00) Pacific Time (US & Canada).
Where: UCSD Social Sciences Public Engagement Building, 7th Floor Terrace

Please join us for an exciting new workshop led by our UCSD collaborators. This workshop would provide an initial convening of County of San Diego leadership and departments engaged in the implementation of decarbonization across municipal functions:  (1) Departmental Sustainability Planning, led by LUEG; (2) the Land Acquisition Roundtable, led by Parks & Recreation; and (3) the renewable energy siting framework in the RDF.  This workshop would focus on the County departments’ short/mid/long term goals towards sustainability; geospatial and policy relationships, conflicts, and potential synergies among and between land acquisition for park, conservation, and recreation purposes; and the extent of land area for new solar and wind energy required by alternative strategies in the RDF.  This approach would help build a common understanding of the policy levers and constraints for the departments in relationship to GHG reduction, and the distribution and extent of each set of land use needs, supporting the goal of identifying potential synergies including opportunities for multi-benefit uses of land for agriculture, water and watershed sustainability, recreation, and regional habitat linkage.

LOCATION: UCSD Social Sciences Public Engagement Building, 7th Floor Conference Room, in the new 6th College at UCSD, 9am - 4pm.
Location: https://goo.gl/maps/WzYiL8WjLEesmtyj8

Specific Parking Instructions will come soon.

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

Nicole from our office is leading this effort, and I wanted you all to be acquainted with it (see her email below) since it may come up in our meetings on RDF implementation and USP workshops. If you would like we can set up a meeting with Nicole.

Subject: [External] RDF Clarity and New Direction

Hi Rimga!

Thanks again for being the moderator for Nexus! It's going to be great to have you there!

Regarding the RDF, after our last meeting, we've done some internal discussions and clarified our scope a bit. With the new direction around focusing on identifying specific climate action projects, I wanted to quickly confirm that we are on the right track.

*	Instead of focusing on engaging as many individuals as possible from Communities of Concerns, we will focus now on reaching organizations who are actively working on climate action projects that would benefit from the County's support or would help inform the Regional CAP and other future climate policies. These organizations will continue to be within and uplift Communities of Concern.
*	We will also highlight and focus on reaching local council offices and policy makers who are actively working on or identifying capital improvement projects that may benefit from the RDF as a reference or that may become part of future CAPs.
*	We are communicating that the RDF is a guide for implementing climate action throughout the region and can be used to inform climate policies on local and regional levels. While the County cannot lead the projects themselves, the County may be able to help provide resources in the form of grants, the RDF guidebook, etc.
*	After speaking with the Water Equity Team, we are incorporating water questions into our community gatherings and surveys.

Going forward, we do have a few followup questions as well!

*	When will the Convenings be? After speaking with the Water Equity team, it sounds like they will be in November afterall. Can we schedule a meeting ASAP to discuss programming, roles, and next steps? We are running out of time to book places and we should start promoting those soon for effective turnout.
*	If we are to focus on gathering feedback from organizations about specific projects, do you still need demographic data? If so, do you want that data coupled in a full survey like it currently is, or should we create a smaller demographic data only survey that accompanies the feedback that we receive in other ways (discussion, posters, notes, testimonies, etc.)
*	What do your project portfolios look like? How can we best compile project information to match and add to your existing portfolios?

Thank you!! I super appreciate your time and collaboration on this!

In Gratitude,

ali

From: Gordon McCord <gmccord@ucsd.edu>
Sent: Friday, August 19, 2022 9:27 PM
To: Baxamusa, Murtaza <Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Amy Lerner <amlerner@ucsd.edu>; Juli Beth Hinds <jhinds@ucsd.edu>
Cc: Appel, Rebeca <Rebeca.Appel@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Boghossian Ambrose, Nicole <Nicole.Ambrose@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Jeffrey Myers <jmyers@ucsd.edu>
Subject: RE: [External] Dept Sustainability Plans Information

Dear Murtaza, Rebeca and Nicole,

Thanks for the very useful conversation today.  As follow-up, I’ve drafted the attached concept note on what benchmarking the County’s efforts against the SDGs could look like.  I stress that this is meant to be complementary to the existing sustainability framework used by the county, but the benefit is that it benchmarks the county’s progress against internationally-recognized goals for environmental sustainability and social inclusion.

I’d be eager to hear your feedback and incorporate your advice.  I’m excited about a data-driven, integrated strategic planning process to meet the SDGs, using the common framework they provide and the quantitative 2030 as an useful organizing principle for some of our conversations (again, as a complement to existing county vision and goals around sustainability).  The SDGs also open the door to strategic collaborations with other jurisdictions in the region to meet the SDGs (including the City of San Diego, which has announced it wants to do a VLR but has not yet started).

Regards,

Gordon

PS Copying Jeff Myers who supports me on SDGPI work.

subject: FW: UCSD workshops
body:
FYI - sending to you for awareness/background. More info about November 7th workshop that Murtaza is organizing with UCSD. Highlighted some relevant info about departmental sustainability plans.

This is the first I am seeing this, but happy to chat if you have any questions or thoughts.

From: Baxamusa, Murtaza <Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Sent: Wednesday, July 27, 2022 2:33 PM
To: Amy Lerner <amlerner@ucsd.edu>; Juli Beth Hinds <jhinds@ucsd.edu>; Gordon McCord <gmccord@ucsd.edu>
Cc: Hanson, Elise A <EliseA.Hanson@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Appel, Rebeca <Rebeca.Appel@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: UCSD workshops

Dear UCSD team,

The approach on the following workshops has been approved. The next steps for the UCSD team are:

Workshop #1: Please place a hold on November 7 on all your calendars and reserve the PEB space. It would be helpful to begin drafting an agenda/program that we would be discuss with Sarah on September 2.
Workshop #2: We will be coordinating with the Planning and Development Services Department and get back to you.
Workshop #3: It would be helpful if we can develop a timeline. We will be coordinating with our Vice Chair Nora Vargas.

Thank you!
Murtaza
____________________________

  1.  Enterprise-wide Alignment of RDF
Date: November 7, 2022 (back-up would be November 4, 2022)
Participants:  County of San Diego internal department leadership, internal stakeholders
Duration: Full-day 2-part workshop
Location: 7th floor terrace at the Public Engagement Building

This workshop would provide an initial convening of County of San Diego leadership and departments engaged in the implementation of decarbonization across municipal functions:  (1) Departmental Sustainability Planning, led by LUEG; (2) the Land Acquisition Roundtable, led by Parks & Recreation; and (3) the renewable energy siting framework in the RDF.  This workshop would focus on the County departments’ short/mid/long term goals towards sustainability; geospatial and policy relationships, conflicts, and potential synergies among and between land acquisition for park, conservation, and recreation purposes; and the extent of land area for new solar and wind energy required by alternative strategies in the RDF.  This approach would help build a common understanding of the policy levers and constraints for the departments in relationship to GHG reduction, and the distribution and extent of each set of land use needs, supporting the goal of identifying potential synergies including opportunities for multi-benefit uses of land for agriculture, water and watershed sustainability, recreation, and regional habitat linkage.

***This workshop would be in tandem with the preparation of document defining the scope of work regarding the team’s advisory role for LUEG and the RDF. [Ref: Tasks 2.1 & 2.2]

  2.  Sustainable Land Use Framework (SLUF)
Timeline: Early 2023
Participants: County’s Planning & Development Services Department, external stakeholders
Location: First floor lab on the ground floor of the Public Engagement Building

This workshop will focus on the themes adopted by the Board in September 2022 in the context of the General Plan for the unincorporated area of the County. It would not be framed as RDF implementation but would examine the potential alignments of SLUF with decarbonization pathways. These themes could include: (1) decarbonization of buildings, communities, and transportation through policies and land use; (2) increase opportunities for sustainable and resilient development and housing for all; (3) support green economies, innovative infrastructure, agriculture, and sustainable best practices; (4) conserve and protect existing natural habitats and resources, and increase access to open and green spaces; and (5) prioritize social equity and environmental justice in sustainable land use policies, programs, and plans.

  3.  Binational Regional Climate Action Plan
Timeframe:  Last quarter 2023/first quarter 2024
Participants:  Jurisdictions in San Diego County with CAPs (municipalities; SANDAG; Unified Port of San Diego; US Department of Defense); California Office of Policy & Research
Invited Guests:  Governments of Baja California Norte; City of Tijuana; UABC

The third workshop would engage stakeholders across the county and San Diego-Tijuana region in evaluating the consistency and commonality of purpose and strategies among and between the individual Climate Action Plans (CAPs) adopted pursuant to State directives and local initiative.  UCSD students would prepare assessments of each plan in a unified framework illustrating the baselines, policies, action steps, and reporting metrics across the region.  The workshop will focus on building common awareness and purpose; exchanging strategies and ideas; identifying areas of potential re-alignment; and building a binational baseline for emissions and measures. This workshop would explore the possibility of a Binational Regional Climate Action Plan.

**UCSD also could extend some of the mapping into Baja California to illustrate trans-border issues, notably for transportation, housing, watersheds, and habitat.

_____________________________________
Murtaza H. Baxamusa, PhD, AICP
Program Manager for Regional Sustainability
Land Use and Environment Group
County of San Diego

Cc: Aghassi, Sarah <Sarah.Aghassi@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Lawson, Jennifer <Jennifer.Lawson@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: Agenda and Goals for Nov 7 workshop at UCSD

We began the journey on the Regional Decarbonization Framework (RDF) last year in January when our Board of Supervisors directed us to work with UCSD on bringing the best available science to address a challenge that none of us can address in silos on our own – that of decarbonizing every major emitting sector in the region no matter where the emissions originate, for emissions know no boundaries.

As we are now transitioning from study to implementation, we are asking what can we do collectively in partnership with universities, business, labor and community, that will give us greater efficiencies in scale and speed to address climate change in the most effective and humane way possible. All of us from the County have sustainability embedded within the strategic direction of each of our departments. The goals of this workshop are to think about what more can we do? How do we implement sustainability within our core functions? How do we add value to our existing programs so that they also meet the goals of decarbonization? What new programs can achieve a better outcome?

We are meeting offsite at the Public Engagement Building at UCSD to visualize that greener future.

This workshop begins a new chapter in our relationship with UCSD as an academic partner to help us figure out how to implement this framework. This will be the first in a series of three workshops over our 3-year partnership. The UCSD team will focus on the implementation of the RDF for this workshop.  While of course there are many intersecting issues, the exercises will focus on land-based implications of RDF as well as simply getting everyone more proficient in the vocabulary and implications of the RDF itself. We will also walk through specific scenarios so that we leave the day with a practical understanding of how this framework can inform the work we do on a day-to-day basis in all our departments.

Thank you and looking forward to seeing you on Monday,

Murtaza and Sarah

-----Original Appointment-----
From: Lawson, Jennifer <Jennifer.Lawson@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Jennifer.Lawson@sdcounty.ca.gov>>
Sent: Tuesday, October 18, 2022 5:12 PM
To: Lawson, Jennifer; Lawson, Jennifer; Cooper, Garrett; Dang, Ha; Alfaro, Suedy; Lintvedt, Inga; Sjoblom, Randall; Beaumont, Anne; Abbott, Jamie; Buonomo, Heather; Glueck, John-Ross; Harbert, Amy; Appel, Rebeca; Baxamusa, Murtaza; De La Rosa, Michael; Demorest, Erin; Hanson, Elise A; Acosta, Migell; Albright, Brian; Oakes, Chelsea; Salomon, Johanna; Trojanowska, Kasia; Bray, Kelly; Farmer, Tyler; Slovick, Mark; Talleh, Rami; Benham, Crystal; James, Kamilah; Gade, Derek; Morgan, William; Pasumarthi, Murali; Pirouzian, Ali; Whipple, Richard; Agahi, Sara; Tubongbanua, Peejay; Rasoulzadeh, Yasamin; Aghassi, Sarah; Boghossian Ambrose, Nicole; Isicson, Robin
Cc: Marchesano, Charles
Subject: All Day Offsite Workshop at UCSD
When: Monday, November 7, 2022 9:00 AM-4:00 PM (UTC-08:00) Pacific Time (US & Canada).
Where: UCSD Social Sciences Public Engagement Building, 7th Floor Terrace

Please join us for an exciting new workshop led by our UCSD collaborators. This workshop would provide an initial convening of County of San Diego leadership and departments engaged in the implementation of decarbonization across municipal functions:  (1) Departmental Sustainability Planning, led by LUEG; (2) the Land Acquisition Roundtable, led by Parks & Recreation; and (3) the renewable energy siting framework in the RDF.  This workshop would focus on the County departments’ short/mid/long term goals towards sustainability; geospatial and policy relationships, conflicts, and potential synergies among and between land acquisition for park, conservation, and recreation purposes; and the extent of land area for new solar and wind energy required by alternative strategies in the RDF.  This approach would help build a common understanding of the policy levers and constraints for the departments in relationship to GHG reduction, and the distribution and extent of each set of land use needs, supporting the goal of identifying potential synergies including opportunities for multi-benefit uses of land for agriculture, water and watershed sustainability, recreation, and regional habitat linkage.

LOCATION: UCSD Social Sciences Public Engagement Building, 7th Floor Conference Room, in the new 6th College at UCSD, 9am - 4pm.
Location: https://goo.gl/maps/WzYiL8WjLEesmtyj8

Specific Parking Instructions will come soon.

body:
Dear UCSD team,

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

Nicole from our office is leading this effort, and I wanted you all to be acquainted with it (see her email below) since it may come up in our meetings on RDF implementation and USP workshops. If you would like we can set up a meeting with Nicole.

Please let me know if you need any other background on this,
Murtaza

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

title: RE_ _External_ Dept Sustainability Plans Information (1).msg
subject: RE: [External] Dept Sustainability Plans Information
to: "Baxamusa; Murtaza" <Murtaza.Baxamusa@sdcounty.ca.gov>; Amy Lerner	<amlerner@ucsd.edu>; Juli Beth Hinds <jhinds@ucsd.edu>
body:
Dear Murtaza, Rebeca and Nicole,

Thanks for the very useful conversation today.  As follow-up, I’ve drafted the attached concept note on what benchmarking the County’s efforts against the SDGs could look like.  I stress that this is meant to be complementary to the existing sustainability framework used by the county, but the benefit is that it benchmarks the county’s progress against internationally-recognized goals for environmental sustainability and social inclusion.

I’d be eager to hear your feedback and incorporate your advice.  I’m excited about a data-driven, integrated strategic planning process to meet the SDGs, using the common framework they provide and the quantitative 2030 as an useful organizing principle for some of our conversations (again, as a complement to existing county vision and goals around sustainability).  The SDGs also open the door to strategic collaborations with other jurisdictions in the region to meet the SDGs (including the City of San Diego, which has announced it wants to do a VLR but has not yet started).

Regards,

Gordon

PS Copying Jeff Myers who supports me on SDGPI work.

body:
Good morning,

Thank you for your time last week; it was great to meet you all! I have attached the slides from Friday’s meeting, with a few minor adjustments based on your feedback. The schedule, most notably, has been updated to reflect the earlier submittal and lengthened review period for the first draft of the Regional Water Equity Report. Please let me know if you would like to see additional edits to the timeline.

We have one initial request to get Task 3 started (Stormwater Capture and Use at Parks/Facilities): ArcGIS polygons for County-owned parks/facilities, including embedded facility information (e.g., name, type, operating department, etc.). The first deliverables for both Tasks 3 and 4 will include additional data requests.

We also be coordinating with Elise on the list of potential interviewees and ongoing OSEJ efforts.

Best regards,
Megan

title: RDF Follow Up.msg
subject: RDF Follow Up
body:
Morning Tyler,

I wanted to follow up on our Monday check in with some more about our existing contracts, as well as a recap of our public meeting last night for your awareness.

Contracts
   *   UCSD – overall policy and implementation support, sustainable agriculture/food systems (screenshot of task below). Contract is through April 2025.

   *   USD EPIC – implementation playbook, implementation playbook with specific/tailored actions for the unincorporated county, supplemental report on other agencies/large companies CAPs and other emissions (Task 3), social equity guidelines (Task 6), and climate equity indicators (Task 7). Contract is through June 2025.
        *   As discussed – we are working with EPIC on timeframes and can follow up with you.

7/26 Public Meeting
   *   Playbook – a lot of questions on why no metrics or targets in this. We explained that this is our first step to work towards implementation, and as this is a visionary framework we want to work collaboratively and with local governments and organization to bring them into this effort to collectively work towards our goal.
        *   Also emphasized that the Playbook actions will be shaped by our working groups, EPIC will provide some places to start based on the Local Policy Opportunity (chapter 8), but we want this shaped and guided by our working groups.
   *   Overall folks were pretty happy with the inclusion of our new sector – food systems & circular economy – many comments around how waste diversion is often not included and overlooked.
   *   Based on feedback we received from Sarah, we included the link to the PDS site with the actions going before the Board on 8/31 and we received a question on whether the climate farming pilot would fall under land use & natural climate solutions or food systems & circular economy – my response was that these sectors intersect and are closely related as carbon farming improves soil health, as well as in agricultural production specific to food. So we kept it general to show that there will be overlap.
        *   Another example is in electricity when we talk about rooftop and infill solar – it starts in electricity (generation), but can intersect with buildings as those will need to connect.

I’ve also attached our PPT from last night. The slides specific to the Playbook will be the base for future stakeholder presentations. Please let me know if you have any questions – I know this is a lot of info, so happy to chat about it to.

Rebeca Appel

to: Gordon McCord <gmccord@ucsd.edu>; Amy Lerner <amlerner@ucsd.edu>; "Juli Beth Hinds" <jhinds@ucsd.edu>
body:
Dear Gordon,

Thank you for putting together this SDG alignment vision. It makes sense to have each of our sustainability efforts in the region add up to internationally-recognized goals. Identifying policy gaps in cities/neighborhoods to achieve those goals could supplement the work we do the RDF, such as coordinating on Climate Action Plans to meet regional goals on decarbonization.

Let me process this internally for the team and get back to you on next steps.
Murtaza

Subject: RE: [External] Dept Sustainability Plans Information

Dear Murtaza, Rebeca and Nicole,

Thanks for the very useful conversation today.  As follow-up, I’ve drafted the attached concept note on what benchmarking the County’s efforts against the SDGs could look like.  I stress that this is meant to be complementary to the existing sustainability framework used by the county, but the benefit is that it benchmarks the county’s progress against internationally-recognized goals for environmental sustainability and social inclusion.

I’d be eager to hear your feedback and incorporate your advice.  I’m excited about a data-driven, integrated strategic planning process to meet the SDGs, using the common framework they provide and the quantitative 2030 as an useful organizing principle for some of our conversations (again, as a complement to existing county vision and goals around sustainability).  The SDGs also open the door to strategic collaborations with other jurisdictions in the region to meet the SDGs (including the City of San Diego, which has announced it wants to do a VLR but has not yet started).

Regards,

Gordon

PS Copying Jeff Myers who supports me on SDGPI work.

Good afternoon Stephanie,
Pursuant to our conversation this afternoon UCSD would like to formalize a request for a minor scope amendment to reflect the change in focus and technical content of the Regional Water Equity Report convening slated for Wednesday, April 26th.  As the focus of the meeting will no longer be based on the contents of the drought impact literature review being conducted by UCSD, and as the need for and focus of presentation content and public information has changed, we would like to request approval of the following:

1. UCSD will focus on completion of a technical presentation highlighting preliminary findings of the literature review, submitted in powerpoint format by Friday, April 14th for editing and translation.  It is our understanding that the length of the presentation may be anywhere from ten minutes to roughly one hour, depending on the County’s selection of additional presenters with technical content.

2.  UCSD will complete a summary of the technical presentation for the public meeting.  This will be a graphic-rich handout in print and web-compatible format (likely powerpoint) by Friday, April 14th, offering key information and links in a form suitable for the general public and with links for further information to technical sources.

3.  For the meeting itself, UCSD will NOT be responsible for agendas, printing, name tags, etc.  as it is our understanding that Murakawa Communications has been contracted to supply these materials.  UCSD will have roughly ten (10) students present to assist with sign-in, logistics, polling, and collecting public comments.  UCSD’s students will have (10) iPads with them, with connectivity suitable for use for PollEverywhere questions for those without devices.

3.  UCSD will resume work on the literature review after the meeting, adding a review of available water rate information for San Diego and Imperial Counties and the bi-national region.  The meeting summary likewise will be completed.

Thank you Stephanie for your support and leadership!
Sincerely,
JB

Dear UCSD team,

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

Nicole from our office is leading this effort, and I wanted you all to be acquainted with it (see her email below) since it may come up in our meetings on RDF implementation and USP workshops. If you would like we can set up a meeting with Nicole.

Please let me know if you need any other background on this,
Murtaza

Good afternoon,

I wanted to share this scope modification request from UCSD regarding the literature review and the content of the April 26 Water Assembly. From: Juli Beth Hinds <jhinds@ucsd.edu<mailto:jhinds@ucsd.edu>>

Subject: County Regional Water Equity Convening - Scope Modification

CAUTION: This email originated from outside of the organization. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe. If you have any suspicion, please confirm with the sender verbally that this email is authentic. If you suspect fraud, click "Phish Alert Report."

Good afternoon Stephanie,
Pursuant to our conversation this afternoon UCSD would like to formalize a request for a minor scope amendment to reflect the change in focus and technical content of the Regional Water Equity Report convening slated for Wednesday, April 26th.  As the focus of the meeting will no longer be based on the contents of the drought impact literature review being conducted by UCSD, and as the need for and focus of presentation content and public information has changed, we would like to request approval of the following:

1. UCSD will focus on completion of a technical presentation highlighting preliminary findings of the literature review, submitted in powerpoint format by Friday, April 14th for editing and translation.  It is our understanding that the length of the presentation may be anywhere from ten minutes to roughly one hour, depending on the County’s selection of additional presenters with technical content.

2.  UCSD will complete a summary of the technical presentation for the public meeting.  This will be a graphic-rich handout in print and web-compatible format (likely powerpoint) by Friday, April 14th, offering key information and links in a form suitable for the general public and with links for further information to technical sources.

3.  For the meeting itself, UCSD will NOT be responsible for agendas, printing, name tags, etc.  as it is our understanding that Murakawa Communications has been contracted to supply these materials.  UCSD will have roughly ten (10) students present to assist with sign-in, logistics, polling, and collecting public comments.  UCSD’s students will have (10) iPads with them, with connectivity suitable for use for PollEverywhere questions for those without devices.

3.  UCSD will resume work on the literature review after the meeting, adding a review of available water rate information for San Diego and Imperial Counties and the bi-national region.  The meeting summary likewise will be completed.

Thank you Stephanie for your support and leadership!
Sincerely,
JB

Juli Beth Hinds, AICP
Staff Research Associate & Instructor

body:
Hi everyone! Looking forward to our brainstorm later today. Here is a proposed agenda:

1.	Discuss goal/outcomes of next regional convenings

	a.	Potential idea: Have regional convenings be a space to start change the understanding of what the RDF is and how we can start to translate RDF into what the community needs and identify next steps for regional initiatives
	b.	Use convenings to discuss how we use RDF as guiding principle for innovative/inspiration initiatives - what would this look like?
	c.	CBOs shared that we could do workshop tables/small group planning
	d.	Are they by theme? Or are they by district?

2.	Timeframe

	a.	For example, if district specific, then District 4 could happen in January 2024 and other districts October and November 2023

3.	Coordinating with CBOs on planning

-----Original Appointment-----

Dear UCSD team,

There is a departmental sustainability planning effort underway at the County that is quite unique, in that the plans were built up from the bottom-up by the staff working on the activities within the departments themselves rather than a high-level plan that may have difficulty getting actually implemented. Another unique feature of this effort is that there is a countywide steering committee with County staff that spans all the four functional groups covering all departments, so that there is coordination at the highest levels.

This departmental sustainability effort was directed by the Board last May, and the countywide sustainability goals were adopted in March this year; so the work (with Arup as consultant) has been proceeding somewhat on parallel track with the RDF.

Nicole from our office is leading this effort, and I wanted you all to be acquainted with it (see her email below) since it may come up in our meetings on RDF implementation and USP workshops. If you would like we can set up a meeting with Nicole.

Please let me know if you need any other background on this,
Murtaza

title: RE_ RDF Clarity and New Direction.msg
subject: RE: RDF Clarity and New Direction
body:
Hi there,

Let me know if you would like me to support the RDF discussion in the small group in any way, or if you just want to circle back with me when you have solidified the topics based of gleaned information or identified gaps. I am all about generating processes to meet the goals/purpose of the convenings.

I would love to support the “data mining” for many reasons, but I feel really swamped with too many priorities at this time. I am wondering if Eden would allow support from our newest team members if they willing and are available? I looked on the most recent monthly reports from CBOs for communities being served and the organizations they reached, not for the content we need by interests and topics. Besides the monthly reports, is there other data we can get pursue?

Elise may have already developed a tool to gather relevant information from the reports that she can share.

Sorry that I could not be more helpful at this time.

B

Bethany Facendini, Community Engagement and Outreach Manager

Regarding the RDF, after our last meeting, we've done some internal discussions and clarified our scope a bit. With the new direction around focusing on identifying specific climate action projects, I wanted to quickly confirm that we are on the right track.

*	Instead of focusing on engaging as many individuals as possible from Communities of Concerns, we will focus now on reaching organizations who are actively working on climate action projects that would benefit from the County's support or would help inform the Regional CAP and other future climate policies. These organizations will continue to be within and uplift Communities of Concern.
*	We will also highlight and focus on reaching local council offices and policy makers who are actively working on or identifying capital improvement projects that may benefit from the RDF as a reference or that may become part of future CAPs.
*	We are communicating that the RDF is a guide for implementing climate action throughout the region and can be used to inform climate policies on local and regional levels. While the County cannot lead the projects themselves, the County may be able to help provide resources in the form of grants, the RDF guidebook, etc.
*	After speaking with the Water Equity Team, we are incorporating water questions into our community gatherings and surveys.

Going forward, we do have a few followup questions as well!

*	When will the Convenings be? After speaking with the Water Equity team, it sounds like they will be in November afterall. Can we schedule a meeting ASAP to discuss programming, roles, and next steps? We are running out of time to book places and we should start promoting those soon for effective turnout.
*	If we are to focus on gathering feedback from organizations about specific projects, do you still need demographic data? If so, do you want that data coupled in a full survey like it currently is, or should we create a smaller demographic data only survey that accompanies the feedback that we receive in other ways (discussion, posters, notes, testimonies, etc.)
*	What do your project portfolios look like? How can we best compile project information to match and add to your existing portfolios?

Thank you!! I super appreciate your time and collaboration on this!

In Gratitude,

ali
