body:
Good Afternoon APG Members,

September 13th and 27th reports are in two segments below:

*September 27th Meeting (Eileen):*

Due to a communication error I was not given complete instructions to
attend the Sept. SANDAG board meeting remotely and be promoted to a
separate screen.

It was difficult to hear the conversations and I was unable to
participate. I am attaching the agenda for your review.

On a different subject… As Robin has let you know, Congressman Issa held a
meeting with the mayors of most of the cities, along with SANDAG’s new CEO,
to discuss their transportation and other needs.  Unfortunately the APGs
which represents ALL of the County’s unincorporated residents was not
included.

When Robin notified the Congressman’s staff, we were given the impression
that this would be rectified and another meeting would be scheduled with us.

Instead, we have been invited to a mixer/open house for their new offices
in Santee “for invited guest” with no plans to sit down for a discussion.

This is a concern on many levels.

Attached please find the emails that Robin and I have both sent.  (Included
at end of this email.)

We’ll let you know if/when we have any updates.

*September 13th Meeting (Robin):*

*SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:*
Mario Orso confirmed he had received the request from the APG to attend a
joint meeting between Congressman Darrell Issa, APG members and himself.
Hannah Stern of SANDAG will coordinate with the APG and Congressman Issa to
ensure attendance at a future meeting.

Background: The Congressional Representative (Darrell Issa), who's district
encompasses the vast majority of the unincorporated area, held a meeting
during his open house in Escondido. In a private meeting before the event
Congressman Issa had invited SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso and staff to discuss
transportation and funding. The Congressman had included Mayors from his
district. There was no County representation nor unincorporated area
through the APG.
This oversight was immediately brought to the attention of the Congressman
and his office staff by the APG. The APG sent a letter to the Congressman
and copied Mario Orso. See complete letter at end of this email.

*SR 125 Investigation Summary:*
"The investigation found ETAN's Fastlane financial reporting cannot be
relied upon, and the Finance department lacks adequate internal controls,
including proper review and supervision, to ensure SR 125 financial
information is accurately recorded and reported. The report recommends an
independent assessment of the Finance department's policies, procedures,
and practices."

*Office of the Independent Auditor - FY 2024 Annual Investigations Report:*
The Independent Performance Auditor, Courtney Ruby, made a defining
statement of the state of SANDAG's contracts invoicing and payment process;
- The system is broken. -
"Most concerning is the finding that invoices totaling $13055,123 or 32.39%
of the sample size, did not include sufficient documentation to determine
what work was completed by contractors."
This report included 7 recommendations by the auditor.

APG Comment to Board: Thank you for the great report. I have done accounts
payable in the past. With a more than 32% failure to follow the process for
accounts payable, I am going to assume there is some overpayment of
taxpayer dollars. And then, recommendations 1 through 7 - I did not see a
plan for recovery or potential recovery of taxpayer dollars. Is there
overpayment out there and how we would know if documentation was not done
correctly? Is there a plan for this? Thank you. (2:10:30)

SANDAG response (Courtney Ruby): When we evaluated the invoice payments.
This would be with the project managers and contracting whether the
information was there. Then it was passed on for payment. So we're seeing
insufficient documentation and it's being passed on for payment. We would
have to drill down further in relation to determine was the work done or
not done. This procedure did not go to evaluating whether everything going
back to project managers that would have been a different audit. A
different audit, this was looking to see based on their procedures. Are
they following their procedures? Is the documentation there? So, in order
to quantify that, that would take, that would be a different audit.

*Public Comment:*
Paul The Bold, comment to the Board: Does SANDAG really work for the whole
county? You've got Robin Joy Maxson sitting over there. Theoretically,
we're sending half the county, yet she doesn't have a vote. Since SANDAG is
in the tax business. This is really taxation without representation...
(2:26:24)

*Questions from APG members:*

*Question* - Is SANDAG informed of freeway projects in the County? Or, are
freeway projects strictly a state affair? Does SANDAG have a role in the
scheduling and decision making?
*Response from Roy Abboud, Caltrans: *The answer is it depends. General
maintenance projects led by Caltrans are managed and scheduled by Caltans.
Projects led by SANDAG, e.g. managed lane conversions, are scheduled by
SANDAG. Caltrans gives updates to the SANDAG Board on the work they are
doing in the County regardless of the lead agency.

*Resources for APG members:*

Link to the Traffic Safety Dashboard https://www.sandag.org/trafficsafety.
It is located in SANDAG’s Open Data Portal.

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Eileen Delaney, Representative Alternate to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

**************************************************************************************
(Response to Congressman Issa - Escondidio Open House)

*Complete Letter:*
August 3, 2024

Good Afternoon Congressman Issa,

The Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County (APG) was formed to
provide unincorporated representation on the SANDAG Board of Directors. The
APG represents over 513,00 unincorporated area residents residing in the
48th District - we are the second largest population in the County of San
Diego and comprise the majority of the constituents in your district.

At Friday's Escondido District Office Open House event there was a closed
meeting with SANDAG CEO Mario Orso, several mayors and yourself discussing
the issue of transportation in your district. There was no representation
from the unincorporated community on the regional issues of
transportation funding and projects. As are the mayors, we are also elected
by our communities to represent them. As such, we need to be included in
all future discussions and planning sessions. Regional Transportation Plans
are a very important subject for the thousands of residents in the area we
represent. It's important that our voices are heard. Moving forward, to
correct the history of incomplete transportation projects and diverted
funding from the traditionally underserved and underrepresented people of
the 48th District, the APG must be part of any regional planning
discussions.

Since there was a meeting with Mario Orso and city mayors - the  APG
requests an equal opportunity to meet for our elected unincorporated
community representatives.

The APG looks forward to meeting in-person with you, Mario Orso, and the
Association of Planning Group members before the end of summer. Please have
your office reach out for available meeting dates and attendee information.

Respectfully,
Robin Joy Maxson
Chair, Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
Board Member, SANDAG Board of Directors
760-705-7435

Eileen Delaney
Vice-Chair, Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
Board Member (Alternate), SANDAG Board of Directors

"The 48th District encompasses the central and eastern parts of San Diego
County and a portion of Riverside County, including the communities of
Fallbrook, Bonsall, Valley Center, Ramona, Escondido, Santee, Poway,
Lakeside, Alpine, Temecula, Murrieta and the mountain and desert areas of
the San Diego-Imperial County line."

*************************************************************************************************
(Response to Congressman Issa - East County Leadership Open House)
September 28, 2024

Hello,

Thank you for the invitation. I am sorry that I won't be able to attend on
behalf of the Association of Planning Groups. I believe our Chair, Robin
Joy Maxson will be there.

As you may be aware, members of the  Association of Planning Groups - San
Diego County are representatives from every Community Planning Group
throughout the unincorporated areas in the County of San Diego. Planning
Group members are elected by the Citizens of each planning area. We
represent nearly 600,000 residents..

I hope we have the opportunity to meet with the Congressman on another
occasion and sit down to discuss the transportation and other needs of
these 600,000 residents. (many of whom are also constituents of the
Congressman:)

Thank you!

Regards,

Eileen Delaney, Chair
Fallbrook Planning Group
Fallbrook Design Review Board
Vice Chair- Assoc. of Planning Groups, SD County

body:
Good Evening APG Members,

Please note our next APG meeting will be in-person on Saturday, January
4th, 2025, from 10:00am to noon at the Lakeside Library.

*APG Announcement to SANDAG Board on Oct. 25th:*
We have good news. The second wildfire and emergency evacuation tour was
held last Friday for SR-94. Organizing the tour were SANDAG's Ariana Galvan
and Jamul-Dulzura Community Planning Group member, Paul Dombkowski. In
addition to several members from the Planning Group and SANDAG there were
participants from Caltrans, San Diego County Sheriff's office, and CalFire,
including Battalion Chief, Sam Friedman. The unincorporated communities
value the partnership and collaboration these tours create as we work
toward a safer travel experience for all. Thank you.

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report on Oct. 11th:*
-Mario Orso said that they were cooperating with the Independent Auditor
and working to build openness and trust.
-Regarding taking the 125 out of the Regional Plan as a toll road - would
we be in compliance with CARB (California Air Resources Board). We would
barely be meeting our GHG emissions and VMT measure.
-Otay Mesa East has 65% of the design completed.

APG comment to Board: Mario, this is October, wildfire season in the rural
areas. What have we done to alleviate the bottleneck issues with the
highways that are used for evacuation heading west? There are bottlenecks
that have been there forever and we've highlighted those as being potential
fatal zones for evacuees. Where are we with resolving bottleneck issues
with lanes that are one lane, two, three, that are continuing to change as
people evacuate west? Thank you. (32:00/ Oct. 11)

SANDAG reponse (Mario Orso): What route did you mention?

APG response: This would be specifically 67, but there are bottlenecks on
other evacuation routes.

SANDAG response (Mario Orso): Everett, do you want to help me on what's the
emergency evacuation plan from Caltrans?

Caltrans response (Everett Townsend): Yeah, so Caltrans has been working
with emergency responders, CalFire, CHP and others to reassess on an annual
basis, is what we do to reassess our highway system. And, to identify where
additional improvements may be made. Over the last few years, Caltrans has
completed projects there that create some widening and create opportunities
to improve traffic flow through there. Most of those issues that state
route 67 project is at some point will be presented here at the Board, but
you know, just to be informed that Caltrans is well aware of the concerns
of the communities in Ramona and further east. As well as CHP and CalFire.
And, we certainly have a plan to address any issues that may come up during
this time.

*State Route 125 Toll Removal Oct. 11th and 25th:*
Oct. 11th, Mario Orso, reported that a pre-environmental analysis and an
equity analysis need to be performed and these two actions will take one
year.

Vivian Moreno, City of San Diego comment: I continue to be extremely
disappointed with how SANDAG is handling the 125. We're the only community
(South Bay Area) that gets tripled taxed on this toll. We pay taxes every
single year. We pay the toll and we pay Transnet funding. We're the only
community that does this. This seems to me like we are slow walking this
issue.... How much longer do we have to wait? 2042?

Oct. 25th Courtney Ruby, SANDAG Independent Performance Auditor, reported
that the Executive Management Team which included former CEO, Hasan
Ikhrata; were aware of and actively working to resolve major issues with
the 125 Tolling System, yet failed to notify the Board of this until
October of 2023. Fully 18 months passed before the Board was informed of
these significant issues impacting residents of the South Bay Region. A
single-source contract was presented and approved by the Board in January
of 2024 based on the Boards belief that they could rely on the
recommendations of Executive Management. As it turned out this contract
between SANDAG and Deloitte to manage the 125 Toll Road systems was
deficient and absent an exchange of basic system requirements.

Ed Musgrove, City of San Marcos comment: We were lied to by the Executive
Team. Until the names of those in charge are revealed I have no confidence.

*Wildfire Evacuation Tour SR-94:*
On Friday, October 18th members of SANDAG, Caltrans and the Janual
Community Planning Group completed an evacuation tour. Please see Paul
Dombkowski's report sent in a previous email on October 23rd.

*News:*
At the October 11th and 25th SANDAG Board meetings we had zero voting
representation from anyone living in the Unincorporated Area. Only Nora
Vargas was present to vote on behalf of the County. Chair Vargas lives in
Chula Vista according to her profile.

*No questions received this month.*

body:
Good Morning APG Members,

Our next APG meeting will be in-person on Saturday, January 4th, 2025, from
10:00am to noon at the Lakeside Library. As always, if you cannot attend,
please send another member from your Group.

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that LAFCO would be conducting a review of SANDAG as a
Metropolitan Planning Organization for the fiscal years 2024-2025.
-Everett Townsend, current Caltrans Rep at SANDAG, announced that Ann Fox
would be returning as the new District 11 Director. She will be the
Caltrans Representative at the SANDAG Board of Directors.

*Border Environmental Task Force Report:*
This is a new task force forming to address regional issues in the
geographical zone of the Pacific Ocean to the Arizona border and 10 miles
both south and north of the border with Mexico. "The Task force will be
comprised of representation from federal, state and local jurisdictions
within the border region and sector advisors with interests involved in
climate adaptation, environmental health, and environmental justice issues.
SANDAG may solicit interest from other entities in participating in the
Task force based on project needs. Taskforce member agencies are asked to
designate an alternate representative when the primary representative is
unable to attend to promote participation in meetings." The task force will
be one location for all work occurring in this area. Identification of gaps
in serving the area and binational coordination will be strengthened. The
meetings will be held remotely (virtually) and the APG has requested
membership on this new task force. For any Community Planning/Sponsor
Groups in this area who wish to be on the task force, please contact
kim.smith@sandag.org

*Otay Mesa East and SR 11 Report:*
More material will be transported to the US side of the port in order to
match the elevation of the facility/road on the Mexican side. There is a
plan to open SR 11 to local traffic in the near future. The flow of
revenues from the completed project are delineated in this attachment:
https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/2988061/Item_11__Att._1_-_Memorandum_from_PFM__SANDAG_Financial_Advisor.pdf

Jack Fisher, City of Imperial Beach comment: The third largest port in the
world -70 miles south of Ensenada is being constructed. Traffic coming
through commercial ports of entry will increase. We need part of the toll
to fix problems. We need to fix this now for our kids' future. The Border
Region needs to fix the problem.

*Transnet Major Corridors Update for North Coast Corridor and SR 78
Corridor:*
Victor Mercado, Caltrans - reported $1.06 billion from Federal, State and
Transnet funds for the region broken into highway improvements, rail
improvements and lagoon, bike, pedestrian improvements. This money funds
active transportation improvements for the north coast corridor.

APG comment to Board: Good morning. I won't be as polished as I'd hoped to
be. Being in the rural area and seeing these wonderful coastal projects, 78
really does need help at both ends. There's a big need there. But when I
see additional bike trails, pedestrian trails; this is a very bedecked out
plan and it's beautiful and it's wonderful, but if we're going to truly be
regional in how we reach out and spend the tax dollars; we're leaving the
unincorporated area in the dirt: literally. It's geographically isolated,
car dependent - it continues to be. You cannot walk anywhere, especially on
anything other than dirt or on the side of a highway. And, this has been
the situation for so long and I would like to see this regional agency
truly think about, okay, we have some healthy transportation alternatives
in parts of the region, but in the other regions there are none. I mean
there's nothing. I cannot walk to my neighbor's house. I must drive. And,
this has been the situation for years and Transnet is paid by everyone
since 1988. What is the percentage that has been spent by the folks in the
unincorporated region? Is that funding amount broken out anywhere? Is that
even available? And, if you were to break it out by population, maybe it
would be that we have received our fair share of the money. But maybe not.
There's a lack of information and it's important that it be transparent, so
that people know, gee, you know, this is really wonderful. Let's keep
improving the north coast there and give them more because the people out
in the unincorporated area have already gotten their share. That would go a
long way to developing trust and transparency. But, we don't know that.
That's an unknown piece of information. And, so, I'm a glass half-full
person and I love seeing these projects. And, I have my mountain bike and I
love to walk. But I have to put everything in my car and go find a park to
go do this. There is not a kid in the neighborhood who can hop on their
bike or walk. That's the life of being out in a rural area. The Youth
Opportunity Pass, wonderful program. Nobody can use it. You know very few
unincorporated communities have that advantage. We're going to have
microtransit. Another great option. Can't use it. So, you know, I want to
be here and to be excited and to rah-rah because these are great programs,
but we need to spread it out a bit more. To share these programs, make this
happen, not just talk about it, but actually have some real programs in
place that operate for people that are outside of the coastal and I-5 and
I-15 corridors. We need to really move this to the unincorporated area too
and include our neighbors. Thank you.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: ...So, I'm a big biker. My
e-bike and I get along really well. And I use it nearly everyday to get to
the UCSD campus from Del Mar. And, I take it to Trader Joe's, which is out
SR 56 on that new bike trail. And, I go north to Solana Beach and beyond.
Because the trails underneath San Elijo Lagoon are just absolutely - under
the highway there are fantastic.....And, I will bring one last - the SR 56
bike trail.  There's a new little piece that's just been put in right at
the old Carmel Valley Road connecting in....But I'll point out that
Sorrento Valley Road is a big part of that bike path. It has the biggest
potholes. It's pretty awful. And I don't know who's maintaining it, but
it's certainly not being attended to.  So I hope that as this new piece is
finished, perhaps Sorrento Valley Road can be improved as well.

John Minto, City of Santee comment: Thank you for the opportunity to speak.
I wasn't going to speak on this at all, but I'm listening to a lot of stuff
and you know what? All these projects are great. If you live in east county
everyone's going to say, no, we need to come out to east county and do ours
first. If you live in north county you say, oh no, don't come up to east
county - come up to north county. And, vice versa. All the way around the
city. Bottom line, all extremely important to get done. And, get it done
before sooner than later. I do have to be a little bit flippant, and I
apologize ahead of time. Maybe not. About the bicycle lane thing. You know,
you talk um, Terry you know you talked about avid bicycling and e-bike and
if you know - with the exception of east county at the 52 there is only one
protected bicycle lane in all of east county. And, that's so you can make
sure to get out of east county. Why they did that? I do not know. And, that
goes into Tierra Santa. I average about 30, 40 sometimes 50 miles on my
bike, e-bike. And I go through La Mesa, San Diego, Lemon Grove. All the way
out to Spring Valley, Dehesa. All the way into Alpine. And you know what? I
still haven't seen any protected bike lanes. The only protection I get is
when I say my prayer before I get on the bike and say, please don't let a
car hit me because they are only a few feet away. Because even where there
is a bicycle lane, most of the time they kind of faked a bicycle lane
because there wasn't enough room. So where you normally have, I think it's
an average four foot bicycle lane, I think we're lucky to get a two foot
bicycle lane and many of those are along the seams of the roadway. And just
talking to Mayor Jones and you know what? When cities do their slurries or
road repairs. They go up to the bike lane and stop. So there's always
potholes and there's always breaks along the seams and things of that
nature. So nobody really cares in east county if you have a good bike lane.
That's just my opinion. And, it goes back to what Robin said earlier about
maybe if we're going to talk about equity, equity should be looking at
safety more than anything else. Because I don't care who you are and you're
riding on a bike lane or a lack of bike lane in those areas; you know what?
Where's the equity and safety? And maybe a new term we ought to bring up in
safety is not just VMT, but EBMT, electric bike miles traveled. And how
safe are you on those EBMT's? That's all I have to say.

*Chief Executive Officer Performance Evaluation Process:*
On December 6th and 13th all SANDAG Board members are invited to
participate in developing performance goals for the CEO position.

*APG News:*
Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the unincorporated
area in San Diego County - has not set a meeting date with the APG as of
this report. Since July, the APG has been working to set up a joint meeting
with the Congressman, SANDAG CEO Mario Orso and our APG members without
success. SANDAG CEO Mario Orso has stated he will be available and happy to
attend our joint meeting. Congressman Issa has not been available and very
little communication has come from his office. The APG sent a request to
his Chief of Staff, Veronica Smith Wong. She has responded, but not with a
set date, yet.
The subject of the meeting will be:
"Transportation funding and safety in the Unincorporated Area; addressing
fatality rate on rural highways, safe wildfire evacuation, lack of public
transportation resulting in geographic isolation of vulnerable populations
and continued diversion of transportation funds from rural highway
projects."

Planning/Sponsor Groups that wish to support the establishment of this
joint meeting with Congressman Issa may also communicate directly with
Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.house.gov

*Questions from APG members*
*No questions received this month.*

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

body:
Good Afternoon APG Members,

Please note that SANDAG will not hold Board meetings in August.

*San Diego Regional Tribal Summit:*
This month SANDAG held their June 14th Board meeting offsite at the Pala
Casino. This was a "Tribal Summit" hosted by the Southern California Tribal
Chairmen's Association and focusing on issues and concerns specifically
related to the tribal residents and SANDAG's role. Takeaways from the
Tribal Summit:

-As Tribal land is located in the rural areas of the County these residents
face many of the same funding and planning challenges from SANDAG as their
non-Tribal. unincorporated area neighbors.

-Bo Mazzetti, Tribal Chairman of the Rincon Band of Luiseno Indians, gave
an impassioned commentary regarding the ongoing lack of attention and
funding from SANDAG to the needs of Tribal residents. Specifically, he
talked about the unreasonable amount of time that has passed with no
appreciable improvement to roadways and other projects. Mr. Mazzetti was
frustrated by SANDAG's procrastination.

-Samual Sanford, Senior Regional Planner SANDAG, presented traffic
statistics that are available to the public through a Traffic Safety
Dashboard. The dashboard contains information related to number of
accidents, severity, etc. If any APG member has the link to this dashboard,
please share with the group. I will reach out to Sam for the link, too.

- To the APG - As an idea, what do we think about holding an
"Unincorporated Area Summit?" This would provide unincorporated area
leaders and residents an opportunity to speak with SANDAG on issues
impacting the unincorporated area.

*SANDAG's New CEO, Mario Orso:*
Mario Orso began work on June 17th. He delivered his first report as CEO at
the June 28th Board meeting. In this report he specifically made note of
the needs of the unincorporated area. He noted that there is a wildfire
evacuation tour planned for SR67 and SR78 and that he would be asking
Caltrans to provide an update on the environmental document for the San
Vicente CMCP (Lakeside to Ramona). Mr. Orso commented that he heard there
wasn't a lot of progress being made. To ensure that a project is moving
along he will request an update on the San Vicente CMCP is added to the
Transportation Committee and the Board agendas.

APG comment to Board: That is good to hear. We have had interest from other
unincorporated areas on having a wildfire evacuation tour, too. This is one
of the corridors, but there are other corridors at risk.

SANDAG reponse (Mario Orso): This is very similar to the LOSSAN Project. We
need to be engaging with the community. That is part of the organization of
excellence and procedure and hearing from the community, taking those
tours, will allow the lead agency Caltrans to implement or consider in
their alternatives or studies, all the appropriate emergency exits and
anything needed to meet the project goals.

*SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:*
APG comment to Board: Regarding the Youth Opportunity Pass. This is a
valuable program. We need data on rider's start point by zip code.
Currently, to utilize this program and to reduce the transit time to a
reasonable length, we must drive our children down to a transportation hub.
Otherwise, the travel time on the bus or other transit options is not
useful.  The more youth who can be protected from accident exposure through
a public transit option is a responsible return on investment for SANDAG.

Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista comment: We will be pursuing these
same benefits for senior citizens with their low incomes and pensions. They
should have these free passes too, in order to get to their destinations.

Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: We need to get a cost per rider
for this program. It is a very popular program that seems to be well
utilized.

Jack Shu, City of La Mesa comment: We heard some great testimony from NCTD
and their micro transit system. On demand systems in which if we can work
with those concepts and ideas in the pilot programs that SANDAG is working
with we can advance our thinking of how transportation can be. Serve rural
areas, serve Robin's concerns in terms of getting kids connected to transit
centers so they don't have to rely on cars in the future.

*Outreach Efforts For Community Feedback On Projects:*
Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: SANDAG reports it is going to
include a survey in order to improve outreach. I'm not sure who decided we
should do a survey and who is going to participate because I believe it
would be very important to have all county feedback, so that we can all
have our unique needs be a part of the plan. I feel like our more rural
areas where they honestly have some more of the greater need, I'm pointing
over to you Robin, but I mean you got a lot of places where they can't even
get out in a safe manner to actually evacuate in a fire or something like
that. So I want to make sure we are getting feedback from all parts of the
county; including our seniors.

SANDAG response (Antoinette Meier): We intend to reach everyone in the
County who needs specialized transportation services.

*Questions from APG members:*

*Question* - Does SANDAG's jurisdiction include the far eastern
unincorporated communities?
*Response* (source SANDAG) - Yes, SANDAG has oversight of the San Diego
region located in the southwestern corner of the United States and is
bordered by Mexico, the Pacific Ocean, Camp Pendleton, Orange and Riverside
Counties, and Imperial County. Our region encompasses more than 4,260
square miles and includes 18 incorporated cities, 17 federally-recognized
tribal governments, and incorporated and unincorporated San Diego County.

*News:* The Borrego Springs Community Sponsor Group voted on June 5th to
accept the APG's invitation to join as an Associate (non-voting) member. We
will formally vote to accept their membership at our next APG meeting
currently scheduled for Saturday, January 4th, 2025. Borrego Springs reps
will be Jim Dax and alternate Becky Falk. Welcome!

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Report Submitted by:

body:
Good Morning APG Members,

*Note:* At the July 26, 2024 SANDAG Board of Directors meeting there was no
(zero) County representation. This means we had no one representing the
Unincorporated Area with the power to vote. Nora Vargas was absent. Joel
Anderson was absent. The County Board of Supervisors has two alternates:
Terra Lawson-Remer and Monica Montgomery Steppe. Neither were present. When
a vote was taken to consider borrowing $20 million of future Transnet funds
for the "Transnet Regional Bike Early Action Program" there was no one from
the County to vote. We had an empty seat.

*SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:*
Mario Orso reported that SANDAG would continue to provide updates to the
Board and stakeholders on the priority corridors of SR 78 and SR 67. He did
not include SRs 76, 79 or 94 in this priority list. The Transnet
Independent Taxpayer Oversight Committee is seeking community members for
their Board. Information located at their website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/transnet-independent-taxpayer-oversight
SANDAG will not hold Board of Director meetings in August, but staff and
working groups will continue with work.

APG comment to Board: This month we held the first Evacuation Tour with
SANDAG and Caltrans staff. The potential evacuation routes in the Ramona
area were thoroughly explored and wildfire hazards such as chimney fire
burn zones were identified for the group by our local fire behavior expert,
Dan Summers. The next Evacuation Tour will explore the SR 94 corridor from
Campo to Jamul; including the dangerous intersection of Otay Lakes and
Honey Springs Road. The Unincorporated Community values these opportunities
to partner with SANDAG and Caltrans to share vital boots-on-the-ground
knowledge in order to develop safe evacuation routes for all travelers in
the region. Thank you.

*California Transportation Commission (CTC):*
Two CTC Commissioners introduced themselves and reported that they are "the
money people" for State and Federal transportation funds. Commissioners
Clarissa Reyes Falcon and Lee Ann Eager invited Board members to attend an
upcoming meeting being held in San Diego from August 15-16. Website for
information:
https://catc.ca.gov/meetings-events/commission-meetings-2024

*Transnet Oversight Annual Report and Performance Audit and Budget:*
The overall feedback from the Board to those presenting on Transnet funds
and projects was that there was a clear lack of information and
accountability is needed. Cost Benefit Analysis was missing. Staff reported
miniscule use of the public transportation options and utilization of
biking or walking - Return On Investment is dismal. SANDAG often quotes the
maxim that limited funds should be used to help the most people.
Historically, the Transnet funds are benefitting very few. As of FY 2023,
total bikeway Program funding was $397.3 million. Transnet funds
represented $187.2 million (47%) of this spending. The promise of the
Transnet funds to improve public safety through corridor projects is not
being met. SANDAG staff's explanation was that the voters had an
expectation and the funding sources for these projects (of which Transnet
funds are only one part/source) come with stipulations that are often in
conflict with what the voters expected. This is the difficult environment
in which planning and funding for projects exists.

Melanie Burkholder, City of Carlsbad comment: We need cost benefit analysis
for these Transnet dollar projects.

Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO comment: We are working toward structural change in
order to provide cost benefit analysis and demonstrate a good use of the
funds

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach comment: I know that many people leave
my city to move east because it is more affordable. This puts more people
on those roads and they need to be improved.

APG Comment to Board: What are the raw numbers for this conclusion that
bike ridership has increased 5x? Does this conclusion represent a change
from 50 to 500 riders, 50 to 5,000? We need to see the numbers. And, do you
see a slower increase in pedestrian travel than expected due to e-bike
encounters on pathways?

SANDAG response (Omar Atayee): Those are great questions. We don't have
those numbers, but will get those to the Board. We don't know if e-bikes
are impacting our numbers, but we are seeing an increase. I don't know if
we have data on that.

Dawn Vettes, SANDAG CFO comment: We acknowledge room for improvement and
are working to strengthen internal controls. Our next audit in 2027 will
show significant progress.

*SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:*
In response to a previous Board question about the cost per ride of those
utilizing the Youth Opportunity Pass, Mario Orso reported .69 cents was the
average cost.

*Questions from APG members:*

*Question* - Is SANDAG informed of freeway projects in the County? Or, are
freeway projects strictly a state affair? Does SANDAG have a role in the
scheduling and decision making?
*Response* - I am still working on this answer.....

*News:* Link to the Traffic Safety Dashboard
https://www.sandag.org/trafficsafety. It is located in SANDAG’s Open Data
Portal.

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

body:
Good Afternoon APG Members,

Note: The SANDAG Board of Directors held three meetings in the month of
January.

*SANDAG Leadership Changes - New Officers Elected:*
New Chair for SANDAG BOD: Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach
New Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: Joe Lacava, City of San Diego
New Second Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: John Minto, City of Santee

Jan. 10th - APG comment to Board: Good morning. Congratulations on your
election as the dream team for the officers. I do represent the
unincorporated area, over 500,000 people, and, of course, this seat is not
a voting seat. Today I want to note for the record that the County is not
present and so, therefore; all action taken by this Board today - voting
action - has effectively disenfranchised the Unincorporated Area. We're not
present. And, we don't have a vote. And, I hope in 2025, I expect in 2025,
that this Board will overall do a better job of ensuring that the
Unincorporated Area is not disenfranchised. I realize County being absent
is not the fault of the Board, but there must be something in place that
takes into account that there's over half a million people who are not
participating in the proceedings today. Thank you.

Jan. 31st - APG Comment to the Board: The County of San Diego is not
present. However, the people of the County of San Diego are present.
(Note: County was completely absent for all of the January 2025 BOD
meetings - 10th & 24th & 31st)

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that the CFO was adjusting revenue projections on
TransNet funds by a couple of percentage points - between 2 to 4%. This
would be a decrease in expected funding and could affect both MTS and NCTD.
-The Grand Jury report findings and recommendations came as no surprise as
the Office of the Independent Performance Auditor had brought these needed
issues and changes to the Board in their earlier report and they are being
addressed.

*Otay Mesa East and SR 11 Report:*
The Federal agreements with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and with
General Services have set the stage for the beginning of construction and
the relationship SANDAG will have with CBP. Caltrans is also a partner.
If the toll revenues of the Port of Entry are not as projected the
shortfall cannot be made up with TransNet funds.

Ann Fox, Caltrans comment: ...We've done the studies that have shown the
many dollars and jobs lost and the air pollution created by the long delays
along our shared borders. California has invested more than half of the
$1.3 billion project cost and has spent hundreds of millions more building
out the corridor and the connections we have with State Routes 905 and 125.
...We have built the infrastructure, the new roads, the utilities, the
technology, the air quality monitors out there, in addition to over 180
acres of environmental mitigation.

Jack Fisher, City of Imperial Beach comment: (reading Brian Bilbray letter)
"... I'm sure some other members will not continue to support the expansion
of the economic growth with the environmental damage without addressing
historical and future environmental and public health threats caused by
such economic development. I ask that every board member here question if
their city council or county board would vote for any project knowing its
environmental and health problems if it was going to be anywhere close to
the disastrous situation that citizens of the South Bay faced everyday?"
I can't tell you how frustrated I am because I know with the increased
traffic and commerce Mexico will continue to grow. Their population will
continue to grow. It was mentioned that just this operation port of entry
opening will create 90,000 jobs on the U.S. side. I would imagine that
number probably doubles or triples on the Mexico side. Still without the
infrastructure.

*TransNet Major Corridor Projects Update: State Route 67:*
Sam Amen, Karina Cantera-Angel & Tracy D'Aoust Roberts of Caltrans -
presented 3 alternatives for the improvement of SR 67 understanding that
evacuation was the highest consideration. Project area is SR 67 from
Highland Valley in Ramona to Mapleview in Lakeside. Alternative #1 provides
4 outbound lanes and one inbound lane dedicated to inbound emergency
vehicles. Alternatives #2 & #3 provide some of these benefits, but not
consistently throughout the project area and include the use of shoulders
as "lanes" in an emergency.

APG comment to Board: The Unincorporated Area has been partnering with
Caltrans and we thank Sam, Karina, Tracy, Melina, Stephen and Tyler for
their dedication. Safety is always first.  Caltrans states, "The primary
goal of the SR 67 Highway Improvements Project is to increase capacity
during emergencies to significantly reduce evacuation times."  Safety is
always first. SANDAG serves over 3.3 million people across the region;
however, some benefit more than others. Had SANDAG delivered on the
promises of TransNet to the Unincorporated Area - Measure G would have
passed. The experience of those patiently awaiting their turn at the
Regional funding bucket has been disheartening. 1988 and 2004 turned into a
resounding "no" in 2024 for rural communities on Measure G. The LA fires
demonstrate a clear and present danger to rural highway travelers -
evacuees may live locally or may be visiting from the city. Caltrans has
stood ready and willing to deliver highway safety. Alternative #1 delivers
on the Promise. Let us immediately put into place emergency widening to
move evacuees through the current SR 67 gauntlet of bottlenecks. Safety is
always first. SANDAG does not want to be the obstacle to improvements
necessary to avoid the catastrophic results of the LA fires. The elected
Board members would not want the public to rightfully be able to say that
they could have done more to prevent a loss of life and property. Thank you.

Steve Vaus, City of Poway; Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista; Rebecca
Jones, City of San Marcos; Kevin Shin, City of Carlsbad; Bill Wells, City
of El Cajon; John Minto, City of Santee;  & Terry Gaasterland, City of Del
Mar all made comments: All of these city representatives were positive in
their comments emphasizing the need to expand SR 67 for evacuation purposes
and Mayors Minto, Jones, Wells and Gaasterland specifically endorsed the
selection of Alternative #1. There were no comments opposing Caltrans
proposed solutions to SR 67. The Board of Directors was supportive.

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach & SANDAG Chair comment:  "What can we do
now?"

Allan Kosup, Caltrans response: We have an emergency widening project that
just began this week on SR 67. The environmental report was received last
week and the project was begun immediately. It will be over the next six
months. This will provide more space in the event of an evacuation.

*APG News:*
-Thank you to all who were able to attend our in-person APG meeting held on
Saturday, January 4th, 2025. A quorum was established and voting actions
were taken.

*APG Officers elected for 2025 (one year terms):*
Chair, Robin Joy Maxson
Vice Chair, Eileen Delaney
Secretary, Carol Hake

*APG Representative to SANDAG Board of Directors (two year terms):*
Primary Representative, Robin Joy Maxson
Alternate Representative, Eileen Delaney

*APG Representatives to SANDAG Policy Advisory Committees:*

Regional Planning Committee:
APG Representative: Ron Nehring
APG Alternate: Kiki Skagen Munshi

Transportation Committee:
APG Representative: Jim Custeau
APG Alternate: Paul Dombkowski

Borders Committee:
APG Representative: Lynne Malinowski
APG Alternate: Harriet Taylor

Public Safety Committee:
APG Representative: Paul Dombkowski
APG Alternate: Eileen Delaney

Audit Committee:
APG Representative: Carol Hake

-Update: Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the
unincorporated area in San Diego County - has not set a meeting date with
the APG as of this report. Since July, the APG has been working to set up a
joint meeting with the Congressman, SANDAG CEO Mario Orso and our APG
members without success. SANDAG CEO Mario Orso has stated he will be
available and happy to attend our joint meeting. Congressman Issa has not
been available and very little communication has come from his office. The
APG sent a request to his Chief of Staff, Veronica Smith Wong. She has
responded, but not with a set date, yet.

The subject of the meeting will be:
"Transportation funding and safety in the Unincorporated Area; addressing
fatality rate on rural highways, safe wildfire evacuation, lack of public
transportation resulting in geographic isolation of vulnerable populations
and continued diversion of transportation funds from rural highway
projects."

Several Planning/Sponsor Groups have already sent letters to Congressman
Issa. If any group wishes to contact Issa directly, email his Chief of
Staff Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.house.gov

*Questions from APG members*
No questions received this month.

*Links*
SANDAG BOD and PAC meetings for calendar 2025:
https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3108009/Item_3_-_Revised_2025_Legislative_Calendar.pdf

body:
Good Afternoon APG Members,

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that the California Air Resources Board (CARB)
accepted SANDAG's methodology for measuring GHG and, therefore, SANDAG can
continue with planning.
-A joint committee meeting between Borders, Regional Plan and
Transportations committees to present the Regional Plan. On track to meet
GHG and air quality conformity targets. This keeps funds flowing to SANDAG,
the region and the city.
-Congratulated North County Transit District for 30 years of service.

*Economic and Budget Outlook:*
Job growth is slowing. Sales tax revenue is down. Source of project funds:
State 37%, Federal 36%, TransNet 16%, Other Local Funds 11%.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: ...."We are in turbulent
times....And, I would really encourage us to be incredibly careful and
conservative as we go forward into the next six months of our budgeting..."

APG Comment to Board: My question is on the job gains and losses forecast.
I have two questions. What consideration was given to the impacts of AI on
the professional, technology, transportation and housing sectors? And, my
second question is do you anticipate a reduction in healthcare sector jobs
as restrictions on our immigration policy take effect? And, the reason I
ask that is that over the last few years the State of California had opened
up Medi-Cal coverage for all who are financially eligible, regardless of
immigration status. In the County of San Diego one-third of the population
receives this coverage. So, that would be a substantial change in
healthcare.

Naomi Young, SANDAG: I think you mentioned all important factors that can
be a source of a drag on our economy and our job creation. We didn't do a
forecast on jobs, we just presented how 2024's data on unemployment has
ended. Well what we saw between 2023 and 2024, looking at where we've seen
the sector impacts and the job growth in 2024 is what makes us think that
2025 will be more of a slow job creation environment rather than a
rebound...the message is volatility, differences in local conditions from
the national and that there are some very strong potential headwinds that
give us cause for caution.

*SR-125 Toll Operations Update:*
SANDAG is actively supporting legislation to assist the implementation of
SANDAG Board Resolution 2023-11, "Declaring support of eliminating the debt
and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027."

*TransNet Regional Transportation Congestion Improvement Program Proposed
(RTCIP) Fee Adjustment:*
SANDAG approved this yearly fee adjustment to be 6% effective FY beginning
July 1, 2025. This 6% increase in RTCIP fees is to keep pace with the cost
of building the roadway infrastructure needed as housing increases. The fee
is collected by each of the 18 cities and the County as part of building
fees paid by the private sector for each new housing unit. Fee will
increase from $2875.06 to $3047.57, per unit.

*County Representation of Unincorporated Communities:*
-The February 14th SANDAG Board meeting was the fourth consecutive meeting
without a County Supervisor present.
-The February 28th meeting was the first time unincorporated communities
had SANDAG voting representation in 2025.
-SANDAG BOD commented as follows:

*-From the February 14th meeting:*
APG Comment to Board: Good morning. I had hoped by now that we would have
representation from the County here. And, I see empty chairs, so I won't
belabor that point. I have a suggestion. Is this Board able to propose an
action such as a censure because I have seen that done recently at a city
when the Board member is not fulfilling their obligations. Is that
something that could be considered on behalf of the over 500,000 people who
were not represented here by a vote today? Thank you.

Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: I can look into that. I know we have an
attendance policy where I know letters can be sent and they're encouraged
to attend and follow up. But, I'll look into specifically whether a censure
can be, I'm not sure it's specifically in our policy as it exists now, but
I will double check.

*-From the February 28th meeting:*
Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: I would like to, since the last
three meetings, I'm glad to see Supervisor Anderson here today. But the
last three meetings, the County had zero representation for over 500,000 in
the unincorporated areas. And, I would like to see if it's possible to move
forward with having that as a voting member, because a lot of our land use
decisions, and maybe it would be something at the planning level or the
regional planning and then only on land use decisions. I don't know what
that would look like. I'm just, I'm very concerned that there is a
possibility and it's happened now for three meetings. We didn't have any
actual action items, but it would be good to have someone that represents
them as a voting member. And, so I'd just like staff to move it.

Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: Yes, for the issue of them becoming a voting
member. That would require a change to legislation. So that is something
that could go to the Executive Committee. And, then ultimately to the
Board. But we need a sponsor to change that by legislation since the voting
members are set in our enabling legislation at the Public Utilities Code.

Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO: I also want to highlight that on the legislative
report. We reported that there was a hold bill, a place bill by Senator
Jones. And, actively being promoted by Supervisor Anderson. Of looking into
this issue.  (Mayor Rebecca Jones: "As a voting member?") We're having the
discussion. We haven't seen the total write up. But that's kind of what's
being indicated to us.

Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos: Yeah, that would definitely support
something like that. So maybe Supervisor Anderson, if we could maybe keep
the board members updated on that because I would certainly support
something like that. It is just a shame that we have a situation where some
land use things really do affect our unincorporated areas....Personally, I
think it would be very beneficial to our outlying communities.

Joel Anderson, County of San Diego comment: I just want to make a
clarification. I'm an alternate. And, my colleagues have all those
positions. So, over the last four and a half years I've made 99% of the
meetings. So, I'm sorry. They appointed themselves. They choose not to
come. That's not on me. But I try to fill in for them as often as possible.
And, we do have a bill. But it's not going to move forward until everyone
on this committee agrees that's what they want. There's not fanciness
going. But we're very lucky to have Robin here. She lives in the
unincorporated. I think that this Board should look and see whether the
County deserves to have a vote at all at SANDAG; because all we're doing is
doubling down on cities where all my colleagues live. And nobody, if I
wasn't on this board, would be representing with a vote from the
unincorporated. And, to your point, it's 600,000 people they are without a
vote. And while we have cities. They are much smaller. That have a vote.
And I think if we want to pass a bond. We need to think about being
inclusive. And, including everybody at the table. Thank you.

APG Comment to Board: Thank you. To follow up on Mayor Jones and Supervisor
Anderson. We are a large unrepresented area as far as the level of
representation that's around the table. But as legislation works its way
and the Executive Committee starts to review. The unincorporated area needs
to have a full vote. Anything less is not really respectful of the citizens
who are living in the unincorporated areas. It is not as if when you buy a
house, you go, is this a city? And, am I going to be represented at SANDAG
the way other city folks are or am I in an unincorporated area? It is
generally not a consideration at all. No one even knows that they're not in
a city. Until they say, I'm unhappy and I want to go down to City Hall.
And, I say well, I'd like to see that place. Tell me when you find it.
Because there isn't a City Hall. We have the County. But the unincorporated
area needs to be part of the conversation. So many conversations that go on
at SANDAG - in other areas - about full representation of voting. Please be
sure that we're included.  And, thank you.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: Yes, thank you. I just want to
say that I strongly support that we pursue the ability to vote. Alpine,
Boulevard, Campo, Lake Moreno, Crest, Dehesea, Granite Hills, Harbison
Canyon, Descanso, Fallbrook, Jamal, Julian, Lakeside, Pine Valley, Potrero,
Rainbow, Ramona, San Dieguito, Spring Valley, Sweetwater, Valle De Oro,
Valley Center, Bonsall, Borrego Springs, Jacumba, and Twin Oaks Valley. I
wanted to read these names because when I first moved here 22 years ago. I
was totally surprised when I learned that Ramona, Borrego Springs, these
towns really had no representation at this level; had no city council or
town council. I learned a lot in my first couple of years moving to San
Diego County. I would suggest that we as a Board make strong and just clear
and simple moves. I even wonder if there is something we could do as an
amendment to SB 10? I just don't know. But I would suggest that we find a
way to, in a streamlined way, give a vote to the 600,000 people who have
these planning groups and have taken such a positive step forward. And, I
have a question. What is the weight of the County's vote? Is it these
600,000?

Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO: Amberlin can probably answer it better. I don't,
can't give you the exact answer. So I know she tracks this all the time.
(Mayor Terry Gaasterland: We can look it up, but maybe you can remind us
when you have it.)

*San Diego LOSSAN Rail Realignment Project:*
The realignment of the rail connection between San Diego and San Luis
Obispo does not normally impact the unincorporated area, but one of the
proposed alignments would. Infrequently, it is mentioned that the rail
connection should be relocated to follow the I-15. The Department of
Defense maintains a controlling interest in the rail location as it is
considered part of the military infrastructure utilized to move troops and
equipment throughout the country. Discussion of the new rail location is
ongoing.

*APG News:*
-At the February 28th meeting, SANDAG approved all of our Policy Advisory
Committee (PAC) membership requests except for the Audit Committee
membership that Carol Hake from the Lakeside CPG volunteered to join. The
explanation was the requirements for membership on this committee were
narrow and we did not qualify....however, Carol is certainly able to attend
as a member of the public. Also, it was recommended that both our primary
and alternate PAC members attend the PAC meetings.

-APG members on PACs have begun submitting reports to the APG. Thank you
for working to increase our presence at SANDAG.

-Update: Conversion of our APG "Advisory" Board seat to a "Voting" Board
seat - Currently California State Senator Brian Jones has submitted SB 240.
It is working its way through the legislative process. Also, State
Assemblyman Carl DeMaio has introduced a "spot bill" on the Assembly side.
More information will follow as these bills develop.

-Del Mar Mayor, Terry Gaasterland, has volunteered to assist the APG with
connecting to State Senator Catherine Blakespear as the spot bills noted

Dill" <theddills@att.net>, Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>
body:
*SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - February 2024*

*Caltrans:*
Roy Abboud and Allan Kosup - A Disaster Declaration from the President
would release funds for highway repairs due to the recent rainstorms.
Highway 78 has experienced significant damage in several locations.
Preventing damage from rainstorms is a shared responsibility as the "system
of streams, trash, trees, plants, and encampments" all contribute to water
overflow and runoff. Caltrans, cities and counties share responsibility to
clear creeks, but Federal and State permits to legally clear out stream
beds are difficult to procure.

*125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
Feb. 9th meeting Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG would be presenting
an action plan for the 125 Toll Road at the February 13th City of Chula
Vista Council meeting. This presentation would include the impact to other
projects with respect to available funds if the payoff date for the toll
road was moved up. If the community wishes to see a sooner payoff date for
the toll road they would need to understand that this money will come from
other projects.
-APG Question to Board - First, will the Sweetwater Community Planning
Group be receiving the same presentation on the toll road that the City of
Chula Vista will receive? And second, regarding determination of the end
date for the toll road - is there consideration of the increased use of
surface streets to bypass the toll road and the danger this presents to the
community?
-SANDAG Response (Nora Vargas) - This is the biggest issue in Bonita! The
County will be sponsoring a community meeting for all parties in the area.
-SANDAG Response (Coleen Clementson) And, yes, we are considering surface
street impacts.
Feb. 23rd meeting Carolina Chavez made a motion to, "Declare support for
eliminating the debt and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027." Board
consensus was for staff to explore the feasibility of this date as this
would be the earliest date that the payoff could be made without penalty.

*Report of SANDAG Draft 2025 Regional Plan:*
Susan Huntington, Antoinette Meier, Ray Majors and Allan Kosup continued
their presentation of an initial concept of the Draft 2025 Regional Plan.
Greenhouse gas reduction needs to be reduced by 18.9% by the year 2035.
Goals are:
Improve transit frequency and hours of operation.
Implement pricing strategies
Expand Youth Opportunity Pass
Provide parking by transit
Funding for these projects comes from 40 different sources: Federal, State
and Local
Budget begins with funds leftover from previous Plan
Review of current and future funding sources to determine viability of
covering a Plan budget range of $139 to $162 billion.
Clarified that managed lanes are only on the interstate/highway system
-NCTD reported a new microtransit/flexible fleet initiative was starting
and Fallbrook/Pala would be one of the first areas to pilot this program.
No additional details available at this time.
-APG Question to Board - First, what is the priority for wildfire
evacuation improvements? And second, regarding the greenhouse gas reduction
goal for 2035 and the use of reduced VMTs to meet that goal - the
unincorporated area has a new generation of youth who have not yet
developed a driving habit. Microtransit and useful bus routes/times
implemented in the next year or two is an opportunity to redirect future
drivers into GHG friendly travel modes. How soon will these options be made
available?
SANDAG Response - Express bus routes from unincorporated communities are
being implemented soon.

*SANDAG Roadside Service:*
General discussion on the increased cost for this program since SANDAG
began running operations. Request for a breakdown and clarification of
budget items to effectively monitor and provide oversight of the program.
Need statistics to see if a full tow truck is required to be the responding
vehicle for every freeway breakdown.

*Inland Rail Trail (bike path):*
Update on Phases 3 and 4 of this bike path from Escondido to Oceanside.
Many Board members noted that this was an example of another expenditure
that did not benefit those in the unincorporated areas of the County.

*Airport Transit Connection:*
Update on the progress of the new plan for moving people from the SD
Airport to downtown and other destinations. Extensive public comment and
Board comments on the unnecessary expense of building an elevated "people
mover" platform to transport people from the Airport to downtown as
trolleys and buses were already in existence. Also, people should be able
to move about all of the County, not just the coastal areas. Overall, this
plan is a substantial change from the multi-billion dollar Central Mobility
Hub vision of former Executive Director, Hasan Ikhrata.

*SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
The SANDAG Board of Directors March 8th meeting will be a Board Retreat
held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to
3:30. Both the APG Representative and Alternate plan to attend.

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

Dill" <theddills@att.net>, Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>, "Sandra Farrell," <tovcsg.chair@gmail.com>, Rebecca Falk <rebfalk7@gmail.com>, petersonenv@hotmail.com, Jennifer Haider <jennehaider@gmail.com>, Lakeside Planning Group <lakesidecpg@gmail.com>, "jimdax8@gmail.com" <jimdax8@gmail.com>, "jimcusteausvcpg@gmail.com" <jimcusteausvcpg@gmail.com>, Ron Nehring <ron@ronnehring.com>, cory.gautereaux@gmail.com, drattray524@aol.com
body:
Good Evening APG Members,

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-We are looking at SB 375 and whether or not the use of VMT as a metric is
really effective. Should we be using these metrics in our Regional Plans or
doing something different?
-Regarding the new Otay Mesa East Port of Entry we discussed with the
Mexican government the topic of Mexico setting up a trust fund to hold some
of the revenue from their side as funds to be used for environmental issues
such as the Tijuana River issue.
-Fewer sole source contracts are being awarded.
-The 4 major California MPOs (representing 80% of state population) met in
Sacramento to discuss shared issues: Housing, Transportation, CARB,
Caltrans and specifically SB 375 and the need to double down on VMTs as a
way to create a better environment.
-We are following Assemblyman DeMaio's AB 24 (
https://legiscan.com/CA/bill/AB24/2025)  and State Senator Jones' SB 240 (
https://legiscan.com/CA/bill/SB240/2025) bills on structural changes to the
SANDAG Board in order to bring a vote for the unincorporated area. We will
discuss this at our next Executive Committee meeting.

Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: We need a voting seat as the
rural needs are very different from the cities.

*Proposed Rapid Bus Routes:*
-Unincorporated communities that utilize the northern section of I-15 for
travel will benefit from this new bus route.
-New Rapid Bus Route 483 to connect San Diego County (San Marcos) with
Riverside County (Temecula) via the I-15 has a survey available for the
public to indicate important stops along the proposed route. Survey is open
until April 23rd. https://engage.sandag.org/Rapid483survey

*Downtown Stopover Program:*
This project for MTS bus drivers to have a dedicated safe and clean break
area in downtown San Diego utilizes TransNet funds. At present $37M has
been spent acquiring land. Staff presented a plan which includes completing
SANDAG's purchase of a complete city block - of which 2/3 is already
purchased - and planning a building for the bus driver's stopovers in
downtown that could also be a multi-use building operated by SANDAG. The
total project cost is $67M. TransNet funds supply 41% of this cost.

APG comment to Board: I'm an extremely budget conscious person. And, you
already own half the block, which is parking lots, so there is no building
in the way. Is there a reason you cannot walk across the street to Columbia
Tower; rent an apartment that would be nice for a break room, would have
bathrooms, it would have a rest area because it could have one bedroom and
you also have kitchen facilities there.  We're not in the business of
operating and running facilities. That is what I would do with the
taxpayer's money. You have a nice parking area there. On one whole side of
the block - plenty of space for the buses - both for egress and ingress.
And then you walk across the street and you go to the Columbia Tower and
you go up to your dedicated break room apartment. It's already there. Is
there any reason why that can't be done? Thank you.

*Draft FY 2026 Program Budget:*
The proposed budget is $1.3B which is the same from the previous fiscal
year. Sources are Federal, State, TransNet and Other Local Funds. SANDAG is
different from cities in that it budgets by project versus by department.
The budget reflects money to be spent in a specific year and not the total
cost of projects as projects go through several phases on the path to
completion. For a project to be part of the budget it must be a part of the
Regional Plan. The Federal portion of the budget is unstable in the current
political climate. The Youth Opportunity Pass is funded only to the end of
FY 2026.

APG comment to Board: I was hoping to hear that the Youth Opportunity Pass
was going to be expanding, not contracting. I am concerned, and somewhat
alarmed, that this is the last fiscal year the Youth Opportunity Pass
program will be funded. Will flexible fleets or micro transit be expanded?
What will SANDAG do to support the non-driving, GHG-friendly youth of the
rural and unincorporated areas? How will we provide a path to opportunity
and success within the larger region for our low income and
geographically-disadvantaged youth? As an idea - using my Columbia Tower
apartment break room suggestion as a way to save funds on the Downtown
Stopover Bus project would provide savings that could fund the Youth
Opportunity Pass for our children.

*APG News:*
-Additional PAC Report Information: Jim Custeau, APG's Representative to
the SANDAG Transportation Committee asked the following question of the
SANDAG Mobility Working Group: I attended the March 21st meeting, during
which there was a presentation (Item #7 on the agenda) titled "Flexible
Fleets Pilot Grant Program Call for Projects". This pilot project grant
opportunity struck me as having the potential of having a positive impact
on our planning group/sponsor group area residents with much needed public
transportation access - particularly in our more economically disadvantaged
zones. I see that you are all members of the SANDAG Mobility Working Group.
I'm curious how County staff plan on soliciting input from our various
planning/sponsor groups in preparation for potential grant proposal
submittals to SANDAG.

Response from Mobility Working Group: The Flexible Fleets Pilot Grant
Program could present a good opportunity to improve transportation access,
especially in disadvantaged communities.

At this stage, SANDAG is still soliciting feedback on the *draft grant
eligibility criteria*—the Call for Projects has not been released yet. One
of the key considerations SANDAG is currently focused on is ensuring
projects have a plan for ongoing funding and sustainability beyond the
initial pilot.

Once the final criteria and application materials are released, we’ll have
a better sense of potential project ideas and the process for gathering
input from planning and sponsor groups. We’ll stay tuned as this develops
and share updates as appropriate.

-Update: Conversion of our APG "Advisory" Board seat to a "Voting" Board
seat - State Assemblyman Carl DeMaio held a press conference on March 21st
to discuss his bill to include the APG as a voting member. Both Robin Joy
Maxson and Eileen Delaney attended. Also, upon the recommendation of SANDAG
Board Member, Terry Gaasterland, the APG has reached out to State Senator
Catherine Blakespear, requesting her assistance with the change in voting
status for unincorporated area residents. We are in contact with Blakespear
and will work with her Chief of Staff, Jack Christensen.

-Update: Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the
unincorporated area in San Diego County - will be holding two events for
Community Planning Groups. One will be for CPGs in the East and one for
those in the North. The APG made it clear to Congressional Field
Representative, Alan Pellicani, that these CPG meetings are considered
separate events from the APG's request for a meeting between the
Congressman, SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso, and APG leaders. That meeting
continues to be a future event.

No questions received this month.

Sweetwater's lake manager, Victor Gaus told me they will not bother people who are walking on Japatul Road to get to the hiking and fishing easment where it intersect the Japatul Road and county bridges.Parking along the road will be a big improvement, not only for CRHT access considering that Sweetwater closes the parking lot earlier than the eaement hours, but also for general use including for automobile breakdowns.

Sweetwater closing the parking lot early has impacts it should not beyond Loveland to the CRHT. This is a fair remedy.
Those no-parkng signs don't exist in other areas of Japatul Road. Other public trails are accessed on other county  public roads like the light traffic connector that Japatul Road is , by pulling off on the shoulder. 
The signs are there as a favor to Sweetwater not the public that Sweetwater has restricted access to since the no-parking signs were put up.
Please help with this matter.

subject: Report on SANDAG's March 2024 meetings to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
to: Robin Joy Maxson <RobinJoyMaxson@gmail.com>, Lynne Malinowski <rustyhorseranch@outlook.com>, Patrick Brown <patrickeng@sbcglobal.net>, "Oday Yousif (Valle De Oro)" <odayyousif@gmail.com>, "Kiki Munshi (Julian)" <kiki@skagenranch.com>, Harriet Taylor <harrietgtaylor1@gmail.com>, Darin Wessel <dlwplanninggroup@gmail.com>, jimcusteausvcpg@cox.net, eileen.fallbrook@gmail.com, "Jan Hedlun, Potrero," <janwrites2013@yahoo.com>, "Billie Jo Jannen, Campo," <campoplanninggroup@nym.hush.com>, Earl Goodnight <blvdgoodnight@gmail.com>, Steve Hutchison <hutchisonsm@gmail.com>, Descanso Planning Group <descansocpg@gmail.com>, Paul Dombkowski <paul.dombkowski@gmail.com>, Story R Vogel <storyvogel@aol.com>, "Douglas S. Dill" <theddills@att.net>, Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>, Cherry Diefenbach <csdiefenbach@sbcglobal.net>, "Sandra Farrell," <tovcsg.chair@gmail.com>, Rebecca Falk <rebfalk7@gmail.com>, petersonenv@hotmail.com, Jennifer Haider <jennehaider@gmail.com>
body:
*SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*

*SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536 13th
Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
(Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.

*Caltrans:*
Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.

*125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
March 22nd Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 29th to specifically discuss the
results of this internal audit.)
Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of 125
Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.

March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf

The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
the 125 Toll Road.
Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
collected and toll user accounts?
Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver on
the contractual requirements?
Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
tolls correctly?
What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
to equipment disconnect sooner?
Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to the
former CEO?
Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
faulty numbers not corrected instead?
How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
the I-15?
How much money in tolls was lost overall?

Board member comments were:
"After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
"This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
"We need to investigate potential fraud."
"We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."

The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.

*Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
Projects:*
SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included the
project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
complaints from its own members.

APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."

Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."

You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
and here is the link to the budget document:
https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2025.pdf#page=6

*SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
areas for housing.
Board discussion on the increased legislation from Sacramento (SB 35 and SB
423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers. Cities
reported that Sacramento was applying a state-wide housing solution to
individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable
land available than others.  Some unincorporated communities are located
near job centers and should not be dismissed as potential housing locations
due to a lack of public transit options.

*APG Update:*
In addition to this SANDAG report the APG has received acceptance of our
Associate membership (non-voting) invitation to Community Sponsor Groups by
Bonsall (Jennifer Haider), Jacumba (Cherry Diefenbach) and Twin Oaks Valley
(Joseph Bunn). We will formally accept their membership at our June 1st APG
meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
