body:
Thanks for the report.  In regards to the regional plan, is there any plan
regarding rural areas in the future?
Kerry Forrest,  DCPG

On Sat, Mar 30, 2024, 10:29 AM APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com>
wrote:

> *SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*
>
> *SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
> March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536
> 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
> (Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
> the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
> regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
> criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
> narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.
>
> *Caltrans:*
> Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
> 2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
> they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.
>
> *125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
> March 22nd Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
> contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
> system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
> Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
> results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
> SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 29th to specifically discuss the
> results of this internal audit.)
> Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of
> 125 Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.
>
> March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
> Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
> a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
> sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf
>
> The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
> failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
> the 125 Toll Road.
> Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
> Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
> collected and toll user accounts?
> Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver
> on the contractual requirements?
> Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
> tolls correctly?
> What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
> Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
> to equipment disconnect sooner?
> Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
> Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
> What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
> Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to
> the former CEO?
> Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
> faulty numbers not corrected instead?
> How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
> other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
> How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
> the I-15?
> How much money in tolls was lost overall?
>
> Board member comments were:
> "After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
> "This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
> "We need to investigate potential fraud."
> "We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."
>
> The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
> Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
> forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.
>
> *Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
> Projects:*
> SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included the
> project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
> projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
> projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
> unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
> the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
> complaints from its own members.
>
> APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
> unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
> use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
> remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
> of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
> have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
> bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
> very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
> injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
> area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
> is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
> that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
> unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
> but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
> that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
> funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
> that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
> still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
> want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."
>
> Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
> toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
> our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
> projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
> prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
> meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
> get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
> implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
> those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."
>
> You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
> and here is the link to the budget document:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2025.pdf#page=6
>
> *SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
> Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
> staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
> The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
> population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
> transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
> areas for housing.
> Board discussion on the increased legislation from Sacramento (SB 35 and
> SB 423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers.
> Cities reported that Sacramento was applying a state-wide housing solution
> to individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
> allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable
> land available than others.  Some unincorporated communities are located
> near job centers and should not be dismissed as potential housing locations
> due to a lack of public transit options.
>
> *APG Update:*
> In addition to this SANDAG report the APG has received acceptance of our
> Associate membership (non-voting) invitation to Community Sponsor Groups by
> Bonsall (Jennifer Haider), Jacumba (Cherry Diefenbach) and Twin Oaks Valley
> (Joseph Bunn). We will formally accept their membership at our June 1st APG
> meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!
>
> Report Submitted by:
> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>

> it done before sooner than later. I do have to be a little bit flippant,
> and I apologize ahead of time. Maybe not. About the bicycle lane thing. You
> know, you talk um, Terry you know you talked about avid bicycling and
> e-bike and if you know - with the exception of east county at the 52 there
> is only one protected bicycle lane in all of east county. And, that's so
> you can make sure to get out of east county. Why they did that? I do not
> know. And, that goes into Tierra Santa. I average about 30, 40 sometimes 50
> miles on my bike, e-bike. And I go through La Mesa, San Diego, Lemon Grove.
> All the way out to Spring Valley, Dehesa. All the way into Alpine. And you
> know what? I still haven't seen any protected bike lanes. The only
> protection I get is when I say my prayer before I get on the bike and say,
> please don't let a car hit me because they are only a few feet away.
> Because even where there is a bicycle lane, most of the time they kind
> of faked a bicycle lane because there wasn't enough room. So where you
> normally have, I think it's an average four foot bicycle lane, I think
> we're lucky to get a two foot bicycle lane and many of those are along the
> seams of the roadway. And just talking to Mayor Jones and you know what?
> When cities do their slurries or road repairs. They go up to the bike lane
> and stop. So there's always potholes and there's always breaks along the
> seams and things of that nature. So nobody really cares in east county if
> you have a good bike lane. That's just my opinion. And, it goes back to
> what Robin said earlier about maybe if we're going to talk about equity,
> equity should be looking at safety more than anything else. Because I don't
> care who you are and you're riding on a bike lane or a lack of bike lane in
> those areas; you know what? Where's the equity and safety? And maybe a new
> term we ought to bring up in safety is not just VMT, but EBMT, electric
> bike miles traveled. And how safe are you on those EBMT's? That's all I
> have to say.
>
> *Chief Executive Officer Performance Evaluation Process:*
> On December 6th and 13th all SANDAG Board members are invited to
> participate in developing performance goals for the CEO position.
>
> *APG News:*
> Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the unincorporated
> area in San Diego County - has not set a meeting date with the APG as of
> this report. Since July, the APG has been working to set up a joint meeting
> with the Congressman, SANDAG CEO Mario Orso and our APG members without
> success. SANDAG CEO Mario Orso has stated he will be available and happy to
> attend our joint meeting. Congressman Issa has not been available and very
> little communication has come from his office. The APG sent a request to
> his Chief of Staff, Veronica Smith Wong. She has responded, but not with a
> set date, yet.
> The subject of the meeting will be:
> "Transportation funding and safety in the Unincorporated Area; addressing
> fatality rate on rural highways, safe wildfire evacuation, lack of public
> transportation resulting in geographic isolation of vulnerable populations
> and continued diversion of transportation funds from rural highway
> projects."
>
> Planning/Sponsor Groups that wish to support the establishment of this
> joint meeting with Congressman Issa may also communicate directly with
> Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.house.gov
>
> *Questions from APG members*
> *No questions received this month.*
>
> Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
> SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
> https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors
>
> Report Submitted by:
> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>

--
*Erika T. Simmons, Ed.D.*

Good Evening Kerry,
Hopefully I understand your question correctly.....plans that would include
the rural area are minimal to virtually non-existent with respect to roads
and housing. The money remains focused on the populated coastal corridor
and southern region. As our APG Representative to SANDAG in addition to
pointing out this inequity - it would be great to include more specifics.
Thank you for any ideas/suggestions/concerns you wish to have communicated
through this venue.
-Robin

Robin Joy Maxson, Chair
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
760-705-7435

> regarding rural areas in the future?

>> *SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*
>>
>> *SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
>> March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536
>> 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
>> (Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
>> the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
>> regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
>> criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
>> narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.
>>
>> *Caltrans:*
>> Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
>> 2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
>> they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.
>>

>> the contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new

>> year.

>> results of this internal audit.)

>> 125 Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.
>>
>> March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
>> Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
>> a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously

>>
>> The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
>> failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
>> the 125 Toll Road.

>> Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
>> collected and toll user accounts?
>> Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver
>> on the contractual requirements?
>> Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor
>> record tolls correctly?
>> What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
>> Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected
>> due to equipment disconnect sooner?
>> Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
>> Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
>> What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
>> Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to
>> the former CEO?
>> Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
>> faulty numbers not corrected instead?

>> other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.

>> the I-15?

>>

>> "After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
>> "This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
>> "We need to investigate potential fraud."
>> "We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."
>>
>> The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by
>> the Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns
>> would be forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.
>>
>> *Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
>> Projects:*
>> SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included
>> the project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
>> projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
>> projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
>> unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
>> the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
>> complaints from its own members.
>>
>> APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
>> unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
>> use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
>> remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
>> of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
>> have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
>> bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
>> very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
>> injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
>> area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
>> is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
>> that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
>> unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;

>> that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
>> funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
>> that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
>> still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
>> want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."
>>
>> Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
>> toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
>> our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
>> projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
>> prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
>> meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
>> get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
>> implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
>> those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."
>>
>> You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
>> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
>> and here is the link to the budget document:
>> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2025.pdf#page=6
>>
>> *SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
>> Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
>> staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
>> The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
>> population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
>> transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
>> areas for housing.

>> SB 423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers.

>> to individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
>> allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable

>> meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!
>>
>> Report Submitted by:
>> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
>> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>>

Robin,Excellent detailed SANDAG meeting notes (as usual !).I would support a "Unincorporated Area Summit" and will get formal recommendation from the San Dieguito Planning Group in the coming months.Thank you for all you do!Best Regards,Doug DillSDPG - ChairElfin Forest/Harmony Grove Town Council - Board Member

    On Monday, July 8, 2024 at 02:00:55 PM PDT, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

 Good Afternoon APG Members,
Please note that SANDAG will not hold Board meetings in August.
San Diego Regional Tribal Summit:This month SANDAG held their June 14th Board meeting offsite at the Pala Casino. This was a "Tribal Summit" hosted by the Southern California Tribal Chairmen's Association and focusing on issues and concerns specifically related to the tribal residents and SANDAG's role. Takeaways from the Tribal Summit:
-As Tribal land is located in the rural areas of the County these residents face many of the same funding and planning challenges from SANDAG as their non-Tribal. unincorporated area neighbors. 
-Bo Mazzetti, Tribal Chairman of the Rincon Band of Luiseno Indians, gave an impassioned commentary regarding the ongoing lack of attention and funding from SANDAG to the needs of Tribal residents. Specifically, he talked about the unreasonable amount of time that has passed with no appreciable improvement to roadways and other projects. Mr. Mazzetti was frustrated by SANDAG's procrastination.
-Samual Sanford, Senior Regional Planner SANDAG, presented traffic statistics that are available to the public through a Traffic Safety Dashboard. The dashboard contains information related to number of accidents, severity, etc. If any APG member has the link to this dashboard, please share with the group. I will reach out to Sam for the link, too.
- To the APG - As an idea, what do we think about holding an "Unincorporated Area Summit?" This would provide unincorporated area leaders and residents an opportunity to speak with SANDAG on issues impacting the unincorporated area.

SANDAG's New CEO, Mario Orso:Mario Orso began work on June 17th. He delivered his first report as CEO at the June 28th Board meeting. In this report he specifically made note of the needs of the unincorporated area. He noted that there is a wildfire evacuation tour planned for SR67 and SR78 and that he would be asking Caltrans to provide an update on the environmental document for the San Vicente CMCP (Lakeside to Ramona). Mr. Orso commented that he heard there wasn't a lot of progress being made. To ensure that a project is moving along he will request an update on the San Vicente CMCP is added to the Transportation Committee and the Board agendas.
APG comment to Board: That is good to hear. We have had interest from other unincorporated areas on having a wildfire evacuation tour, too. This is one of the corridors, but there are other corridors at risk.
SANDAG reponse (Mario Orso): This is very similar to the LOSSAN Project. We need to be engaging with the community. That is part of the organization of excellence and procedure and hearing from the community, taking those tours, will allow the lead agency Caltrans to implement or consider in their alternatives or studies, all the appropriate emergency exits and anything needed to meet the project goals.

SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:APG comment to Board: Regarding the Youth Opportunity Pass. This is a valuable program. We need data on rider's start point by zip code. Currently, to utilize this program and to reduce the transit time to a reasonable length, we must drive our children down to a transportation hub. Otherwise, the travel time on the bus or other transit options is not useful.  The more youth who can be protected from accident exposure through a public transit option is a responsible return on investment for SANDAG.
Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista comment: We will be pursuing these same benefits for senior citizens with their low incomes and pensions. They should have these free passes too, in order to get to their destinations.
Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: We need to get a cost per rider for this program. It is a very popular program that seems to be well utilized.
Jack Shu, City of La Mesa comment: We heard some great testimony from NCTD and their micro transit system. On demand systems in which if we can work with those concepts and ideas in the pilot programs that SANDAG is working with we can advance our thinking of how transportation can be. Serve rural areas, serve Robin's concerns in terms of getting kids connected to transit centers so they don't have to rely on cars in the future.
Outreach Efforts For Community Feedback On Projects:Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: SANDAG reports it is going to include a survey in order to improve outreach. I'm not sure who decided we should do a survey and who is going to participate because I believe it would be very important to have all county feedback, so that we can all have our unique needs be a part of the plan. I feel like our more rural areas where they honestly have some more of the greater need, I'm pointing over to you Robin, but I mean you got a lot of places where they can't even get out in a safe manner to actually evacuate in a fire or something like that. So I want to make sure we are getting feedback from all parts of the county; including our seniors.
SANDAG response (Antoinette Meier): We intend to reach everyone in the County who needs specialized transportation services.
Questions from APG members:
Question - Does SANDAG's jurisdiction include the far eastern unincorporated communities?Response (source SANDAG) - Yes, SANDAG has oversight of the San Diego region located in the southwestern corner of the United States and is bordered by Mexico, the Pacific Ocean, Camp Pendleton, Orange and Riverside Counties, and Imperial County. Our region encompasses more than 4,260 square miles and includes 18 incorporated cities, 17 federally-recognized tribal governments, and incorporated and unincorporated San Diego County.  
News: The Borrego Springs Community Sponsor Group voted on June 5th to accept the APG's invitation to join as an Associate (non-voting) member. We will formally vote to accept their membership at our next APG meeting currently scheduled for Saturday, January 4th, 2025. Borrego Springs reps will be Jim Dax and alternate Becky Falk. Welcome!

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from SANDAG's Board of Directors website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors
Report Submitted by:Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAGAssociation of Planning Groups - San Diego County

body:
As I commented in the past to SanDag video meetings I would like to see
more focus on frequent rapid transit from Jacunba to El Cajon with stops at
the park n rides serving the communities along I- 8. When I suggested this
I was told that the focus was on in town populations. How can the youth or
workers use the transit system if there is only 1 small bus that stops
around 10 am and returns around 3? There is little to no infrastructure
required to be built, only bus routes with reasonable frequency
established. Take some of the empty busses running routes in town and run
them in the rural areas.
Eventually with reliable bus service you may see some use. "If you build it
they will come".
Kerry

On Jul 8, 2024, at 2:00 PM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Good Afternoon APG Members,

Please note that SANDAG will not hold Board meetings in August.

San Diego Regional Tribal Summit:
This month SANDAG held their June 14th Board meeting offsite at the Pala Casino. This was a "Tribal Summit" hosted by the Southern California Tribal Chairmen's Association and focusing on issues and concerns specifically related to the tribal residents and SANDAG's role. Takeaways from the Tribal Summit:

-As Tribal land is located in the rural areas of the County these residents face many of the same funding and planning challenges from SANDAG as their non-Tribal. unincorporated area neighbors.

-Bo Mazzetti, Tribal Chairman of the Rincon Band of Luiseno Indians, gave an impassioned commentary regarding the ongoing lack of attention and funding from SANDAG to the needs of Tribal residents. Specifically, he talked about the unreasonable amount of time that has passed with no appreciable improvement to roadways and other projects. Mr. Mazzetti was frustrated by SANDAG's procrastination.

-Samual Sanford, Senior Regional Planner SANDAG, presented traffic statistics that are available to the public through a Traffic Safety Dashboard. The dashboard contains information related to number of accidents, severity, etc. If any APG member has the link to this dashboard, please share with the group. I will reach out to Sam for the link, too.

- To the APG - As an idea, what do we think about holding an "Unincorporated Area Summit?" This would provide unincorporated area leaders and residents an opportunity to speak with SANDAG on issues impacting the unincorporated area.

SANDAG's New CEO, Mario Orso:
Mario Orso began work on June 17th. He delivered his first report as CEO at the June 28th Board meeting. In this report he specifically made note of the needs of the unincorporated area. He noted that there is a wildfire evacuation tour planned for SR67 and SR78 and that he would be asking Caltrans to provide an update on the environmental document for the San Vicente CMCP (Lakeside to Ramona). Mr. Orso commented that he heard there wasn't a lot of progress being made. To ensure that a project is moving along he will request an update on the San Vicente CMCP is added to the Transportation Committee and the Board agendas.

APG comment to Board: That is good to hear. We have had interest from other unincorporated areas on having a wildfire evacuation tour, too. This is one of the corridors, but there are other corridors at risk.

SANDAG reponse (Mario Orso): This is very similar to the LOSSAN Project. We need to be engaging with the community. That is part of the organization of excellence and procedure and hearing from the community, taking those tours, will allow the lead agency Caltrans to implement or consider in their alternatives or studies, all the appropriate emergency exits and anything needed to meet the project goals.

SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:
APG comment to Board: Regarding the Youth Opportunity Pass. This is a valuable program. We need data on rider's start point by zip code. Currently, to utilize this program and to reduce the transit time to a reasonable length, we must drive our children down to a transportation hub. Otherwise, the travel time on the bus or other transit options is not useful.  The more youth who can be protected from accident exposure through a public transit option is a responsible return on investment for SANDAG.

Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista comment: We will be pursuing these same benefits for senior citizens with their low incomes and pensions. They should have these free passes too, in order to get to their destinations.

Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: We need to get a cost per rider for this program. It is a very popular program that seems to be well utilized.

Jack Shu, City of La Mesa comment: We heard some great testimony from NCTD and their micro transit system. On demand systems in which if we can work with those concepts and ideas in the pilot programs that SANDAG is working with we can advance our thinking of how transportation can be. Serve rural areas, serve Robin's concerns in terms of getting kids connected to transit centers so they don't have to rely on cars in the future.

Outreach Efforts For Community Feedback On Projects:
Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: SANDAG reports it is going to include a survey in order to improve outreach. I'm not sure who decided we should do a survey and who is going to participate because I believe it would be very important to have all county feedback, so that we can all have our unique needs be a part of the plan. I feel like our more rural areas where they honestly have some more of the greater need, I'm pointing over to you Robin, but I mean you got a lot of places where they can't even get out in a safe manner to actually evacuate in a fire or something like that. So I want to make sure we are getting feedback from all parts of the county; including our seniors.

SANDAG response (Antoinette Meier): We intend to reach everyone in the County who needs specialized transportation services.

Questions from APG members:

Question - Does SANDAG's jurisdiction include the far eastern unincorporated communities?
Response (source SANDAG) - Yes, SANDAG has oversight of the San Diego region located in the southwestern corner of the United States and is bordered by Mexico, the Pacific Ocean, Camp Pendleton, Orange and Riverside Counties, and Imperial County. Our region encompasses more than 4,260 square miles and includes 18 incorporated cities, 17 federally-recognized tribal governments, and incorporated and unincorporated San Diego County.

News: The Borrego Springs Community Sponsor Group voted on June 5th to accept the APG's invitation to join as an Associate (non-voting) member. We will formally vote to accept their membership at our next APG meeting currently scheduled for Saturday, January 4th, 2025. Borrego Springs reps will be Jim Dax and alternate Becky Falk. Welcome!

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from SANDAG's Board of Directors website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

Robin :)

Questions from APG members:

Question - Is SANDAG informed of freeway projects in the County? Or, are freeway projects strictly a state affair? Does SANDAG have a role in the scheduling and decision making?

Response - I am still working on this answer..

       Via

Sent from the all new AOL app for iOS

On Saturday, July 27, 2024, 9:00 AM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

Good Morning APG Members,
Note: At the July 26, 2024 SANDAG Board of Directors meeting there was no (zero) County representation. This means we had no one representing the Unincorporated Area with the power to vote. Nora Vargas was absent. Joel Anderson was absent. The County Board of Supervisors has two alternates: Terra Lawson-Remer and Monica Montgomery Steppe. Neither were present. When a vote was taken to consider borrowing $20 million of future Transnet funds for the "Transnet Regional Bike Early Action Program" there was no one from the County to vote. We had an empty seat.
SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:
Mario Orso reported that SANDAG would continue to provide updates to the Board and stakeholders on the priority corridors of SR 78 and SR 67. He did not include SRs 76, 79 or 94 in this priority list. The Transnet Independent Taxpayer Oversight Committee is seeking community members for their Board. Information located at their website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/transnet-independent-taxpayer-oversightSANDAG will not hold Board of Director meetings in August, but staff and working groups will continue with work.

APG comment to Board: This month we held the first Evacuation Tour with SANDAG and Caltrans staff. The potential evacuation routes in the Ramona area were thoroughly explored and wildfire hazards such as chimney fire burn zones were identified for the group by our local fire behavior expert, Dan Summers. The next Evacuation Tour will explore the SR 94 corridor from Campo to Jamul; including the dangerous intersection of Otay Lakes and Honey Springs Road. The Unincorporated Community values these opportunities to partner with SANDAG and Caltrans to share vital boots-on-the-ground knowledge in order to develop safe evacuation routes for all travelers in the region. Thank you.
California Transportation Commission (CTC):Two CTC Commissioners introduced themselves and reported that they are "the money people" for State and Federal transportation funds. Commissioners Clarissa Reyes Falcon and Lee Ann Eager invited Board members to attend an upcoming meeting being held in San Diego from August 15-16. Website for information: https://catc.ca.gov/meetings-events/commission-meetings-2024

Transnet Oversight Annual Report and Performance Audit and Budget:The overall feedback from the Board to those presenting on Transnet funds and projects was that there was a clear lack of information and accountability is needed. Cost Benefit Analysis was missing. Staff reported miniscule use of the public transportation options and utilization of biking or walking - Return On Investment is dismal. SANDAG often quotes the maxim that limited funds should be used to help the most people. Historically, the Transnet funds are benefitting very few. As of FY 2023, total bikeway Program funding was $397.3 million. Transnet funds represented $187.2 million (47%) of this spending. The promise of the Transnet funds to improve public safety through corridor projects is not being met. SANDAG staff's explanation was that the voters had an expectation and the funding sources for these projects (of which Transnet funds are only one part/source) come with stipulations that are often in conflict with what the voters expected. This is the difficult environment in which planning and funding for projects exists.
Melanie Burkholder, City of Carlsbad comment: We need cost benefit analysis for these Transnet dollar projects.
Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO comment: We are working toward structural change in order to provide cost benefit analysis and demonstrate a good use of the funds

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach comment: I know that many people leave my city to move east because it is more affordable. This puts more people on those roads and they need to be improved.
APG Comment to Board: What are the raw numbers for this conclusion that bike ridership has increased 5x? Does this conclusion represent a change from 50 to 500 riders, 50 to 5,000? We need to see the numbers. And, do you see a slower increase in pedestrian travel than expected due to e-bike encounters on pathways?
SANDAG response (Omar Atayee): Those are great questions. We don't have those numbers, but will get those to the Board. We don't know if e-bikes are impacting our numbers, but we are seeing an increase. I don't know if we have data on that.
Dawn Vettes, SANDAG CFO comment: We acknowledge room for improvement and are working to strengthen internal controls. Our next audit in 2027 will show significant progress.

SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:In response to a previous Board question about the cost per ride of those utilizing the Youth Opportunity Pass, Mario Orso reported .69 cents was the average cost.

Question - Is SANDAG informed of freeway projects in the County? Or, are freeway projects strictly a state affair? Does SANDAG have a role in the scheduling and decision making?Response - I am still working on this answer.....
News: Link to the Traffic Safety Dashboard https://www.sandag.org/trafficsafety. It is located in SANDAG’s Open Data Portal.
Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from SANDAG's Board of Directors website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

body:
Thank you for this good report…but it made me wonder, as many things do, about the “bikeway” move.  The questions here are pertinent because there are real constraints on bicycle use.  First, the rider has to be reasonably fit; those of us who are aged, infirm, or handicapped are much less likely to use bicycles—or to be able to use bicycles.  Then the rider has to be close enough to the workplace to make commuting by bike feasible…AND to have access that doesn’t include freeways.  That leaves almost all of us in the County out.  Finally, there needs to be a place to change into office clothes (assuming these are still worn) at the workplace.  Also time and perhaps a place to keep office clothes.

And there is a limit to what can be carried on a bike.  The week’s grocery shopping on the way home?  Other shopping errands?  Not likely.  How much work related material can be hauled?

The bottom line is that it’s possible the whole “bikeway” move in the city will only end up making life more difficult for the majority of us who don’t or can’t use bicycles.

> SANDAG will not hold Board of Director meetings in August, but staff and
> working groups will continue with work.
>
> APG comment to Board: This month we held the first Evacuation Tour with
> SANDAG and Caltrans staff. The potential evacuation routes in the Ramona
> area were thoroughly explored and wildfire hazards such as chimney fire
> burn zones were identified for the group by our local fire behavior expert,
> Dan Summers. The next Evacuation Tour will explore the SR 94 corridor from
> Campo to Jamul; including the dangerous intersection of Otay Lakes and
> Honey Springs Road. The Unincorporated Community values these opportunities
> to partner with SANDAG and Caltrans to share vital boots-on-the-ground
> knowledge in order to develop safe evacuation routes for all travelers in
> the region. Thank you.
>
> *California Transportation Commission (CTC):*
> Two CTC Commissioners introduced themselves and reported that they are
> "the money people" for State and Federal transportation funds.
> Commissioners Clarissa Reyes Falcon and Lee Ann Eager invited Board members
> to attend an upcoming meeting being held in San Diego from August 15-16.
> Website for information:
> https://catc.ca.gov/meetings-events/commission-meetings-2024
>
> *Transnet Oversight Annual Report and Performance Audit and Budget:*
> The overall feedback from the Board to those presenting on Transnet funds
> and projects was that there was a clear lack of information and
> accountability is needed. Cost Benefit Analysis was missing. Staff reported
> miniscule use of the public transportation options and utilization of
> biking or walking - Return On Investment is dismal. SANDAG often quotes the
> maxim that limited funds should be used to help the most people.
> Historically, the Transnet funds are benefitting very few. As of FY 2023,
> total bikeway Program funding was $397.3 million. Transnet funds
> represented $187.2 million (47%) of this spending. The promise of the
> Transnet funds to improve public safety through corridor projects is not
> being met. SANDAG staff's explanation was that the voters had an
> expectation and the funding sources for these projects (of which Transnet
> funds are only one part/source) come with stipulations that are often in
> conflict with what the voters expected. This is the difficult environment
> in which planning and funding for projects exists.
>
> Melanie Burkholder, City of Carlsbad comment: We need cost benefit
> analysis for these Transnet dollar projects.
>
> Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO comment: We are working toward structural change in
> order to provide cost benefit analysis and demonstrate a good use of the
> funds
>
> Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach comment: I know that many people leave
> my city to move east because it is more affordable. This puts more people
> on those roads and they need to be improved.
>
> APG Comment to Board: What are the raw numbers for this conclusion that
> bike ridership has increased 5x? Does this conclusion represent a change
> from 50 to 500 riders, 50 to 5,000? We need to see the numbers. And, do you
> see a slower increase in pedestrian travel than expected due to e-bike
> encounters on pathways?
>
> SANDAG response (Omar Atayee): Those are great questions. We don't have
> those numbers, but will get those to the Board. We don't know if e-bikes
> are impacting our numbers, but we are seeing an increase. I don't know if
> we have data on that.
>
> Dawn Vettes, SANDAG CFO comment: We acknowledge room for improvement and
> are working to strengthen internal controls. Our next audit in 2027 will
> show significant progress.
>
> *SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:*
> In response to a previous Board question about the cost per ride of those
> utilizing the Youth Opportunity Pass, Mario Orso reported .69 cents was the
> average cost.
>
> *Questions from APG members:*
>
> *Question* - Is SANDAG informed of freeway projects in the County? Or,
> are freeway projects strictly a state affair? Does SANDAG have a role in
> the scheduling and decision making?
> *Response* - I am still working on this answer.....
>
> *News:* Link to the Traffic Safety Dashboard
> https://www.sandag.org/trafficsafety. It is located in SANDAG’s Open Data
> Portal.
>
> Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
> SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
> https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors
>
> Report Submitted by:
> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>

body:
Robin and Eileen,
Another sterling recounting. :) 
Unlike  Sisyphus and that darn rock I expect that you will eventually prevail upon the other members to give the unincorporated areas a voting seat . Just a matter of time. 
Story

Sent from the all new AOL app for iOS

On Saturday, February 1, 2025, 3:32 PM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

Good Afternoon APG Members,

Note: The SANDAG Board of Directors held three meetings in the month of January.

SANDAG Leadership Changes - New Officers Elected:
New Chair for SANDAG BOD: Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach
New Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: Joe Lacava, City of San Diego
New Second Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: John Minto, City of Santee

Jan. 10th - APG comment to Board: Good morning. Congratulations on your election as the dream team for the officers. I do represent the unincorporated area, over 500,000 people, and, of course, this seat is not a voting seat. Today I want to note for the record that the County is not present and so, therefore; all action taken by this Board today - voting action - has effectively disenfranchised the Unincorporated Area. We're not present. And, we don't have a vote. And, I hope in 2025, I expect in 2025, that this Board will overall do a better job of ensuring that the Unincorporated Area is not disenfranchised. I realize County being absent is not the fault of the Board, but there must be something in place that takes into account that there's over half a million people who are not participating in the proceedings today. Thank you.
Jan. 31st - APG Comment to the Board: The County of San Diego is not present. However, the people of the County of San Diego are present.(Note: County was completely absent for all of the January 2025 BOD meetings - 10th & 24th & 31st)
SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:
-Mario Orso reported that the CFO was adjusting revenue projections on TransNet funds by a couple of percentage points - between 2 to 4%. This would be a decrease in expected funding and could affect both MTS and NCTD.-The Grand Jury report findings and recommendations came as no surprise as the Office of the Independent Performance Auditor had brought these needed issues and changes to the Board in their earlier report and they are being addressed. 
Otay Mesa East and SR 11 Report:
The Federal agreements with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and with General Services have set the stage for the beginning of construction and the relationship SANDAG will have with CBP. Caltrans is also a partner.If the toll revenues of the Port of Entry are not as projected the shortfall cannot be made up with TransNet funds.
Ann Fox, Caltrans comment: ...We've done the studies that have shown the many dollars and jobs lost and the air pollution created by the long delays along our shared borders. California has invested more than half of the $1.3 billion project cost and has spent hundreds of millions more building out the corridor and the connections we have with State Routes 905 and 125. ...We have built the infrastructure, the new roads, the utilities, the technology, the air quality monitors out there, in addition to over 180 acres of environmental mitigation.
Jack Fisher, City of Imperial Beach comment: (reading Brian Bilbray letter) "... I'm sure some other members will not continue to support the expansion of the economic growth with the environmental damage without addressing historical and future environmental and public health threats caused by such economic development. I ask that every board member here question if their city council or county board would vote for any project knowing its environmental and health problems if it was going to be anywhere close to the disastrous situation that citizens of the South Bay faced everyday?"I can't tell you how frustrated I am because I know with the increased traffic and commerce Mexico will continue to grow. Their population will continue to grow. It was mentioned that just this operation port of entry opening will create 90,000 jobs on the U.S. side. I would imagine that number probably doubles or triples on the Mexico side. Still without the infrastructure. 
TransNet Major Corridor Projects Update: State Route 67:
Sam Amen, Karina Cantera-Angel & Tracy D'Aoust Roberts of Caltrans - presented 3 alternatives for the improvement of SR 67 understanding that evacuation was the highest consideration. Project area is SR 67 from Highland Valley in Ramona to Mapleview in Lakeside. Alternative #1 provides 4 outbound lanes and one inbound lane dedicated to inbound emergency vehicles. Alternatives #2 & #3 provide some of these benefits, but not consistently throughout the project area and include the use of shoulders as "lanes" in an emergency.

APG comment to Board: The Unincorporated Area has been partnering with Caltrans and we thank Sam, Karina, Tracy, Melina, Stephen and Tyler for their dedication. Safety is always first.  Caltrans states, "The primary goal of the SR 67 Highway Improvements Project is to increase capacity during emergencies to significantly reduce evacuation times."  Safety is always first. SANDAG serves over 3.3 million people across the region; however, some benefit more than others. Had SANDAG delivered on the promises of TransNet to the Unincorporated Area - Measure G would have passed. The experience of those patiently awaiting their turn at the Regional funding bucket has been disheartening. 1988 and 2004 turned into a resounding "no" in 2024 for rural communities on Measure G. The LA fires demonstrate a clear and present danger to rural highway travelers - evacuees may live locally or may be visiting from the city. Caltrans has stood ready and willing to deliver highway safety. Alternative #1 delivers on the Promise. Let us immediately put into place emergency widening to move evacuees through the current SR 67 gauntlet of bottlenecks. Safety is always first. SANDAG does not want to be the obstacle to improvements necessary to avoid the catastrophic results of the LA fires. The elected Board members would not want the public to rightfully be able to say that they could have done more to prevent a loss of life and property. Thank you.
Steve Vaus, City of Poway; Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista; Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos; Kevin Shin, City of Carlsbad; Bill Wells, City of El Cajon; John Minto, City of Santee;  & Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar all made comments: All of these city representatives were positive in their comments emphasizing the need to expand SR 67 for evacuation purposes and Mayors Minto, Jones, Wells and Gaasterland specifically endorsed the selection of Alternative #1. There were no comments opposing Caltrans proposed solutions to SR 67. The Board of Directors was supportive.
Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach & SANDAG Chair comment:  "What can we do now?" 
Allan Kosup, Caltrans response: We have an emergency widening project that just began this week on SR 67. The environmental report was received last week and the project was begun immediately. It will be over the next six months. This will provide more space in the event of an evacuation.
APG News:
-Thank you to all who were able to attend our in-person APG meeting held on Saturday, January 4th, 2025. A quorum was established and voting actions were taken.

APG Officers elected for 2025 (one year terms):
Chair, Robin Joy Maxson
Vice Chair, Eileen Delaney
Secretary, Carol Hake

APG Representative to SANDAG Board of Directors (two year terms):
Primary Representative, Robin Joy Maxson
Alternate Representative, Eileen Delaney

APG Representatives to SANDAG Policy Advisory Committees:

Regional Planning Committee:
APG Representative: Ron Nehring
APG Alternate: Kiki Skagen Munshi

Transportation Committee:
APG Representative: Jim Custeau
APG Alternate: Paul Dombkowski

Borders Committee:
APG Representative: Lynne Malinowski
APG Alternate: Harriet Taylor

Public Safety Committee:
APG Representative: Paul Dombkowski
APG Alternate: Eileen Delaney

Audit Committee:
APG Representative: Carol Hake

-Update: Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the unincorporated area in San Diego County - has not set a meeting date with the APG as of this report. Since July, the APG has been working to set up a joint meeting with the Congressman, SANDAG CEO Mario Orso and our APG members without success. SANDAG CEO Mario Orso has stated he will be available and happy to attend our joint meeting. Congressman Issa has not been available and very little communication has come from his office. The APG sent a request to his Chief of Staff, Veronica Smith Wong. She has responded, but not with a set date, yet.

The subject of the meeting will be:
"Transportation funding and safety in the Unincorporated Area; addressing fatality rate on rural highways, safe wildfire evacuation, lack of public transportation resulting in geographic isolation of vulnerable populations and continued diversion of transportation funds from rural highway projects."

Several Planning/Sponsor Groups have already sent letters to Congressman Issa. If any group wishes to contact Issa directly, email his Chief of Staff Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.house.gov

Questions from APG members
No questions received this month.

Links
SANDAG BOD and PAC meetings for calendar 2025:https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3108009/Item_3_-_Revised_2025_Legislative_Calendar.pdf

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from SANDAG's Board of Directors website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

> Good Afternoon APG Members,
>
> *SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
> -Mario Orso reported that the California Air Resources Board (CARB)
> accepted SANDAG's methodology for measuring GHG and, therefore, SANDAG can
> continue with planning.
> -A joint committee meeting between Borders, Regional Plan and
> Transportations committees to present the Regional Plan. On track to meet
> GHG and air quality conformity targets. This keeps funds flowing to SANDAG,
> the region and the city.
> -Congratulated North County Transit District for 30 years of service.
>
> *Economic and Budget Outlook:*
> Job growth is slowing. Sales tax revenue is down. Source of project funds:
> State 37%, Federal 36%, TransNet 16%, Other Local Funds 11%.
>
> Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: ...."We are in turbulent
> times....And, I would really encourage us to be incredibly careful and
> conservative as we go forward into the next six months of our budgeting..."
>
> APG Comment to Board: My question is on the job gains and losses forecast.
> I have two questions. What consideration was given to the impacts of AI on
> the professional, technology, transportation and housing sectors? And, my
> second question is do you anticipate a reduction in healthcare sector jobs
> as restrictions on our immigration policy take effect? And, the reason I
> ask that is that over the last few years the State of California had opened
> up Medi-Cal coverage for all who are financially eligible, regardless of
> immigration status. In the County of San Diego one-third of the population
> receives this coverage. So, that would be a substantial change in
> healthcare.
>
> Naomi Young, SANDAG: I think you mentioned all important factors that can
> be a source of a drag on our economy and our job creation. We didn't do a
> forecast on jobs, we just presented how 2024's data on unemployment has
> ended. Well what we saw between 2023 and 2024, looking at where we've seen
> the sector impacts and the job growth in 2024 is what makes us think that
> 2025 will be more of a slow job creation environment rather than a
> rebound...the message is volatility, differences in local conditions from
> the national and that there are some very strong potential headwinds that
> give us cause for caution.
>
> *SR-125 Toll Operations Update:*
> SANDAG is actively supporting legislation to assist the implementation of
> SANDAG Board Resolution 2023-11, "Declaring support of eliminating the debt
> and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027."
>
> *TransNet Regional Transportation Congestion Improvement Program Proposed
> (RTCIP) Fee Adjustment:*
> SANDAG approved this yearly fee adjustment to be 6% effective FY beginning
> July 1, 2025. This 6% increase in RTCIP fees is to keep pace with the cost
> of building the roadway infrastructure needed as housing increases. The fee
> is collected by each of the 18 cities and the County as part of building
> fees paid by the private sector for each new housing unit. Fee will
> increase from $2875.06 to $3047.57, per unit.
>
> *County Representation of Unincorporated Communities:*
> -The February 14th SANDAG Board meeting was the fourth consecutive
> meeting without a County Supervisor present.
> -The February 28th meeting was the first time unincorporated communities
> had SANDAG voting representation in 2025.
> -SANDAG BOD commented as follows:
>
> *-From the February 14th meeting:*
> APG Comment to Board: Good morning. I had hoped by now that we would have
> representation from the County here. And, I see empty chairs, so I won't
> belabor that point. I have a suggestion. Is this Board able to propose an
> action such as a censure because I have seen that done recently at a city
> when the Board member is not fulfilling their obligations. Is that
> something that could be considered on behalf of the over 500,000 people who
> were not represented here by a vote today? Thank you.
>
> Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: I can look into that. I know we have an
> attendance policy where I know letters can be sent and they're encouraged
> to attend and follow up. But, I'll look into specifically whether a censure
> can be, I'm not sure it's specifically in our policy as it exists now, but
> I will double check.
>
> *-From the February 28th meeting:*
> Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: I would like to, since the last
> three meetings, I'm glad to see Supervisor Anderson here today. But the
> last three meetings, the County had zero representation for over 500,000 in
> the unincorporated areas. And, I would like to see if it's possible to move
> forward with having that as a voting member, because a lot of our land use
> decisions, and maybe it would be something at the planning level or the
> regional planning and then only on land use decisions. I don't know what
> that would look like. I'm just, I'm very concerned that there is a
> possibility and it's happened now for three meetings. We didn't have any
> actual action items, but it would be good to have someone that represents
> them as a voting member. And, so I'd just like staff to move it.
>
> Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: Yes, for the issue of them becoming a voting
> member. That would require a change to legislation. So that is something
> that could go to the Executive Committee. And, then ultimately to the
> Board. But we need a sponsor to change that by legislation since the voting
> members are set in our enabling legislation at the Public Utilities Code.
>
> Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO: I also want to highlight that on the legislative
> report. We reported that there was a hold bill, a place bill by Senator
> Jones. And, actively being promoted by Supervisor Anderson. Of looking into
> this issue.  (Mayor Rebecca Jones: "As a voting member?") We're having the
> discussion. We haven't seen the total write up. But that's kind of what's
> being indicated to us.
>
> Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos: Yeah, that would definitely support
> something like that. So maybe Supervisor Anderson, if we could maybe keep
> the board members updated on that because I would certainly support
> something like that. It is just a shame that we have a situation where some
> land use things really do affect our unincorporated areas....Personally, I
> think it would be very beneficial to our outlying communities.
>
> Joel Anderson, County of San Diego comment: I just want to make a
> clarification. I'm an alternate. And, my colleagues have all those
> positions. So, over the last four and a half years I've made 99% of the
> meetings. So, I'm sorry. They appointed themselves. They choose not to
> come. That's not on me. But I try to fill in for them as often as possible.
> And, we do have a bill. But it's not going to move forward until everyone
> on this committee agrees that's what they want. There's not fanciness
> going. But we're very lucky to have Robin here. She lives in the
> unincorporated. I think that this Board should look and see whether the
> County deserves to have a vote at all at SANDAG; because all we're doing is
> doubling down on cities where all my colleagues live. And nobody, if I
> wasn't on this board, would be representing with a vote from the
> unincorporated. And, to your point, it's 600,000 people they are without a
> vote. And while we have cities. They are much smaller. That have a vote.
> And I think if we want to pass a bond. We need to think about being
> inclusive. And, including everybody at the table. Thank you.
>
> APG Comment to Board: Thank you. To follow up on Mayor Jones and
> Supervisor Anderson. We are a large unrepresented area as far as the level
> of representation that's around the table. But as legislation works its way
> and the Executive Committee starts to review. The unincorporated area needs
> to have a full vote. Anything less is not really respectful of the citizens
> who are living in the unincorporated areas. It is not as if when you buy a
> house, you go, is this a city? And, am I going to be represented at SANDAG
> the way other city folks are or am I in an unincorporated area? It is
> generally not a consideration at all. No one even knows that they're not in
> a city. Until they say, I'm unhappy and I want to go down to City Hall.
> And, I say well, I'd like to see that place. Tell me when you find it.
> Because there isn't a City Hall. We have the County. But the unincorporated
> area needs to be part of the conversation. So many conversations that go on
> at SANDAG - in other areas - about full representation of voting. Please be
> sure that we're included.  And, thank you.
>
> Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: Yes, thank you. I just want to
> say that I strongly support that we pursue the ability to vote. Alpine,
> Boulevard, Campo, Lake Moreno, Crest, Dehesea, Granite Hills, Harbison
> Canyon, Descanso, Fallbrook, Jamal, Julian, Lakeside, Pine Valley, Potrero,
> Rainbow, Ramona, San Dieguito, Spring Valley, Sweetwater, Valle De Oro,
> Valley Center, Bonsall, Borrego Springs, Jacumba, and Twin Oaks Valley. I
> wanted to read these names because when I first moved here 22 years ago. I
> was totally surprised when I learned that Ramona, Borrego Springs, these
> towns really had no representation at this level; had no city council or
> town council. I learned a lot in my first couple of years moving to San
> Diego County. I would suggest that we as a Board make strong and just clear
> and simple moves. I even wonder if there is something we could do as an
> amendment to SB 10? I just don't know. But I would suggest that we find a
> way to, in a streamlined way, give a vote to the 600,000 people who have
> these planning groups and have taken such a positive step forward. And, I
> have a question. What is the weight of the County's vote? Is it these
> 600,000?
>
> Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO: Amberlin can probably answer it better. I don't,
> can't give you the exact answer. So I know she tracks this all the time.
> (Mayor Terry Gaasterland: We can look it up, but maybe you can remind us
> when you have it.)
>
> *San Diego LOSSAN Rail Realignment Project:*
> The realignment of the rail connection between San Diego and San Luis
> Obispo does not normally impact the unincorporated area, but one of the
> proposed alignments would. Infrequently, it is mentioned that the rail
> connection should be relocated to follow the I-15. The Department of
> Defense maintains a controlling interest in the rail location as it is
> considered part of the military infrastructure utilized to move troops and
> equipment throughout the country. Discussion of the new rail location is

> Committee (PAC) membership requests except for the Audit Committee

On Feb 26, 2024, at 8:41 AM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - February 2024

Caltrans:
Roy Abboud and Allan Kosup - A Disaster Declaration from the President would release funds for highway repairs due to the recent rainstorms. Highway 78 has experienced significant damage in several locations. Preventing damage from rainstorms is a shared responsibility as the "system of streams, trash, trees, plants, and encampments" all contribute to water overflow and runoff. Caltrans, cities and counties share responsibility to clear creeks, but Federal and State permits to legally clear out stream beds are difficult to procure.

125 Toll Road Action Plan:
Feb. 9th meeting Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG would be presenting an action plan for the 125 Toll Road at the February 13th City of Chula Vista Council meeting. This presentation would include the impact to other projects with respect to available funds if the payoff date for the toll road was moved up. If the community wishes to see a sooner payoff date for the toll road they would need to understand that this money will come from other projects.
-APG Question to Board - First, will the Sweetwater Community Planning Group be receiving the same presentation on the toll road that the City of Chula Vista will receive? And second, regarding determination of the end date for the toll road - is there consideration of the increased use of surface streets to bypass the toll road and the danger this presents to the community?

-SANDAG Response (Nora Vargas) - This is the biggest issue in Bonita! The County will be sponsoring a community meeting for all parties in the area.
-SANDAG Response (Coleen Clementson) And, yes, we are considering surface street impacts.
Feb. 23rd meeting Carolina Chavez made a motion to, "Declare support for eliminating the debt and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027." Board consensus was for staff to explore the feasibility of this date as this would be the earliest date that the payoff could be made without penalty.

Report of SANDAG Draft 2025 Regional Plan:
Susan Huntington, Antoinette Meier, Ray Majors and Allan Kosup continued their presentation of an initial concept of the Draft 2025 Regional Plan. Greenhouse gas reduction needs to be reduced by 18.9% by the year 2035. Goals are:
Improve transit frequency and hours of operation.
Implement pricing strategies
Expand Youth Opportunity Pass
Provide parking by transit
Funding for these projects comes from 40 different sources: Federal, State and Local
Budget begins with funds leftover from previous Plan
Review of current and future funding sources to determine viability of covering a Plan budget range of $139 to $162 billion.
Clarified that managed lanes are only on the interstate/highway system
-NCTD reported a new microtransit/flexible fleet initiative was starting and Fallbrook/Pala would be one of the first areas to pilot this program. No additional details available at this time.
-APG Question to Board - First, what is the priority for wildfire evacuation improvements? And second, regarding the greenhouse gas reduction goal for 2035 and the use of reduced VMTs to meet that goal - the unincorporated area has a new generation of youth who have not yet developed a driving habit. Microtransit and useful bus routes/times implemented in the next year or two is an opportunity to redirect future drivers into GHG friendly travel modes. How soon will these options be made available?

SANDAG Response - Express bus routes from unincorporated communities are being implemented soon.

SANDAG Roadside Service:
General discussion on the increased cost for this program since SANDAG began running operations. Request for a breakdown and clarification of budget items to effectively monitor and provide oversight of the program. Need statistics to see if a full tow truck is required to be the responding vehicle for every freeway breakdown.

Inland Rail Trail (bike path):
Update on Phases 3 and 4 of this bike path from Escondido to Oceanside. Many Board members noted that this was an example of another expenditure that did not benefit those in the unincorporated areas of the County.

Airport Transit Connection:
Update on the progress of the new plan for moving people from the SD Airport to downtown and other destinations. Extensive public comment and Board comments on the unnecessary expense of building an elevated "people mover" platform to transport people from the Airport to downtown as trolleys and buses were already in existence. Also, people should be able to move about all of the County, not just the coastal areas. Overall, this plan is a substantial change from the multi-billion dollar Central Mobility Hub vision of former Executive Director, Hasan Ikhrata.

SANDAG Retreat 2024:
The SANDAG Board of Directors March 8th meeting will be a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative and Alternate plan to attend.

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

> Good Evening APG Members,
>
> *SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
> -We are looking at SB 375 and whether or not the use of VMT as a metric is
> really effective. Should we be using these metrics in our Regional Plans or
> doing something different?
> -Regarding the new Otay Mesa East Port of Entry we discussed with the
> Mexican government the topic of Mexico setting up a trust fund to hold some
> of the revenue from their side as funds to be used for environmental issues
> such as the Tijuana River issue.
> -Fewer sole source contracts are being awarded.
> -The 4 major California MPOs (representing 80% of state population) met in
> Sacramento to discuss shared issues: Housing, Transportation, CARB,
> Caltrans and specifically SB 375 and the need to double down on VMTs as a
> way to create a better environment.
> -We are following Assemblyman DeMaio's AB 24 (
> https://legiscan.com/CA/bill/AB24/2025)  and State Senator Jones' SB 240 (
> https://legiscan.com/CA/bill/SB240/2025) bills on structural changes to
> the SANDAG Board in order to bring a vote for the unincorporated area. We
> will discuss this at our next Executive Committee meeting.
>
> Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: We need a voting seat as the
> rural needs are very different from the cities.
>
> *Proposed Rapid Bus Routes:*
> -Unincorporated communities that utilize the northern section of I-15 for
> travel will benefit from this new bus route.
> -New Rapid Bus Route 483 to connect San Diego County (San Marcos) with
> Riverside County (Temecula) via the I-15 has a survey available for the
> public to indicate important stops along the proposed route. Survey is open
> until April 23rd. https://engage.sandag.org/Rapid483survey
>
> *Downtown Stopover Program:*
> This project for MTS bus drivers to have a dedicated safe and clean break
> area in downtown San Diego utilizes TransNet funds. At present $37M has
> been spent acquiring land. Staff presented a plan which includes completing
> SANDAG's purchase of a complete city block - of which 2/3 is already
> purchased - and planning a building for the bus driver's stopovers in
> downtown that could also be a multi-use building operated by SANDAG. The
> total project cost is $67M. TransNet funds supply 41% of this cost.
>
> APG comment to Board: I'm an extremely budget conscious person. And, you
> already own half the block, which is parking lots, so there is no building
> in the way. Is there a reason you cannot walk across the street to Columbia
> Tower; rent an apartment that would be nice for a break room, would have
> bathrooms, it would have a rest area because it could have one bedroom and
> you also have kitchen facilities there.  We're not in the business of
> operating and running facilities. That is what I would do with the
> taxpayer's money. You have a nice parking area there. On one whole side of
> the block - plenty of space for the buses - both for egress and ingress.
> And then you walk across the street and you go to the Columbia Tower and
> you go up to your dedicated break room apartment. It's already there. Is
> there any reason why that can't be done? Thank you.
>
> *Draft FY 2026 Program Budget:*
> The proposed budget is $1.3B which is the same from the previous fiscal
> year. Sources are Federal, State, TransNet and Other Local Funds. SANDAG is
> different from cities in that it budgets by project versus by department.
> The budget reflects money to be spent in a specific year and not the total
> cost of projects as projects go through several phases on the path to
> completion. For a project to be part of the budget it must be a part of the
> Regional Plan. The Federal portion of the budget is unstable in the current
> political climate. The Youth Opportunity Pass is funded only to the end of
> FY 2026.
>
> APG comment to Board: I was hoping to hear that the Youth Opportunity Pass
> was going to be expanding, not contracting. I am concerned, and somewhat
> alarmed, that this is the last fiscal year the Youth Opportunity Pass
> program will be funded. Will flexible fleets or micro transit be expanded?
> What will SANDAG do to support the non-driving, GHG-friendly youth of the
> rural and unincorporated areas? How will we provide a path to opportunity
> and success within the larger region for our low income and
> geographically-disadvantaged youth? As an idea - using my Columbia Tower
> apartment break room suggestion as a way to save funds on the Downtown
> Stopover Bus project would provide savings that could fund the Youth
> Opportunity Pass for our children.
>
> *APG News:*
> -Additional PAC Report Information: Jim Custeau, APG's Representative to
> the SANDAG Transportation Committee asked the following question of the
> SANDAG Mobility Working Group: I attended the March 21st meeting, during
> which there was a presentation (Item #7 on the agenda) titled "Flexible
> Fleets Pilot Grant Program Call for Projects". This pilot project grant
> opportunity struck me as having the potential of having a positive impact
> on our planning group/sponsor group area residents with much needed public
> transportation access - particularly in our more economically disadvantaged
> zones. I see that you are all members of the SANDAG Mobility Working Group.
> I'm curious how County staff plan on soliciting input from our various
> planning/sponsor groups in preparation for potential grant proposal
> submittals to SANDAG.
>
> Response from Mobility Working Group: The Flexible Fleets Pilot Grant
> Program could present a good opportunity to improve transportation access,
> especially in disadvantaged communities.
>
> At this stage, SANDAG is still soliciting feedback on the *draft grant
> eligibility criteria*—the Call for Projects has not been released yet.
> One of the key considerations SANDAG is currently focused on is ensuring
> projects have a plan for ongoing funding and sustainability beyond the
> initial pilot.
>
> Once the final criteria and application materials are released, we’ll have
> a better sense of potential project ideas and the process for gathering
> input from planning and sponsor groups. We’ll stay tuned as this develops
> and share updates as appropriate.
>
> -Update: Conversion of our APG "Advisory" Board seat to a "Voting" Board
> seat - State Assemblyman Carl DeMaio held a press conference on March 21st
> to discuss his bill to include the APG as a voting member. Both Robin Joy
> Maxson and Eileen Delaney attended. Also, upon the recommendation of
> SANDAG Board Member, Terry Gaasterland, the APG has reached out to State
> Senator Catherine Blakespear, requesting her assistance with the change in
> voting status for unincorporated area residents. We are in contact with
> Blakespear and will work with her Chief of Staff, Jack Christensen.
>
> -Update: Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the
> unincorporated area in San Diego County - will be holding two events for
> Community Planning Groups. One will be for CPGs in the East and one for
> those in the North. The APG made it clear to Congressional Field
> Representative, Alan Pellicani, that these CPG meetings are considered
> separate events from the APG's request for a meeting between the
> Congressman, SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso, and APG leaders. That meeting
> continues to be a future event.
