> Report to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County (APG)
> On July 16th the first scheduled evacuation tour for SANDAG and Caltrans
> staff was held in the Ramona area. Currently in the planning stages is an
> evacuation tour for the SR 94 area.
>
> APG's representative on the SANDAG Board of Directors, Robin Joy Maxson,
> extended an invitation to SANDAG and Caltrans staff to participate in a
> tour of the expected routes for evacuation in the event of a wildfire or
> other emergency. Maxson emphasised the importance of experiencing the
> evacuation routes in-person in order to accurately evaluate the routes for
> safety and viability in an emergency.
>
> Roadways examined were Wildcat Canyon, SR 67, Highland Valley Road and SR
> 78.
>
> Issues considered and discussed were:
> - Shelter-in-place orders and the likelihood of evacuees choosing to heed
> evacuation orders. Visitors will most likely choose to leave the area.
> - Physical constraints to safe and effective evacuation,  e.g., present
> roadway design, traffic bottlenecks due to changes in the number of lanes
> and/or their configuration.
> - The presence of deadly chimney effect fires and other geographical
> hazards to evacuee safety.
> - Residents and visitors vary in familiarity with the roadways.
> - Fluctuation in the numbers of evacuees on any given day as the number of
> residents is not a static indicator of how many people may need to
> evacuate; the number of weekend visitors to the area greatly expands the
> number of evacuees.
>  - Types of vehicles utilized during an evacuation in rural areas have
> historically been large vehicles/trucks and many vehicle/trailer
> combinations in order to evacuate livestock.
> - The unpredictability of fire during a firestorm created by the combined
> conditions of high temperatures, dry fuel and high winds.
>
> Local fire behavior expert, Dan Summers, identified and explained to the
> group the behavior of fire as it relates to evacuees safety during an
> evacuation event on these four routes. Evacuees are exposed to:
> - Oxygen deprivation which also deprives combustion engine vehicles of the
> oxygen required to operate.
> - Extreme heat which impairs human judgement.
> - Chimney effect fires which are corridors in the landscape where heavy
> brush and trees combine to create a rapid, deadly, blistering, upward burn
> path.
>
> The tour was educational as attendees shared their knowledge of roadway
> construction, fire behavior and human behavior during a crisis.
> Attendees were:
>
> Robin Joy Maxson, Chair, Association of Planning Groups and Representative
> on the SANDAG Board of Directors
> Dan Summers, Former County of San Diego Fire Advisory Board and
> Fire/Paramedic Technology Instructor

Subject: [External]Re: Questions on Planning Group Procedure

EXTERNAL: This email originated from outside of the organization. Do not click any links or open any attachments unless you trust the sender and know the content is safe.

Good afternoon Brian,

The applicant and county will make a presentation about the project.  That will be followed by public comment, so during the agenda item G.2.  During public comment members of the public will have the opportunity to speak for up to 3 minutes.  During that time they can provide questions that they have, however, it will not be a Q & A session.  Normally once all public comment is completed the group will have the county/applicant provide answers to the questions posed by the public and/or questions that the group has for the county/applicant.  I expect we will follow a similar process at tomorrow's meeting.

The planning group is an advisory board only.  We make recommendations (ie approve, not approve, or approve with conditions).  The county takes those recommendations into consideration, but our recommendations are not binding.  Planning groups are also public forums where members of the public can speak about projects and the county takes note of the public comments received.

I believe this project would have any final approvals made at the county of San Diego Planning Commission.  That is a 7 member board appointed by the County Board of Supervisors.  For reference, the feedback I have received is that this project would not be going in front of the Planning Commission till later this year, likely in the fall at earliest.

I would recommend that if you have specific questions it would be productive to bring the questions in writing and provide it to the applicant or the group during your public comment and ask that they be answered during the meeting.

I hope this helps.  Please let me know if you have any other questions.

On Sun, Jan 21, 2024 at 9:06 PM Steffen, Bree N <Bree.Steffen@charter.com<mailto:Bree.Steffen@charter.com>> wrote:
Hi Travis! I’m a TV reporter for Spectrum News. The station is based in LA, but I live in and cover San Diego County for them! I’m working on a TV story on the Alpine County Park and the lawsuit that was just filed to stop it. I have an interview with someone on-camera who is against the park, but I am trying to find someone to interview on-camera who can talk about why they support it, so the story is balanced! I was chatting with the County, and since they are not allowed to comment on pending litigation, they thought you might be a good option for an interview since you spoke in favor of the project! If you are willing, we would just meet at the site and look around and talk about why it would be good for the community and why you support it! I shouldn’t need more than half hour or so, and this would be an on-camera pre-recorded interview that we would schedule sometime in February!

Let me know if you are interested, and if you are not, if you know of any other Alpine residents who support the project who might talk to me! Thank you so much!!!! Have a great night!

--
Bree Steffen
Multimedia Journalist
310-413-0224
bree.steffen@charter.com<mailto:bree.steffen@charter.com>

body:
Carlos,
We would very much appreciate You, the general manager of Sweetwater
Authority speaking to the community of Alpine for the proposed trail
enhancements. To my knowledge, the FOLR group has no official ties to SWA,
yet in a carefully worded FB post makes it sound as if they are Sharing in
the 750K trail enhancement grant...not just the information regarding it!
FOLR does not necessarily represent the opinions nor interest of Alpine
residents, but instead seems to be using this platform by jumping on the
bandwagon and pretending to be an affiliated entity.
Alpine would certainly prefer to hear any proposed Loveland improvement
ideas straight from You, the actual source, rather than 2nd hand
information!
Thank you for your time and involving the Alpine community for our input!

Elisa Peskin
Japatul resident 24 years

>
>
> ---------- Forwarded message ---------
> From: Ron Nehring, Crest Planning Group Chairman <
> ronnehring@ronnehring.ccsend.com>
> Date: Mon, Jan 27, 2025 at 3:26 PM
> Subject: PLANNING GROUP: What we have done so far on wildfire
> To: <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com>
>
>
> Fellow Planning Group Chairs,
>
>
> Following the interest and feedback I received regarding our new Firewise
> USA site, I wanted to share additional resources and insights from our work
> on wildfire preparedness and evacuation in our subregion. I’m also
> interested in knowing what work your Planning Group has done that perhaps
> we have not thought of so we can strengthen our efforts.
>
>
> In 2021, our Planning Group established a dedicated working group on
> wildfire and evacuation. Over the course of three years, we held meetings
> and engaged extensively with stakeholders—including our local fire
> district, Cal Fire, the Crest Fire Safe Council, representatives from the
> County, the Sheriff’s Department, and others—to identify the most effective
> ways to reduce wildfire risk and enhance evacuation capacity.
>
>
> This effort culminated in a comprehensive package of seven
> wildfire-related resolutions, which our Planning Group unanimously adopted
> in the summer of 2024. Given our advisory role to the County of San Diego,
> each resolution is framed as a recommendation to County. You can review the
> full package of resolutions, along with a summary, here: Crest Planning
> Group Fire Resolutions.
> <https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJVShatP__5WDqsOxEzOSLt0N1DkC0uglT12fnpaypLueU2s1G3PpLX2QIxvykqsJlEMDcC2miEM8Bqv622WJ-69pcxx7i8NhOTmgjqk0B0mJfPKWnaIxBjT80ovcsz0UKyYqnOwPhYVdrhyFb7VvbHFgfL3SukQfI6qrOJzATK-R_tAmMvo4ITcM4-w9Z2LD4LLQyr3L6ijIc_JBgR4xPXZ5jMCN4IXalwne9xF64Dap01AmRYnkT7NxXK9j5oEi_w==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>
>
>
> One key takeaway from our work was the value of the Firewise USA program
> <https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyDxoyackA2RcQNTEfRlDPkbHmX2MuO8PBPswQ8KgE-rcyjYWxx1MCWnw0BK9QNwVPRmMPe--vv-_HOnhwjgONujomYHLomm1G-istWt-z54Z9ytb_uSjY54cNszAN2-4h6nrYtrH8BE9W20iK5zGCgg==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>,
> which allows groups of at least eight homeowners to establish a Firewise
> USA site, take steps to reduce wildfire risk, and potentially qualify for
> homeowners insurance discounts.
>
>
> Recognizing its benefits, one of our seven resolutions specifically
> encourages and supports the formation of Firewise USA sites throughout our
> subregion.
>
>
> After I became Chairman of our Planning Group, we launched a website to
> better serve our residents by providing access to essential information.
> While the County’s webpage for our Planning Group exists, it is difficult
> to find and lacks comprehensive resources. Our goal was to create a one-stop
> hub where residents can find details about our Planning Group’s work,
> wildfire preparedness, code enforcement, defensible space requirements, and
> more. You can visit the site at: CrestPlanningGroup.com
> <https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyNiKG57PrvAcVhxPjLGUulw37A996ASKMyLn1vsnrei-gZWKYuy2livonBtHIF9k9VG_wnP-b7EVEi0hg9ftQc50vEBE2M1Z12ueCdNq6VOI=&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>
> .
>
>
> At our next Planning Group meeting on Monday, February 10 at 6:30 PM at
> the Crest Community Association Clubhouse, 113 North Park Drive, El Cajon
> <https://www.google.com/maps/search/113+North+Park+Drive,+El+Cajon?entry=gmail&source=g>
> we will discuss the Firewise USA program and how to establish additional
> sites in our subregion. I invite you to join us for this discussion—if you
> or members of your Planning Group plan to attend, please let me know in
> advance so I can ensure you are introduced. Google maps

Attached are documents pertaining to a Discretionary Permit for PDS2024-MUP-24-003 Major Use Permit.  If you normally receive a plot plan, it will be delivered through regular mail within the next few days.
Pursuant to Board Policy I-1,
(https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/cob/docs/policy/I-1.pdf), this request for a recommendation is being sent to you because a discretionary permit application has been submitted to Planning & Development Services (PDS) for a project within your Community/Design Review Area.  Once a recommendation is made, please forward it to PDS with Form #534 so the recommendation can be included in correspondence to the project applicant and as part of the staff report for the appropriate hearing body of officer.

Every effort should be made to submit a group recommendation within seven calendar days following the CPG/DRB/CSG meeting.

If you have any questions or comments regarding PDS2024-MUP-24-003, please reach out to Enrique Aponte directly at (619) 539-6946 or email at enrique.aponte@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:enrique.aponte@sdcounty.ca.gov>. If for any reason the project is reassigned, Enrique Aponte will reach out and provide an updated point of contact for the project.

> Good Afternoon APG Members,

> "Remember, a childhood is a limited opportunity. Use it well!"

> ---------- Forwarded message ---------
> From: Michael V Garcia <Michael.Garcia@sandag.org>
> Date: Tue, Apr 1, 2025 at 1:01 PM
> Subject: On behalf of SANDAG CEO Mario Orso: Legislative Update
> To:
> Cc: Clerk of the Board <clerkoftheboard@sandag.org>
>
>
> Dear Members of the Board,
>
> As mentioned at the Board of Directors meeting last Friday, I wanted to
> provide an update on two pieces of legislation recently introduced in the
> state legislature that, if enacted, would modify the composition of the
> SANDAG Board of Directors:
>
> *AB 24 (DeMaio)*
> This bill, introduced by Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, proposes modifying
> the SANDAG Board of Directors by removing one of the two County Board of
> Supervisors seats and replacing it with a representative from the San Diego
> County Association of Planning Groups. It would also require the remaining
> County Board representative to be from an unincorporated area of the
> county. The bill has been double-referred to the Assembly Local Government
> Committee and the Assembly Transportation Committee. It currently does not
> have a scheduled hearing date.
>
> *SB 240 (Jones)*
> This bill, introduced by Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, proposes to
> replace the secondary representative from the County Board of Supervisors
> with a resident from an unincorporated area of the County, as selected by a
> majority of the county’s community planning groups, to serve a 1-year term.
> The bill also eliminates the requirement that one Board of Supervisors
> member be from a substantially incorporated district and the other from an
> unincorporated district. This bill has not yet been referred to a policy
> committee in the Senate.
>
> We will continue to monitor these bills and provide you with updates
> accordingly.
>
> Thank you,
> Mario
>

> provide an update on two pieces of legislation recently introduced in the
> state legislature that, if enacted, would modify the composition of the
> SANDAG Board of Directors:
>
> *AB 24 (DeMaio)*
> This bill, introduced by Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, proposes modifying
> the SANDAG Board of Directors by removing one of the two County Board of
> Supervisors seats and replacing it with a representative from the San Diego
> County Association of Planning Groups. It would also require the remaining
> County Board representative to be from an unincorporated area of the
> county. The bill has been double-referred to the Assembly Local Government
> Committee and the Assembly Transportation Committee. It currently does not
> have a scheduled hearing date.
>
> *SB 240 (Jones)*
> This bill, introduced by Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, proposes to
> replace the secondary representative from the County Board of Supervisors
> with a resident from an unincorporated area of the County, as selected by a
> majority of the county’s community planning groups, to serve a 1-year term.
> The bill also eliminates the requirement that one Board of Supervisors
> member be from a substantially incorporated district and the other from an
> unincorporated district. This bill has not yet been referred to a policy
> committee in the Senate.
>
> We will continue to monitor these bills and provide you with updates
> accordingly.
>
> Thank you,
> Mario
>

title: RE_ Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine.eml
subject: RE: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine
body:
Good morning,

Thank you for your continued coordination with our Objective Design Standards (ODS) project. As discussed, State laws that are already in effect require that any housing developments eligible for streamlining approval be reviewed with clear, objective standards regarding design aspects such as materials, colors, etc. Typically, these would be projects that include affordable housing units.  Design standards that are not objective cannot be applied to these projects.

To ensure we have objective design standards available for any potential applications, our team used your existing Design Review Checklist as a template to create an Objective Design Review Checklist that clarifies any subjective language and maintains the visual integrity of housing developments in your community. We kindly request your group send any feedback on the checklist by August 15th, 2024.

The Objective Design Review Checklist will serve as a supplemental form for projects eligible for streamlined approval under state law. It will not replace the current Design Review Checklist<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/drb/AlpineDesignReviewChecklistFINAL1.pdf>, which will continue to apply to projects not eligible for the streamlined review. While no applications for this streamlined process have been submitted in your Community Planning Area, the Objective Design Review Checklist will be applicable if one is received. We are finalizing this Objective Design Review Checklist and will make it easily accessible online for potential applications eligible for these State laws.

Attached is the draft Objective Design Review version of your community’s existing Design Review Checklist, and a map delineating potentially eligible areas for this streamlined process. A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates a proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.  There are additional details in the original e-mail below.

We will work to incorporate your suggestions into the checklist which will be accessible on our website in Fall 2024. While there is some flexibility to make changes in the future, staff availability and allocation may make it challenging to respond urgently to suggestions for edits after that date. Therefore, please ensure you submit any requests for modifications by August 15th, 2024, so your feedback can be incorporated into the checklist before it is made available online.

Please let us know if you have any questions as you review the document. We appreciate your continued collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

[cid:image001.png@01DA7ABA.EF015A80]<http://www.sdcpds.org/>
Luis Duran
Planner III | Planning & Development Services | Long Range Planning
County of San Diego | 5510 Overland Ave. Suite 310 | San Diego, CA 92123|
• (619) 214-4698  |  • Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov>

From: Duran, Luis
Sent: Friday, March 22, 2024 4:03 PM
To: travislyonacpg@gmail.com
Subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine

Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

body:
Nicholas Brust

Deputy District Director

CA Senator Brian Jones

Good Morning, Mr. Brust,

Thank you for working on this meeting for the trails and other Loveland community priorities, such as fish restocking, reasonable public access hours that server working people and families, and a balance of recreation and wildlife protection in conjunction with water storage policies.

I would like to add that some things are not allowed : 

1}Contractors interested in bidding projects are excluded from steering the proposals.

2)Proposals that push AB 1O2 funds through any brand, for instance, a nonprofit or commercial interest.

One exception might be costs associated with paperwork or title work/  an escrow to incorporate the SDGE easements into public access trails. 

What I would like to suggest:

1) Before the meeting: Clarity from Congressman Issa's office on the legality and restoration of  Forest Service easement-protected hours of Sunrise to Sunset and the encumbrance of the fishing program on Sweetwater's minimum pool. 

2) Invite an SDGE public affairs specialist to discuss the public use of the  Sunrise Powerlink easement roads at Loveland.

3) A neutral subject matter expert contractor on trails, fishing infrastructure,  and other related matters who is in an advisory role only and will not unduly steer or bid on proposals.

4) Participation from a  Regional Waterboards  permitting expert to help define or give feedback on impacts that water regulation standards will or won’t have on our proposals. Confusion on these matters has been stifling in previous meetings.

5) A rubric for choosing proposals created by the Loveland stakeholders in attendance or designed by Mr. Jantz with consideration for feedback from Sweetwater Authority and Loveland advocates/stakeholders.

Please let me know if I can assist you or others in Senator Jones's office with this important meeting. 

Appreciatively,

Russell Walsh

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Erica Wolski <ewolski@rmwd.org>
Date: Sun, Jan 19, 2025 at 11:08 AM
Subject: upcoming PSPS event - potentially dangerous over 3500 feet

Hi all
I am not sure how widely SDGE spreads this info so I thought we might want to put it out to the Assoc of Planning Groups, the Backcountry Chamber Coalition or our local social media in case any of those residents are in the area of concern. School districts, water districts, the County gets this info. But just because the county gets the info, doesn't mean it reaches the right people (as we learned in Dec). 
SDGE is predicting hurricane force winds in some areas of the county Monday night/Tuesday. Temperature above 3500 feet is going to be 28 to 30 deg F overnight with a wind chill that brings it down to the low teens. The backcountry areas may experience power outages starting Monday night and due to another smaller event coming Thurs/Fri, may not get restored until Friday/Saturday. SDGE is planning to provide more resources to the affected areas.
Seniors, disabled, low income residents, etc should be encouraged to contact 211 (858-300-1211). SDGE can provide both transportation to a hotel and a free hotel room stay if you have no source of heat during the outage. 211 flyer link (I have also attached in a zip file in English and Spanish): S2350023-WFS-AFN-Flyer_FINAL_DIGITAL.pdf   
My suggested social media post along with the two 211 graphics:
"SDGE is predicting Public Safety Power Shutoffs, or PSPS, in the backcountry areas of San Diego County between Mon Jan 20 and Wed Jan 22. Weather is predicted to be dangerously cold overnight below freezing at elevations above 3,500 feet. SDGE is encouraging affected residents in the outage area over 3,500 feet to take advantage of the resources that can be provided by 211 to seniors, people with disabilities and low-income residents. 211 can provide transportation, free hotel stays and other resources:Public Safety Power Shutoff - 211  Note that if 211 does not connect, please call the alternate number 858-300-1211. "
Note that residents near the Mexican border need to call the 858# instead of 211.
PS: Downtown Ramona should be fine - they said they learned from the Dec event the importance of trying to keep the Creelman substation fed with power either via other transmission or a generator. So while transmission may be affected, they are not predicting a community wide outage like Dec, only the "fringes" of Ramona.
Erica

General Manager

Ramona Municipal Water District

Cell: (760) 877-9247

www.rmwd.org

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Michael V Garcia <Michael.Garcia@sandag.org>
Date: Tue, Apr 1, 2025 at 1:01 PM
Subject: On behalf of SANDAG CEO Mario Orso: Legislative Update
To:
Cc: Clerk of the Board <clerkoftheboard@sandag.org>

Dear Members of the Board,

As mentioned at the Board of Directors meeting last Friday, I wanted to provide an update on two pieces of legislation recently introduced in the state legislature that, if enacted, would modify the composition of the SANDAG Board of Directors:

AB 24 (DeMaio)
This bill, introduced by Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, proposes modifying the SANDAG Board of Directors by removing one of the two County Board of Supervisors seats and replacing it with a representative from the San Diego County Association of Planning Groups. It would also require the remaining County Board representative to be from an unincorporated area of the county. The bill has been double-referred to the Assembly Local Government Committee and the Assembly Transportation Committee. It currently does not have a scheduled hearing date.

SB 240 (Jones)
This bill, introduced by Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, proposes to replace the secondary representative from the County Board of Supervisors with a resident from an unincorporated area of the County, as selected by a majority of the county’s community planning groups, to serve a 1-year term. The bill also eliminates the requirement that one Board of Supervisors member be from a substantially incorporated district and the other from an unincorporated district. This bill has not yet been referred to a policy committee in the Senate.

We will continue to monitor these bills and provide you with updates accordingly.  

Thank you,
Mario

Subject: [External] Fwd: Major Use Permit - Action Required Please - PDS2024-MUP-24-013

Good morning all,

I received the project packet and wanted to provide notice that this project will be included on the ACPG agenda for this week's meeting on Thursday September 26, 2024 at 6pm.  The meeting will be at the Alpine Community Center located at 1830 Alpine, Blvd, Alpine, CA 91901.

Please note that the group generally does not take action on projects until it receives a scoping letter from the County of San Diego so there is a good chance a formal recommendation on this project will be tabled at this meeting.  However, we will take public input and the project owner/applicants are encouraged to attend.

Also note, the application references an additional document "standalone Project Description" as an attachment.  I did not receive that file in my packet.  Please send if available.

Feel free to contact me if you have any questions or concerns.

Thank you,

Subject: Engagement Opportunity: Land Development Cost Recovery Proposal

Dear CPSG Chairs,

I'm reaching out to let you know about the proposed Land Development Cost Recovery (fee) package and to invite you to provide your feedback, comments, and questions via several options - whichever is most convenient for you!

Meeting to Discuss Cost Recovery (Fee) Package:
You are invited to join us on Tuesday, April 9, 2024 at 1:00pm to learn more about the proposed cost recovery package and discuss your questions, concerns, and feedback.  This meeting will be held via Zoom and the link to join is below for your convenience.

Join Zoom Meeting
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/88547050405?pwd=eIpnetmCRRbFFZNb7TuF1DVIinDncA.1

Passcode: 841594

E-mail Your Feedback:
Please feel free to submit any questions or comments via email to Sam Murray at samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

Request a Meeting:
We are happy to meet with you at your request.  Please reach out to Sam Murray at samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov> to request a meeting.

A bit more background...

What is the Land Development Cost Recovery (Fee) Package?
Fee adjustments are primarily driven by County Policy B-29, which mandates that departments recover the full cost for services provided to agencies or individuals. Like most organizations, our costs fluctuate over time. The proposed fee adjustment reflects changes that will take effect in the upcoming fiscal year, as outlined in the existing labor contract. Approving this adjustment is crucial for ensuring departmental compliance with state mandates, making informed policy decisions based on data, and addressing expanded community needs assessments.

Our comprehensive cost recovery analysis is uniformly applied across the entire County enterprise. The fee development methodology aligns with Board Policy B-29 and adheres to existing cost policies and procedures.

To determine fees and rates, all three departments (Planning & Development Services, Department of Public Works, and Department of Parks & Recreation) initiate time studies. Staff members allocate their time to specific permits and record types as they work on projects. By analyzing historical hours per project, we estimate the time needed to process each project type.

Despite rising costs, our commitment to cost containment remains steadfast. Our innovative approaches not only lower County operating costs, but also enhance efficiency for our customers. Notably:

  *   Online Processes: Over 65% of building permits are now issued online, and 70% of payments are processed digitally, reducing staff workload, and minimizing the need for in-person visits to County offices.
  *   Expanded Digital Services: Our Land Development team offers convenient online services, including permit applications, self-service reports, digital approvals, text-based inspection management, and mobile field inspections.

These cost-saving measures result in approximately $2.4 million in annual savings for our departments. By passing these benefits on to our customers, we maintain lower fees. Without these measures, plan check and building permit fees would be 8.8% higher on average, and hourly rates for PDS would increase by 3.3% (equivalent to $8.10 more per hour).

Fee Overview:
Planning and Development Services:
Average Fee Increase: $55 or 3.0%
Average Intake Deposit Increase: $279 or 3.9%
Average Hourly Rate Increase: $11.00 or 4.6%

Department of Public Works:
Average Fee Increase: $18 or 6.4%
Average Intake Deposit Increase: $132 or 4.6%
Average Hourly Rate Increase: $8 or 3.6%

Department of Parks & Recreation
                Average Hourly Rate Increase: $14 or 9.7%.

We are also proposing changing from a deposit to a flat fee for Boundary Adjustments. Currently, the deposit stands at $2,284, while the proposed flat fee is $3,643. This change reflects a significant $1,361 increase (equivalent to 59.6%). Our calculation is based on 116 applications completed over the past four years.

Please feel free to reach out with any questions or if our team may be of further assistance.  We truly appreciate your time and feedback!

Best regards,
Heather

title: RE_ Electronic Filing of Form 700 for 2024.eml
subject: RE: Electronic Filing of Form 700 for 2024
body:
Good morning Community Group Members,

The eDisclosure online filing portal is now prepared to accept your electronic Form 700 financial disclosure filings. Emails were sent to you yesterday from Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:form700@sdcounty.ca.gov> containing your login information, including a temporary password.

If you have any questions about the system, please contact the Clerk of the Boards Disclosures Services team at (619) 531-5601 or at Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

Thank you,

[cid:image001.png@01DA5A68.06D4F810]
Kenneth Melton
County of San Diego, Planning & Development Services
5510 Overland Avenue | Suite 310 | San Diego, CA 92123
* (858) 761-8993 | * Kenneth.Melton@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Kenneth.Melton@sdcounty.ca.gov>
PDS Home Page: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/pds

Alternate Work Schedule:
Mon- Thur: 6:30am to 5:00pm
Off Fridays

From: LUEG, CommunityGroups
Sent: Wednesday, December 20, 2023 3:45 PM
Cc: Melton, Kenneth <Kenneth.Melton@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: Electronic Filing of Form 700 for 2024

Good afternoon Community Group Members,

As we approach the new year, this email is to inform you that annual Form 700 filings shall no longer be mailed to PDS.

On October 25, 2023, the Board of Supervisors approved an update to Policy I-1<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/Groups/Chair_Resources/I-001.pdf> which requires all Form 700 filings by CPG members AFTER their initial filing to be done with the Clerk of the Board. Previously, all CPG members were required to mail all filings to PDS, who in turn submitted them to the Registrar of Voters. The exact language is as follows: "All initial statements by new planning group members or candidates shall be filed with the Registrar of Voters. All other statements shall be filed with the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors."

To simplify the filing process for you, as well as to align with the County of San Diego's sustainability initiatives, as of January 1, 2024, the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors is requiring all Form 700 filings to be submitted electronically via its online filing portal, eDisclosure<https://www.southtechhosting.com/SanDiegoCounty/eDisclosure/>.

As final arrangements are made to update each group's Conflict of Interest codes and to prepare for the transition, we ask that all members please hold their filing of Form 700 until they receive their login information. We are working to complete this process as quickly as we can, and we anticipate it to be completed by the end of February.

Please feel free to reach out with any questions you may have. Below is more information regarding eDisclosure from the Clerk of the Board.

________________________________

As an online system, eDisclosure provides the ability to file forms whenever and wherever is most convenient for filers. The system prepopulates forms with the filer's name and position information, and automatically reviews forms for missing information. Submitted forms are automatically stored in eDisclosure for easy access by the filer, Agency Officials, and Clerk of the Board staff. eDisclosure also pulls information from the previous year to assist annual filers. Electronic filings will alleviate the need to mail or submit a Form 700 in person. Filings will no longer be rejected for illegible or incomplete information. Agency officials are able to update their filers' information, track filer submissions, and view filed forms as they are submitted.

The Clerk of the Board of Supervisors introduced eDisclosure in 2012, with the intent of providing a simple and secure method for filers to file their Form 700 electronically. Since its inception, filers have submitted more than 20,000 Form 700s via eDisclosure. Year after year, the use of eDisclosure has continued to grow. During the annual filing season this year, more than 90% of filings were submitted electronically. These numbers show that more and more filers are converting from paper filing to electronic filing.

Our office is committed to make the transition to electronic filing as smooth as possible. We strongly believe that eDisclosure will guide filers and agencies through a simplified and sustainable Form 700 filing future.

If you have any questions, please contact our Disclosures Services team at (619) 531-5601 or via e-mail at Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

________________________________

Respectfully,

[cid:image001.png@01DA5A68.06D4F810]

On Tue, Oct 29, 2024 at 11:58 AM Lauren Rowley <lrnrwly@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello Travis and Mary,
>
> I really enjoyed attending the Alpine Community Planning Group meeting
> last week and am feeling very excited about joining upon confirmation from
> the County.
>
> The conversation around BESS recommendations for local planning groups
> spurred my interest, as I am closely watching the energy transition. As I
> mentioned to Mary after the meeting, I invested in Earthgrid
> <https://earthgrid.io/> and am optimistic about creating safer, more
> reliable energy infrastructure. While Mary mentioned that this may
> theoretically pose a conflict of interest, I am not invested in any BESS
> projects specifically and have no relationship with Amberjack.
>
> While I certainly understand the desire to prevent the implementation of
> BESS projects that pose a safety and health risk to our community, I also
> think there is an opportunity to lead with recommendations that would allow
> our community to benefit from BESS, such as grid reliability and resilience
> during outages and natural disasters, as well as economic benefits.
>
> If possible, I would like to be able to contribute to the work you spoke
> about at the meeting regarding BESS recommendations that prioritize
> features of BESS projects known to be safer for communities. Here's an
> outline
> <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1l52VwWDf3FH8VL9hRe_mrI1mMTi_Zktmt9Udq0slMP8/edit?usp=sharing>,
> which you can use as is, or I can build upon with your blessing.
>
> While I am not an official member of the Alpine Community Planning Group
> yet, I'd be happy to help as an interested community member. If this help
> is not needed, just let me know. I want to respect the relationships and
> rules in place that may prevent my participation.
>
> Thanks!
> Lauren Rowley
>

Subject: Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Dear Interested Stakeholder,

We want to hear from you! The San Diego County Fire Protection District invites you to attend a public meeting to share your thoughts on the San Diego County
 Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Best Practices Report (Report). BESS are technology designed to store and manage energy for later use. It typically uses rechargeable batteries to store energy from various sources, such as the electrical grid, renewable
 energy sources like solar or wind power, or other power generation methods. On September 11, 2024, the Board of Supervisors directed San Diego County Fire to develop a technical study with recommendations that consider setbacks from residential uses as well
 as best practice safety standards, including 2023 NFPA 855. The completed report can be accessed at the project website. County Staff is looking for your feedback on the recommended best practices, safety standards, and siting recommendations for new and existing
 BESS applications. PDS is hosting this virtual public meeting to receive your input
on
November 14, 2024, at 6:00 PM (registration link provided below).

Disability-related accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting participation, language interpretation, including American Sign Language, and written materials
 in alternative languages and formats are available upon request. Please submit your request at least 72 hours in advance of event to: Mike Madrid at
PDS.LongRangePlanning@sdcounty.ca.gov

Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Dear Interested Stakeholder,

We want to hear from you! The San Diego County Fire Protection District invites you to attend a public meeting to share your thoughts on the San Diego County Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Best Practices Report (Report). BESS are technology designed to store and manage energy for later use. It typically uses rechargeable batteries to store energy from various sources, such as the electrical grid, renewable energy sources like solar or wind power, or other power generation methods. On September 11, 2024, the Board of Supervisors directed San Diego County Fire to develop a technical study with recommendations that consider setbacks from residential uses as well as best practice safety standards, including 2023 NFPA 855. The completed report can be accessed at the project website. County Staff is looking for your feedback on the recommended best practices, safety standards, and siting recommendations for new and existing BESS applications. PDS is hosting this virtual public meeting to receive your input on November 14, 2024, at 6:00 PM (registration link provided below).

Disability-related accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting participation, language interpretation, including American Sign Language, and written materials in alternative languages and formats are available upon request. On Jan 4, 2024, at 8:59 AM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Good Morning APG Members,

Happy New Year!Our effective date for membership on the SANDAG Board of Directors was January 1st!

Our first APG meeting of the year is an in-person meeting on Wednesday, January 10th at 6:30pm. The location is to be the County Operations Center in Kearny Mesa and the details for securing this location are still being worked through.....

The agenda for this meeting will be provided to each of you and posted in a public location within the timelines of the Brown Act.

SANDAG has reached out to our group to communicate the process for being seated as a new Board of Director member. For example, the APG will need to send an official letter to SANDAG naming our Representative and Alternate for the Board. And, the Representative and Alternate will need to complete a new Form 700 listing SANDAG as one of the agencies covered by the form.

SANDAG's first meeting of the new year will be Friday, January 12th. So, the APG will work quickly to ensure all requirements are met in order to be seated on that date.

2024 is a historic year for unincorporated area residents. Thank you for your dedication to our communities.

Robin Joy Maxson, Chair
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

title: Re_ Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG).eml
subject: Re: Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG)
body:
There is nothing we can do to stop it.  My email accounts have never been compromised. The scammers just take group members’ publicly available emails (they are on our agenda) and email them from an account named “Travis Lyon”.  But it’s clearly not my email address.

Members just have to be aware this is a common scam. I receive the same phishing emails from scammers impersonating the AYSO commissioner and the Little League president because I am a member of those boards and am listed online with my email address.

The only way to stop it would be to take our emails off the public agendas. The resulting lack of accessibility for members of the public outweigh the hassle it creates for our board.

Thanks for bringing to my attention. Hope you and the family have a fun weekend planned for Easter.

Travis Lyon619.952.8607

body:
Hey Angie,

I will confirm with the county, but because it is your property, you can’t vote but you can present on your own behalf.  You would step down from the dais once we get to this item and present.  You can also let Greg present (or any agent authorized on your behalf) once you step down off dais.

It’s kind of odd… if you have any other conflict (like if it’s your neighbor presenting for their property, or some client/business affiliate that you have financial ties to that is presenting) you are required to recuse yourself and leave the room during presentation and vote.  The exception to that recusal rule is when it is 100% your property. Then you aren’t allowed to vote, but you don’t have to leave room and you can present on your behalf.

Please let me know if you have any questions.
Travis Lyon619.952.8607

Hi Travis:

Thanks for the agenda.

I attended the Back Country Economic Development Council meeting yesterday.  We discussed the Socially Equitqable Cannibis Program that the County will be creating for all unincorporated San Diego County.  Has this been addressed at the Alpine Planning Goup meetings?  It will allow for cannabis growers, dispensaries and cannabis cafes in all unincorporated areas.  The effect in Alpine could be substantial.

We were told that Planning Groups would be providing input at a meeting at the end of March.  The County would then determine what the program would entail.

If you would like information on this, please let me know.

Thank you,

Hi Travis –
Confirming receipt of John Sullivan’s resignation. This has also been sent to the Clerk of the Board, and they will send him his leaving office Form 700 via email.
The attached Vacancy Notice has also been sent to the Clerk of the Board for posting and has been posted on the PDS website here: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/Groups/alpine/VNSeats2025.pdf
The Alpine CPG roster has been updated on the PDS website here: https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/Groups/alpine/ALROSTER.pdf

Also, I attached is the only application I currently have on file for the Alpine CPG, which is from Lauren Rowley. Was she ever considered for membership by the Alpine CPG members? The last email I have was from her saying she was going to reach out to you. She will need to have the attached certification form completed and her application certified by the ROV to be considered for membership. Please let me know. Thanks!

Good morning Travis,

It is with a heavy heart that I must resign my seat on the planning group effective immediately. These past few years have been without a doubt some of the best, as I've grown as a community leader and person. I will be moving out of Alpine and wanted to give you all time to fill the seat.

subject: Re: [External] Loveland , Parking and Access  Improvement Question.
cc: Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>, "eric.becker@waterboards.ca.gov" <eric.becker@waterboards.ca.gov>, Carlos Quintero <cquintero@sweetwater.org>, Nicholas Brust <nicholas.brust@sen.ca.gov>
body:
Hi Russell!

I would love to provide a definitive answer but what I can do is provide the “it depends” answer that I used to provide as a land use consultant.

The biggest question is if it’s all being used in the existing condition and if it’s all disturbed (i.e. previously cleared or graded). If that’s the case, there shouldn’t be a requirement for any traffic-related study or biological resources study.

The key will be if it can all fit within a previously disturbed footprint. Sometimes road standards can be wider than one would think and the Fire authority that has jurisdiction may also have some requirements on access in case of emergency.

Hope this helps!

Thanks,
Greg

body:
Carlos QuinteroGeneral ManagerSweetwater AuthorityChula Vista.

Good Morning, General Manager Quintero.

The local group Friends of Loveland Reservoir (FOLR) appears to be advertising on Facebook  that it will be in charge of presenting a Sweetwater proposal for Trails Enhancement  at the Alpine Community Planning Group meeting tomorrow. The understanding is that this document will go for a full BOD vote soon with public comment possible before. 

Their website claims that all community proposals are considered in this Sweetwater Proposal. It also loosk like they have an ownership stake in the $750K from Senator Jones' office and are "sharing it". These are people who know how to wrtie better than to leave more questions than answers if so inclined. Please intervene for good faith operations of the Trails Enhancement proposal track. 
It has come to my attention that some community members who view this proposal FOLR intends to present as a Sweetwater creation and  find it inappropriate for a small, peripheral group to present it. We believe Sweetwater should be the first presenter of Sweetwater materials in this case. 

Please send a copy of the proposal today, and I will do my best to share it with our communities.

We look forward to Sweetwater being transparently and responsibly in front of the projects and proposals with respect to all the advocates you and your staff have worked with up until now. 

Appreciatively,

Russell

Carl DeMaio Wins Endorsement of Latino American Political Association (LAPA)

As Democrats and the liberal media howl and cry racism about DeMaio’s opening TV ad featuring Pete Wilson and call for border security and an end to California’s Sanctuary State laws, LAPA’s endorsement proves Latinos stand with DeMaio on the issues.

The Latino American Political Association (LAPA) of San Diego has officially endorsed Carl DeMaio for State Assembly — highlighting DeMaio’s efforts to promote and increase Latino engagement in the political process.

LAPA was founded to build Latino involvement and representation in the government, and the organization endorses candidates who they believe “demonstrate the greatest ability to promote benefits for the Hispanic community in line with the mission of LAPA as well as all San Diegans.”

In endorsing for Assembly District 75, Past President of LAPA Delores Chavez Harmes praised DeMaio and noted that he “has been a great partner in encouraging and supporting Latino candidates to succeed and in helping to boost Latino turnout in elections.”

“Carl DeMaio has been a longtime champion for educating and involving Californians from every walk of life in the political process, and we are confident he will continue to pave the way in the State Assembly for getting Latinos engaged in the fight to Reform California and make it a better place for all,” Chavez Harmes continued.

Carl DeMaio thanked LAPA for their support.

"Latino voters agree with our Reform California agenda of fighting costly and unfair tax hikes, improving schools, empowering parents, and combatting crime,” DeMaio noted. “Contrary to the false narrative being spun by Democrats and their allies in the liberal media, Latino voters want a secure border too,” DeMaio declared.

body:
Fellow Planning/Sponsor Group Chairs:

At our Saturday meeting I mentioned the work the Crest Dehesa Granite Hills Harbison Canyon Planning Group undertook in the area of wildfire threat mitigation, making this our top public policy priority.

After meeting with stakeholders for almost three years, we unanimously adopted the attached set of seven resolutions.  The attachment contains summary and background information as well.

In our subregion, wildfire is our number one threat to the safety of our residents, and we are using every power we have under the county’s I-1 policy to move wildfire threat mitigation to the top of the agenda.

The events taking place today in Pacific Palisades are a powerful reminder of the importance of taking every step possible before the next fire hits.

I also mentioned the website we put up at CrestPlanningGroup.com to serve as a community resource and to increase public engagement with the Planning Group.

Please let me know if I can provide any additional information.

Ron Nehring

title: Park Fee Changes Starting February 18, 2025.eml
subject: Park Fee Changes Starting February 18, 2025
body:
Hi Travis,

At the County of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department, we take great pride in maintaining beautiful, safe, and accessible outdoor spaces for everyone to enjoy. To continue providing high-quality parks, trails, and recreation services, we will be making some adjustments to our park service fees starting February 18, 2025.
This is our first fee update in nearly 11 years, and while we’ve worked hard to keep costs as low as possible, this change is necessary to help offset rising maintenance and operating expenses. The updates also align our fees with similar parks and facilities in the region while ensuring that we continue to deliver best-in-nation outdoor experiences.

What’s Changing?
Most of the fee increases are just a few dollars, but they will help us keep our parks safe, clean, and well-maintained for generations to come. Here are a few examples of the adjustments:

  *   Day Use Parking: Increasing from $3.00 to $5.00 per day
  *   RV Partial Hook-Up Campsite: Increasing from $29 to $35 per night
  *   Camping Reservations: Now include up to two pets and one extra vehicle at no additional cost
  *   Other small increases apply to rentals, permits, and additional park services

To see the full list of updated fees, please visit our 2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf>. For more information on why these changes are happening, check out our FAQs_Park User Fee Increase 01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/FAQs_Park%20User%20Fee%20Increase%2001.17.25.pdf>.

Why Are Fees Increasing?
The cost of maintaining our 158 parks, 389 miles of trails, and over 58,000 acres of land has risen significantly over the past decade. Adjusting our fees will allow us to:
✔ Continue offering high-quality park experiences and amenities
✔ Keep trails, facilities, and green spaces safe and well-maintained
✔ Expand and improve park programs and services for all ages and abilities
Even with these updates, our park fees remain affordable and continue to offer exceptional value compared to similar park systems.

Ensuring Parks Remain Accessible for Everyone
We believe that everyone should have access to nature—which is why we continue to offer financial assistance programs and free or low-cost activities:
🌿 Discounted Programs: Veterans, seniors, and groups may qualify for discounts on fees and reservations.
🏕 First-Time Camping Program: A free initiative designed to introduce new campers to the joys of the outdoors.
🎉 Low-Cost or Free Activities: Most of our recreation programs and events are available at reduced or no cost.
We are committed to making the outdoors accessible and enjoyable for all members of our community.

Thank You for Your Support!
We appreciate your understanding and continued support as we make these necessary updates. Your visits, participation, and enthusiasm help keep our parks vibrant and welcoming for everyone.
If you have any questions or would like more details, please visit our Fees Increase Feb. 18<https://www.sdparks.org/content/sdparks/en/news-events/news-stories/Fees-Increase-Feb-18.html>.

We look forward to seeing you at the parks!

Thanks & Go Aztecs,

subject: Options to Streamline Affordable and Attainable Housing Project
body:
Dear CPG Chairs,

I hope this email finds you well. We wanted to reach out to each of you regarding some upcoming outreach opportunities related to the Options to Streamline Affordable and Attainable Housing Project.

The Board of Supervisors has directed staff to explore the feasibility of developing three potential housing programs aimed at enhancing housing production across all income levels. These programs include:

  *   A Small Lot Subdivision Program to increase homeownership opportunities through the construction of smaller homes.
  *   A Senior and Assisted Living Housing Program to incentivize the construction of more senior and assisted living housing facilities.
  *   A County By-Right Program to provide streamlined project approvals for specific housing developments, with a focus on affordability.

The PDS Long Range Planning team is actively developing options for these programs to improve affordability in unincorporated communities and promote diverse housing opportunities for residents. These efforts aim to ensure that everyone, including teachers, tradespeople, healthcare workers, individuals with disabilities, young professionals, young families, and seniors, has accessible and affordable housing choices within their community.

On February 7th, a GovDelivery was sent regarding public meetings for these housing programs. We held the first public webinar on February 15, 2024, during which we presented draft options for each program and addressed questions from the public. We have scheduled a second webinar for March 13th at 6pm, and you can register for the meeting using the link provided below. Both meetings will cover the same presentation.

In addition to the virtual public meetings, we would like to engage with community planning and sponsor groups to gain insight and feedback on the draft options. Would your group be interested in having County staff provide a brief presentation during an upcoming meeting in either March or April? The feedback received during these meetings will be instrumental in refining the draft options before presenting them to the Board later this Fall.

We kindly ask for your assistance in spreading the word about these important initiatives. Please feel free to share this message with your friends and colleagues who may be interested in participating.

Thank you for your support and collaboration in this critical effort.

title: Only 5 days away _ Bob Figari starts SF to LA Arthritis Foundation ride on Saturday.eml
subject: Only 5 days away / Bob Figari starts SF to LA Arthritis Foundation ride on Saturday
body:
Hi everyone,

First, thanks to everyone who has donated. I’m blown away by the generosity of all of you. I’ve raised $11,900, just $3100 shy of my $15,000 goal. Wow!

It’s not too late to donate. Just follow this link to my official web page and click on the “Support Me” button:

https://events.arthritis.org/participant/333448￼
2024 California Coast Classic Bike
events.arthritis.org

I’m one of nearly 250 riders supporting the cause. Our journey begins this Saturday at Fisherman’s Wharf in San Francisco. The first day is an 89 mile ride down the coast on Hwy 1 to Santa Cruz. My hope is that the offshore winds will be from the NW to give us a little push! We’ll camp out at a local school and then on Sunday head for Monterey.

I took a training ride last Saturday in San Diego with one of our “Ambassadors” who share their stories of battling arthritis each night at our camp. Delightful young woman (30’s?) who looked to be in fantastic shape. Had a chance to hear some of her story. You wouldn’t know looking at her how difficult it has been. She’s had a childhood form of arthritis since she was a toddler. She tries to stay off the medications that, while not a cure, do help to ease the painful effects. She told me that the arthritis flairs up often with debilitating pain that starts in her ankles and knees, forcing her to go back on the meds. Nonetheless she’s totally psyched about the ride!

I was truly impressed with her determination and amazingly positive attitude. Learning about her situation makes it so much easier for me to move past my own issues! While I lost a hip from arthritis and struggle with osteoarthritis, it is nothing compared to her having to deal with the disease her whole life! Very humbling.

Your support increases the chances of finding a cure for people like her. So, once again, thank you so much for your kindness in contributing.

I’ll check in with you all at the end of the ride to let you know how things went.

Take care,

Bob

Robert Figari
figari@well.com
415 259-8153

title: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine.eml
subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine
body:
Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

Just wanted to let you now that yesterday, Calfire released its latest & greatest wildfire severity maps, at https://osfm.fire.ca.gov/what-we-do/community-wildfire-preparedness-and-mitigation/fire-hazard-severity-zones

You should probably re-evaluate whether facilities which increase fire danger, such as battery energy storage (BESS,) solar panel arrays, or utility (SDGE mostly) grids, and even car dealerships with a high amount of EV's, are appropriately placed.

  *  Dark Red: Very High Risk
  *  Brick Red: High Risk
  *  Orange: Moderate Risk

One interesting thing to note is how many coastal areas are now in high fire severity zones.

This map is State Responsibility Fire Hazard Severity

County staff provided Supervisor Anderson with a progress report on the community outreach and implementation the 16 measures, which we have attached for you.
The Supervisor's goal is always to provide transparency to you about what actions are coming before the Board of Supervisors and give you the opportunity to have your voice heard.

title: Loveland Parallel Trail. Other options_ Fish Stocking..eml
subject: Loveland Parallel Trail. Other options/ Fish Stocking.
cc: Nicholas Brust <nicholas.brust@sen.ca.gov>, Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>, Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@sen.ca.gov>
body:
Carlos Quintero,Sweetwater Authority General Manager. 

Hello GM Quintero.

How are you? 
As you know ,what actual lake users wanted and want at Loveland was more access. Both you and Andrew Hayes frequently said there are no limits on the possiblities with the funding. I fail to see how the parallel trail makes any sense. For the path shown The elevattion drop is the same as the existing trail.It requires new brush and tree clearing whereas as switch back stays even in the "user defined " area. It requires maintance the same as the exsting trail, and a trash can, or two.It costs more with the 250K bridge plus 200k "parallel trail" plus maintenance than the $400k bridge.As much as I hate to say it the $400k brige makes more sense. Not ast much sense as a switch back and pipe hard scape but more than the current proposal.
Please consider more practical and cost effective option or go with the big bridge and use the additional 50k to put a pedestrian gate on the east end of the lake.
Alternately,  please find a cost effective crossing at the ravine, I have more ideas,  and stock threadfin shad heavily when weather and other conditions are good for it. .DFW will allow that and these forage fish  are good for birds and other wildlife as well as fish. 
Even with the SDGE easement approved, access from the south side is needed. 
Please call me if you want to talk about any of this or email.

A pedestrian gate here and any forward momentum along the shoreling  at this yellow line  is well within the easement and it's legal to walk on Japatul Road.

Thank you,
Russell Walsh.

title: Loveland  Area _CRHT Parking..eml
subject: Loveland  Area /CRHT Parking.
body:
Hi Travis, 

Thanks again for the sunrise to sunset letter. Obviously, Sweetwater is ignoring all of them because of the gift the Forest Service allows them to close early. 

If I can make it Thursday , I'll bring this up with your group.

A few months back,  The COSD, including  Joel Anderson’s office, Trails Planner, Lizzy Bendrick and others from Parks and Recreation,  tried to help me open an old dirt parking lot near the reservoir. Amazingly, opening it was cleared through DPW, no major issues!  I think some pretty generous offers were made including indemnifying Sweetwater  which,of course, won't cooperate. The parking lot is on land that the FS transferred to Sweetwater in the Land Swap, but was closed shortly after, in part because the new Sweetwater parking lot was supposed to be opened from sunrise to sunset and a new connector to the CRHT was built from there. 

Also with regards to parking for public access to the CRHT , No-parking signs were put up along Japatul Road near the reservoir. These don't exist in other areas ,for example on both sides of the Japatul Road  at the trailhead to hike up to Lawson peak.  As you know, it is common to pull off of county roads to access public property for recreation, but not around Loveland.

In light of Sweetwater's early closing of the only open public parking lot at the reservoir/CRHT trail heads I hope the ACPG will be willing to learn about this and take action to either add pressure to open the CRHT parking lot, or selectively remove no parking signs around the CRHT and reservoirs.

Related development, For the time being Sweetwater has allowed entering the lake from Japatul Road by the bridges. There  is barbed wire in the 50' wide easement and that easement also intersects  the very public Japatul road and the bike path in the east end. At one point lake users can’t get around the easement without swimming or going up on Japatul road.  Parking compliments this kind of access and could even be safer than walking down Japatul road from the current Loveland Parking lot. 

Just going to put out that info for now. and post an image of the area where the CRHT parking lot is.  I know it's a bit to learn, but not too much really. Sweetwater's hoarding deserves no favors from us. 
The CRHT Parking lot is at the yellow dots. This area could be reviewed for informal roadside parking like exists many other places in the county. The Califronina Riding and Hiking trail goes up to Bell Bluff Mesa and beyond.

body:
[ConPlan]

Community Planning Group Chairs,

Each year, the County's Housing and Community Development Services (HCDS) receives approximately $14 million in federal entitlement funding from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. This funding is intended to provide increased affordable housing opportunities, support access to public services, and expand community infrastructure to create thriving communities. Every five years, HCDS creates what is referred to as the Consolidated Plan. The Consolidated Plan is an evaluation of all housing and community development needs in the region, especially in the unincorporated County. The Consolidated Plan is a strategic 5-year plan for the four federal entitlement programs that are administered by HCDS.

HCDS is hosting a series of community forums to gather feedback and help plan for the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan. We invite you and your community partners, neighbors, and friends, to share community priorities related to these funds. Receiving community input is vital in determining County of San Diego community development and housing needs, as well as developing the 5-year goals for the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan.

The 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan Community Forums will be hosted in person and virtually:

Based on feedback from the community meetings and questionnaires, HCDS will propose strategic goals for the upcoming 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan. These proposed goals will be available for public comment for 30 days and presented to the Board of Supervisors as the conclusion of the public comment period for approval. The full Consolidated Plan, including a review of community feedback, in-depth market profiles, and an assessment of current County policies and procedures related to housing and community development is available for review. In addition to the Consolidated Plan, the 2025-2026 Annual Plan will be presented which will identify projects recommended for funding in the upcoming year. The documents will also be available for public review for at least 30 days.

If you cannot attend one of the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan community forums, more information and engagement opportunities will be available on Engage San Diego County<https://lnks.gd/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..IU1BqOpk_79gWcwmhupZZ6ToJAYckzi9LuA_bLA26s0/s/1803603093/br/243532259872-l> in mid-June.

HCDS' Consolidated Plan covers four federal entitlement programs:

Community Development Block Grant (CDBG): These funds are used to improve community development by providing decent housing and a suitable living environmental for low- to moderate-income households. Community forums will also provide information about eligible CDBG projects, the annual application process, and requirements for implementation.

Areas Served: Unincorporated San Diego County, Coronado, Del Mar, Imperial Beach, Lemon Grove, Poway, and Solana Beach.

HOME Investment Partnerships Program: These programs fund affordable housing opportunities such as the County's First-Time Homebuyer Program and multi-family affordable housing. Notices of HOME funding availability are posted as money becomes available.

Areas Served: Unincorporated San Diego County, Carlsbad, Coronado, Del Mar, Encinitas, Imperial Beach, La Mesa, Lemon Grove, Poway, San Marcos, Santee, Solana Beach, and Vista.

Emergency Solutions Grants: These funds are for improving the quality and number of emergency housing solutions, including shelters and transitional facilities for the homeless, and to prevent at-risk families or individuals from becoming homeless.

Areas Served: Unincorporated San Diego County, Coronado, Del Mar, Imperial Beach, Lemon Grove, Poway, and Solana Beach.

Housing Opportunities for Persons with HIV/AIDS: The funds are for housing and supportive services for those living with HIV/AIDS.

Areas Served: All San Diego County.

Community members, particularly those in our entitlement jurisdictions, are welcome to share their ideas. Please share the word with your stakeholders and constituents! If you have any questions, please contact HCDS at Community.Development@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Community.Development@sdcounty.ca.gov> or by phone at 858-694-8756.

Thank you,

Sarah Snook Brunson, Housing Program Analyst IV

You are receiving this project update because you have asked to be added to our stakeholder list for this Caltrans project from Viejas Creek to Pine Valley on Interstate 8. This is a update for the work being performed at Tavern Road.

* On Wednesday, May 1 and Thursday, May 2 from 6am to 3pm, the two left lanes of eastbound I-8 at Tavern Road will close. The right lane and off-ramp will remain open

This work at Tavern Road is a separate project from the I-8 Viejas Creek to Pine Valley Pavement Rehabilitation Project. The work at Tavern Road needs to take place immediately to repair the damaged culverts in the area.

Hayden Manning
Caltrans Public Information Officer

title: Introducing Street Stewards - A grassroots initiative to keep San DiegoΓÇÖs street clean one block at a time!.eml
subject: Introducing Street Stewards - A grassroots initiative to keep San Diego’s street clean one block at a time!
body:
Dear East County Community Groups,

I am writing to inform you of a powerful new mapping tool developed specifically for San Diegans to help keep our streets clean together. My non-profit organization is called Street Stewards, and we are nearly 1,000 volunteers strong… and counting! We have developed a website where any San Diego County citizen can log in, find their local community, and adopt a block by recording litter pickups on our live interactive map.

Our powerful interactive map shows the health of the entire county’s streets with a color coded system which enables Stewards to decide to simply clean their own block OR go to where their efforts are needed most. Please see the attached graphics for an overview of how it works and an example of how our interactive map appears.

This website was developed with generous help from San Diego County’s Neighborhood Reinvestment Program grants, and it is a free tool for anyone to use! We would love your help in spreading the word about it with your membership, organization, and constituents. The strength of this model relies on participation and widespread adoption, so it is time to get the word out.

We are excited to collaborate to spread the word in your newsletters, emails, social media posts, and among your friends and colleagues! You can learn much more and sign up here: www.streetstewards.com. I am happy to provide more information, attend meetings and present, or explain further. Please don’t hesitate to get in touch with ideas about how to get the word out! Thank you for your time, and I look forward to working with you to make San Diego a more beautiful place - one block at a time.

Sincerely,

Aaron Null
Founder, Executive Director
Street Stewards
484-883-9476

title: How to Request Road Repairs and Check Future Paving Projects.eml
subject: How to Request Road Repairs and Check Future Paving Projects
body:
Good morning, Chairs!

We wanted to spread the word regarding road repairs. We have been receiving inquiries from our constituents about how to report potholes, graffiti removals, lifted sidewalks, and a number of issues.

Given the rain we've received this year, we felt as if this may be beneficial to pass along these two tools to those in the community.

Roads Service Request
https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/dpw/roads/Roads_Service_Request.html

Within this form, you first enter a location. This can even be a point along any road.

You can then report the category of the issue. This can be road maintenance, drainage, traffic issues, or signs.

Please let our office know how the response time is from Public Works and if you're satisfied with the customer service.

Road Pavement Projects
If you are curious about when a certain road will undergo resurfacing, this link to an interactive map is helpful:
https://gis-portal.sandiegocounty.gov/arcgis/home/webmap/viewer.html?webmap=41097e0474f242cbbd9b1e0a3a74763f

We have noticed in a few instances that some portions may not be up to date. If you notice that, please feel free to contact my office and we will work with Public Works to get it updated.

In addition, please let us know if you would like to consider reprioritizing certain roads to be paved based on community input. We are happy to help and facilitate.

Thanks again for serving our communities and helping us make government work for our constituents.

Greg Kazmer
Senior Land Use Advisor
District 2, Office of Joel Anderson
Cell: (858) 289-9234
