Dear Community Partners,

We want to express our appreciation to everyone who contributed to the engagement activities surrounding the Housing Blueprint (Blueprint) and to those who joined us for our recent community sessions. Your input, whether provided through interviews, focus groups, meetings, webinars, or community sessions, has been instrumental in shaping our understanding of the housing needs in our county.

For those who couldn't attend the recent community sessions or wish to offer further feedback, we strongly encourage you to complete our survey. This survey provides another opportunity for community members to share their perspectives on the proposed strategic actions and suggest any enhancements to better address the housing needs of our county. It should take approximately 10 minutes to complete and can be accessed on the Engage San Diego webpage: [https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/housing-blueprint]. Please note that the survey closing date has been extended to Sunday, May 12th.

Your ongoing engagement is essential as we strive to develop a housing strategy that balances resources, priorities, and values to effectively respond to the housing crisis in San Diego County.

title: Honey Hill Ranch TM Condo Conversion (PDS2023-TM-5650).eml
subject: Honey Hill Ranch TM Condo Conversion (PDS2023-TM-5650)
body:
Hi Travis,

I wanted to notify you that the Honey Hill Ranch TM Condo Conversion Project (PDS2023-TM-5650) that the Alpine CPG approved back in February 2023 is now ready to move forward for Decision to the Planning Commission.  The project is tentatively docketed for August 23, 2024. There have been no changes to the project since it was submitted to the Alpine CPG but if you wanted to attend the Hearing or have any questions, please let me know.

Project Description:
The applicant requests a Tentative Map for condominium conversion purposes for 17 existing residential units. The 4.17-acre project site is located at Jubilee Lane and Verity Court that connects to Honey Hill Ranch Road, in the Alpine Community Plan Area, within the unincorporated San Diego County. The project is subject to the General Plan Regional Category Village, Land Use Designation General Commercial which permits subdivision of land for condominium conversion purposes upon the approval of a Tentative Map pursuant to Section 81.105 of the Subdivision Ordinance. Zoning for the site is General Commercial Residential (C34). Access is provided by an existing private road called Jubilee Lane which merges into a private cul-de-sac called Verity Court. This private road connects to Honey Hill Ranch Road, a County-maintained road.

Regards,

reason is one of the accepted reasons. This is in place for the Board when
at least a quorum continues to meet in person.:
Individual board members may participate in board meetings remotely, if
they notify the Board at their earliest opportunity, and have one of the
following:

*Just Cause:* Individual board members can participate remotely when
caregiving of a family member, a contagious illness, a physical or mental
disability, or LEA-related travel prevents them from appearing in person;

–          May not be used more than two meetings per calendar year per
Board member.

Please consider this request from Congressman Darrell Issa's office as this

*The smell of weed is wreaking havoc across California*
The state's largest indoor cannabis farm is under fire thanks to the
"disgusting" smell of pot
By Lester Black, Cannabis editorMarch 5, 2025

David Bernard, left, the COO of C4 USA, said the company plans to push
forward with an expansion even as neighbors complain about cannabis odor.
Courtesy of C4 USA
California is globally synonymous with cannabis, but the plant’s
distinctive smell has become a major headache for people across the state.
From Northern California to the desert to the coast, California residents
have been complaining for years that the smell of legal cannabis farms is
destroying their quality of life. And in some places, local governments are
beginning to act.

In Cathedral City, a small enclave near Palm Springs, the city council
approved a moratorium last week that will block any new cannabis businesses
from opening or expanding after years of complaints over cannabis odors.
The moratorium was aimed directly at Cat City Cannabis Co., a massive
indoor marijuana cultivation facility that has generated complaints for
years from nearby residents who say the facility emits a “disgusting” smell.
Mayor Pro Tem Raymond Gregory said during the meeting that the moratorium
would stop the facility from expanding further.

“That won’t affect what we’re going to be continuing to work with on the
current issue, but it will stop them building a whole ’nother building,”
Gregory said.

David Bernard, the COO of C4 USA, which owns the facility, said in an
emailed statement to SFGATE that they are actively working with the city to
develop an “effective odor management solution” but that they are also
pushing forward with their phase 2 expansion. It will add 168,000 square
feet of space to the existing 325,000-square-foot facility, which is
already the largest indoor pot farm in the state, according to the
company’s website.
“Though the moratorium has impacted our timeline, we view this as an
opportunity to work collaboratively with the city and the local community
to develop a long-term, effective odor management solution,” Bernard said.

The Cathedral City action comes after the Santa Barbara County Planning
Commission unanimously recommended last month that all greenhouse cannabis
growers install carbon filters within a year. The area near the coastal
town of Carpinteria is a major hub for greenhouse cannabis growers, and
residents have been complaining about the “sewer-like” smell of cannabis
for years. The recommendation still needs to be approved by the county’s
Board of Supervisors before it becomes law.

Some of the greenhouses have already installed the filtration systems,
which can cost millions of dollars, while others have installed misting
systems that attempt to camouflage the smell of fresh marijuana, although
those systems have been panned as making entire neighborhoods smell like
laundromats.
Most agricultural companies are protected from neighborhood complaints over
nuisances like odor through so-called “Right to Farm” laws, but most local
governments, including Santa Barbara’s, have exempted cannabis farms from
receiving those protections.

Some California residents are saying the smell of cannabis is more than
just a nuisance and that it could actually be causing health problems. The
Sonoma Neighborhood Coalition, a group that is critical of cannabis
policies, has been pushing for the county to ban outdoor cannabis farms
entirely because, according to the group, pot plants release toxic
chemicals including beta-myrcene. In December, the group warned against
allowing outdoor cannabis farms, saying allowing pot farms would be
“assaulting your right to defend your home from businesses that spew
carcinogens into your yard and your house.”

Beta-myrcene is a naturally occurring compound found in thousands of
plants. Studies have shown it can have carcinogenic effects when exposed at
high levels, but SFGATE was not able to independently verify if cannabis
farms would ever produce enough of the chemical to meet those toxic levels
to nearby residents. Hops also produce the compound, and there do not
appear to be problems in Yakima Valley where over 50,000 acres of hops are
planted every year.

In Cathedral City, the smell of cannabis has tainted what was originally a
genial relationship between the town and the pot industry. Locals were
ecstatic when plans for the Cat City Cannabis Co. facility were first
announced in 2018, with the planning commission unanimously approving the
project and local neighbors telling the Desert Sun that they were happy a
long vacant lot was becoming a job creator. The facility, which ballooned
in price to $120 million, traded hands before opening under its current
ownership.

Now, the mood is decidedly angry. Debbie Price, a local resident, told the
council that “we are all flipping trapped” and called for an injunction to
cease operations immediately until “there is no smell.”

“Is Cathedral City slated to be another Salton Sea area? You may laugh, but
you know what, so did they,” Price said.
Gregory, the mayor pro tem, said that the council would have acted
differently in 2020 if they knew about the smell and directed the company
to end the odor.

“Stop the odor, and we’ll be done,” Gregory said.

Lester Black
CANNABIS EDITOR
Lester Black is SFGATE's cannabis editor. He was born in Torrance, raised
in Seattle, and has written for FiveThirtyEight.com, High Country News, The
Guardian, The Albuquerque Journal, The Tennessean, and many other
publications. He was previously the cannabis columnist for The Stranger.

--
*Kathleen M. Lippitt, MPH*

From: Erica Wolski <ewolski@rmwd.org>
Date: Sun, Jan 19, 2025 at 11:08 AM
Subject: upcoming PSPS event - potentially dangerous over 3500 feet

Hi all

I am not sure how widely SDGE spreads this info so I thought we might want
to put it out to the Assoc of Planning Groups, the Backcountry Chamber
Coalition or our local social media in case any of those residents are in
the area of concern. School districts, water districts, the County gets
this info. But just because the county gets the info, doesn't mean it
reaches the right people (as we learned in Dec).

SDGE is predicting hurricane force winds in some areas of the county Monday
night/Tuesday. Temperature above 3500 feet is going to be 28 to 30 deg F
overnight with a wind chill that brings it down to the low teens. The
backcountry areas may experience power outages starting Monday night and
due to another smaller event coming Thurs/Fri, may not get restored until
Friday/Saturday. SDGE is planning to provide more resources to the affected
areas.

Seniors, disabled, low income residents, etc should be encouraged to
contact 211 (858-300-1211). SDGE can provide both transportation to a hotel
and a free hotel room stay if you have no source of heat during the outage.
211 flyer link (I have also attached in a zip file in English and Spanish):
S2350023-WFS-AFN-Flyer_FINAL_DIGITAL.pdf
<https://www.sdge.com/sites/default/files/S2350023-WFS-AFN-Flyer_FINAL_DIGITAL.pdf>

*My suggested social media post along with the two 211 graphics:*

"SDGE is predicting Public Safety Power Shutoffs, or PSPS, in the
backcountry areas of San Diego County between Mon Jan 20 and Wed Jan 22.
Weather is predicted to be dangerously cold overnight below freezing at
elevations above 3,500 feet. SDGE is encouraging affected residents in the
outage area over 3,500 feet to take advantage of the resources that can be
provided by 211 to seniors, people with disabilities and low-income
residents. 211 can provide transportation, free hotel stays and other
resources: Public Safety Power Shutoff - 211 <https://211sandiego.org/psps>
Note that if 211 does not connect, please call the alternate number
858-300-1211. "

*Note that residents near the Mexican border need to call the 858# instead
of 211.*

PS: Downtown Ramona should be fine - they said they learned from the Dec
event the importance of trying to keep the Creelman substation fed with
power either via other transmission or a generator. So while transmission
may be affected, they are not predicting a community wide outage like Dec,
only the "fringes" of Ramona.

Erica

Ramona Municipal Water District

SANDAG issues a statement following notification from the U.S. Department
of Justice:

“SANDAG is pleased to report that it has been notified by the U.S.
Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California and the FBI that
the federal investigation has been concluded, and that no federal criminal
charges will be filed against the agency or its employees. Although SANDAG
was not provided with complete information about the nature and scope of
the investigation, we understand that it focused on the contracting
activities of SANDAG, and whether those activities had violated federal
law.

Consistent with previous findings by agency management, the Office of the
Independent Performance Auditor, and other external audits, substantive
improvements are being made to strengthen policies and internal controls,
deploy tools and training, and create consistent business practices across
the agency.

These measures will help to ensure that procurement practices are fair and
competitive, staff are adequately trained to perform their
responsibilities, and that consultant resources are managed in line with
contract terms and conditions and established budgets.”

Road Resurfacing Projects in Alpine

Dear Friends,

My constituents in the unincorporated communities deserve to have
high-quality infrastructure, including roads that are in good condition.

Since taking office, I've been laser-focused ensuring we allocate more
resources to road repairs. Last year,* I successfully fought to include a
$25 million increase* in the County budget dedicated specifically to road
resurfacing projects, for a total of $213,223,620.

This fall, the County's Department of Public Works (DPW) will *resurface roads
in Alpine.* In addition, some of this work includes new traffic signal
improvements and ADA-compliant ramps. DPW Staff continue to work diligently
every day to maintain and enhance our infrastructure and they do a terrific
job.

*Plan Ahead! Alpine Road Resurfacing Projects*

*Nearly six miles of Alpine roads will be repaved.* While road repairs are
necessary, they often can cause minor delays or unexpected detours. My hope
is that with this information, parents dropping off or picking up their
kids at school, daily commuters, and local residents can plan ahead and
adjust their routine accordingly.

*Please forward or share this email with your family and neighbors, so that
they can plan ahead, too!  *

Keep scrolling to view a *colorful flyer with a list of road improvements*
coming to Alpine or you can click the blue button below for a *detailed
list of road improvement projects* coming to Alpine and a few other
unincorporated communities.

10:00am to noon at the Lakeside Library. As always, if you cannot attend,
please send another member from your Group.

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that LAFCO would be conducting a review of SANDAG as a
Metropolitan Planning Organization for the fiscal years 2024-2025.
-Everett Townsend, current Caltrans Rep at SANDAG, announced that Ann Fox
would be returning as the new District 11 Director. She will be the
Caltrans Representative at the SANDAG Board of Directors.

*Border Environmental Task Force Report:*
This is a new task force forming to address regional issues in the
geographical zone of the Pacific Ocean to the Arizona border and 10 miles
both south and north of the border with Mexico. "The Task force will be
comprised of representation from federal, state and local jurisdictions
within the border region and sector advisors with interests involved in
climate adaptation, environmental health, and environmental justice issues.
SANDAG may solicit interest from other entities in participating in the
Task force based on project needs. Taskforce member agencies are asked to
designate an alternate representative when the primary representative is
unable to attend to promote participation in meetings." The task force will
be one location for all work occurring in this area. Identification of gaps
in serving the area and binational coordination will be strengthened. The
meetings will be held remotely (virtually) and the APG has requested
membership on this new task force. For any Community Planning/Sponsor
Groups in this area who wish to be on the task force, please contact
kim.smith@sandag.org

*Otay Mesa East and SR 11 Report:*
More material will be transported to the US side of the port in order to
match the elevation of the facility/road on the Mexican side. There is a
plan to open SR 11 to local traffic in the near future. The flow of
revenues from the completed project are delineated in this attachment:
https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/2988061/Item_11__Att._1_-_Memorandum_from_PFM__SANDAG_Financial_Advisor.pdf

Jack Fisher, City of Imperial Beach comment: The third largest port in the
world -70 miles south of Ensenada is being constructed. Traffic coming
through commercial ports of entry will increase. We need part of the toll
to fix problems. We need to fix this now for our kids' future. The Border
Region needs to fix the problem.

*Transnet Major Corridors Update for North Coast Corridor and SR 78
Corridor:*
Victor Mercado, Caltrans - reported $1.06 billion from Federal, State and
Transnet funds for the region broken into highway improvements, rail
improvements and lagoon, bike, pedestrian improvements. This money funds
active transportation improvements for the north coast corridor.

APG comment to Board: Good morning. I won't be as polished as I'd hoped to
be. Being in the rural area and seeing these wonderful coastal projects, 78
really does need help at both ends. There's a big need there. But when I
see additional bike trails, pedestrian trails; this is a very bedecked out
plan and it's beautiful and it's wonderful, but if we're going to truly be
regional in how we reach out and spend the tax dollars; we're leaving the
unincorporated area in the dirt: literally. It's geographically isolated,
car dependent - it continues to be. You cannot walk anywhere, especially on
anything other than dirt or on the side of a highway. And, this has been
the situation for so long and I would like to see this regional agency
truly think about, okay, we have some healthy transportation alternatives
in parts of the region, but in the other regions there are none. I mean
there's nothing. I cannot walk to my neighbor's house. I must drive. And,
this has been the situation for years and Transnet is paid by everyone
since 1988. What is the percentage that has been spent by the folks in the
unincorporated region? Is that funding amount broken out anywhere? Is that
even available? And, if you were to break it out by population, maybe it
would be that we have received our fair share of the money. But maybe not.
There's a lack of information and it's important that it be transparent, so
that people know, gee, you know, this is really wonderful. Let's keep
improving the north coast there and give them more because the people out
in the unincorporated area have already gotten their share. That would go a
long way to developing trust and transparency. But, we don't know that.
That's an unknown piece of information. And, so, I'm a glass half-full
person and I love seeing these projects. And, I have my mountain bike and I
love to walk. But I have to put everything in my car and go find a park to
go do this. There is not a kid in the neighborhood who can hop on their
bike or walk. That's the life of being out in a rural area. The Youth
Opportunity Pass, wonderful program. Nobody can use it. You know very few
unincorporated communities have that advantage. We're going to have
microtransit. Another great option. Can't use it. So, you know, I want to
be here and to be excited and to rah-rah because these are great programs,
but we need to spread it out a bit more. To share these programs, make this
happen, not just talk about it, but actually have some real programs in
place that operate for people that are outside of the coastal and I-5 and
I-15 corridors. We need to really move this to the unincorporated area too
and include our neighbors. Thank you.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: ...So, I'm a big biker. My
e-bike and I get along really well. And I use it nearly everyday to get to
the UCSD campus from Del Mar. And, I take it to Trader Joe's, which is out
SR 56 on that new bike trail. And, I go north to Solana Beach and beyond.
Because the trails underneath San Elijo Lagoon are just absolutely - under
the highway there are fantastic.....And, I will bring one last - the SR 56
bike trail.  There's a new little piece that's just been put in right at
the old Carmel Valley Road connecting in....But I'll point out that
Sorrento Valley Road is a big part of that bike path. It has the biggest
potholes. It's pretty awful. And I don't know who's maintaining it, but
it's certainly not being attended to.  So I hope that as this new piece is
finished, perhaps Sorrento Valley Road can be improved as well.

John Minto, City of Santee comment: Thank you for the opportunity to speak.
I wasn't going to speak on this at all, but I'm listening to a lot of stuff
and you know what? All these projects are great. If you live in east county
everyone's going to say, no, we need to come out to east county and do ours
first. If you live in north county you say, oh no, don't come up to east
county - come up to north county. And, vice versa. All the way around the
city. Bottom line, all extremely important to get done. And, get it done
before sooner than later. I do have to be a little bit flippant, and I
apologize ahead of time. Maybe not. About the bicycle lane thing. You know,
you talk um, Terry you know you talked about avid bicycling and e-bike and
if you know - with the exception of east county at the 52 there is only one
protected bicycle lane in all of east county. And, that's so you can make
sure to get out of east county. Why they did that? I do not know. And, that
goes into Tierra Santa. I average about 30, 40 sometimes 50 miles on my
bike, e-bike. And I go through La Mesa, San Diego, Lemon Grove. All the way
out to Spring Valley, Dehesa. All the way into Alpine. And you know what? I
still haven't seen any protected bike lanes. The only protection I get is
when I say my prayer before I get on the bike and say, please don't let a
car hit me because they are only a few feet away. Because even where there
is a bicycle lane, most of the time they kind of faked a bicycle lane
because there wasn't enough room. So where you normally have, I think it's
an average four foot bicycle lane, I think we're lucky to get a two foot
bicycle lane and many of those are along the seams of the roadway. And just
talking to Mayor Jones and you know what? When cities do their slurries or
road repairs. They go up to the bike lane and stop. So there's always
potholes and there's always breaks along the seams and things of that
nature. So nobody really cares in east county if you have a good bike lane.
That's just my opinion. And, it goes back to what Robin said earlier about
maybe if we're going to talk about equity, equity should be looking at
safety more than anything else. Because I don't care who you are and you're
riding on a bike lane or a lack of bike lane in those areas; you know what?
Where's the equity and safety? And maybe a new term we ought to bring up in
safety is not just VMT, but EBMT, electric bike miles traveled. And how
safe are you on those EBMT's? That's all I have to say.

*Chief Executive Officer Performance Evaluation Process:*
On December 6th and 13th all SANDAG Board members are invited to
participate in developing performance goals for the CEO position.

*APG News:*
Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the unincorporated
area in San Diego County - has not set a meeting date with the APG as of
this report. Since July, the APG has been working to set up a joint meeting
with the Congressman, SANDAG CEO Mario Orso and our APG members without
success. SANDAG CEO Mario Orso has stated he will be available and happy to
attend our joint meeting. Congressman Issa has not been available and very
little communication has come from his office. The APG sent a request to
his Chief of Staff, Veronica Smith Wong. She has responded, but not with a
set date, yet.
The subject of the meeting will be:
"Transportation funding and safety in the Unincorporated Area; addressing
fatality rate on rural highways, safe wildfire evacuation, lack of public
transportation resulting in geographic isolation of vulnerable populations
and continued diversion of transportation funds from rural highway
projects."

Planning/Sponsor Groups that wish to support the establishment of this
joint meeting with Congressman Issa may also communicate directly with
Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.house.gov

*Questions from APG members*
*No questions received this month.*

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

Good Afternoon APG Members,

Note: The SANDAG Board of Directors held three meetings in the month of
January.

*SANDAG Leadership Changes - New Officers Elected:*
New Chair for SANDAG BOD: Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach
New Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: Joe Lacava, City of San Diego
New Second Vice Chair for SANDAG BOD: John Minto, City of Santee

Jan. 10th - APG comment to Board: Good morning. Congratulations on your
election as the dream team for the officers. I do represent the
unincorporated area, over 500,000 people, and, of course, this seat is not
a voting seat. Today I want to note for the record that the County is not
present and so, therefore; all action taken by this Board today - voting
action - has effectively disenfranchised the Unincorporated Area. We're not
present. And, we don't have a vote. And, I hope in 2025, I expect in 2025,
that this Board will overall do a better job of ensuring that the
Unincorporated Area is not disenfranchised. I realize County being absent
is not the fault of the Board, but there must be something in place that
takes into account that there's over half a million people who are not
participating in the proceedings today. Thank you.

Jan. 31st - APG Comment to the Board: The County of San Diego is not
present. However, the people of the County of San Diego are present.
(Note: County was completely absent for all of the January 2025 BOD
meetings - 10th & 24th & 31st)

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that the CFO was adjusting revenue projections on
TransNet funds by a couple of percentage points - between 2 to 4%. This
would be a decrease in expected funding and could affect both MTS and NCTD.
-The Grand Jury report findings and recommendations came as no surprise as
the Office of the Independent Performance Auditor had brought these needed
issues and changes to the Board in their earlier report and they are being
addressed.

*Otay Mesa East and SR 11 Report:*
The Federal agreements with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and with
General Services have set the stage for the beginning of construction and
the relationship SANDAG will have with CBP. Caltrans is also a partner.
If the toll revenues of the Port of Entry are not as projected the
shortfall cannot be made up with TransNet funds.

Ann Fox, Caltrans comment: ...We've done the studies that have shown the
many dollars and jobs lost and the air pollution created by the long delays
along our shared borders. California has invested more than half of the
$1.3 billion project cost and has spent hundreds of millions more building
out the corridor and the connections we have with State Routes 905 and 125.
...We have built the infrastructure, the new roads, the utilities, the
technology, the air quality monitors out there, in addition to over 180
acres of environmental mitigation.

Jack Fisher, City of Imperial Beach comment: (reading Brian Bilbray letter)
"... I'm sure some other members will not continue to support the expansion
of the economic growth with the environmental damage without addressing
historical and future environmental and public health threats caused by
such economic development. I ask that every board member here question if
their city council or county board would vote for any project knowing its
environmental and health problems if it was going to be anywhere close to
the disastrous situation that citizens of the South Bay faced everyday?"
I can't tell you how frustrated I am because I know with the increased
traffic and commerce Mexico will continue to grow. Their population will
continue to grow. It was mentioned that just this operation port of entry
opening will create 90,000 jobs on the U.S. side. I would imagine that
number probably doubles or triples on the Mexico side. Still without the
infrastructure.

*TransNet Major Corridor Projects Update: State Route 67:*
Sam Amen, Karina Cantera-Angel & Tracy D'Aoust Roberts of Caltrans -
presented 3 alternatives for the improvement of SR 67 understanding that
evacuation was the highest consideration. Project area is SR 67 from
Highland Valley in Ramona to Mapleview in Lakeside. Alternative #1 provides
4 outbound lanes and one inbound lane dedicated to inbound emergency
vehicles. Alternatives #2 & #3 provide some of these benefits, but not
consistently throughout the project area and include the use of shoulders
as "lanes" in an emergency.

APG comment to Board: The Unincorporated Area has been partnering with
Caltrans and we thank Sam, Karina, Tracy, Melina, Stephen and Tyler for
their dedication. Safety is always first.  Caltrans states, "The primary
goal of the SR 67 Highway Improvements Project is to increase capacity
during emergencies to significantly reduce evacuation times."  Safety is
always first. SANDAG serves over 3.3 million people across the region;
however, some benefit more than others. Had SANDAG delivered on the
promises of TransNet to the Unincorporated Area - Measure G would have
passed. The experience of those patiently awaiting their turn at the
Regional funding bucket has been disheartening. 1988 and 2004 turned into a
resounding "no" in 2024 for rural communities on Measure G. The LA fires
demonstrate a clear and present danger to rural highway travelers -
evacuees may live locally or may be visiting from the city. Caltrans has
stood ready and willing to deliver highway safety. Alternative #1 delivers
on the Promise. Let us immediately put into place emergency widening to
move evacuees through the current SR 67 gauntlet of bottlenecks. Safety is
always first. SANDAG does not want to be the obstacle to improvements
necessary to avoid the catastrophic results of the LA fires. The elected
Board members would not want the public to rightfully be able to say that
they could have done more to prevent a loss of life and property. Thank you.

Steve Vaus, City of Poway; Carolina Chavez, City of Chula Vista; Rebecca
Jones, City of San Marcos; Kevin Shin, City of Carlsbad; Bill Wells, City
of El Cajon; John Minto, City of Santee;  & Terry Gaasterland, City of Del
Mar all made comments: All of these city representatives were positive in
their comments emphasizing the need to expand SR 67 for evacuation purposes
and Mayors Minto, Jones, Wells and Gaasterland specifically endorsed the
selection of Alternative #1. There were no comments opposing Caltrans
proposed solutions to SR 67. The Board of Directors was supportive.

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach & SANDAG Chair comment:  "What can we do
now?"

Allan Kosup, Caltrans response: We have an emergency widening project that
just began this week on SR 67. The environmental report was received last
week and the project was begun immediately. It will be over the next six
months. This will provide more space in the event of an evacuation.

*APG News:*
-Thank you to all who were able to attend our in-person APG meeting held on
Saturday, January 4th, 2025. A quorum was established and voting actions
were taken.

Good Afternoon APG Members,

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that the California Air Resources Board (CARB)
accepted SANDAG's methodology for measuring GHG and, therefore, SANDAG can
continue with planning.
-A joint committee meeting between Borders, Regional Plan and
Transportations committees to present the Regional Plan. On track to meet
GHG and air quality conformity targets. This keeps funds flowing to SANDAG,
the region and the city.
-Congratulated North County Transit District for 30 years of service.

*Economic and Budget Outlook:*
Job growth is slowing. Sales tax revenue is down. Source of project funds:
State 37%, Federal 36%, TransNet 16%, Other Local Funds 11%.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: ...."We are in turbulent
times....And, I would really encourage us to be incredibly careful and
conservative as we go forward into the next six months of our budgeting..."

APG Comment to Board: My question is on the job gains and losses forecast.
I have two questions. What consideration was given to the impacts of AI on
the professional, technology, transportation and housing sectors? And, my
second question is do you anticipate a reduction in healthcare sector jobs
as restrictions on our immigration policy take effect? And, the reason I
ask that is that over the last few years the State of California had opened
up Medi-Cal coverage for all who are financially eligible, regardless of
immigration status. In the County of San Diego one-third of the population
receives this coverage. So, that would be a substantial change in
healthcare.

Naomi Young, SANDAG: I think you mentioned all important factors that can
be a source of a drag on our economy and our job creation. We didn't do a
forecast on jobs, we just presented how 2024's data on unemployment has
ended. Well what we saw between 2023 and 2024, looking at where we've seen
the sector impacts and the job growth in 2024 is what makes us think that
2025 will be more of a slow job creation environment rather than a
rebound...the message is volatility, differences in local conditions from
the national and that there are some very strong potential headwinds that
give us cause for caution.

*SR-125 Toll Operations Update:*
SANDAG is actively supporting legislation to assist the implementation of
SANDAG Board Resolution 2023-11, "Declaring support of eliminating the debt
and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027."

*TransNet Regional Transportation Congestion Improvement Program Proposed
(RTCIP) Fee Adjustment:*
SANDAG approved this yearly fee adjustment to be 6% effective FY beginning
July 1, 2025. This 6% increase in RTCIP fees is to keep pace with the cost
of building the roadway infrastructure needed as housing increases. The fee
is collected by each of the 18 cities and the County as part of building
fees paid by the private sector for each new housing unit. Fee will
increase from $2875.06 to $3047.57, per unit.

*County Representation of Unincorporated Communities:*
-The February 14th SANDAG Board meeting was the fourth consecutive meeting
without a County Supervisor present.
-The February 28th meeting was the first time unincorporated communities
had SANDAG voting representation in 2025.
-SANDAG BOD commented as follows:

*-From the February 14th meeting:*
APG Comment to Board: Good morning. I had hoped by now that we would have
representation from the County here. And, I see empty chairs, so I won't
belabor that point. I have a suggestion. Is this Board able to propose an
action such as a censure because I have seen that done recently at a city
when the Board member is not fulfilling their obligations. Is that
something that could be considered on behalf of the over 500,000 people who
were not represented here by a vote today? Thank you.

Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: I can look into that. I know we have an
attendance policy where I know letters can be sent and they're encouraged
to attend and follow up. But, I'll look into specifically whether a censure
can be, I'm not sure it's specifically in our policy as it exists now, but
I will double check.

*-From the February 28th meeting:*
Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos comment: I would like to, since the last
three meetings, I'm glad to see Supervisor Anderson here today. But the
last three meetings, the County had zero representation for over 500,000 in
the unincorporated areas. And, I would like to see if it's possible to move
forward with having that as a voting member, because a lot of our land use
decisions, and maybe it would be something at the planning level or the
regional planning and then only on land use decisions. I don't know what
that would look like. I'm just, I'm very concerned that there is a
possibility and it's happened now for three meetings. We didn't have any
actual action items, but it would be good to have someone that represents
them as a voting member. And, so I'd just like staff to move it.

Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: Yes, for the issue of them becoming a voting
member. That would require a change to legislation. So that is something
that could go to the Executive Committee. And, then ultimately to the
Board. But we need a sponsor to change that by legislation since the voting
members are set in our enabling legislation at the Public Utilities Code.

Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO: I also want to highlight that on the legislative
report. We reported that there was a hold bill, a place bill by Senator
Jones. And, actively being promoted by Supervisor Anderson. Of looking into
this issue.  (Mayor Rebecca Jones: "As a voting member?") We're having the
discussion. We haven't seen the total write up. But that's kind of what's
being indicated to us.

Rebecca Jones, City of San Marcos: Yeah, that would definitely support
something like that. So maybe Supervisor Anderson, if we could maybe keep
the board members updated on that because I would certainly support
something like that. It is just a shame that we have a situation where some
land use things really do affect our unincorporated areas....Personally, I
think it would be very beneficial to our outlying communities.

Joel Anderson, County of San Diego comment: I just want to make a
clarification. I'm an alternate. And, my colleagues have all those
positions. So, over the last four and a half years I've made 99% of the
meetings. So, I'm sorry. They appointed themselves. They choose not to
come. That's not on me. But I try to fill in for them as often as possible.
And, we do have a bill. But it's not going to move forward until everyone
on this committee agrees that's what they want. There's not fanciness
going. But we're very lucky to have Robin here. She lives in the
unincorporated. I think that this Board should look and see whether the
County deserves to have a vote at all at SANDAG; because all we're doing is
doubling down on cities where all my colleagues live. And nobody, if I
wasn't on this board, would be representing with a vote from the
unincorporated. And, to your point, it's 600,000 people they are without a
vote. And while we have cities. They are much smaller. That have a vote.
And I think if we want to pass a bond. We need to think about being
inclusive. And, including everybody at the table. Thank you.

APG Comment to Board: Thank you. To follow up on Mayor Jones and Supervisor
Anderson. We are a large unrepresented area as far as the level of
representation that's around the table. But as legislation works its way
and the Executive Committee starts to review. The unincorporated area needs
to have a full vote. Anything less is not really respectful of the citizens
who are living in the unincorporated areas. It is not as if when you buy a
house, you go, is this a city? And, am I going to be represented at SANDAG
the way other city folks are or am I in an unincorporated area? It is
generally not a consideration at all. No one even knows that they're not in
a city. Until they say, I'm unhappy and I want to go down to City Hall.
And, I say well, I'd like to see that place. Tell me when you find it.
Because there isn't a City Hall. We have the County. But the unincorporated
area needs to be part of the conversation. So many conversations that go on
at SANDAG - in other areas - about full representation of voting. Please be
sure that we're included.  And, thank you.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: Yes, thank you. I just want to
say that I strongly support that we pursue the ability to vote. Alpine,
Boulevard, Campo, Lake Moreno, Crest, Dehesea, Granite Hills, Harbison
Canyon, Descanso, Fallbrook, Jamal, Julian, Lakeside, Pine Valley, Potrero,
Rainbow, Ramona, San Dieguito, Spring Valley, Sweetwater, Valle De Oro,
Valley Center, Bonsall, Borrego Springs, Jacumba, and Twin Oaks Valley. I
wanted to read these names because when I first moved here 22 years ago. I
was totally surprised when I learned that Ramona, Borrego Springs, these
towns really had no representation at this level; had no city council or
town council. I learned a lot in my first couple of years moving to San
Diego County. I would suggest that we as a Board make strong and just clear
and simple moves. I even wonder if there is something we could do as an
amendment to SB 10? I just don't know. But I would suggest that we find a
way to, in a streamlined way, give a vote to the 600,000 people who have
these planning groups and have taken such a positive step forward. And, I
have a question. What is the weight of the County's vote? Is it these
600,000?

Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO: Amberlin can probably answer it better. I don't,
can't give you the exact answer. So I know she tracks this all the time.
(Mayor Terry Gaasterland: We can look it up, but maybe you can remind us
when you have it.)

*San Diego LOSSAN Rail Realignment Project:*
The realignment of the rail connection between San Diego and San Luis
Obispo does not normally impact the unincorporated area, but one of the
proposed alignments would. Infrequently, it is mentioned that the rail
connection should be relocated to follow the I-15. The Department of
Defense maintains a controlling interest in the rail location as it is
considered part of the military infrastructure utilized to move troops and
equipment throughout the country. Discussion of the new rail location is
ongoing.

*APG News:*
-At the February 28th meeting, SANDAG approved all of our Policy Advisory
Committee (PAC) membership requests except for the Audit Committee
membership that Carol Hake from the Lakeside CPG volunteered to join. The
explanation was the requirements for membership on this committee were
narrow and we did not qualify....however, Carol is certainly able to attend
as a member of the public. Also, it was recommended that both our primary
and alternate PAC members attend the PAC meetings.

-APG members on PACs have begun submitting reports to the APG. Thank you
for working to increase our presence at SANDAG.

-Update: Conversion of our APG "Advisory" Board seat to a "Voting" Board
seat - Currently California State Senator Brian Jones has submitted SB 240.
It is working its way through the legislative process. Also, State
Assemblyman Carl DeMaio has introduced a "spot bill" on the Assembly side.
More information will follow as these bills develop.

-Del Mar Mayor, Terry Gaasterland, has volunteered to assist the APG with
connecting to State Senator Catherine Blakespear as the spot bills noted
above progress through the legislative process.

-Update: Congressman Darrell Issa - representing the majority of the
unincorporated area in San Diego County - continues to communicate through
his District Rep, Alan Pellicani, that a meeting will happen at some point
in the future. If any group wishes to contact Issa directly, email his
Chief of Staff Veronica Smith Wong: veronica.smith@mail.
<veronica.smith@mail.house.gov>house.gov <veronica.smith@mail.house.gov>

No questions received this month.

Robin...please forward to all members of the APG.  Of note, this meeting
was the first where I attended as an appointed Advisory Member to the
Public Safety Committee.  Ed Musgrove, Councilmember, City of San Marcos
and Chair of the SANDAG Public Safety Committee, warmly introduced me to
the committee at the beginning of the meeting.  He emphasized to all how
important it was that this committee have APG representation from the
Unincorporated Areas of the County.  I must mention that Joel Anderson also
attended this meeting representing the Board of Supervisors which was
encouraging to see.
Thanks!  Paul

Paul Dombkowski, Vice Chair
Jamul - Dulzura CPG

It's important to note again that the Public Safety Committee advises the
SANDAG Board of Directors on major policy-level matters related to public
safety. The goals of the Committee are to improve the quality of life in
the region by promoting public safety and justice through collaboration,
information sharing, effective technology, and objective monitoring and
assessment. The Public Safety Committee also receives input from the
Chiefs/Sheriff’s Management Committee. Recommendations of the Public Safety
Committee are forwarded to the SANDAG Board of Directors for action.

At this March 21st Public Safety Committee Meeting, there were three main
Public Safety-related topics discussed. The first was an update from San
Diego's Automated Regional Justice Information System (ARJIS) which was
followed by an overview of the final SANDAG Regional Vision Zero Action
Plan.  The meeting concluded with a presentation from AB Livewell
which focused on the reduction of gun violence in the county.  Highlights
of these presentations are listed below for the APG's review. If there are
any questions, please let me know.  Best Regards!  Paul Dombkowski, Vice
Chair, Jamul-Dulzura CPG

*1. ARJIS (Automated Regional Justice Information System) Update*

As mentioned in my February Committee Report, ARJIS was established in 1976
and designed to enhance the identification and apprehension of suspected
criminals by facilitating information exchange among law enforcement
personnel in San Diego County.

Anthony Ray, Director, ARJIS, presented an update on a main initiative that
will enhance local law enforcement's response capabilities across the
county.

This main initiative is centered around the continued implementation
of the *Live
911* Program.  Tested and proven with both the Oceanside and Chula Vista
Police Departments, Live 911 allows field law enforcement to actually hear
live 911 calls as they are dialed into the 911 dispatcher.  Hearing these
911 calls live has allowed field law enforcement to better understand the
severity level of the situation before they arrive on the scene of the
call.  Both Oceanside and Chula Vista Police Departments have confirmed
that their police officers are better prepared for what they may encounter
upon arrival.  Both police departments have lauded the benefits of Live 911
as life saving.  As such, ARJIS is now working to obtain additional grants
to support implementing Live 911 in other San Diego county police
departments.

*2. SANDAG Review - (VZAP) Final Regional Vision Zero Action Plan *

*https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3223286/Item_4_-_Presentation.pdf
<https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3223286/Item_4_-_Presentation.pdf>*

*Overview*
On June 22, 2022, the Board of Directors adopted Resolution 2023-02
directing staff to seek funding and develop a Regional Vision Zero Action
Plan (VZAP) to advance traffic safety goals for the San Diego region. This
planning effort is included in the 2021 Regional Plan as a near-term
implementation action and safety is a goal area for the 2025 Regional Plan.
At this Public Safety Committee Meeting, SANDAG's Information Staff
presented the final Regional Vision Zero Action Plan, supporting safety
tools, and regional safety statistics.

*Key Considerations *
Developed in collaboration with local agency staff, the VZAP Technical
Advisory Group, community-based organizations and the public, the VZAP
identifies local traffic safety challenges and solutions that help the
region achieve the goal of zero fatal and serious injuries by 2050. The
plan identifies where the most fatal and serious injury crashes occur and
provides resources to improve safety in those areas. The plan also details
SANDAG’s role in implementing safety solutions and how progress toward
Vision Zero will be evaluated. With the completion of the VZAP, local
agencies are now eligible for Safe Streets and Roads for All implementation
grants. The final VZAP and its technical appendices are available on
SANDAG’s Vision Zero webpage. Note that the Regional VZAP was completed on
November 15, 2024.

The Regional VZAP includes implementation steps that are organized under
seven focus areas: Coordinate, Advocate, Plan, Fund, Educate, Evaluate, and
Implement. Multiple implementation efforts are currently in progress and
SANDAG has recently launched three: including California Assembly Bill 43
(Friedman, 2021) technical support, local agency countermeasure tool
development, and grant criteria updates.

• California Assembly Bill 43 (AB 43) establishes a more flexible speed
limit setting for municipalities. SANDAG is developing a Safety Corridor
Network for each jurisdiction to identify portions of their roadway network
that can be eligible for a 5-mph speed limit reduction.
• An online platform for local agencies is being developed to share safety
data, resources, support safety project development, and countermeasure
selection. • Regional Active Transportation Program and Smart Growth
Incentive Program evaluation criteria are being updated to further safety
goals and leverage the Regional VZAP analyses.

The Regional VZAP also included the development of a Traffic Safety
Dashboard for ongoing monitoring. On an annual basis, SANDAG will obtain,
clean, and review regional safety data. These will be evaluated for changes
in performance. A parallel process will evaluate progress on implementation
steps included in the Regional VZAP. Beginning in 2025, staff will develop
a report summarizing the results from this process.

*Next Steps *
Annual updates on the plan’s progress will be provided to SANDAG working
groups and policy advisory committees. Completion of the VZAP makes SANDAG
and local agencies eligible for federal safety grant funds.

*3.  AB Livewell - Ending Gun Violence in our Communities *

AB Livewell's overview was presented by Amanda Brown, CEO.  She emphasized
throughout her presentation that AB Livewell is dedicated to promoting
non-violence within communities. Their advocates work to empower
communities to rise above difficult circumstances, assess community needs
and provide suggestions for improvement. They also focus on empowering
individuals in communities most affected by violence, poverty, and other
detrimental life circumstances to make positive changes in their lives.

AB Livewell's Mission and Vision enhances and advocates for restorative
practices, to ultimately shift mindsets, through "credible messengers",
government relationships, community relations and coalition building. AB
Livewell's goal is for society to realize that individuals with a criminal
history, background or organized crime affiliations can transform their
lives and be a contribution to society - this transformation is the
foundation of the "credible messenger" program mentioned above.

For more details who AB Livewell is and what services and programs
they provide, please see the link below for their actual
presentation during the meeting.

https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3223321/Item_7_-_Presentation.pdf

paul.dombkowski@gmail.com>, Story R Vogel <storyvogel@aol.com>, Douglas S.
Dill <theddills@att.net>, Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>

*SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - February 2024*

*Caltrans:*
Roy Abboud and Allan Kosup - A Disaster Declaration from the President
would release funds for highway repairs due to the recent rainstorms.
Highway 78 has experienced significant damage in several locations.
Preventing damage from rainstorms is a shared responsibility as the "system
of streams, trash, trees, plants, and encampments" all contribute to water
overflow and runoff. Caltrans, cities and counties share responsibility to
clear creeks, but Federal and State permits to legally clear out stream
beds are difficult to procure.

*125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
Feb. 9th meeting Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG would be presenting
an action plan for the 125 Toll Road at the February 13th City of Chula
Vista Council meeting. This presentation would include the impact to other
projects with respect to available funds if the payoff date for the toll
road was moved up. If the community wishes to see a sooner payoff date for
the toll road they would need to understand that this money will come from
other projects.
-APG Question to Board - First, will the Sweetwater Community Planning
Group be receiving the same presentation on the toll road that the City of
Chula Vista will receive? And second, regarding determination of the end
date for the toll road - is there consideration of the increased use of
surface streets to bypass the toll road and the danger this presents to the
community?
-SANDAG Response (Nora Vargas) - This is the biggest issue in Bonita! The
County will be sponsoring a community meeting for all parties in the area.
-SANDAG Response (Coleen Clementson) And, yes, we are considering surface
street impacts.
Feb. 23rd meeting Carolina Chavez made a motion to, "Declare support for
eliminating the debt and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027." Board
consensus was for staff to explore the feasibility of this date as this
would be the earliest date that the payoff could be made without penalty.

*Report of SANDAG Draft 2025 Regional Plan:*
Susan Huntington, Antoinette Meier, Ray Majors and Allan Kosup continued
their presentation of an initial concept of the Draft 2025 Regional Plan.
Greenhouse gas reduction needs to be reduced by 18.9% by the year 2035.
Goals are:
Improve transit frequency and hours of operation.
Implement pricing strategies
Expand Youth Opportunity Pass
Provide parking by transit
Funding for these projects comes from 40 different sources: Federal, State
and Local
Budget begins with funds leftover from previous Plan
Review of current and future funding sources to determine viability of
covering a Plan budget range of $139 to $162 billion.
Clarified that managed lanes are only on the interstate/highway system
-NCTD reported a new microtransit/flexible fleet initiative was starting
and Fallbrook/Pala would be one of the first areas to pilot this program.
No additional details available at this time.
-APG Question to Board - First, what is the priority for wildfire
evacuation improvements? And second, regarding the greenhouse gas reduction
goal for 2035 and the use of reduced VMTs to meet that goal - the
unincorporated area has a new generation of youth who have not yet
developed a driving habit. Microtransit and useful bus routes/times
implemented in the next year or two is an opportunity to redirect future
drivers into GHG friendly travel modes. How soon will these options be made
available?
SANDAG Response - Express bus routes from unincorporated communities are
being implemented soon.

*SANDAG Roadside Service:*
General discussion on the increased cost for this program since SANDAG
began running operations. Request for a breakdown and clarification of
budget items to effectively monitor and provide oversight of the program.
Need statistics to see if a full tow truck is required to be the responding
vehicle for every freeway breakdown.

*Inland Rail Trail (bike path):*
Update on Phases 3 and 4 of this bike path from Escondido to Oceanside.
Many Board members noted that this was an example of another expenditure
that did not benefit those in the unincorporated areas of the County.

*Airport Transit Connection:*
Update on the progress of the new plan for moving people from the SD
Airport to downtown and other destinations. Extensive public comment and
Board comments on the unnecessary expense of building an elevated "people
mover" platform to transport people from the Airport to downtown as
trolleys and buses were already in existence. Also, people should be able
to move about all of the County, not just the coastal areas. Overall, this
plan is a substantial change from the multi-billion dollar Central Mobility
Hub vision of former Executive Director, Hasan Ikhrata.

*SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
The SANDAG Board of Directors March 8th meeting will be a Board Retreat
held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to
3:30. Both the APG Representative and Alternate plan to attend.

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

*https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3223286/Item_4_-_Presentation.pdf
<https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3223286/Item_4_-_Presentation.pdf>*

*Overview*
On June 22, 2022, the Board of Directors adopted Resolution 2023-02
directing staff to seek funding and develop a Regional Vision Zero Action
Plan (VZAP) to advance traffic safety goals for the San Diego region. This
planning effort is included in the 2021 Regional Plan as a near-term
implementation action and safety is a goal area for the 2025 Regional Plan.
At this Public Safety Committee Meeting, SANDAG's Information Staff
presented the final Regional Vision Zero Action Plan, supporting safety
tools, and regional safety statistics.

*Key Considerations *
Developed in collaboration with local agency staff, the VZAP Technical
Advisory Group, community-based organizations and the public, the VZAP
identifies local traffic safety challenges and solutions that help the
region achieve the goal of zero fatal and serious injuries by 2050. The
plan identifies where the most fatal and serious injury crashes occur and
provides resources to improve safety in those areas. The plan also details
SANDAG’s role in implementing safety solutions and how progress toward
Vision Zero will be evaluated. With the completion of the VZAP, local
agencies are now eligible for Safe Streets and Roads for All implementation
grants. The final VZAP and its technical appendices are available on
SANDAG’s Vision Zero webpage. Note that the Regional VZAP was completed on
November 15, 2024.

The Regional VZAP includes implementation steps that are organized under
seven focus areas: Coordinate, Advocate, Plan, Fund, Educate, Evaluate, and
Implement. Multiple implementation efforts are currently in progress and
SANDAG has recently launched three: including California Assembly Bill 43
(Friedman, 2021) technical support, local agency countermeasure tool
development, and grant criteria updates.

• California Assembly Bill 43 (AB 43) establishes a more flexible speed
limit setting for municipalities. SANDAG is developing a Safety Corridor
Network for each jurisdiction to identify portions of their roadway network
that can be eligible for a 5-mph speed limit reduction.
• An online platform for local agencies is being developed to share safety
data, resources, support safety project development, and countermeasure
selection. • Regional Active Transportation Program and Smart Growth
Incentive Program evaluation criteria are being updated to further safety
goals and leverage the Regional VZAP analyses.

The Regional VZAP also included the development of a Traffic Safety
Dashboard for ongoing monitoring. On an annual basis, SANDAG will obtain,
clean, and review regional safety data. These will be evaluated for changes
in performance. A parallel process will evaluate progress on implementation
steps included in the Regional VZAP. Beginning in 2025, staff will develop
a report summarizing the results from this process.

*Next Steps *
Annual updates on the plan’s progress will be provided to SANDAG working
groups and policy advisory committees. Completion of the VZAP makes SANDAG
and local agencies eligible for federal safety grant funds.

*3.  AB Livewell - Ending Gun Violence in our Communities *

AB Livewell's overview was presented by Amanda Brown, CEO.  She emphasized
throughout her presentation that AB Livewell is dedicated to promoting
non-violence within communities. Their advocates work to empower
communities to rise above difficult circumstances, assess community needs
and provide suggestions for improvement. They also focus on empowering
individuals in communities most affected by violence, poverty, and other
detrimental life circumstances to make positive changes in their lives.

AB Livewell's Mission and Vision enhances and advocates for restorative
practices, to ultimately shift mindsets, through "credible messengers",
government relationships, community relations and coalition building. AB
Livewell's goal is for society to realize that individuals with a criminal
history, background or organized crime affiliations can transform their
lives and be a contribution to society - this transformation is the
foundation of the "credible messenger" program mentioned above.

For more details who AB Livewell is and what services and programs
they provide, please see the link below for their actual
presentation during the meeting.

https://legistarweb-production.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/attachment/pdf/3223321/Item_7_-_Presentation.pdf

*****Next SANDAG Public Safety Committee Meeting scheduled for Friday,
April 18th at 1:00 PM. *****

February 21st

Robin...please forward to all members of the APG.  I did attend as a
member of the public but now see that I'm officially listed on the
committee's website as an Advisory Member representing our APG.
Eileeen Delaney, likewise, is also listed as our Alternate.  Thanks!  Paul

To begin, it's important to note that the Public Safety Advisory Committee
advises the SANDAG Board of Directors on major policy-level matters related
to public safety. The goals of the Committee are to improve the quality of
life in the region by promoting public safety and justice through
collaboration, information sharing, effective technology, and objective
monitoring and assessment. The Public Safety Committee also receives input
from the Chiefs/Sheriff’s Management Committee. Recommendations of the
Public Safety Committee are forwarded to the SANDAG Board of Directors for
action.

At this February 21st Public Safety Committee Meeting, there were two main
Public Safety-related topics discussed. The first was an overview of San
Diego's Automated Regional Justice Information System (ARJIS) which was
followed by an overview of the very important work being conducted by the
San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force. Highlights of these presentations
are listed below for the APG's review. If there are any questions, please
let me know and I'll do my best to address them as needed.

1. ARJIS - Automated Regional Justice Information System

Anthony Ray, Director, ARJIS, presented a very detailed overview of the
function of ARJIS.  Highlights of his presentation are listed below:

Established in 1976, the Automated Regional Justice Information System
(ARJIS) was designed to enhance the identification and apprehension of
suspected criminals by facilitating information exchange among law
enforcement personnel in San Diego County, California.

Since November 1980, ARJIS usage has increased, accompanied by tangible
benefits in terms of arrests and cleared crime cases with ARJIS
information. The system's effectiveness is anticipated to rise with
additional officer training in data access, improved information quality,
full utilization of components by all law enforcement agencies in the
region, and proposed system development and enhancements.

In 2004, ARJIS was consolidated with SANDAG and the Joint Powers Agency
(JPA - see below) and modified to include the formation of the Public
Safety Committee, replacing the ARJIS Board of Directors with
representation by elected officials, law enforcement executives, emergency
medical services, and homeland security officials. Governed by the Public
Safety Committee (PSC) who advises the SANDAG Board of Directors, SANDAG is
the only place where all of the jurisdictions (the 18 cities and the
county) sit at the table and have a voice in decision-making.

ARJIS as a Joint Powers Agency

Created as a Joint Powers Agency, it serves as a vital information-sharing
platform among justice agencies throughout San Diego and Imperial Counties,
California. Evolving into a complex criminal justice enterprise network, it
is utilized by over 80 local, state, and federal agencies in the two
California counties bordering Mexico. The governance structure emphasizes
data sharing and cooperation at all levels, fostering collaboration among
chiefs, officers, and technical staff within member agencies.

Major Public Safety Initiatives

Instrumental in various public safety initiatives, including wireless
access to critical data like photos and warrants in the field.
Additionally, it supports crime and sex offender mapping, evaluates crime
analysis tools, and manages an enterprise system of applications aiding in
crime solving and offender identification. Serves as the region's
information hub for officer notification, data sharing, and the real-time
uploading of various public safety data types.

Key Contributions and Features

   -

   Cross jurisdictional data sharing enhances crime series identification
   and results in better-informed policy decisions.
   -

   Real-time data access expedites case closures.
   -

   Common validation codes ensure data standardization.
   -

   Standardized classification and reporting.
   -

   Economies of scale achieved through pooled resources and shared
   enterprise licenses & procurements.

2.  San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force (SDHTTF)

Geanie Franco, Task Force Commander, CA Dept of Justice, presented a very
interesting and informative overview of the SDHTTF.  Highlights of her
presentation are listed below:

The SDHTTF, a cooperative effort led by the California Department of
Justice, consists of the federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies
(LE) listed below. SDHTTF’s mission is to significantly disrupt and
dismantle both sex and labor trafficking child exploitation organizations
through a comprehensive, collaborative, and regional response.

California Department of Justice/Attorney General's Office (DOJ/AGO),
California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR), California
Highway Patrol (CHP), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Homeland
Security Investigations (HSI), National City Police Department (NCPD), San
Diego City Attorney's Office (SDCAO), San Diego District Attorney's Office
(SDCDAO), San Diego County Probation Department (SDCPD), San Diego
Sheriff's Department (SDSD), San Diego Police Department (SDPD), United
States Attorney's Office, Southern District of California (USAO), and other
supporting agencies to include Carlsbad Police Department (CPD), Chula
Vista Police Department (CVPD), Coronado Police Department (CPD), Escondido
Police Department (EPD), Immigration and Customs Enforcement
(ICE)/Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), Internal Revenue Service
(IRS), La Mesa Police Department (LMPD), Naval Criminal Investigative
Service (NCIS), Oceanside Police Department (OPD), San Diego Unified School
District Police Department (SDUSDPD), United States Customs & Border
Protection, San Diego Sector Border Patrol (US CBP), and the United States
Marshals Service (USMS).

Below is an example of the great work that the SDHTTF does day in, day out
- this one at the most recent San Diego Comic-Con Convention:

As part of a joint investigation through the SDHTTF, California Attorney
General Rob Bonta today announced the results of a human trafficking sting,
aimed at recovering victims of sex trafficking and targeting sex buyers
using the San Diego Comic-Con Convention to seek out potential victims.
From July 25 to 27, 2024, the California Department of Justice’s (DOJ) San
Diego Human Trafficking Task Force (SDHTTF) conducted an anti-human
trafficking operation coinciding with the Comic-Con Convention that
resulted in 14 arrests and 10 victims recovered and offered services.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Ron Nehring, Crest Planning Group Chairman <
ronnehring@ronnehring.ccsend.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 27, 2025 at 3:26 PM
Subject: PLANNING GROUP: What we have done so far on wildfire
To: <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com>

Fellow Planning Group Chairs,

Following the interest and feedback I received regarding our new Firewise
USA site, I wanted to share additional resources and insights from our work
on wildfire preparedness and evacuation in our subregion. I’m also
interested in knowing what work your Planning Group has done that perhaps
we have not thought of so we can strengthen our efforts.

In 2021, our Planning Group established a dedicated working group on
wildfire and evacuation. Over the course of three years, we held meetings
and engaged extensively with stakeholders—including our local fire
district, Cal Fire, the Crest Fire Safe Council, representatives from the
County, the Sheriff’s Department, and others—to identify the most effective
ways to reduce wildfire risk and enhance evacuation capacity.

This effort culminated in a comprehensive package of seven wildfire-related
resolutions, which our Planning Group unanimously adopted in the summer of
2024. Given our advisory role to the County of San Diego, each resolution
is framed as a recommendation to County. You can review the full package of
resolutions, along with a summary, here: Crest Planning Group Fire
Resolutions.
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJVShatP__5WDqsOxEzOSLt0N1DkC0uglT12fnpaypLueU2s1G3PpLX2QIxvykqsJlEMDcC2miEM8Bqv622WJ-69pcxx7i8NhOTmgjqk0B0mJfPKWnaIxBjT80ovcsz0UKyYqnOwPhYVdrhyFb7VvbHFgfL3SukQfI6qrOJzATK-R_tAmMvo4ITcM4-w9Z2LD4LLQyr3L6ijIc_JBgR4xPXZ5jMCN4IXalwne9xF64Dap01AmRYnkT7NxXK9j5oEi_w==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>

One key takeaway from our work was the value of the Firewise USA program
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyDxoyackA2RcQNTEfRlDPkbHmX2MuO8PBPswQ8KgE-rcyjYWxx1MCWnw0BK9QNwVPRmMPe--vv-_HOnhwjgONujomYHLomm1G-istWt-z54Z9ytb_uSjY54cNszAN2-4h6nrYtrH8BE9W20iK5zGCgg==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>,
which allows groups of at least eight homeowners to establish a Firewise
USA site, take steps to reduce wildfire risk, and potentially qualify for
homeowners insurance discounts.

Recognizing its benefits, one of our seven resolutions specifically
encourages and supports the formation of Firewise USA sites throughout our
subregion.

After I became Chairman of our Planning Group, we launched a website to
better serve our residents by providing access to essential information.
While the County’s webpage for our Planning Group exists, it is difficult
to find and lacks comprehensive resources. Our goal was to create a one-stop
hub where residents can find details about our Planning Group’s work,
wildfire preparedness, code enforcement, defensible space requirements, and
more. You can visit the site at: CrestPlanningGroup.com
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyNiKG57PrvAcVhxPjLGUulw37A996ASKMyLn1vsnrei-gZWKYuy2livonBtHIF9k9VG_wnP-b7EVEi0hg9ftQc50vEBE2M1Z12ueCdNq6VOI=&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>
.

At our next Planning Group meeting on Monday, February 10 at 6:30 PM at the
Crest Community Association Clubhouse, 113 North Park Drive, El Cajon we
will discuss the Firewise USA program and how to establish additional sites
in our subregion. I invite you to join us for this discussion—if you or
members of your Planning Group plan to attend, please let me know in
advance so I can ensure you are introduced. Google maps
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydykexf6WkHNMJC4WTlUCRh3jzKPtSIxU6PCR-kc7cGljF6zwy53RYBlN1oKlhju9Q-BW6Qd2q3qIReUPxhXLessZ-z2CIaStIq64BZ0WyPags=&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>

We have made progress but we have a very long way to go before the wildfire
threat in our subregion has been materially reduced. To this end,
Resolution 1 in our package established wildfire threat reduction as the
top priority for our Planning Group.

I think sharing ideas and best practices at, and in between, our APG
meetings can help us all in our efforts to improve our communities and make
them safer. I hope you find this information useful, and look forward to
hearing about the work you've done.

All the best,
[image: Ron Nehring]

Ron Nehring

Chairman, Crest-Dehesa-Granite Hills-Harbison Canyon Planning Group

Planning Group <descansocpg@gmail.com>, Paul Dombkowski <
paul.dombkowski@gmail.com>, Story R Vogel <storyvogel@aol.com>, Douglas S.
