Diefenbach <csdiefenbach@sbcglobal.net>, Sandra Farrell, <
tovcsg.chair@gmail.com>, Rebecca Falk <rebfalk7@gmail.com>, <
petersonenv@hotmail.com>, Jennifer Haider <jennehaider@gmail.com>

*SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*

*SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536 13th
Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
(Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.

*Caltrans:*
Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.

*125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
March 22nd Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 29th to specifically discuss the
results of this internal audit.)
Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of 125
Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.

March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf

The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
the 125 Toll Road.
Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
collected and toll user accounts?
Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver on
the contractual requirements?
Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
tolls correctly?
What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
to equipment disconnect sooner?
Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to the
former CEO?
Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
faulty numbers not corrected instead?
How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
the I-15?
How much money in tolls was lost overall?

Board member comments were:
"After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
"This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
"We need to investigate potential fraud."
"We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."

The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.

*Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
Projects:*
SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included the
project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
complaints from its own members.

APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."

Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."

You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
and here is the link to the budget document:
https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2025.pdf#page=6

*SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
areas for housing.
Board discussion on the increased legislation from Sacramento (SB 35 and SB
423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers. Cities
reported that Sacramento was applying a state-wide housing solution to
individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable
land available than others.  Some unincorporated communities are located
near job centers and should not be dismissed as potential housing locations
due to a lack of public transit options.

*APG Update:*
In addition to this SANDAG report the APG has received acceptance of our
Associate membership (non-voting) invitation to Community Sponsor Groups by
Bonsall (Jennifer Haider), Jacumba (Cherry Diefenbach) and Twin Oaks Valley
(Joseph Bunn). We will formally accept their membership at our June 1st APG
meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

Attached are documents pertaining to a Discretionary Permit for a *Site
Plan* - *PDS2024-STP-24-015*.  If you normally receive a plot plan, it will
be delivered through regular mail within the next few days.

Pursuant to Board Policy I-1,

(https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/cob/docs/policy/I-1.pdf),
this request for a recommendation is being sent to you because a
discretionary permit application has been submitted to Planning &
Development Services (PDS) for a project within your Community/Design
Review Area.  Once a recommendation is made, please forward it to PDS with
Form #534 so the recommendation can be included in correspondence to the
project applicant and as part of the staff report for the appropriate
hearing body of officer.

Every effort should be made to submit a group recommendation within seven
calendar days following the CPG/DRB/CSG meeting.

If you have any questions or comments regarding *PDS2024-STP-24-015*,
please reach out to *Aidan Pulley* via email at aidan.pulley@sdcounty.ca.gov.
If for any reason the project is reassigned, * Aidan Pulley* will reach out
and provide an updated point of contact for the project.

*Kushinga Carlos Pfende, *Land Use Aide

Pronouns: (he/him/his)

Planning & Development Services

Building Division

Phone: 858-694-3010

Previous Number: 858-694-3042

Email: kushinga.pfende@sdcounty.ca.gov

*Second Opinion: *A second opinion is available on any interpretation or
correction provided and will not affect the level of customer service you
receive. We ask you to provide your interpretation of the code along with
any health and safety concerns that the interpretation may cause and how
this will affect your project. The second opinion will come from one of our
senior staff or a supervisor who will have a chance to take a deeper look
at supporting documentation on both sides of the issue.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Michael V Garcia <Michael.Garcia@sandag.org>
Date: Tue, Apr 1, 2025 at 1:01 PM
Subject: On behalf of SANDAG CEO Mario Orso: Legislative Update
To:
Cc: Clerk of the Board <clerkoftheboard@sandag.org>

Dear Members of the Board,

As mentioned at the Board of Directors meeting last Friday, I wanted to
provide an update on two pieces of legislation recently introduced in the
state legislature that, if enacted, would modify the composition of the
SANDAG Board of Directors:

*AB 24 (DeMaio)*
This bill, introduced by Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, proposes modifying the
SANDAG Board of Directors by removing one of the two County Board of
Supervisors seats and replacing it with a representative from the San Diego
County Association of Planning Groups. It would also require the remaining
County Board representative to be from an unincorporated area of the
county. The bill has been double-referred to the Assembly Local Government
Committee and the Assembly Transportation Committee. It currently does not
have a scheduled hearing date.

*SB 240 (Jones)*
This bill, introduced by Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, proposes to
replace the secondary representative from the County Board of Supervisors
with a resident from an unincorporated area of the County, as selected by a
majority of the county’s community planning groups, to serve a 1-year term.
The bill also eliminates the requirement that one Board of Supervisors
member be from a substantially incorporated district and the other from an
unincorporated district. This bill has not yet been referred to a policy
committee in the Senate.

We will continue to monitor these bills and provide you with updates
accordingly.

Thank you,
Mario

[image: San Diego County District 5 Supervisor Jim Desmond]
<https://www.supervisorjimdesmond.com/?e=95833993db322c37c1cd90cee589f623&utm_source=desmond&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=batteryenergyboard1&n=1>

Travis --

Over the past year, we’ve discussed extensively the challenges and risks
associated with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), particularly their
safety concerns when located near homes and sensitive areas. This week, the
Board of Supervisors took an important step toward addressing these
concerns.

This year alone, three BESS facilities have caught fire in San Diego
County, including the Otay Mesa facility, which burned for over two weeks.
These incidents underscore the urgency of improving safety measures for
these projects.

In response to these events, the Board voted to receive the *“San Diego
County BESS Best Practices Report”* and implement interim guidelines based
on its recommendations. These measures aim to make BESS projects safer for
our communities while ensuring we stay ahead of evolving technology.

*Key Highlights of Today’s Decision:*

   - *Interim Guidelines Implementation:* County Fire will adopt updated
   standards, requiring technical studies, plume modeling, and safety measures
   such as 100-foot setbacks between project sites and property lines.
   - *Enhanced Collaboration:* County Fire will continue working with
   industry leaders to refine best practices as technology advances.
   - *Future Statewide Fire Codes:* With state-level fire codes for BESS
   expected next year, these interim guidelines provide a critical bridge to
   protect public safety.
   - *Procedural Clarifications:* The Fire Chief has the authority to
   implement these guidelines without needing further Board action, allowing
   for prompt and effective implementation.

Safety for our residents remains our top priority. These updated
regulations are a step forward in protecting our communities while
continuing to research and improve the safety of BESS technology.

As always, we remain committed to balancing innovation with public safety
and will revisit this issue as new information and technologies become
available.

Thank you for your engagement in this vital matter. Together, we are
working to safeguard our neighborhoods and ensure a safer future.

San Diego County District 5 Supervisor Jim Desmond

body:
Good Evening APG members,

Here is an upcoming change to communication options in our unincorporated
areas. Please see Kevin May's and Paul Dombkowski's request to have this
distributed to APG members.

Robin Joy Maxson, Chair
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
760-705-7435
"Remember, a childhood is a limited opportunity. Use it well!"

___________________________________________________

Robin

Kevin May and I believe that AT&T's proposal before the CPUC to end its
obligation to provide landline service to many areas of Unincorporated San
Diego County is an issue that all APG CPSGs should be aware of and given an
opportunity to respond back to the media request sent out below.

We appreciate your thoughts on distributing this email string out to all
APG members....

Best Regards!  Paul Dombkowski, Jamul Dulzura CPG

Hello folks,

Below is an email I had received yesterday, including the attachments that
came with it.  Recently, I also had received another personal phone call
from a concerned resident of Dulzura regarding the same thing. I would like
you to review this email and attachments in preparation for discussion and
possible action at the next CPG meeting on Feb. 20th*.  Please refrain from
any discussion outside the meeting so as not to break any Brown Act issues.
*

If you wish to respond individually to this media request feel free to do
so as a citizen.

I will be letting them know that as a group, we will be responding after
our next meeting.

Kevin

Cell: 619-987-2586

*****************************************************************************************

Dear East County and Backcountry community planning group chairs:

AT&T has a proposal before the CPUC to end its obligation to provide land
line service for our entire region. See attached letter and map.

There are public hearings in Feb. and March but none are in San Diego
County.

Please provide comments for the article we’re preparing, as I’m aware that
many rural/backcountry areas lack adequate cell phone service.   Also I
believe there should be a hearing in rural San Diego County, since our
border areas have unique issues such as  not being able to make cell calls
near the border without international charges.  No doubt there are other
issues.

Specifically please comment on:

   1. Are there reasonable alternatives to land lines in all areas that
   your planning group serves, such as adequate cell service,  Cox service,
   etc.?  If not, please describe the problems.
   2. Do you believe eliminating land lines will jeopardize public safety?
   3. Have you had issues of cell phone towers burning down or being
   knocked offline by wildfires, high winds,etc?
   4. How risky is it to be left without land lines when power goes out for
   days, as is common during “public safety shutoffs” by SDG&E,  given this
   means even those with cell phones may not be able to charge them easily?
   And what if your cell phone battery is dead when there is an emergency and
   an outage?
   5. Do you believe the CPUC should block AT&T’s request?
   6. Can you provide examples of people harmed when land lines were down
   for other reasons, or people who were saved by having a landline?  Example,
   I’m aware of a rancher whose llama died of a rattlesnake bite during an
   AT&T outage and he could not get cell reception at his home to call for
   help, even though he’d recently bought a cell phone days before that the
   company promised would work in his rural location.
   7. Do you believe the CPUC should hold a hearing in San Diego’s East
   County, such as Alpine, for rural residents to access?
   8. Will you be contacting the CPUC to register comments and/or request a
   hearing here?
   9. What else should the public know about this proposal and its
   implications for residents and businesses in our region?

Please respond ASAP as the first hearing was this week.....we’d like to get
a story up right away.   Thanks.

Please share this with anyone else who may be interested, such as other
community groups,  backcountry businesses or business groups, etc.

Miriam Raftery,  Editor

www.EastCountyMagazine.org

619 698 7617

editor@eastcountymagazine.org

Dear Interested Stakeholder,

We want to hear from you! The San Diego County Fire Protection District
invites you to attend a public meeting to share your thoughts on the San
Diego County Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Best Practices Report
(Report). BESS are technology designed to store and manage energy for later
use. It typically uses rechargeable batteries to store energy from various
sources, such as the electrical grid, renewable energy sources like solar
or wind power, or other power generation methods. On September 11, 2024,
the Board of Supervisors directed San Diego County Fire to develop a
technical study with recommendations that consider setbacks from
residential uses as well as best practice safety standards, including 2023
NFPA 855. The completed report can be accessed at the project website. County
Staff is looking for your feedback on the recommended best practices, safety
standards, and siting recommendations for new and existing BESS applications.

    Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Dear Interested Stakeholder,

We want to hear from you! The San Diego County Fire Protection District invites you to attend a public meeting to share your thoughts on the San Diego County Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Best Practices Report (Report). BESS are technology designed to store and manage energy for later use. It typically uses rechargeable batteries to store energy from various sources, such as the electrical grid, renewable energy sources like solar or wind power, or other power generation methods. On September 11, 2024, the Board of Supervisors directed San Diego County Fire to develop a technical study with recommendations that consider setbacks from residential uses as well as best practice safety standards, including 2023 NFPA 855. The completed report can be accessed at the project website. County Staff is looking for your feedback on the recommended best practices, safety standards, and siting recommendations for new and existing BESS applications. PDS is hosting this virtual public meeting to receive your input on November 14, 2024, at 6:00 PM (registration link provided below).

Disability-related accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting participation, language interpretation, including American Sign Language, and written materials in alternative languages and formats are available upon request. body:
Good afternoon,

Please see the attached information on the candidate filing period that is
now open.  If you are receiving this email your term expires at the end of
this year and you will need to file for re-election if you would like to
continue on the Planning Group.

The filing has to be completed in person at the county ROV.  The deadline
to complete the paperwork is August 9, 2024, but my advice is to get it
completed this week or next week because the closer we get to the
deadline the longer it takes to process at the ROV because the last few
days there are a rush of candidates who wait till the deadline.

I am happy to answer any questions you may have.  Please feel free to reach
out to me on my cell.

*Travis Lyon* | Chair
Alpine Community Planning Group

619.952.8607

body:
Hi Travis, 
Nice job on the BESS email . Those points  look like good talking point material for defending our communities from really bad battery storage projects.
Parks and Recs. Trail Master, Lizzy Bendrick got back to me about the "no-parking" signs at Loveland.She said she will look into it. Just keeping you in the loop as we see how it is evolving. I will get back with Supervisor Anderson's staff about the idea soon.

Russell 
   ----- Forwarded Message ----- From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>To: Lizzy Bendrick <lizzy.bendrick@sdcounty.ca.gov>Sent: Monday, December 9, 2024 at 08:49:30 PM PSTSubject: Fw: [External] Re: Follow-Up on Japatul Road Parking Lot
  Hi Lizzy,
Thank you for letting me know you are looking into this parking. 
I bring up the removal of the No Parking signs about it at last weeks Alpine Community Planning Group. I was there to thank the members for their  letter of support on Sunrise to Sunset opening of the recreation program at Loveland per the public easement which is cited in the letter of support.

|
|
|  |
ltr - SWA re Sunrise to Sunset at Loveland - 10.23.2024 (1).pdf

 |

 |

Alpine & Jamul Neighbors, Regional Trails Advocates, 

The proposal and ask for using the Use of the SDGE easement for recreation at Loveland  is below.
It would be good to create as much enthusiasm and make as much progress as we can before the March 14 , Trails and Access meeting in Alpine. 
I am workiing at getting a decent decision making contact, or at least a legit public relations person at SDGE . We might have that by tommorrow. The proposal I sent out on Feb 20  is below.  It has been sent  to all the local politician's staff, Friends of Loveland Reservoir,  and others. Any help with promoting use of the SDGE easement at Loveland  would be beneficial. 
Contacting the Sweetwater General Manager, Directors, and Public affairs is important because Loveland Stakeholders(that's us) and  SDGE will need Sweetwater's cooperation.

The big Sweewater parking lot with approved use of the SDGE easements could be a great hub for connections to trails around the reservoir. It also makes getting to the shoreline much easier than what exists. There is a man , John Allen , working on connector trails, north , south, east, and west,  around the area including possibly to Sloan Canyon. He will need help from user groups. I am willing to help motivated individuals or groups.  Getting the use of the Easement is a great improvement with or without future connections. 

Jamul Dulzura Planning Group link for Thursday's Meeting. 
So far Friends of Loveland has offered to support the proposal and It seems likely that the Jamul Dulzura planning group will.. I am updating them and asking for a letter of support on the SDGE easement on Thursday. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/Groups/jamuldulzura/2024/JD240307AGSPCL.pdf
Please promote a win on opening this SDGE easement. 

Thank you,
Russell 

Dear SDGE  Public Affairs Manager and Land Use Professionals, 

There is an opportunity for SDGE leadership and the Land Use Department to step up for shared regional goals of public welfare recreation opportunities and conservation. 

This is a once in a generation style opportunity to better the lives of people in our region through increased access to public land while avoiding negative conservation impacts that normally come with such important improvements. I am sure SDGE is broadly supported by government partners, such as the county of San Diego and Sweetwater Authority in cooperating with this proposal
I am involved in a meetings for a California   recreation program enhancement grant to the Sweetwater Authority that is being lead by Senator Brian Jones's local staff and Sweetwater Authority General Manager, Carlos Quintero. 

One proposal is to use the SDGE Easement in one or more locations to facilitate the ability of  hikers, fishers, and nature watchers to enjoy this beautiful but difficult to access area. The goal is to allow lake users to benefit from the US Forest Service , 5 mile shoreline fishing easement. 

I would like to present reassurance that by working with partners on opening up access throught the Sunrise Powerlink Easement on  Sweewtater managed public property, SDGE would be accomplishing important Livewell partnership goals for the County of San Diego and Region and our diverse friends and neighbors, including income limited and mobility challenged people. 
Furthermore, access around Loveland Resevoir is not a new goal or solely connected to this current opportunity.Maximizing Hiking and Fishing at Loveland Reservoir is a goal stated several times in the Alpine Communtity Plan. 

I am including a google earth image of the area with the SDGE easement and a map of  the Forest Service easement for reference.
Please provide a contact person who I can talk with and introduce to our government partners, Sweetewater Authority and Loveland user group stakeholders as appropriate during this great Loveland  trails and access enhancement effort some of whom I am CC'ing this email. 
Conservation and taxpayer Benefits"
Public money savings and conservation wins:. 
Since the land disturbance is already there this is a huge conservation win. California money from the AB 102 grant can be better utilized elsewhere on the stie.

Forest Service Public hiking, fishing and bird watching, easment map. 

Please let me know who our contact for the goal of increasing this access is and how I can help with this effort.

Subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine

Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

The Board voted to receive the “San Diego County BESS Best Practices Report” and implement interim guidelines based on its recommendations.

[San Diego County District 5 Supervisor Jim Desmond] <https://www.supervisorjimdesmond.com/?e=ea03d1deffe541df037d50b29d69f37c&utm_source=desmond&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=batteryenergyboard1&n=1>

Darlene --

Over the past year, we’ve discussed extensively the challenges and risks associated with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), particularly their safety concerns when located near homes and sensitive areas. This week, the Board of Supervisors took an important step toward addressing these concerns.

This year alone, three BESS facilities have caught fire in San Diego County, including the Otay Mesa facility, which burned for over two weeks. These incidents underscore the urgency of improving safety measures for these projects.

In response to these events, the Board voted to receive the “San Diego County BESS Best Practices Report” and implement interim guidelines based on its recommendations. These measures aim to make BESS projects safer for our communities while ensuring we stay ahead of evolving technology.

Key Highlights of Today’s Decision:

  *   Interim Guidelines Implementation: County Fire will adopt updated standards, requiring technical studies, plume modeling, and safety measures such as 100-foot setbacks between project sites and property lines.
  *   Enhanced Collaboration: County Fire will continue working with industry leaders to refine best practices as technology advances.
  *   Future Statewide Fire Codes: With state-level fire codes for BESS expected next year, these interim guidelines provide a critical bridge to protect public safety.
  *   Procedural Clarifications: The Fire Chief has the authority to implement these guidelines without needing further Board action, allowing for prompt and effective implementation.

Safety for our residents remains our top priority. These updated regulations are a step forward in protecting our communities while continuing to research and improve the safety of BESS technology.

As always, we remain committed to balancing innovation with public safety and will revisit this issue as new information and technologies become available.

Thank you for your engagement in this vital matter. Together, we are working to safeguard our neighborhoods and ensure a safer future.

Goodmorning. 

   ----- Forwarded Message ----- From: Carl DeMaio <carl@carldemaio.org>To: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>; Carl DeMaio <carl@reformcalifornia.org>Cc: Brett Wilkins <brett@reformhq.org>; Brett Wilkins <brett@reformcalifornia.org>; Brett Wilkins <brett@capitolmedia.co>Sent: Saturday, August 31, 2024 at 07:45:24 AM PDTSubject: RE: Loveland Reservoir , Local Politicians Holding us Down, Should Help.

Russell – just now coming up for air and able to catch up on emails.  I will take office Dec 1 – and we will go to bat STRONGLY on this using the official status of State Assembly.  Help is on the way!

  

From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>
Sent: Monday, August 19, 2024 1:44 PM
To: Carl DeMaio <carl@carldemaio.org>; Carl DeMaio <carl@reformcalifornia.org>
Cc: Brett Wilkins <brett@reformhq.org>; Brett Wilkins <brett@reformcalifornia.org>; Brett Wilkins <brett@capitolmedia.co>
Subject: Loveland Reservoir , Local Politicians Holding us Down, Should Help.

You don't often get email fromrussellwalsh2003@yahoo.com. Learn why this is important
  |  |

Carl Demaio

Brett Wilkins

  

  

Hello Carl and Brett,

  

I hope you are both doing well. 

  

As you know, maybe you recall,  I have practically dedicated four years of my life to bringing conscientiousness and lawfulness to fair  protection and maintenance and public access at Loveland Reservoir  for the environment and current and future generations of people needing and deserving of the recreation Sweetwater Authority owes us there.  

  

I want to report that the east county is infected by an interconnection of Sweetwater Authority sycophants and protectors and Travis Lyon's has the disease. I think you can understand this without me making a grid or something like that! Everybody, it turns out, is less naive than I am or was.

 

  

The Alpine Community Planning Group Chair  has subjugated Loveland advocates appealing to his board even when we have been given unanimous support from the members.

I am not sure the extent to which this is Joel Anderson's game and I hope little, but your opponent Andrew Hayes and everybody under Senator Jones' has chosen to walk a much finer line than they had to in deference to this Sweetwater Authority and their friends. That office has now dumped us with unfulfilled promise from Nicholas Brust.  Honest efforts at justice for Loveland have been hurt badly. 

We don't quit, but it would be nice to see a change in Travis, Darlene Cossio, and her Friends of Lovleand group in favor of people who have given so much more than they have in the Loveland fight  for no fame , no political benefits and no financial gain.

  

I don't really care about Darlene, I don't think her schtick works out for her. but Travis is a disaster for us. When the Chair of our Planning Group  betrays our efforts for our community and his community,, how many important people in Alpine stay in the shadows instead of supporting Loveland Advocates in this terribly asymmetrical fight against Sweetwater and their allies throughout the county , Sacramento, and  California regulatory agencies? Mr. Lyon's  own board won't say anything even though they have repeatedly voted to support Loveland fighters starting seven months before Sweetwater destroyed it all on November 15th ,2022.

  

Most recently but already long ago, about 4 months ago, the ACPG voted unanimously with one abstention, Darlene Cossio, to write letters of support to the Sweetwater Authority and Forest Service for restoration of the Sunrise to Sunset access Sweetwater is robbing lake users of since started shutting the lake early about 12 years ago. We can't make progress on fish restocking or guarantees of minimum pool with our local leaders prioritizing keeping outsiders happy with them. 

  

Thank you for your previous encouragement and for reading this far if you have. I know politics must be a tricky  business but I never imagined constituents would flat out be subjugated on recreational access at Loveland given such a plain set of facts, including land use facts that are in the Chair of the ACPG’s  wheelhouse.

  

Sincerely,

  

Russell Walsh

From: Duran, Luis
Sent: Friday, March 22, 2024 4:03 PM
To: travislyonacpg@gmail.com<mailto:travislyonacpg@gmail.com>
Subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine

Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

Here is the community  Powerpoint.
It's not exactly what Andrew Hayes asked me for last year.   He wanted a concensus on what to do with the 750k,  but I thought our loses at Loveland merited getting more community input and selling some bigger enthusiasm for projects than the 750k and I hope that does work out. Thanks for being there with us these last months and last night. 
I felt like you walked back on the SDGE  thing compared to our phone call, but will assume you are being careful not to get yourself, or Senator Jones blamed for setbacks in this possibly complicated scheme. Russell

Subject: Engagement Opportunity: Land Development Cost Recovery Proposal

Dear CPSG Chairs,

I'm reaching out to let you know about the proposed Land Development Cost Recovery (fee) package and to invite you to provide your feedback, comments, and questions via several options - whichever is most convenient for you!

Meeting to Discuss Cost Recovery (Fee) Package:
You are invited to join us on Tuesday, April 9, 2024 at 1:00pm to learn more about the proposed cost recovery package and discuss your questions, concerns, and feedback.  This meeting will be held via Zoom and the link to join is below for your convenience.

Join Zoom Meeting
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/88547050405?pwd=eIpnetmCRRbFFZNb7TuF1DVIinDncA.1

Meeting ID: 885 4705 0405
Passcode: 841594

E-mail Your Feedback:
Please feel free to submit any questions or comments via email to Sam Murray at samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

Request a Meeting:
We are happy to meet with you at your request.  Please reach out to Sam Murray at samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov> to request a meeting.

A bit more background...

What is the Land Development Cost Recovery (Fee) Package?
Fee adjustments are primarily driven by County Policy B-29, which mandates that departments recover the full cost for services provided to agencies or individuals. Like most organizations, our costs fluctuate over time. The proposed fee adjustment reflects changes that will take effect in the upcoming fiscal year, as outlined in the existing labor contract. Approving this adjustment is crucial for ensuring departmental compliance with state mandates, making informed policy decisions based on data, and addressing expanded community needs assessments.

Our comprehensive cost recovery analysis is uniformly applied across the entire County enterprise. The fee development methodology aligns with Board Policy B-29 and adheres to existing cost policies and procedures.

To determine fees and rates, all three departments (Planning & Development Services, Department of Public Works, and Department of Parks & Recreation) initiate time studies. Staff members allocate their time to specific permits and record types as they work on projects. By analyzing historical hours per project, we estimate the time needed to process each project type.

Despite rising costs, our commitment to cost containment remains steadfast. Our innovative approaches not only lower County operating costs, but also enhance efficiency for our customers. Notably:

  *   Online Processes: Over 65% of building permits are now issued online, and 70% of payments are processed digitally, reducing staff workload, and minimizing the need for in-person visits to County offices.
  *   Expanded Digital Services: Our Land Development team offers convenient online services, including permit applications, self-service reports, digital approvals, text-based inspection management, and mobile field inspections.

These cost-saving measures result in approximately $2.4 million in annual savings for our departments. By passing these benefits on to our customers, we maintain lower fees. Without these measures, plan check and building permit fees would be 8.8% higher on average, and hourly rates for PDS would increase by 3.3% (equivalent to $8.10 more per hour).

Fee Overview:
Planning and Development Services:
Average Fee Increase: $55 or 3.0%
Average Intake Deposit Increase: $279 or 3.9%
Average Hourly Rate Increase: $11.00 or 4.6%

Department of Public Works:
Average Fee Increase: $18 or 6.4%
Average Intake Deposit Increase: $132 or 4.6%
Average Hourly Rate Increase: $8 or 3.6%

Department of Parks & Recreation
                Average Hourly Rate Increase: $14 or 9.7%.

We are also proposing changing from a deposit to a flat fee for Boundary Adjustments. Currently, the deposit stands at $2,284, while the proposed flat fee is $3,643. This change reflects a significant $1,361 increase (equivalent to 59.6%). Our calculation is based on 116 applications completed over the past four years.

Please feel free to reach out with any questions or if our team may be of further assistance.  We truly appreciate your time and feedback!

Best regards,
Heather

Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Dear Interested Stakeholder,

We want to hear from you! The San Diego County Fire Protection District invites you to attend a public meeting to share your thoughts on the San Diego County Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Best Practices Report (Report). BESS are technology designed to store and manage energy for later use. It typically uses rechargeable batteries to store energy from various sources, such as the electrical grid, renewable energy sources like solar or wind power, or other power generation methods. On September 11, 2024, the Board of Supervisors directed San Diego County Fire to develop a technical study with recommendations that consider setbacks from residential uses as well as best practice safety standards, including 2023 NFPA 855. The completed report can be accessed at the project website. County Staff is looking for your feedback on the recommended best practices, safety standards, and siting recommendations for new and existing BESS applications. PDS is hosting this virtual public meeting to receive your input on November 14, 2024, at 6:00 PM (registration link provided below).

Disability-related accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting participation, language interpretation, including American Sign Language, and written materials in alternative languages and formats are available upon request. From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>
Sent: Tuesday, July 23, 2024 4:53 PM
To: Sleeper, Maggie <Maggie.Sleeper@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: [External] Please Read, Maggie, Loveland Sunrise to Sunset Petition.

  

Hi Maggie, 

  

I hope you and your family are doing great! 

  

Thank you for your efforts in utilizing  Supervisor Anderson's lakes initiative to reverse the recent threat of further reductions to the access at some of the east county area lakes. Your work has not gone unnoticed. The idea of Supervisor Anderson the COSD becoming involved in rural lakes is always popular.

  

One part of Supervisor Anderson's success with the recent threat of access loss was a petition.

  

Given Supervisor Anderson's many letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset access and other issues at Loveland Reservoir, combined with the inclusion of Sweetwater Authority lakes named in Supervisor Anderson's initiative and work by Brian Albright's Parks and Recreation,  I am hoping that Supervisor Anderson would consider spearheading a petition to open Loveland Reservoir from Sunrise to Sunset. I understand there is a possibility of the petition failing in the short term, which is undesirable. Still, it could get us out of the hopeless situation we are currently in regarding legal and practical access at the Loveland Reservoir for working people.

  

You may know that the non-profit, Friends of Loveland Reservoir's,  compromise to have volunteers close the gates at Sunset failed. Please consider a powerful petition for Sunrise to Sunset according to the easement as the credible land-use policy and next possible productive step.

  

As you have seen, Maggie, there is a growing coalition on lake access and improvements. I have been sharing what has been happening with the Lakes initiative since we met almost four years ago with these leading individuals and groups.  I believe this is a potential case of " a rising tide lifts all boats," which fits Supervisor Anderson's goals and recognition for his district's values and effort for outdoor enthusiasts. A petition for Loveland would be broadly recognized as further commitment to  Supervisor Anderson's commitment to rural area lakes for the broadest range of recreation and subsistence fishers. It would be inspirational to advocates that we both have seen as nearly hopeless in the face of losses at our lakes. 

  

Please help make this a reality. I am considering asking the individuals and groups who have begun to form a coalition on a better future for our rural lakes to initiate a petition. However, given your significant contributions to the Loveland cause, it's crucial to ask Supervisor Anderson's office to spearhead this and add willing groups as endorsers of the petition to open Loveland from Sunrise to Sunset. I can help recruit the various leading individuals and non-profits. 

  

Best regards,

  

Russell

Through these conversations, we gained critical feedback on the key issues impacting your community.  Assemblymember DeMaio has asked me to keep you updated on what we heard and how we are setting priorities for each community in our district.

First, for any constituent needing any help with service, we have set up a one-stop portal for them to contact us at www.AskCarlForHelp.org<http://www.askcarlforhelp.org/>

Second, we welcome feedback on legislation and on issues at www.ContactCarl.org<http://www.contactcarl.org/>.  Additionally, if you want Carl at an event in your area or want to set up a meeting with him or any staff, contact us at www.MeetCarl.org<http://www.meetcarl.org/>

title: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board.eml
subject: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board
body:
Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if you're interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As the Alpine Community Planning Group, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities east of Alpine, near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Marissa Twite (she/her/hers)
Account Supervisor

body:
Dear CPSG Chairs,

I'm reaching out to let you know about the proposed Land Development Cost Recovery (fee) package and to invite you to provide your feedback, comments, and questions via several options - whichever is most convenient for you!

Meeting to Discuss Cost Recovery (Fee) Package:
You are invited to join us on Tuesday, April 9, 2024 at 1:00pm to learn more about the proposed cost recovery package and discuss your questions, concerns, and feedback.  This meeting will be held via Zoom and the link to join is below for your convenience.

Join Zoom Meeting
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/88547050405?pwd=eIpnetmCRRbFFZNb7TuF1DVIinDncA.1

Meeting ID: 885 4705 0405
Passcode: 841594

E-mail Your Feedback:
Please feel free to submit any questions or comments via email to Sam Murray at samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

Request a Meeting:
We are happy to meet with you at your request.  Please reach out to Sam Murray at samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:samuel.murray@sdcounty.ca.gov> to request a meeting.

A bit more background...

What is the Land Development Cost Recovery (Fee) Package?
Fee adjustments are primarily driven by County Policy B-29, which mandates that departments recover the full cost for services provided to agencies or individuals. Like most organizations, our costs fluctuate over time. The proposed fee adjustment reflects changes that will take effect in the upcoming fiscal year, as outlined in the existing labor contract. Approving this adjustment is crucial for ensuring departmental compliance with state mandates, making informed policy decisions based on data, and addressing expanded community needs assessments.

Our comprehensive cost recovery analysis is uniformly applied across the entire County enterprise. The fee development methodology aligns with Board Policy B-29 and adheres to existing cost policies and procedures.

To determine fees and rates, all three departments (Planning & Development Services, Department of Public Works, and Department of Parks & Recreation) initiate time studies. Staff members allocate their time to specific permits and record types as they work on projects. By analyzing historical hours per project, we estimate the time needed to process each project type.

Despite rising costs, our commitment to cost containment remains steadfast. Our innovative approaches not only lower County operating costs, but also enhance efficiency for our customers. Notably:

  *   Online Processes: Over 65% of building permits are now issued online, and 70% of payments are processed digitally, reducing staff workload, and minimizing the need for in-person visits to County offices.
  *   Expanded Digital Services: Our Land Development team offers convenient online services, including permit applications, self-service reports, digital approvals, text-based inspection management, and mobile field inspections.

These cost-saving measures result in approximately $2.4 million in annual savings for our departments. By passing these benefits on to our customers, we maintain lower fees. Without these measures, plan check and building permit fees would be 8.8% higher on average, and hourly rates for PDS would increase by 3.3% (equivalent to $8.10 more per hour).

Fee Overview:
Planning and Development Services:
Average Fee Increase: $55 or 3.0%
Average Intake Deposit Increase: $279 or 3.9%
Average Hourly Rate Increase: $11.00 or 4.6%

Department of Public Works:
Average Fee Increase: $18 or 6.4%
Average Intake Deposit Increase: $132 or 4.6%
Average Hourly Rate Increase: $8 or 3.6%

Department of Parks & Recreation
                Average Hourly Rate Increase: $14 or 9.7%.

We are also proposing changing from a deposit to a flat fee for Boundary Adjustments. Currently, the deposit stands at $2,284, while the proposed flat fee is $3,643. This change reflects a significant $1,361 increase (equivalent to 59.6%). Our calculation is based on 116 applications completed over the past four years.

Please feel free to reach out with any questions or if our team may be of further assistance.  We truly appreciate your time and feedback!

Best regards,
Heather

title: Electronic Filing of Form 700 for 2024.eml
subject: Electronic Filing of Form 700 for 2024
body:
Good afternoon Community Group Members,

As we approach the new year, this email is to inform you that annual Form 700 filings shall no longer be mailed to PDS.

On October 25, 2023, the Board of Supervisors approved an update to Policy I-1<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/Groups/Chair_Resources/I-001.pdf> which requires all Form 700 filings by CPG members AFTER their initial filing to be done with the Clerk of the Board. Previously, all CPG members were required to mail all filings to PDS, who in turn submitted them to the Registrar of Voters. The exact language is as follows: "All initial statements by new planning group members or candidates shall be filed with the Registrar of Voters. All other statements shall be filed with the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors."

To simplify the filing process for you, as well as to align with the County of San Diego's sustainability initiatives, as of January 1, 2024, the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors is requiring all Form 700 filings to be submitted electronically via its online filing portal, eDisclosure<https://www.southtechhosting.com/SanDiegoCounty/eDisclosure/>.

As final arrangements are made to update each group's Conflict of Interest codes and to prepare for the transition, we ask that all members please hold their filing of Form 700 until they receive their login information. We are working to complete this process as quickly as we can, and we anticipate it to be completed by the end of February.

Please feel free to reach out with any questions you may have. Below is more information regarding eDisclosure from the Clerk of the Board.

________________________________

As an online system, eDisclosure provides the ability to file forms whenever and wherever is most convenient for filers. The system prepopulates forms with the filer's name and position information, and automatically reviews forms for missing information. Submitted forms are automatically stored in eDisclosure for easy access by the filer, Agency Officials, and Clerk of the Board staff. eDisclosure also pulls information from the previous year to assist annual filers. Electronic filings will alleviate the need to mail or submit a Form 700 in person. Filings will no longer be rejected for illegible or incomplete information. Agency officials are able to update their filers' information, track filer submissions, and view filed forms as they are submitted.

The Clerk of the Board of Supervisors introduced eDisclosure in 2012, with the intent of providing a simple and secure method for filers to file their Form 700 electronically. Since its inception, filers have submitted more than 20,000 Form 700s via eDisclosure. Year after year, the use of eDisclosure has continued to grow. During the annual filing season this year, more than 90% of filings were submitted electronically. These numbers show that more and more filers are converting from paper filing to electronic filing.

Our office is committed to make the transition to electronic filing as smooth as possible. We strongly believe that eDisclosure will guide filers and agencies through a simplified and sustainable Form 700 filing future.

If you have any questions, please contact our Disclosures Services team at (619) 531-5601 or via e-mail at Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Form700@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

________________________________

Respectfully,

body:
Hello CPSG Chairs,

Yesterday you should have received a GovDelivery notice announcing that the Draft Program Environmental Impact Report (Draft EIR) and draft ordinances for the proposed Socially Equitable Cannabis Program (Cannabis Program) are now available for public review through March 31, 2025.

We have made the documents available for review and comment on the Engage San Diego County Cannabis Program Environmental Impact Report page<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/cannabis-program-eir>. This feature allows people to view and provide their comments directly into the draft documents.

We have also created several fact sheets about the Draft EIR and ordinances to assist in your review - you can find these under "Documents" on the Engage page linked above and attached:

  *   Draft EIR Fact Sheet
  *   Draft EIR - How to Comment Tip Sheet
  *   Draft Zoning Ordinance Fact Sheet
  *   Draft Regulatory Code Fact Sheet

I wanted to personally invite you and the other members of your groups to attend one of our upcoming public comment meetings and open houses.

Virtual Meetings

*       February 6, 2025, 6:00 p.m.
*       February 12, 2025, 6:00 p.m.

body:
Hello Community Planning and Sponsor Group Chairs,

As presented at the quarterly meeting in March, we have been working to revise Climate Action Plan (CAP) Update project materials to reflect comments received during the public review period. Revised documents are now available on our project website<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/sustainability/climateactionplan/seir.html>, including a Draft Final CAP Update and a Final Supplemental Environmental Impact Report (SEIR). You can find a summary of revisions to the documents alongside comments received and responses to comments in Chapter 9 of the Final SEIR. Staff will be presenting these materials to the Planning Commission at the June 14th hearing. At this public hearing, staff will request that the Planning Commission recommend that the Board of Supervisors adopt the CAP Update.

We appreciate the time that you have taken and the perspectives that you have shared to help shape the CAP Update. Please do not hesitate to reach out with questions or comments as you review the Planning Commission staff report and revised documents.

I am happy to meet to discuss any aspects of the project ahead of the June 14th hearing, or at any time in the lead up to the proposed CAP Update adoption this fall. If you would like to meet, please reach out by email<http://meghan.kelly@sdcounty.ca.gov> or call me at (619)323-6462.

Thank you again for your time,

Meghan

title: COUNTY OF SAN DIEGOΓÇÖS ANNUAL ROAD RESURFACING PROGRAM UPDATE (2024).eml
subject: COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO’S ANNUAL ROAD RESURFACING PROGRAM UPDATE (2024)
body:
Dear Chairperson:

The purpose of this email is to provide you with an update on our progress to resurface public roads in the County of San Diego’s (County) unincorporated areas.  The Department of Public Works (DPW) Annual Resurfacing Program (Program) was developed to balance community input, funding availability, pavement management software recommendations, and operational safety requirements.  Our Program was first introduced in 2015 and has been successful in developing resurfacing projects for our 1,947.44 publicly maintained miles of roadway that meet community and maintenance needs Countywide through multiple resurfacing projects.

As you know, DPW must respond to unforeseen occurrences such as natural disasters, public safety emergencies, and other changes that could affect future project funding availability.  As with previous years, construction costs continue to increase due to inflation, higher energy, labor, and construction material costs.  Therefore, it became necessary to make various revisions to our planning lists certain roads.  DPW’s Annual Roadway Resurfacing Program<http://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/dpw/roads/Resurfacing_Program.html> website has been updated to reflect completed and planned work, including 2024-25 resurfacing lists.  The website provides status of individual road segments.  It is updated as projects are completed and/or changes become necessary to our Program.  Resurfacing projects can be found by clicking on the link and navigating to your community or neighborhood for more detailed information.

The table below sums up the distribution of resurfacing miles since the beginning of our Program in 2017-18 to 2022-23.  Resurfacing projects include replacement of culverts and other accessibility improvements.

The 2023-24 resurfacing projects (Year Seven) list of roads is updated and available on the interactive map, currently being prepared for competitive bid and estimated to include approximately 120.23 miles of road resurfacing.

The 2024-25 resurfacing projects (Year Eight) list of roads is complete, sorted by community, and attached for your convenience.  These projects are in the design process and are being evaluated for potential utility, private development project conflicts, drainage, and accessibility improvement needs, and include 100.32 miles of roads.

The total anticipated road resurfacing for the first eight years of our Program will result in the completion of almost 950 miles of resurfaced roads, or about 49% of the total number of DPW’s publicly maintained roads.  DPW will continue to work on future year projects for the County’s Road resurfacing program and will share updates on our interactive website, when available.

We appreciate your ongoing support for this program as we work to address road resurfacing needs throughout the unincorporated County. subject: County of San Diego Department of Public Works:  Resurfacing Program Status FY 25-26
attachments: Attachment A Exhibit A1 -Road List FY 2526.pdf
body:
San Diego County Community Group Chairs,

The San Diego County Department of Public Works (DPW) is reaching out with an update regarding the status of our FY 2025-26 annual resurfacing program. No action is required from you related to this update.

DPW is committed to ensuring safe and efficient roadways.  To achieve this, DPW has implemented a robust resurfacing program focused on improving the Pavement Condition Index (PCI), a measure of pavement quality.  The program aims to identify, design and construct resurfacing projects for the County's approximately 2,000 miles of roads based upon several factors including funding, need and community input. In order to receive state Senate Bill 1 funding,  DPW is required to submit an annual list of proposed projects to the state by July 1st.

For FY 25-26, DPW is proposing the attached list of roads to the Board of Supervisors for approval.

If approved, these roads are planned for construction sometime in 2026-2027 following design related activities.  As construction nears, DPW will reach out to Community Planning Groups with a final list of roads in their respective area and a further refined schedule.

To learn more about DPW's resurfacing plan or to view our interactive map with current and past resurfacing projects please visit  https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/dpw/roads/Resurfacing_Program.html.

Sincerely,

County of San Diego DPW

title: County Fire Fee Increases.eml
subject: County Fire Fee Increases
body:
Dear Planning/ Sponsor Group Chair,

San Diego County Fire (County Fire) provides essential life and safety services, which includes annual business and State-mandated fire inspections and plan check reviews of development projects. This work is done to ensure residents and visitors are safe from potential fire hazards. Like nearly all local governments, County Fire has fees and charges that are approved by our governing body, the San Diego County Board of Supervisors, and we review those charges to account for and offset the cost of providing fire inspections and plan check reviews.

Please accept this email as early notification that County Fire has reviewed our fees and will be proposing a revision to the Board of Supervisors. The current fee schedule has not been updated since early 2020. One proposed change to highlight is to begin charging for business and State-mandated inspections. These updates would be effective on July 1, 2025, and only impact the San Diego County and Deer Springs Fire Protection Districts. Residents living in other unincorporated fire protection districts are not impacted by this proposal. The Board of Supervisors is expected to receive the proposed fee schedule on April 22, 2025, at a noticed public hearing.

County Fire remains committed to working collaboratively and staying engaged with our communities. For more information on the proposed fee schedule, please visit our Engage Site, Fire District Fees Increase Engage page<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/fire-fees>. A community listening session will be held on March 27, 2025, at 6pm to answer questions and obtain feedback that will be shared with the Board of Supervisors. We encourage you to submit any questions to the Engage Site and participate in the listening session.

Sincerely,

DAVID SIBBET, Fire Services Coordinator

title: Controversial Cottonwood Sand Mine Project Heads to County Planning Commission.eml
subject: Controversial Cottonwood Sand Mine Project Heads to County Planning Commission
body:
Media AdvisoryContact:Barry Jantz619-300-3795
Following years of growing public opposition, Cottonwood Sand Mine proposal now on its way to County Planning CommissionLocal Planning Group to meet Tuesday, as community is again called to actionFollowing a more than six year process, including thousands of members of the public signing opposition petitions, expressing concerns at several public meetings, and sending hundreds of letters detailing the many significant safety, environmental, and community impacts, the controversial Cottonwood Sand Mine proposal is now making its way to the San Diego County Planning Commission.While the Planning Commission is slated to consider the project application and EIR in April, the Valle de Oro Community Planning Group will meet Tuesday night to finalize a recommendation to the County:Valle de Oro Community Planning Group - Public MeetingTuesday, March 18, 2025, 7:00 p.m.Rancho San Diego Library11555 Via Rancho San DiegoEl Cajon, CA 92019 The Stop Cottonwood Sand Mine Committee will present its opposition to the project during the meeting. The Committee is expressing continued concerns that a Major Use Permit for a more than 10-year open pit sand mining operation — on the site of the Cottonwood Golf Course along the Sweetwater River — is out of character with the already established Rancho San Diego community, made up of nearby homes, schools, and businesses. The project is also inconsistent with the County General Plan and Community Specific Plan.The Committee is calling on the thousands of individuals who have signed up online and previously expressed opposition to the project to again take action by expressing their opposition to the Planning Commission. For more information:https://www.stopcottonwoodsandmine.com/###Detailed Background: The Cottonwood sand mine is proposed by New West Investment and investor Michael Schlesinger, who purchased Cottonwood Golf Course in 2015, four years after the golf course filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. As originally filed, the proposal is to mine 4.7 million cubic yards with approximately 3.8 million cubic yards (5.7 million tons) of construction aggregate produced over ten years, in phases with reclamation planned after each phase. Approximately 214.4 acres of the approximately 280-acre site are proposed for extractive use. The project application was filed in November 2018. In the case of the Major Use Permit sought by the developer, the detailed list of requirements previously released by the County underscores the same concerns expressed by the community regarding a long-term mine along the Sweetwater River, most notably in the middle of an established residential neighborhood surrounded by homes, schools and businesses.  Those concerns, detailed at www.stopcottonwoodsandmine.org, include traffic, safety and noise, health hazards, impacts on the environment, and decreased property values. Among the Major Project Issues identified by County Planning & Development Services:  Consistency with the San Diego County General Plan, along with the Valle De Oro Community Plan and Rancho San Diego Specific Plan – County “staff cannot move forward with a recommendation of approval until the project is found consistent with all applicable General Plan and community plan policies.” Land Use/Community Character Consistency – “The character of the area consists of residential, recreational, civic and open space uses, and the project request is for a sand mining, an extractive use ... The Rancho Specific Plan identifies the golf course serving as a buffer area and providing a larger setback to sensitive habitat areas. In order to assess the potential impacts to community character a land use and community character analysis shall be prepared…” Major Use Permit Findings – The location, size, design, and operating characteristics of the proposed use must “be compatible with adjacent uses, residents, buildings, or structures.” Among other things, consideration must be given to “the harmful effect, if any, upon desirable neighborhood character; the generation of traffic and the capacity and physical character of surrounding streets; (and) the suitability of the site for the type and intensity of use or development which is proposed.” Biological Resource Constraints – The site contains jurisdictional waters of the State of California and the United States, including protected wetlands, requiring approval from State and Federal resource agencies. “Several federally endangered and/or threatened species have been identified on the project site or within the vicinity of the project.” Given the sensitivity of the area, the agencies that must provide project approval, including the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and California Department of Fish & Wildlife. “Any impacts proposed within the National Wildlife Refuge would require…an environmental document that addresses both state and federal environmental requirements.” Visual Resources – “Based on an initial review, it appears the proposed project may adversely affect visual resources. Willow Glen Drive is designated as a County Scenic Road. Views from scenic vistas, scenic highways and County Scenic Routes, and public recreation areas will need to be analyzed further to determine the extent of any adverse impacts.” Additionally, a 115-page Scoping Letter issued by the County in May 2019 provides other details on the approval requirements, including the need to address impacts involving noise, air quality, altered hydrogeologic conditions, and overall “significant impacts on the environment.” The Sweetwater Authority, the public water agency that manages Loveland and Sweetwater Reservoirs, also previously sent a letter to the County detailing its concerns about the potential impacts, “…as this project proposes a variety of activities that could significantly increase pollution of the Sweetwater Reservoir.” In late 2018 over 2,300 petition signatures, emails, and comments were submitted to the County of San Diego from area residents opposed to the plan.In 2022 and 2023, well over 400 residents took part in public meetings, as County Planning & Development Services and the local Valle de Oro Community Planning Group received hundreds of comments on the proposed project and related draft Environment Impact Report circulations.

Code of Conduct for County of San DiegoBoards, Commissions, Committees, Planning and Sponsor Groups
The County of San Diego’s (County’s) wide range of boards, commissions, committees, and planning and sponsor groups serve a critical role as a mechanism for civic engagement.  While no single code of conduct can address the varied board, commission, committee and planning and sponsor group circumstances, the purpose of this universal Code of Conduct is to create standards and expectations of conduct that align with the County’s values and the “Code of Civil Discourse” from the National Conflict Resolution Center as adopted by the County’s Board of Supervisors.
All members of County boards, commissions, committees and planning and sponsor groups are expected to abide by this Code of Conduct.
By our conduct, we create an environment in which we adhere to and pledge to uphold the following values:
We acknowledge that the principal function of County of San Diego boards, commissions, committees and planning and sponsor groups (or representatives) is public service, and we therefore commit to serving the public interest and promoting the greatest public good.We recognize that our actions impact the community's trust in the County and government as a whole and commit to act with honesty and integrity.We commit to vigilance in avoiding bias or conflict of interest whether they be real or perceived, acknowledging that even the perception of such corrodes public trust.We commit to fairness, impartiality, active listening, and consideration of all points of view by setting aside our personal agendas, affiliations, and biases.  We make informed decisions after carefully weighing relevant data and assessing the merits and possible impacts.  We recognize that diversity is a strength and commit to promoting an inclusive and welcoming culture at public meetings and with each other to foster participation and representation across all our varied communities. We practice civility by fostering a professional environment of courteous, respectful, and equitable treatment of our fellow members, elected officials, County staff and the residents we serve, through our words and actions whether we agree or disagree.We are committed to fostering an environment free from violence, discrimination, intimidation, or harassment of any kind.We are committed to transparency, access to information, and promoting broad public engagement.We will respect and comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and County policies including Board of Supervisors’ Policy A-74, “Participation in County Boards, Commissions and Committees," the County’s Code of Ethics, the Political Reform Act, and the Ralph M. Brown Act.Each individual board, commission, committee or planning and sponsor group may adopt additional standards of conduct based on specific needs.  Any code of conduct violations should be addressed according to the bylaws adopted by that board, commission, committee or planning and sponsor group.
